PREFACE

前言

I conducted my first qualitative interviews while a graduate student at the University of Michigan. I had recently transferred into sociology from a master’s program in mathematical statistics and was employed part time by the university’s survey research center at the usual marginally adequate student salary. At the next desk sat another graduate student, who augmented her income on evenings and weekends by conducting qualitative interviews for a commercial firm, Ernest Dichter, Inc. I was intrigued not only by her success in income augmentation but also by the firsthand contact with respondents afforded by her method of doing so. My survey center assignment, analyzing sociometric data, brought with it no such firsthand contact. I asked whether the Dichter firm could use another interviewer, learned that it could, and started in.

我在密歇根大学读研究生时进行了我的第一次定性访谈。当时我刚从数理统计硕士项目转到社会学专业，并在大学的调查研究中心做兼职，拿着一份勉强够用的研究生薪水。我的隔壁桌坐着另一位研究生，她利用晚上和周末时间为一家名为Ernest Dichter, Inc.的商业公司做定性访谈来增加收入。我不仅对她增加收入的成功感到好奇，也对她这种方式能够与受访者直接接触而感到好奇。我在调查中心的工作是分析社会计量数据，却无法获得这种直接接触的机会。我询问Dichter公司是否需要另一位访谈员，得知他们确实需要后，便开始了这项工作。

Ernest Dichter, a Viennese refugee, was retained by American manufacturers and advertisers to tell them why people bought or failed to buy particular products. He called his data-gathering approach “depth interviewing,” probably to suggest that it dredged up its findings from respondents’ unconscious, where their buying decisions were made unbeknownst to themselves. One of Dichter’s more widely reported observations was that people saw prunes as representations of old age. He advised prune packers to put their products in a “sunshine jar” and, in their advertising, to link prunes with children. 1

维也纳难民欧内斯特·迪希特受美国制造商和广告商委托，分析人们购买或不购买特定产品的原因。他将自己的数据收集方法称为“深度访谈”，这或许暗示着这种方法能够挖掘受访者潜意识中那些他们自己都未曾意识到的购买决策。迪希特广为人知的观察之一是，人们将西梅视为老年的象征。他建议西梅包装商将产品装在“阳光罐”里，并在广告中将西梅与儿童联系起来。

I didn’t conduct interviews for the prune study, but I did for studies of fiberglass curtains, brands of scotch, and a correspondence school that promised its students it would turn them into artists. Once I received my graduate degree, I ended my work with the Dichter firm to concentrate on what was then my full-time employment, the collection and analysis of survey data. However, I continued to use qualitative interviewing for pilot studies and other small-scale studies. Gradually, I became convinced that the qualitative approach, while quite different from that of survey research, was preferable for some problems. I was particularly struck by the density of information provided by qualitative interview studies and by their usefulness for understanding the complexities of respondents’ experiences.

我没有为李子研究进行访谈，但我为玻璃纤维窗帘、苏格兰威士忌品牌以及一所承诺将学生培养成艺术家的函授学校的研究进行了访谈。获得研究生学位后，我结束了在迪希特公司的工作，专注于当时我的全职工作——收集和分析调查数据。然而，我仍然在一些试点研究和其他小规模研究中使用定性访谈。渐渐地，我确信定性方法虽然与调查研究截然不同，但在某些问题上更胜一筹。我尤其印象深刻的是定性访谈研究所提供的丰富信息，以及它们在理解受访者复杂经历方面的实用性。

Over the years I learned more about how to do qualitative interview research from many friends, colleagues, and teachers: Carol Kaye, Arlene Daniels, Ira Glick, Peter Marris, Lisa Peattie, Lee Rainwater, Martin Rein, and, through his publications as well as personal contact, Anselm Strauss. Most important for me was Everett Hughes, who brought with him to the Brandeis department of sociology, of which I was then a member, the Chicago School’s commitment to firsthand learning about people and their lives. I was the beneficiary of a long tutorial with him under the guise of acting as his co-instructor. I have also had the good fortune to work as a junior colleague with Margaret Mead and David Riesman: with the former on only a few occasions, with the latter for many years.

多年来，我从许多朋友、同事和老师那里学习了更多关于定性访谈研究的知识：卡罗尔·凯伊、阿琳·丹尼尔斯、艾拉·格里克、彼得·马里斯、丽莎·皮蒂、李·雷恩沃特、马丁·雷恩，以及通过他的著作和私人交往了解到的安塞尔姆·施特劳斯。对我而言，最重要的是埃弗雷特·休斯，他将芝加哥学派对人们及其生活的亲身学习理念带到了我当时所在的布兰迪斯大学社会学系。我曾以他的助教身份接受过他长期的指导。此外，我还有幸与玛格丽特·米德和戴维·里斯曼共事：与前者仅有几次合作，而与后者则合作多年。

Despite all this instruction, much of what I have learned about qualitative interview studies has been a product of experience, of trial and error—rather a lot of error—and trial again. Each of the qualitative interview studies I have done—and at this point there have been many, including studies of marital separation, single parenting, bereavement, and the management of work stress—has been an exploration of method as well as of substance.

尽管接受过这些指导，但我对定性访谈研究的理解大多来自于实践经验，来自于反复试验——而且是大量的试验——以及不断的尝试。我所做的每一项定性访谈研究——迄今为止已经有很多，包括关于婚姻分居、单亲抚养、丧亲之痛和工作压力管理等方面的研究——都是对方法和实质内容的探索。

I have on several occasions been responsible for teaching others to interview or to conduct interview studies. With Everett Hughes I helped establish the field training program in the Brandeis sociology department; more recently, I offered a qualitative interviewing course at the University of Massachusetts in Boston. I have also demonstrated the approach for colleagues with whom I have worked, and I have supervised Ph.D. theses based on qualitative interviews.

我曾多次负责指导他人进行访谈或开展访谈研究。我与埃弗雷特·休斯（Everett Hughes）共同在布兰迪斯大学社会学系建立了实地培训项目；最近，我还在波士顿的马萨诸塞大学开设了一门定性访谈课程。此外，我还向合作过的同事演示了这种方法，并指导过基于定性访谈的博士论文。

This book came about partly as a consequence of my offering workshops on qualitative interview studies at two annual conferences of the American Sociological Association. Those workshops convinced me that a guide to the method would be useful to people in my field and, very likely, in other fields as well.

本书的出版部分源于我在美国社会学协会的两届年会上举办的定性访谈研究工作坊。这些工作坊让我确信，编写一本关于该方法的指南对我的研究领域以及很可能对其他领域的研究人员都会有所帮助。

In this book I try to take the reader from conceptualization of a research project using qualitative interviewing as its method to production of its report. I try to be candid about the problems of this kind of research, but I hope my openness does not obscure my belief in the method’s importance for the social sciences. Some issues can be investigated in no other way. I also believe that every investigator in the social sciences should know how to conduct a qualitative interview, just as he or she should be able to interpret a statistical table. Qualitative interviewing is a fundamental method for learning about the experience of others.

本书旨在引导读者从构思以质性访谈为研究方法的研究项目，到最终撰写研究报告。我力求坦诚地探讨此类研究的不足之处，但我希望我的坦率不会掩盖我对该方法在社会科学领域重要性的信念。有些问题唯有通过质性访谈才能探究。我也认为，每一位社会科学研究者都应该掌握质性访谈的技巧，正如他们应该能够解读统计表格一样。质性访谈是了解他人经验的基本方法。

Many people have helped me with this book. I want to thank Lisa Peattie for many clarifying discussions of qualitative interview studies, Mark Kramer for his insights into the principles of nonfiction study and writing, and the other friends and colleagues who contributed ideas, observations, and suggestions: Deborah Belle, Arlene Daniels, Uta Gerhardt, David Jacobson, Marie Killilea, Gina Prenowitz, Martin Rein, and Shulamit Reinharz. Erwin Glikes, who was the book’s editor and publisher, died not long after the book’s publication. His enthusiasm encouraged me to write the book and his editorial skill helped shape it. I remain grateful to him. Mary Coffey and John Drabik, fellow members of the University of Massachusetts Work and Family Research Unit, contributed to the book’s production and cheered it on. My greatest indebtedness, as always, is to my wife, Joan Hill Weiss.

许多人都帮助我完成了这本书。我要感谢丽莎·皮蒂（Lisa Peattie）就定性访谈研究进行的诸多阐释性讨论，感谢马克·克雷默（Mark Kramer）对非虚构研究和写作原则的深刻见解，以及其他贡献了想法、观察和建议的朋友和同事：黛博拉·贝尔（Deborah Belle）、阿琳·丹尼尔斯（Arlene Daniels）、乌塔·格哈特（Uta Gerhardt）、大卫·雅各布森（David Jacobson）、玛丽·基利利亚（Marie Killilea）、吉娜·普雷诺维茨（Gina Prenowitz）、马丁·雷恩（Martin Rein）和舒拉米特·雷恩哈茨（Shulamit Reinharz）。本书的编辑和出版商欧文·格利克斯（Erwin Glikes）在本书出版后不久便去世了。他的热情鼓励我完成了这本书，他的编辑才能也帮助塑造了本书。我永远感激他。马萨诸塞大学工作与家庭研究中心的同事玛丽·科菲（Mary Coffey）和约翰·德拉比克（John Drabik）也为本书的出版做出了贡献，并给予了大力支持。一如既往，我最感激的是我的妻子琼·希尔·韦斯（Joan Hill Weiss）。

Chapter 1
INTRODUCTION

第一章 引言

WHY WE INTERVIEW

我们为什么要进行面试

Interviewing gives us access to the observations of others. Through interviewing we can learn about places we have not been and could not go and about settings in which we have not lived. If we have the right informants, we can learn about the quality of neighborhoods or what happens in families or how organizations set their goals. Interviewing can inform us about the nature of social life. We can learn about the work of occupations and how people fashion careers, about cultures and the values they sponsor, and about the challenges people confront as they lead their lives.

访谈让我们得以了解他人的观察。通过访谈，我们可以了解我们未曾到访或无法前往的地方，以及我们未曾生活过的环境。如果我们找到了合适的受访者，就能了解社区的状况、家庭内部的情况，以及组织如何设定目标。访谈能够帮助我们了解社会生活的本质。我们可以了解各种职业的工作内容以及人们如何规划职业生涯，了解不同的文化及其所秉持的价值观，以及人们在生活中所面临的挑战。

We can learn also, through interviewing, about people’s interior experiences. We can learn what people perceived and how they interpreted their perceptions. We can learn how events affected their thoughts and feelings. We can learn the meanings to them of their relationships, their families, their work, and their selves. We can learn about all the experiences, from joy through grief, that together constitute the human condition.

我们还可以通过访谈了解人们的内心体验。我们可以了解人们的感知以及他们如何解读这些感知。我们可以了解事件如何影响他们的思想和情感。我们可以了解他们的人际关系、家庭、工作以及自我对他们的意义。我们可以了解构成人类生存状态的所有体验，从喜悦到悲伤。

Interviewing gives us a window on the past. We may become aware of a riot or a flood only after the event, but by interviewing the people who were there we can picture what happened. We can also, by interviewing, learn about settings that would otherwise be closed to us: foreign societies, exclusive organizations, and the private lives of couples and families.

访谈为我们打开了一扇了解过去的窗口。我们或许只能在骚乱或洪水发生后才有所察觉，但通过采访亲历者，我们就能想象出当时的情景。此外，通过访谈，我们还能了解那些原本与我们隔绝的领域：外国社会、精英组织，以及夫妻和家庭的私密生活。

Interviewing rescues events that would otherwise be lost. The celebrations and sorrows of people not in the news, their triumphs and failures, ordinarily leave no record except in their memories. And there are, of course, no observers of the internal events of thought and feeling except those to whom they occur. Most of the significant events of people’s lives can become known to others only through interview.

访谈能挽救那些原本会被遗忘的事件。那些不常出现在新闻报道中的人们的喜怒哀乐、成功与失败，通常除了他们自己的记忆之外，不会留下任何记录。当然，除了亲身经历者之外，没有人能够观察到他们内心的想法和感受。人们生活中的大多数重要事件，只有通过访谈才能为他人所知。

SURVEY INTERVIEWING AND QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWING

调查访谈和定性访谈

Interviews can be as prepackaged as the polling or survey interview in which questions are fixed and answers limited: “Do you consider yourself to be a Republican, a Democrat, or something else?” There is a high art to developing such items and analyzing them, and for years this has been a respected way to collect interview information.

访谈可以像民意调查或问卷调查那样预先设计好，问题固定，答案有限：“您认为自己是共和党人、民主党人，还是其他什么党派？” 设计和分析这类问题需要高超的技巧，多年来，这一直是一种备受推崇的访谈信息收集方法。

The great attraction of fixed-item, precategorized-response survey interviews is that because they ask the same questions of every respondent, with the same limited options for response, they can report the proportion of respondents who choose each option: 40% Democrat, 38% Republican, 15% Independent, 7% Other or Don’t Know. Furthermore, the standardization of question and response permits comparisons among subgroups, so that, for example, the responses of men can be compared with those of women. Categorized responses to fixed-item interviews can also serve as the raw material for statistical models of social dynamics.

固定选项、预先分类的调查访谈的最大优势在于，由于所有受访者都被问到相同的问题，且答案选项也相同，因此可以统计选择每个选项的受访者比例：40% 为民主党人，38% 为共和党人，15% 为独立人士，7% 为其他或不知道。此外，问题和答案的标准化使得不同群体之间的比较成为可能，例如，可以比较男性和女性的回答。固定选项访谈的分类回答还可以作为构建社会动态统计模型的原始数据。

Studies whose ultimate aim is to report how many people are in particular categories or what the relationship is between being in one category and another are justly called quantitative . They are quantitative not because they collect numbers as information, although they may (for example, in response to the question “How many years have you lived at this address?”), but, rather, because their results can be presented as a table of numbers (for example, in a table entitled Proportions of People in the Labor Force, Grouped by Age, Who Have at Least Some SelfEmployment Income).

那些最终目的是报告特定类别的人数或某一类别与其他类别之间关系的研究，理所当然地被称为定量研究。它们之所以被称为定量研究，并非因为它们收集数字信息（尽管它们可能收集数字信息，例如，回答“您在这个地址住了多少年？”这个问题时），而是因为它们的结果可以以数字表格的形式呈现（例如，标题为“按年龄分组的劳动力人口中至少有一些自雇收入的人口比例”的表格）。

Quantitative studies pay a price for their standardized precision. Because they ask the same questions in the same order of every respondent, they do not obtain full reports. Instead, the information they obtain from any one person is fragmentary, made up of bits and pieces of attitudes and observations and appraisals.

定量研究因其标准化的精确性而付出代价。由于它们对所有受访者提出相同的问题，且问题顺序也相同，因此无法获得完整的报告。相反，它们从任何一个人那里获得的信息都是零散的，由态度、观察和评价等片段组成。

If we want more from respondents than a choice among categories or brief answers to open-ended items, we would do well to drop the requirement that the questions asked of all respondents be exactly the same. For example, if we are free to tailor questions to respondents in a study of working mothers, we can ask a working mother who has a special-needs child about the quality of the school program she has found, and we can ask a working mother whose children are not yet school age about the worries of leaving her children in day care. And we can make clear to each respondent when we need further examples or explanations or discussions. Furthermore, we can establish an understanding with the respondents that it is their full story we want and not simply answers to standardized questions.

如果我们希望从受访者那里获得的信息不仅仅是选项或对开放式问题的简短回答，那么我们最好放弃要求所有受访者回答的问题必须完全相同的规定。例如，如果我们允许在针对职业母亲的研究中根据受访者的具体情况调整问题，我们可以询问一位有特殊需求孩子的职业母亲她所选择的学校项目的质量如何，也可以询问一位孩子尚未入学的职业母亲她对将孩子送去日托中心的担忧。我们还可以明确告知每位受访者，何时需要进一步的例子、解释或讨论。此外，我们还可以与受访者达成共识：我们想要的是他们完整的故事，而不仅仅是标准化问题的答案。

Interviews that sacrifice uniformity of questioning to achieve fuller development of information are properly called qualitative interviews, and a study based on such interviews, a qualitative interview study. Because each respondent is expected to provide a great deal of information, the qualitative interview study is likely to rely on a sample very much smaller than the samples interviewed by a reasonably ambitious survey study. And because the fuller responses obtained by the qualitative study cannot be easily categorized, their analysis will rely less on counting and correlating and more on interpretation, summary, and integration. The findings of the qualitative study will be supported more by quotations and case descriptions than by tables or statistical measures.

为了更全面地获取信息而牺牲提问一致性的访谈，恰当地被称为定性访谈；基于此类访谈的研究，则被称为定性访谈研究。由于预期每位受访者都会提供大量信息，定性访谈研究的样本量通常远小于规模适中的调查研究的样本量。而且，由于定性研究获得的更全面的回答难以归类，其分析将更多地依赖于解释、总结和整合，而非计数和关联。定性研究的发现将更多地以引文和案例描述为支撑，而非表格或统计指标。

In general, if statistical analysis is our goal, we would do better to use a survey approach. The survey approach is preferable if we want to compare some specific aspect of different groups: to compare, for example, the job satisfaction of workers in different firms. It is also preferable if we hope to use statistical analysis to identify linkages among phenomena, especially where the phenomena are unlikely to be recognized by respondents as linked. An example would the contribution of parental loss in childhood to vulnerability to depression in adult life.

一般来说，如果我们的目标是进行统计分析，那么采用调查方法会更好。如果我们想要比较不同群体的某些特定方面，例如比较不同公司员工的工作满意度，那么调查方法就更为可取。如果我们希望利用统计分析来识别现象之间的联系，尤其是在受访者不太可能意识到这些现象之间存在联系的情况下，调查方法也同样适用。例如，童年时期失去父母会对成年后患抑郁症的风险产生影响。

On the other hand, if we depart from the survey approach in the direction of tailoring our interview to each respondent, we gain in the coherence, depth, and density of the material each respondent provides.1 We permit ourselves to be informed as we cannot be by brief answers to survey items. The report we ultimately write can provide readers with a fuller understanding of the experiences of our respondents.

另一方面，如果我们摒弃问卷调查的方式，转而根据每位受访者的具体情况定制访谈内容，就能获得更具连贯性、深度和密度的信息。¹ 我们得以深入了解受访者的经历，而这仅靠问卷调查的简短回答是无法实现的。最终撰写的报告能够让读者更全面地了解受访者的经历。

We need not restrict ourselves to just the one approach. Standardized items can be appended to qualitative interviews. And usually we can produce numerical data from qualitative interview studies that have explored the same area with different respondents, although we may have to engage in a time-consuming and cumbersome coding procedure and tolerate lots of missing data.

我们不必局限于单一方法。标准化项目可以添加到定性访谈中。通常，我们可以从针对同一领域、不同受访者的定性访谈研究中获得数值数据，尽管这可能需要耗费大量时间进行繁琐的编码工作，并且可能存在大量数据缺失。

The following excerpt, from an interview conducted for a study of adjustment to retirement, provides an example of the material that can be obtained in qualitative interviews. The respondent is a woman of 66, formerly a department head in a firm in the creative arts, retired for almost 2 years at the time of the interview. This is the third interview in which she was a respondent. The first had been held before her retirement, the second a few months after it.

以下摘录自一项关于退休适应性研究的访谈记录，它提供了一个定性访谈可获取素材的范例。受访者是一位66岁的女性，曾是一家创意艺术公司的部门主管，在接受访谈时已退休近两年。这是她第三次接受访谈。第一次是在她退休前进行的，第二次是在她退休几个月后进行的。

The interview took place in one of the research project’s offices. In this excerpt the interviewer and respondent have just taken a few minutes to recall the project’s aims, and now the respondent is describing her current situation:

访谈是在该研究项目的一间办公室进行的。在这段摘录中，访谈者和受访者刚刚花了几分钟时间回顾了项目的目标，现在受访者正在描述她目前的状况：

R ESPONDENT : My life is—the euphemism I guess today is “couch potato.” I stay home. I try to go out as infrequently as I can. When I say “out,” I mean, like shopping … um, going any place. I listen to a lot of music. I read a great deal. And I watch television a great deal. I don’t see anyone. I do speak to my daughter; I speak to her on the phone. That’s it! All the things that I thought I would do, if I weren’t in a working situation … I’d be writing, I’d create, I’d start a business. I had so many ideas while I was still working. I sort of—now maybe this is fanciful thinking—but I sort of pride myself on being a person who comes up with ideas fairly easily. When I say “ideas,” I mean practical, good ideas and creative ideas. But I have no opportunity to … Oh, my only hobby is crossword puzzles, [ chuckles ] Which is more of the same, just sitting there in isolation.

受访者：我的生活——我想现在委婉的说法应该是“沙发土豆”。我待在家里。我尽量少出门。我说的“出门”是指，比如购物……嗯，去任何地方。我听很多音乐。我读很多书。我也看很多电视。我不见任何人。我会和女儿说话；我会和她打电话。就这些！所有我曾经想过，如果我不工作的话，我会做的事情……我会写作，我会创作，我会创业。我还在工作的时候，我有很多想法。我有点——现在这可能有点异想天开——但我一直很自豪自己是一个很容易想出点子的人。我说的“点子”是指实用的好点子和有创意的点子。但我没有机会……哦，我唯一的爱好是填字游戏，[轻笑] 但这其实也一样，只是独自一人坐在那里。

I’m not unhappy with my situation. But just that I feel like that the past year … wasn’t unpleasant—none of it is unpleasant—but it really didn’t matter whether I … had been alive last year or not. Except in terms of what I can offer to my daughter, who’s in Syracuse. I haven’t been to visit my daughter and her husband in almost a year. Well, partly it’s because of health. I’m afraid to drive a full six and a half hours. Because I do get very, very dizzy and have to pull up to the side of the road. So, you know, it’s difficult. But, you know, if I really wanted to open my door, I could take a plane. I could take a taxi over to the airport, and I could fly there. I mean, I could be doing things. I could find alternative ways. But I just don’t want to. I don’t know if you remember, but I’ve sort of let myself go. I’m all gray now, practically. Which is okay. If you decide to be. I’m going around in sneakers. I don’t have a pair of shoes anymore. It’s not a sloppiness. It’s just like I’m wearing house slippers all the time, you know, except that it’s acceptable in the street. It’s like nothing really matters that much. I was going to put on shoes—I mean, you know, real pumps, I mean, the kind that I used to wear—when I came here. And I … it was like I was torn between pride in my appearance and the fact that it doesn’t really matter. As long as I can be comfortable.

我对现状并不不满。只是感觉过去一年……虽然并不难熬——其实一切都挺好的——但我去年是否还活着，似乎都无关紧要了。除了我能为住在锡拉丘兹的女儿做些什么之外。我已经快一年没去看望女儿和女婿了。一部分原因是身体不好。我不敢开车六个半小时。因为我会感到非常非常晕，不得不把车停在路边。所以，你知道，这很困难。但是，你知道，如果我真的想敞开心扉，我可以坐飞机。我可以打车去机场，然后飞过去。我的意思是，我可以做很多事。我可以找到其他的办法。但我就是不想。不知道你是否还记得，我有点放任自己了。我现在几乎全白了。不过，这也没什么。如果你决定的话。我现在穿着运动鞋到处走。我已经没有鞋了。这不是邋遢。就像我一直穿着拖鞋一样，你知道，只不过这样出门是可以接受的。感觉好像什么都不重要了。我本来打算来的时候穿鞋——我是说，你知道，那种真正的高跟鞋，我以前常穿的那种。然后我……我感觉自己很纠结，一方面是对自己外表的自豪，另一方面又觉得其实穿什么都无所谓。只要舒服就好。

I NTERVIEWER : Yeah. It’s like you’ve gone through a metamorphosis?

采访者：是啊。感觉你好像经历了一场蜕变？

R ESPONDENT : Yeah. But the problem … I can understand my reacting this way for a brief time. Hey, I’m going to have the luxury of sloth. And no demands. I’m going to do whatever I want to. If I want to sleep late, I’ll sleep late. If I want to stay up ’til two or three in the morning, which I do … [ chuckles ] I could understand that as a reaction. The fact that it’s extended like almost two years just doesn’t worry me. Because if it worried me I’d do something about it. I just don’t think about it. It’s just that I don’t see any changes coming into my life, unless someone knocks on that door for me. And that’s not going to happen.

答辩人：是啊。但问题是……我能理解自己这种反应会持续一段时间。嘿，我要享受懒惰的奢侈了。而且没人要求我。我想干嘛就干嘛。想睡懒觉就睡懒觉。想熬夜到凌晨两三点，而我的确经常熬夜……（轻笑）我能理解这种反应。但这种状态持续了将近两年，我倒是不担心。因为如果担心的话，我肯定会采取行动。我只是不去想它。只是我觉得我的生活不会有任何改变，除非有人来敲我的门。而这种情况不会发生。

I NTERVIEWER : Yeah. Is this a way to capture what you’re feeling about it: that it doesn’t worry you, exactly, but it perplexes you?

采访者：是的。这是不是表达你对此感受的一种方式：它并不让你感到担忧，但让你感到困惑？

R ESPONDENT : Yeah, I just don’t understand it. INTERVIEWER: Is that right?

受访者：是啊，我就是不明白。采访者：是这样吗？

R ESPONDENT : Yeah. I really don’t understand why I’ve become a nothing person. Even just talking to you, now, I’m rambling. I’m not sure I even know how to talk to people anymore, in terms of conversation. I used to be pretty good at it. You know, I would go to all kinds of functions at work. I thought I handled myself fairly well. And now I don’t. If I were invited to a party now, I wouldn’t go. My nephew’s getting married. I just got an invitation last night in the mail. And my first reaction—I have to be honest with you here; I would never say this to anyone else—wasn’t joy for him. That was my second reaction. My first was fear. He wanting me to come to Iowa for the wedding, to meet people, to be with my family, friends, and so on. I’m not going to go. I don’t want to be seen this way. I don’t want to be with people. I had a call from my college roommate about a year ago. And I haven’t called her back. I don’t call anyone back. I’ve severed all my phone friendships, even. She’s retired … just, I mean, at that time she had just retired, and she was sending away for Chamber of Commerce “What’s On,” and “What’s to Do.” And I admired her. And I was able to enter into the conversation with her, you know, how exciting it sounded. And once I hung up, that was the end of it. And she’s not going to do anything either.

答辩人：是啊。我真的不明白为什么我变得这么没精打采。现在就算只是跟你说话，我也开始语无伦次了。我甚至不确定自己现在还能不能跟人好好说话了。我以前还挺擅长的。你知道，以前我会参加公司里各种各样的活动。我觉得自己表现得还不错。但现在不行了。如果现在有人邀请我去参加派对，我肯定不会去。我侄子要结婚了。我昨晚刚收到邀请函。说实话，我的第一反应——我绝对不会跟别人说——不是为他高兴。那是我的第二反应。我的第一反应是害怕。他想让我去爱荷华参加婚礼，见见亲朋好友，和家人朋友聚聚。我不会去的。我不想让别人看到我这副样子。我不想和人待在一起。大约一年前，我接到大学室友的电话。之后我就没再给她回过电话。我从来不回任何人的电话。我甚至断绝了所有电话里的联系。她退休了……我是说，当时她刚退休，正在帮商会寄送“活动指南”和“玩乐指南”。我很欣赏她。跟她聊起那些事，感觉挺有意思的。挂断电话后，一切就结束了。她也不会再联系我了。

I NTERVIEWER : Why do you say that, that she’s not going to do anything?

采访者：你为什么说她不会做任何事？

R ESPONDENT : Because the first thought that you have is, “Here’s an opportunity for a new life.” But I think it takes either tremendous confidence in yourself to start a new life on your own without any support or you have to be a certain kind of person who’s always been a doer and you keep doing. I think most people don’t know how to start a new life. School’s told us what to do, bosses’ve told us what to do, husbands’ve told us what to do, It’s very difficult to tell yourself what to do.

答：因为你首先想到的就是，“这是一个开启新生活的机会。”但我认为，要么你需要极强的自信才能在没有任何支持的情况下独自开始新生活，要么你必须是那种一直以来都是行动派并且会坚持不懈的人。我认为大多数人不知道如何开启新生活。学校告诉我们该做什么，老板告诉我们该做什么，丈夫告诉我们该做什么，所以很难告诉自己该做什么。

I NTERVIEWER : Yeah. Suppose somebody suggested to you, say, volunteer work. What would that mean to you?

采访者：是的。假设有人建议你去做志愿者工作，这对你来说意味着什么？

R ESPONDENT : [ short pause ] My daughter said that to me yesterday. Which is very funny. She despairs, not so much of me, but in terms of my attitude. Which is a non-attitude. Again, I’ve always hated limits, and here I’m asking for them. Isn’t that odd? Freedom, total freedom, is what I’ve always espoused. But if you were to say to me, “There’s a need for some more people to take care of this hospice or to work in this hospital and so on. Could you help out next Tuesday?” Hey, of course. But when I’ve looked at the volunteer lists—and there’s so much need—it’s two things. I don’t know where to go. Because I don’t know anyone. And second, part of it goes back to not wanting to open that door to be among people. I feel that I’ve gotten so heavy, so gray, I don’t even want people to look at me.

答辩人：[短暂的停顿] 我女儿昨天也跟我说过这话。真是太搞笑了。她感到绝望，倒不是因为我这个人，而是因为我的态度。我的态度根本就谈不上什么态度。再说一遍，我一直讨厌限制，现在我却在寻求限制。这难道不奇怪吗？自由，完全的自由，一直是我所追求的。但如果你跟我说：“这家临终关怀中心需要更多人手，或者这家医院需要更多人手等等。你下周二能来帮忙吗？” 当然可以。但是当我看了志愿者名单——而且需求量真的很大——我有两个顾虑。首先，我不知道该去哪里。因为我谁也不认识。其次，部分原因在于我不想敞开心扉去接触人群。我觉得自己变得如此沉重，如此苍白，我甚至不想让别人看到我。

I NTERVIEWER : Could you walk me through that conversation with your daughter where she made the suggestion to volunteer?

采访者：您能跟我说说您和女儿的那次谈话吗？就是她提出想做志愿者的那次谈话？

R ESPONDENT : We were talking about my mother, who died a couple of years ago. And we used to visit Ma, who lived in an apartment complex for the elderly. And there were all kinds of activities on the premises. You know, they had classes and they had socials and they had dances and so on. And we would try to coerce her into joining. You know: “Don’t sit by yourself all day in your apartment. Take a class in ceramics. Do this, do that.” And … and “There’s a Thanksgiving Dance; go down and join them.” And she wouldn’t want to do that. And we felt it would be so much better for her if she were more active, if she did meet other people and did participate. And I said that I … I suddenly understood how Ma felt. And that we were wrong in imposing our values, just because we needed people and we needed activity, on her. And I said, “Now, for the first time, I can really understand why she would prefer reading a book to going to a card game.” And my daughter said, “There has to be some way in which you can use your mind and feel that you still make a difference. And why don’t you volunteer?” I like the thought of helping others. But I don’t know now that I’m as capable of giving as I once was. When I was feeling good, I wanted to share that feeling good. I’m not feeling empty. I still care about my daughter. I still care about the sick person. I still care about what’s going on. I still … even on my pension, I still make charitable kinds of contributions. Because I do care what’s happening in this world. It’s just that I don’t know whether I can give anything.

受访者：我们当时在聊我母亲，她几年前去世了。我们以前经常去看望她，她住在一个老年公寓里。公寓里有很多活动，比如上课、社交聚会、舞会等等。我们总是想方设法劝她参加。比如：“别整天一个人待在公寓里。去上陶艺课吧。做做这个，做做那个。”还有，“感恩节舞会，去参加吧。”但她就是不愿意去。我们觉得如果她能更积极一些，多认识其他人，多参与一些活动，对她会好得多。我说，我……我突然明白了母亲的感受。我们不应该把自己的价值观强加给她，仅仅因为我们需要人陪伴，需要一些活动。我说：“现在，我第一次真正理解了她为什么宁愿读书也不愿去玩牌。”我女儿说：“你总得找个方式发挥你的才智，让自己感觉还能有所作为。为什么不去做志愿者呢？”我喜欢帮助别人的想法。但我现在不知道自己是否还能像以前那样乐于奉献。以前心情好的时候，我渴望与人分享这份快乐。我并不觉得空虚。我仍然关心我的女儿。我仍然关心病人。我仍然关心世事变迁。我仍然……即使靠退休金生活，我仍然会做一些慈善捐赠。因为我真心关心这个世界正在发生的事情。只是我不知道自己是否还能贡献什么。

I NTERVIEWER : What did your daughter say?

采访者：你女儿说了什么？

R ESPONDENT : Well, she feels that I ought to try. She feels that I ought to go … someplace. If I find it unpleasant, I can always stop. It isn’t like taking a job. But it’s that tremendous inertia. It looks like I’d have to climb a mountain to take the first step out. I think once I made that step I could do it. It’s climbing a psychological mountain, [pause] Maybe it’s just the fact that I feel so alone. You know, maybe there’s a difference when a person is retiring and has someone—or some ones—there to help.

答辩人：嗯，她觉得我应该试试。她觉得我应该去……某个地方。如果我觉得不舒服，随时可以停下来。这跟找工作不一样。但就是那种巨大的惯性。感觉就像要爬一座高山才能迈出第一步。我想一旦迈出那一步，我就能坚持下去。这就像攀登一座心理上的高山，[停顿] 也许只是因为我感到太孤独了。你知道，也许一个人退休的时候，如果有人——或者几个人——在身边帮忙，情况就会不一样。

The excerpt displays the depth and development achievable in qualitative interviewing. It also suggests the contribution qualitative interviewing can make to understanding a situation. Although we would need corroboration from interviews with others among the retired to have confidence in generalization, we see in this interview a process by which retirement makes it easy for those who live alone to slide into isolation.

这段摘录展现了定性访谈所能达到的深度和广度，也表明了定性访谈对理解特定情境的贡献。虽然我们需要对其他退休人士进行访谈以验证其结论的普遍性，但从这次访谈中我们可以看到，退休生活使得独居者更容易陷入孤立。

The process begins with the removal, following retirement from work, of the obligation to participate in social activity. To be sure, the newly retired person may for a time find solitude rewarding after the stresses and demands of work life. Solitude can then be a welcome opportunity for reading and lazing and puttering around the house. But as social withdrawal becomes more established, the prospect of having to mobilize energy to interact with others may bring increasing discomfort to the person who is alone. The person may, like the woman in the interview excerpt, be uncertain of having anything to give and so of being worthy of respect, and may think, “Why subject myself to discomfort when it is possible just to stay home?” Withdrawal thus becomes selfreinforcing.

这个过程始于退休后摆脱了参与社交活动的义务。诚然，新退休人士在经历了工作的压力和种种要求后，或许会发现独处一段时间是一种享受。独处可以成为阅读、休闲和在家闲逛的绝佳机会。但随着社交退缩逐渐成为一种习惯，需要调动精力与他人互动可能会给独处者带来越来越多的不适。就像访谈摘录中的那位女士一样，她可能会怀疑自己是否还有什么可以付出，是否值得被尊重，并会想：“既然可以待在家里，何必让自己承受这种不适呢？” 如此一来，社交退缩便形成了一种自我强化的恶性循环。

What we have gained from this qualitative interview is an observer’s report of one possible impact of retirement. The report could have been provided only by the respondent herself; only she was in a position to make its observations. And the report could have been developed only in an interview that encouraged the respondent to provide a full account.

我们从这次定性访谈中获得的是一位观察者对退休可能产生的一种影响的报告。这份报告只能由受访者本人提供；只有她才能做出这样的观察。而且，这份报告也只能在鼓励受访者全面讲述的访谈中形成。

Qualitative interviews can have different emphases. In this interview excerpt the respondent provided information about her internal state: her mental and emotional functioning, her thoughts, and her feelings. If the interview had been collected in a study with a different focus, the respondent might have given more emphasis to external events, for example, the functioning of the retirement program provided by her company. Qualitative interviews may focus on the internal or the external; what is common to them all is that they ask the respondent to provide an observer’s report on the topic under study.

定性访谈可以侧重不同的方面。在这段访谈摘录中，受访者提供了关于她内心状态的信息：她的心理和情绪状态、想法和感受。如果这段访谈是在其他研究的重点领域进行的，受访者可能会更侧重于外部事件，例如她所在公司提供的退休计划的运作情况。定性访谈可以关注内部因素，也可以关注外部因素；它们的共同之处在于，都要求受访者以观察者的视角，就研究主题提供一份报告。

The style of the qualitative interview may appear conversational, but what happens in the interview is very different from what happens in an ordinary conversation. In an ordinary conversation each participant voices observations, thoughts, feelings. Either participant can set a new topic, either can ask questions. In the qualitative interview the respondent provides information while the interviewer, as a representative of the study, is responsible for directing the respondent to the topics that matter to the study. Note that the interviewer in the excerpt asked, about the college roommate, not what her work had been or where she was now living, but why the respondent believed that she too would fail to achieve the active postretirement life she was planning. The interviewer was also responsible for judging when the respondent’s report was adequate and when it needed elaboration, and, should elaboration have seemed desirable, for helping the respondent expand her responses without constraining the information she might provide. As would be the case with any interviewer in an interview that was going well, the interviewer here said much less than the respondent. The interviewer at no point engaged the respondent in the small exchanges of ordinary conversation by, for example, matching one of the respondent’s observations with an observation of his own. Nor did he at any point introduce his own experiences, not even to note, by saying something like “Yeah, I know what you mean,” that he had had experiences similar to the respondent’s. It was the respondent’s account that was important.

定性访谈的风格看似对话式，但访谈内容与日常对话截然不同。在日常对话中，每位参与者都会表达自己的观察、想法和感受。任何一方都可以提出新的话题，也可以提出问题。而在定性访谈中，受访者提供信息，而作为研究代表的访谈者则负责引导受访者讨论与研究相关的关键主题。例如，在节选中，访谈者询问受访者的大学室友，并非她之前的工作或现在的居住地，而是她认为自己无法实现退休后积极生活计划的原因。访谈者还负责判断受访者的回答是否充分，何时需要进一步阐述；如果需要进一步阐述，访谈者则应帮助受访者扩展回答，同时又不限制其提供的信息。正如任何一次进展顺利的访谈一样，访谈者在此的发言远少于受访者。访谈者始终没有与受访者进行任何日常对话式的交流，例如，将受访者的某个观察与自己的观察进行呼应。他也没有提及自己的经历，甚至没有像“是的，我明白你的意思”那样表示自己有过类似的经历。受访者的叙述才是最重要的。

The interviewer was often encouraging. If you were to listen to the tape of this excerpt, you would hear an occasional murmured “Yeah” and “Uh-huh,” by which the interviewer not only indicated that he understood but also affirmed that, yes, this is the right sort of material. The interviewer’s voice was mostly serious, respectful, interested. The respondent’s voice was mostly relaxed, unhurried, reflective, and inward. If you had watched the interview, you would have seen the interviewer smile when the respondent reported an incident she believed comic and become more sober as she described her withdrawal. But mostly the interviewer expressed a desire to understand whatever it was the respondent was saying.

采访者常常给予鼓励。如果你听这段录音，会听到偶尔低声的“嗯”和“啊哈”，这不仅表明采访者理解了受访者的诉求，也肯定了受访者所说的内容是正确的。采访者的语气大多严肃、尊重且充满兴趣。受访者的语气则大多放松、不慌不忙、沉思且内敛。如果你看过这段采访，你会看到，当受访者讲述一件她认为滑稽的事情时，采访者会微笑；而当她描述自己如何退缩时，采访者的语气则会变得严肃起来。但总的来说，采访者表达的是想要理解受访者所讲述的一切。

SOME CONSIDERATIONS IN UNDERTAKING A QUALITATIVE INTERVIEW STUDY

开展定性访谈研究时需要考虑的一些因素

REASONS TO CONDUCT A QUALITATIVE INTERVIEW STUDY

开展定性访谈研究的理由

Research aims should dictate research method. Here are research aims that could make the qualitative interview study the method of choice:

研究目的应决定研究方法。以下研究目的可能使定性访谈研究成为首选方法：

  1. Developing detailed descriptions . We may want to learn as much as we can about an event or development that we weren’t there to see. For example, we may want the fullest report possible of how it happened that someone began drug use, of what the daily round is like for someone who is retired, or of the events of a prison rebellion. We may well want to interview more than one informant and integrate their reports, but we will in any event want from our informants the fullest, most detailed description possible.
    撰写详尽的描述。我们可能希望尽可能多地了解我们未曾亲眼目睹的事件或发展。例如，我们可能想要获得尽可能完整的报告，了解某人是如何开始吸毒的，退休人员的日常生活是怎样的，或者监狱暴动的经过。我们很可能需要采访多位线人并整合他们的报告，但无论如何，我们都希望从线人那里获得尽可能完整、详细的描述。
  2. Integrating multiple perspectives . We may want to describe an organization, development, or event that no single person could have observed in its totality. We may want, for example, to describe the structure and functioning of a federal agency or the impact on a community of a flood. Although interviews are necessary, standardized questions won’t work, because every respondent will have different observations to contribute. Historians, biographers, and journalists deal regularly with problems of this sort and regularly do qualitative interview studies.
    整合多方视角。我们可能想要描述某个组织、发展或事件，而这并非任何个人都能全面观察到的。例如，我们可能想要描述联邦机构的结构和运作方式，或者洪水对社区的影响。虽然访谈必不可少，但标准化的问卷并不适用，因为每位受访者都会有不同的见解。历史学家、传记作家和记者经常处理这类问题，并经常进行定性访谈研究。
  3. Describing process . We may want to know, about some human enterprise, how events occur or what an event produces. Economists assume that retailers set prices to maximize profit. But is this in fact the basis for price setting, and if it is, just how do merchants go about deciding how to maximize their profits? Qualitative interviews with merchants can make evident the processes they use. 2 Or we read in the newspapers about “deadbeat dads” and assume that divorced fathers who withhold child support must be indifferent to the welfare of their children. But is this the case? What leads some fathers who no longer live with their children to fail to contribute to the children’s support? Again, qualitative interviews can elicit the processes antecedent to an outcome of interest. Each of the questions in these examples is a particular expression of the more general question “What are the processes by which an event occurs?” We might also be interested in the consequences of events; for example, how do husbands and wives go about resolving marital quarrels?
    描述过程。我们可能想了解某些人类活动中，事件是如何发生的，或者事件会产生什么结果。经济学家假设零售商定价是为了实现利润最大化。但这真的是定价的依据吗？如果是，商家究竟是如何决定如何最大化利润的？对商家进行定性访谈可以揭示他们所使用的过程。或者，我们在报纸上读到关于“不负责任的父亲”的报道，并认为那些拒付子女抚养费的离异父亲一定对子女的福祉漠不关心。但事实真是如此吗？是什么导致一些不再与子女共同生活的父亲不支付子女的抚养费？同样，定性访谈可以揭示导致我们感兴趣的结果的过程。这些例子中的每一个问题都是对更普遍的问题“事件发生的流程是什么？”的具体表达。我们可能也对事件的后果感兴趣；例如，夫妻如何解决婚姻争吵？
  4. Developing holistic description . By putting together process reports from people whose behaviors interrelate—putting together the reports of retailers and customers or of institutional psychiatrists and institutionalized patients—we can learn about systems. Qualitative interview study may well be the method of choice if our aim is to describe how a system works or fails to work. Thus, we might rely on qualitative interviewing of members of a family to understand the nature of their family life, and qualitative interviewing of members of an organization to understand how the organization works, how it moves toward goals or is paralyzed by internal friction. In general, the dense information obtained in qualitative interviewing permits description of the many sectors of a complex entity and how they go together.
    发展整体描述。通过整合行为相互关联的人员的过程报告——例如零售商和顾客的报告，或机构精神科医生和住院患者的报告——我们可以了解系统。如果我们的目标是描述一个系统如何运作或失效，那么定性访谈研究很可能是最佳方法。因此，我们可以通过对家庭成员进行定性访谈来了解其家庭生活的本质，也可以通过对组织成员进行定性访谈来了解组织的运作方式、如何朝着目标前进或如何因内部摩擦而停滞不前。总的来说，定性访谈中获得的丰富信息能够帮助我们描述复杂实体的各个组成部分及其相互关系。
  5. Learning how events are interpreted . We might want to learn not so much about an event as about how it is interpreted by participants and onlookers. For example, we might be interested in studying responses to a film. Here we already know the “event” but want to learn the reactions of those who were its audience. 3 We might want to know how they thought about what happened in the film, what sorts of causes they identified, and what sorts of consequences they worried about. Qualitative interviewing enables us to learn about perceptions and reactions known only to those to whom they occurred. 4
    了解事件的解读方式。我们或许更想了解参与者和旁观者如何解读事件，而非事件本身。例如，我们可能对研究观众对一部电影的反应感兴趣。我们已经知道“事件”本身，但想了解观众的反应。我们可能想知道他们如何看待电影中发生的事情，他们识别出了哪些原因，以及他们担心哪些后果。定性访谈使我们能够了解只有亲历者才能体会到的感知和反应。
  6. Bridging intersubjectivities . We might want to produce a report that makes it possible for readers to grasp a situation from the inside, as a participant might. Qualitative interview studies can approach the “you are there” vividness of a documentary. They can foster the kind of understanding that might be expressed as “Had I been in that situation, I’d have acted that way too.” Quotations from interview material can help the reader identify with the respondent, if only briefly, by presenting events as the respondent experienced them, in the respondent’s words, with the respondent’s imagery. 5
    弥合主体间性。我们或许希望撰写一份报告，让读者能够像参与者一样，从内部视角理解某个情境。定性访谈研究可以达到纪录片那种“身临其境”的生动效果。它们能够促进一种理解，这种理解可以表达为“如果我身处那种情境，我也会那样做”。访谈材料的引述能够帮助读者与受访者产生共鸣，即使只是短暂的共鸣，因为这些引述是通过受访者的语言和描述，呈现他们亲身经历的事件。
  7. Identifying variables and framing hypotheses for quantitative research . Qualitative interview studies can provide preparation for quantitative research. Those who do quantitative research require variables to measure, issues about which to frame questions, and hypotheses to test. Variables, issues, and hypotheses can come from prior research, be inferred from theory, or be proposed on grounds of common sense, but where none of these does well enough, qualitative interviewing often is asked to fill the gap. The descriptions of process and system that are likely to emerge from a qualitative interview study can inform quantitative investigators about what matters in their intended topic. 6
    识别变量和构建定量研究的假设。定性访谈研究可以为定量研究做好准备。定量研究人员需要测量变量、构建问题所关注的问题以及检验假设。变量、问题和假设可以来自先前的研究、从理论中推断，或基于常识提出，但如果这些方法都不够完善，通常会借助定性访谈来弥补不足。定性访谈研究中可能出现的关于过程和系统的描述，可以帮助定量研究人员了解其研究主题的关键所在。

Young investigators are sometimes discouraged from undertaking qualitative research studies because of the time they require and their purportedly limited scientific utility. Let us consider each of these issues.

年轻的研究者有时会因为定性研究耗时较长且其科学价值被认为有限而望而却步。让我们逐一探讨这些问题。

TIME

时间

Qualitative interview studies have the reputation of being labor intensive. Indeed, if undertaken as a Ph.D. thesis, where there are likely to be large ambitions and limited resources, a qualitative interview study can stretch on and on. Several months may be required for the interviewing, and the analysis of the interviews can take even longer.

定性访谈研究素来以耗时费力著称。的确，如果将其作为博士论文的研究课题，由于目标远大而资源有限，定性访谈研究可能会旷日持久。访谈本身可能需要数月时间，而访谈分析则可能需要更长时间。

But journalists, working against deadlines, find any number of shortcuts available for the completion of qualitative interview studies: They can limit their interviewing to those whom they can reach quickly, and they can do much of their interviewing by telephone. They can not only analyze as they go—most people who do qualitative interview studies do this—but also work out their story in their minds. Once their interviewing is done, they may need to devote only a bit more time to thinking about the meanings of their material before they move to writing about it. A qualitative interviewing study can be enormously time consuming, but it need not be.

但记者们在截稿期限的压力下，会想方设法走捷径来完成定性访谈研究：他们可以只采访那些能够快速联系到的人，而且大部分访谈都可以通过电话进行。他们不仅可以边访谈边分析——大多数进行定性访谈研究的人都会这样做——还可以在脑海中构思故事。访谈结束后，他们可能只需要花一点时间思考素材的意义，就可以开始撰写文章了。定性访谈研究可能非常耗时，但并非一定如此。

It should also be noted that the time required by qualitative interview studies tends to be well invested. Most of it goes into an effort to understand the issues of the research. It is entirely possible for investigators who do quantitative work to end a study knowing more about the statistical packages they have used for computer analysis than about the topic of their study. By contrast, those who do qualitative interview studies invariably wind up knowing a lot about the topic of their study. 7

还应注意的是，定性访谈研究所需的时间往往是值得的。大部分时间都用于理解研究问题。从事定量研究的研究人员完全有可能在研究结束时，对他们用于计算机分析的统计软件包的了解，比对研究主题的了解还要多。相比之下，从事定性访谈研究的研究人员最终总是会对他们的研究主题有深入的了解。

VALUE AS CONTRIBUTION TO KNOWLEDGE

价值即对知识的贡献

As I noted earlier in this chapter, a qualitative interview study is poorly suited to the production of statistics or the numerical raw materials for statistical models. In consequence, economists and others committed to the development of statistical models sometimes disparage the reports produced by qualitative interview studies. They may characterize these results as anecdotal, because they rely on accounts provided by a relatively small sample of respondents, or as impressionistic, implying not only that they are imprecise but also that they are more a product of art than of objective scientific method. 8

正如我在本章前面提到的，定性访谈研究并不适合生成统计数据或为统计模型提供数值原始数据。因此，致力于统计模型开发的经济学家和其他人士有时会贬低定性访谈研究的报告。他们可能会将这些结果描述为轶事性的，因为它们依赖于相对较小的受访者样本提供的描述；或者将其描述为印象式的，这不仅意味着它们不够精确，而且意味着它们更像是艺术的产物，而非客观科学方法的产物。

The disparagement is unwarranted. Much of the important work in the social sciences, work that has contributed in fundamental ways to our understanding of our society and ourselves, has been based on qualitative interview studies. Qualitative interview studies have provided descriptions of phenomena that could have been learned about in no other way, including the human consequences of a disastrous flood9 and the experiences of participants in the women’s movement.10 What we know about the effects of crises in personal lives comes largely from such studies,11 as does much of what we know about the dynamics of post-traumatic stress disorder.12 Nor should qualitative interview studies be thought of as only exploratory and ground-breaking, preliminary to other more structured approaches. While it can be valuable for the results of qualitative interview studies to be verified by other methods, it can also be valuable for the results of studies done by other methods to be illuminated by qualitative interview studies.

这种贬低毫无根据。社会科学领域许多重要的研究，那些从根本上增进了我们对社会和自身的理解的研究，都建立在定性访谈研究的基础之上。定性访谈研究描述了一些其他方法无法了解的现象，例如灾难性洪水造成的人道主义后果<sup>9</sup>以及妇女运动参与者的经历<sup>10</sup>。我们对个人生活中危机影响的了解，很大程度上也来自这类研究<sup>11</sup>，我们对创伤后应激障碍动态的了解也同样如此<sup>12</sup>。定性访谈研究也不应被视为仅仅是探索性的、开创性的，或是其他更结构化方法的先导性研究。虽然用其他方法验证定性访谈研究的结果很有价值，但用其他方法进行的研究结果也可以通过定性访谈研究得到阐释。

A COMPROMISE? FIXED QUESTION, OPEN RESPONSE

折衷方案？固定问题，开放式回答

Investigators who are attracted to the richness of the materials produced by qualitative interview studies but concerned about what may seem to be their looseness sometimes conclude that fixed-question-open-response interviewing provides a desirable compromise. Here respondents are asked carefully crafted questions but are free to answer them in their own words rather than required simply to choose one or another predetermined alternative.

一些研究者被定性访谈研究产生的丰富素材所吸引，但又担心其可能存在的随意性，因此他们有时会认为固定问题开放式访谈是一种理想的折衷方案。在这种访谈中，受访者会被问到精心设计的问题，但他们可以自由地用自己的语言回答，而不是被要求从预设的选项中选择一个。

The hope of those who elect the fixed-question-open-response approach is that it will systematize the collection of qualitative material and facilitate the quantitative treatment of the material. In this approach qualitative information (albeit more in the form of summary statements than developed stories) will be collected, but because everyone will have been asked the same questions, the responses to each question can be categorized and worked with statistically. This approach makes it possible to report proportions and correlations as well as experiences and meanings.

选择固定问题开放式回答方法的研究者希望，这种方法能够系统化地收集定性资料，并便于对这些资料进行定量分析。在这种方法中，虽然会收集到定性信息（尽管更多是以总结性陈述而非完整叙述的形式），但由于所有受访者都被问到相同的问题，因此可以对每个问题的回答进行分类，并进行统计分析。这种方法使得报告比例和相关性，以及经验和意义成为可能。

Unfortunately, the fixed-question-open-response approach to data collection turns out to sacrifice as much in quality of information as it gains in systematization. The interviewer is not actually free to encourage a respondent to develop any response at length. A very long response, just like a shorter one, will have to be fitted into code categories, and interviewers, aware of this, tend to limit the length of respondents’ answers.

遗憾的是，这种固定问题开放式回答的数据收集方法，虽然在系统化方面有所提升，但在信息质量方面却牺牲了同样多。访谈者实际上无法鼓励受访者畅所欲言。过长的回答和较短的回答一样，都必须归入相应的代码类别，而访谈者也意识到这一点，因此往往会限制受访者回答的长度。

Furthermore, the very style of question asking weighs against full response. Not only must interviewers ask every question of every respondent for whom it is appropriate, but they must also follow the same ordering of the questions. The interview is directed by the schedule rather than by the respondent’s associations. The result is that the respondent, rather than being free to tell the story of what happened, is forced into a stance of answering a question, waiting for the next question, answering the next question, and so on.

此外，提问方式本身就不利于受访者充分作答。访谈者不仅必须向每位受访者提出所有合适的问题，而且还必须遵循相同的提问顺序。访谈的走向是由既定的流程决定的，而不是由受访者的联想决定的。结果是，受访者无法自由地讲述事情经过，而是被迫陷入一种被动的模式：回答一个问题，等待下一个问题，再回答下一个问题，如此循环往复。

Consider how the respondent in the excerpt given earlier in this chapter would have been dealt with in an interview using the fixed-question—open-response format. The respondent might have been asked, “Could you tell me whether your retirement is satisfactory or unsatisfactory?” Suppose the respondent replied, as she did to a similar question in the qualitative interview, “My life is—the euphemism I guess today is ߢcouch potato.ߣ I stay home.” The fixed-question interviewer would very likely then have asked, “Well, is that satisfactory or unsatisfactory?” On being told it was all right, the interviewer might have gone on to the next question. Suppose, however, that instead of going on to the next question, the interviewer had used the standard probe “Why do you say that?” to obtain further material. Now the respondent might have said, as she did in the qualitative interview, “I’m not unhappy with my situation.” Almost surely that would have been the end of the discussion of the couch potato issue. The fixed-question—open-response approach would have succeeded in getting a headline but would have missed the story.

想想本章前面摘录的受访者，如果采用固定问题-开放式回答的访谈形式，会如何应对。受访者可能会被问到：“您能告诉我您的退休生活是否满意吗？”假设受访者像在定性访谈中回答类似问题时那样回答：“我的生活——我想现在委婉的说法是‘沙发土豆’。我整天待在家里。”采用固定问题的访谈者很可能会接着问：“那么，您觉得这样满意还是不满意呢？”如果受访者回答“还好”，访谈者可能会继续问下一个问题。但是，假设访谈者没有继续问下一个问题，而是使用了标准的追问句“您为什么这么说？”来获取更多信息。这时，受访者可能会像在定性访谈中那样回答：“我对我的现状并不感到不满意。”几乎可以肯定，关于“沙发土豆”问题的讨论就此结束。这种固定问题加开放式回答的方式或许能博得头条，但却会错过故事的真正核心。

The material obtained in fixed-question—open-response interviews has another defect: it tends to be generalized rather than concrete. In our example of the retiree we probably would not have been told the significant detail of the respondent’s having traded her pumps for sneakers but would instead learn only that she would “just rather stay at home.” Indeed, because the study directors of a fixed-question—open-response survey want a brief response that covers a lot of ground, they write their questions to elicit generalizations. Thus, a typical question would be “Taking it all together, what has been the most important determinant of the way you feel these days?”

固定问题-开放式访谈所获得的信息还有另一个缺陷：它往往是概括性的，而非具体的。以我们提到的退休人士为例，我们可能不会了解到受访者用运动鞋代替高跟鞋这一重要细节，而只会知道她“只想待在家里”。事实上，由于固定问题-开放式调查的研究负责人希望获得简洁明了、涵盖面广的回答，他们设计的问题旨在引导受访者给出概括性的答案。因此，一个典型的问题可能是：“总而言之，您最近感觉如何，最重要的决定因素是什么？”

Even though fixed-question—open-response interviewing may at first appear to be a systematic approach to qualitative interviewing, it is not. It is a different approach entirely. While studies using this approach may avoid some of the vulnerabilities of qualitative interviewing studies, they also lack their strengths.

尽管固定问题-开放式访谈乍看之下似乎是一种系统化的定性访谈方法，但实际上并非如此。它完全是一种不同的方法。采用这种方法的研究或许可以避免定性访谈研究的一些缺陷，但也缺乏其优势。

THE PHASES OF QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWING RESEARCH

定性访谈研究的各个阶段

Qualitative interview studies generally begin with decisions regarding the sample to interview, move on to data collection, and conclude with analysis. But more so than is the case in quantitative research, the phases of work in qualitative research overlap and are intermeshed. Analysis of early data contributes to new emphases in interviewing, and the new data collected by the modified interviewing then produces new analyses. The investigator may draft brief reports early in a study, instead of waiting until its report-writing phase, and interviewing can continue even through the report-writing phase. Nevertheless, the focus of the research effort necessarily shifts as the study progresses from its early stages, when recruitment of respondents is likely to be a major issue, to its concluding stages, during which the investigator is primarily concerned with how best to interpret and report the data.

定性访谈研究通常始于确定访谈样本，进而进行数据收集，最后进行分析。但与定量研究相比，定性研究的各个阶段之间重叠交织的现象更为显著。早期数据的分析有助于调整访谈重点，而改进后的访谈方法所收集的新数据又会产生新的分析结果。研究者可以在研究初期就撰写简要报告，而无需等到报告撰写阶段，访谈甚至可以在报告撰写阶段继续进行。然而，随着研究的推进，研究工作的重点必然会发生变化：从早期阶段（此时招募受访者可能是一个主要问题）到后期阶段（此时研究者主要关注如何最好地解释和报告数据）。

The chapters that follow trace the likely sequence of the investigator’s concerns in a qualitative interview study: sampling, preparing for interviewing, conducting the interviews, analyzing the data, and, finally, writing the report.

接下来的章节将追溯定性访谈研究中调查人员可能关注的顺序：抽样、准备访谈、进行访谈、分析数据，以及最后撰写报告。

CHAPTER 2
RESPONDENTS: CHOOSING
THEM AND RECRUITING THEM

第二章 受访者：选择和招募他们

AIMS AND SUBSTANTIVE FRAME OF THE STUDY

研究目的和实质框架

Any research project hopes to make something known that was previously uncertain: to answer a specific question, such as how patients react to a diagnosis of a life-threatening illness; or to illuminate an area, as by showing how the family life of single parents is different from the family life of married parents. In pursuit of its aims, the research project will almost surely have to explore several related topics. To investigate how patients react to a diagnosis of a life-threatening illness, a project might explore how the patient was told, by whom, and within what context, what the patient’s anticipations were, how the patient interpreted the news, and how those close to the patient dealt with the news. The set of topics the study explores, taken together, might be said to constitute the substantive frame of the study.

任何研究项目都希望揭示此前未知的事物：解答特定问题，例如患者对危及生命的疾病诊断的反应；或阐明某个领域，例如揭示单亲家庭与已婚家庭生活的差异。为了实现其目标，研究项目几乎必然需要探索若干相关主题。例如，为了调查患者对危及生命的疾病诊断的反应，一个项目可能会探讨患者是如何被告知的、由谁告知的、在何种情况下告知的，患者的预期是什么，患者如何解读这一消息，以及患者的亲友如何应对这一消息。研究探讨的这些主题共同构成了研究的实质性框架。

The initial step in a study is to decide, provisionally, what its aims will be and what topics will be included in its substantive frame. Once these are decided, who should be talked with, and about what, can be worked out. As the investigator learns more about the area of the study, the study’s aims and frame may well be modified. One good reason for doing pilot interviews is to clarify the aims and frame of the study before interviewing its primary respondents. Even with pilot interviewing, how ever, the boundaries of the study’s frame are likely to shift as more is learned, although as the study proceeds they should shift less and less.

研究的第一步是初步确定研究目标和涵盖的主题。一旦确定了这些，就可以着手制定访谈对象和访谈内容。随着研究者对研究领域的了解不断深入，研究目标和框架很可能会进行调整。进行试点访谈的一个重要原因就是在正式访谈主要受访者之前明确研究目标和框架。然而，即使进行了试点访谈，随着了解的深入，研究框架的边界仍可能发生变化，但随着研究的推进，这种变化应该会越来越小。

The breadth of a study’s substantive frame is often a compromise between the investigator’s desires for clarity of focus and for inclusiveness. The narrower the substantive frame, the easier it is to say who should be talked with and about what. The broader the substantive frame, the more the study will eventually be able to report and, presumably, the more significant will be the study. Melville included the biology of whales and the technology of whaling within the frame of Moby Dick . Doing so enlarged his story from an account of one person’s obsession to a mythic enactment of man’s self-aggrandizing and self-destructive assault on the wonderfully complex natural order. However, in social research, when balancing clarity of focus on the one hand and ambition on the other, clarity of focus might be given preference. It’s hard enough to do a limited study well.

一项研究的实质性框架的广度通常是研究者在追求清晰聚焦和包容性之间寻求的妥协。实质性框架越窄，就越容易确定应该与谁交谈以及谈论什么。实质性框架越宽，研究最终能够报告的内容就越多，研究的意义也就越大。梅尔维尔在《白鲸》中将鲸鱼的生物学和捕鲸技术纳入其中。这样做将他的故事从一个人的痴迷叙述扩展到对人类自我膨胀和自我毁灭的、对奇妙而复杂的自然秩序的冲击的神话式演绎。然而，在社会研究中，当需要在清晰聚焦和宏大视野之间取得平衡时，清晰聚焦可能更为重要。做好一项范围有限的研究已经相当困难了。

Quite apart from the issue of its breadth, deciding just what areas the substantive frame should include can be difficult. Not only is it likely that an initial listing of areas of useful information would be incomplete, but there may be several different approaches that could be taken to explanation or description, each of which would require development of different areas.

撇开涵盖范围的问题不谈，确定实质性框架究竟应该包含哪些领域本身就是一个难题。不仅最初列出的有用信息领域很可能并不完整，而且对于解释或描述，可能存在几种不同的方法，每种方法都需要对不同的领域进行阐述。

Early in my career I was asked by a consulting group to undertake a study of a university-based executive development program. The aim was to help the administrators of the program understand the program’s problems and strengths. Without giving the matter a lot of thought, I defined the study’s frame as the experiences of the executives during their residency in the program, and so I investigated relationships among the executives and between faculty and executives, the executives’ reactions to classes and colloquia, and the home life of the executives while they were in residency. Only later did I learn that the program’s administrators would have preferred a frame that included the use executives made of the program when they were back at their jobs. The administrators, reasonably enough, wanted to know whether the program was doing the students any good. Because I did not develop the study’s substantive frame in consultation with members of its primary audience, I omitted issues of critical importance to them.

职业生涯初期，我受一家咨询公司委托，对一所大学的高管发展项目进行研究。目的是帮助项目管理者了解项目的优势和不足。我当时并未深思熟虑，便将研究框架设定为高管在项目驻场期间的体验，因此我调查了高管之间的关系、师生关系、高管对课程和研讨会的反应，以及他们在驻场期间的家庭生活。后来我才知道，项目管理者更希望研究框架能够涵盖高管重返工作岗位后如何利用项目成果。管理者们想知道项目是否真正对学员有益，这无可厚非。由于我在制定研究框架时没有与主要受众群体进行充分沟通，因此我忽略了一些对他们至关重要的问题。

If there is a clearly defined audience for the study—if, for example, the study has been commissioned, as it was in this instance—the study’s proposed substantive frame might be examined from the perspective of that audience. If representatives of that audience are available, the frame might usefully be discussed with them.

如果研究有明确的目标受众——例如，如果这项研究是受委托进行的，就像本例一样——那么可以从该受众的角度审视研究的实质性框架。如果能够联系到该受众的代表，与他们讨论该框架或许会很有帮助。

The study’s substantive frame decides who should be interviewed and what they should be asked. The “Who should be interviewed?” question will be considered in this chapter; the “What should they be asked?” question will be considered in the next.

本研究的实质性框架决定了应该采访哪些人以及应该问他们什么问题。本章将探讨“应该采访哪些人？”这个问题；下一章将探讨“应该问他们什么问题？”这个问题。

PANELS AND SAMPLES

面板和样品

There are two distinct categories of potential respondents: people who are uniquely able to be informative because they are expert in an area or were privileged witnesses to an event; and people who, taken together, display what happens within a population affected by a situation or event.

潜在的受访者分为两大类：一类是某个领域的专家，另一类是某个事件的亲历者，他们能够提供独特的信息；还有一类是能够反映受某种情况或事件影响的人群整体情况的人。

Suppose the aim of our study is to describe an event or development or institution: the management of a political convention, the operation of a nursing service, or the system governing the granting of divorce. We would do best to interview people who are especially knowledgeable or experienced. To enrich or extend our understanding, we might also want to include as respondents people who view our topic from different perspectives or who know about different aspects of it. Our aim would be to develop a wide-ranging panel of knowledgeable informants . Each member of the panel would be chosen because he or she could significantly instruct us.

假设我们的研究目的是描述某个事件、发展或机构：例如政治会议的管理、护理服务的运作或离婚制度。我们最好采访那些对此领域有深入了解或经验丰富的人士。为了丰富或拓展我们的理解，我们可能还需要邀请那些从不同角度看待我们研究主题或了解其不同方面的人士作为受访者。我们的目标是建立一个涵盖广泛领域的知识渊博的受访者小组。小组中的每一位成员都应因其能够为我们提供重要的指导而被选中。

Take the study of a bill that made it through Congress. We might want to report, eventually, on the bill’s success as a way of illuminating governmental functioning. To produce a dense description of what happened, we might talk with members of Congress who backed the bill and with people on their staff, with members of Congress who opposed the bill and people on their staff, and with reporters who cover Congress. We would try to talk with everyone in a position to know what happened in the hope that each would provide part of the story and that all of their accounts together would provide the story in full.

以一项在国会获得通过的法案为例。我们最终可能希望报道该法案的成功，以此来阐明政府运作机制。为了全面描述事件经过，我们可能会采访支持该法案的国会议员及其工作人员、反对该法案的国会议员及其工作人员，以及报道国会的记者。我们会尽可能与所有了解情况的人交谈，希望每个人都能提供部分信息，最终汇集所有信息，从而还原事件全貌。

Our approach would be different if we wanted to study the experiences or behaviors of people who have some common characteristic, people who are, in this respect, in the same boat. Suppose we wanted to know about the experiences with retirement of a sample of former professionals or how single parents manage everything they have to do or what is the impact on people’s morale and functioning of going through marital separation. For these studies what we need is a sample of people who together can represent the population of concern. If before we wanted a panel of knowledgeable informants, what we want now is a sample of representatives .

如果我们想研究具有某些共同特征的人的经历或行为，也就是那些在这方面处境相同的人，那么我们的方法就会有所不同。例如，假设我们想了解一组退休专业人士的退休经历，或者单亲父母如何兼顾所有事情，又或者婚姻破裂对人们的士气和生活状态有何影响。对于这些研究，我们需要的是一个能够代表目标人群的样本。如果说以前我们需要的是一群知识渊博的受访者，那么现在我们需要的则是一个具有代表性的样本。

Often the study of an issue can be cast in a way that requires a panel of informants but with what seems to be only slight redefinition can be recast to require a sample of representatives. Take the issue of child visitation after divorce. If we define the study’s aim as learning what is the institutional structure that governs what is done, we would want a panel of informants: scholars of family law, judges, lawyers, family court officers, and, possibly, a few parents. But if we define the study’s aim as learning how divorced mothers and fathers arrange visitation and how they are affected by their arrangements, we would want a sample of divorced mothers and fathers who might together represent the range of parental experiences.

对某个问题的研究，有时需要一组信息提供者，但只需稍作调整，就能从需要一组代表性样本转变为需要一组信息提供者。以离婚后子女探视权问题为例。如果我们把研究目标定义为了解现行制度框架如何运作，那么我们需要一组信息提供者：包括家庭法学者、法官、律师、家事法庭工作人员，以及可能还有一些父母。但如果我们把研究目标定义为了解离异父母如何安排探视权以及这些安排对他们自身的影响，那么我们需要一组离异父母样本，他们能够代表各种不同的父母经历。

We might, of course, decide to do both studies. We might want a panel of informants to tell us about the institution of child visitation and a sample of parents to tell us how it works in practice.We would then be doing two distinct studies. They would enrich each other, but our work load would be greater.

当然，我们也可以决定同时开展这两项研究。我们可能需要一组知情人士来了解儿童探视制度，也可能需要抽取一些家长样本来了解该制度在实践中的运作情况。这样一来，我们就开展了两项独立的研究。这两项研究可以相互补充，但我们的工作量也会更大。

Sometimes a respondent can be treated either as a representative of a population or as an informant, although not both at the same time. In a pilot study I did of burn victims a respondent was first an informant on the nature of advocacy organizations for burn victims—he was a member of one—and then, in a later interview, a reporter on what it had been like when he himself was burned. My relationship with the respondent was a bit different in the two interviews: in the first he was an expert instructing me; in the second he was a former victim whose story I was helping to elicit.

有时，受访者既可以被视为某个群体的代表，也可以被视为信息提供者，但两者不能同时存在。在我之前对烧伤患者进行的一项试点研究中，一位受访者最初是烧伤患者权益倡导组织的知情者（他本人就是其中之一），之后在另一次访谈中，他又以记者的身份讲述了自己被烧伤时的经历。在这两次访谈中，我与受访者的关系略有不同：第一次访谈中，他是一位专家，指导我；第二次访谈中，他是一位曾经的烧伤患者，我需要帮助他讲述自己的故事。

THE PANEL OF INFORMANTS

线人小组

The idea in a panel of informants is to include as respondents the people who together can provide the information the study requires. How do we decide just who these people are? The kind of entity we want to learn about makes a difference.

设立信息小组的目的是为了邀请那些能够共同提供研究所需信息的人员作为受访者。那么，我们如何确定这些人是谁呢？我们想要了解的群体类型至关重要。

  1. Events . We may want to report on a happening like a flood, an epidemic, a riot, or a football game; that is, an event that involves people of different backgrounds, with different perspectives, who became involved in different ways. To get a sense of the scope of the event we might begin with professionals or experts: meteorologists in a study of a flood or public health officers in a study of an epidemic. The professionals and experts can suggest the issues that have been attended to in the past and that ought to be attended to now. There may be a literature with which we should become acquainted, and the experts may be able to direct us to studies of similar events. Following this, it would make sense to find people who were caught up in the event, so that we could learn how it was experienced.
    事件。我们可能想要报道诸如洪水、疫情、骚乱或足球比赛之类的事件；也就是说，这类事件涉及不同背景、不同视角的人们，他们以不同的方式参与其中。为了了解事件的规模，我们可以先咨询专业人士或专家：例如，在研究洪水时咨询气象学家，在研究疫情时咨询公共卫生官员。这些专业人士和专家可以指出过去关注过的问题以及现在应该关注的问题。或许有一些文献值得我们了解，专家们也可以指导我们找到类似事件的研究。接下来，找到那些身处事件之中的人，了解他们的经历，就显得尤为重要。
  3. An organization . We might want to study an institution or an organization of coordinated effort: a lying-in hospital, a school, the Navy. Here people in well-defined roles meet to produce planned events. In a study of this sort we can expect to encounter subgroups, or cliques, and politics. Interviews should be held with people in different jobs on different levels, in different relationships to the institution, and from different informal groups.
    组织。我们可能想研究一个机构或一个协同运作的组织：例如妇产医院、学校或海军。在这些机构或组织中，角色明确的人员聚集在一起，共同完成既定的计划。在这类研究中，我们可能会遇到各种小组、小团体以及政治因素。访谈对象应涵盖不同职位、不同层级、与机构关系各异以及来自不同非正式群体的人员。
  5. A study of an organization requires that the investigator succeed in obtaining informants without being perceived as an intrusive foreign presence. How to survive in the field is discussed in books on field methods, but it may be useful here to note that success is dependent on a certain amount of social grace, including sensitivity, considerateness, and tact; self-confidence; awareness of the politics of the institution; and persistence. Of great value is the ability to move through the institution without being blocked by barriers designed to protect its staff from bothersome outsiders. Being unobtrusive can help. It has been said of one brilliant field worker: “Other people have presence; he has absence.” But a selfconfident presence can also work.
    对一个组织的研究要求调查员成功获取线人，同时又不被视为一个咄咄逼人的外来者。关于如何在实地工作中生存，田野调查方法方面的书籍中已有论述，但在此值得一提的是，成功取决于一定的社交技巧，包括敏感、体贴和机智；自信；对机构政治的了解；以及坚持不懈。能够自由出入机构内部而不被那些旨在保护内部人员免受外来干扰的障碍所阻挡，这一点至关重要。保持低调会有所帮助。有人曾这样评价一位杰出的田野调查员：“其他人给人一种存在感，而他却给人一种缺席感。” 但自信的存在感同样有效。
  7. A loose collectivity . We might want to study a collection of people in touch with one another but not as closely linked as those in an organization; for example, a community, a network of associates, or the residents of a neighborhood. With luck it may be possible to find someone who is central and knowledgeable and who can provide both orientation and sponsorship, like William F. Whyte’s Doc. 1 1 Failing this, any member may provide entry, but the sponsorship of higher-ranking members will count for more.
    一个松散的群体。我们可能想研究一群彼此有联系但联系不如组织成员紧密的人；例如，一个社区、一个同事网络或一个街区的居民。如果运气好的话，或许能找到一位核心人物，他知识渊博，能够提供指导和支持，就像威廉·F·怀特的医生那样。如果找不到这样的人，任何成员都可以提供入会资格，但级别更高的成员的推荐更有分量。
  9. A social institution . Many social forms, like marriage or parenthood or the profession of politics, help shape people’s lives. To learn about these forms, we have to interview a sample of the people who have been affected by them. In addition, it is likely that there are people who are studying the social institution, and there may be others who serve as therapists for people negatively affected by it. At least a few of these professionals should be consulted.
    社会制度。许多社会形式，例如婚姻、为人父母或政治职业，都会影响人们的生活。为了了解这些形式，我们需要采访一些受其影响的人。此外，可能还有一些人正在研究这些社会制度，也可能有一些人为受其负面影响的人提供心理咨询。至少应该咨询其中几位专业人士的意见。

The Key Informant

关键线人

A good person to start with in any study requiring a panel is a knowledgeable insider willing to serve as an informant on informants. But others who might help include a knowledgeable marginal or disaffected figure within the system. Such a person may be more willing to describe the system’s failings than would someone central to the system and committed to it. Still another possibility would be a retiree, a person who has a career’s experience with the system and now has time to reminisce. 2 I myself prefer the informed insider, assuming I can find someone like that who is willing to coach me. But all sorts of people can help.

在任何需要专家小组的研究中，理想的人选是了解情况的内部人士，并且愿意担任线人的线人。其他可能提供帮助的人选包括了解情况的边缘人物或心怀不满的体制内人士。这类人可能比体制核心人物和忠于体制的人更愿意描述体制的弊端。另一种选择是退休人士，他们拥有在体制内工作多年的经验，现在有时间回忆往事。 2 我个人更倾向于选择了解情况的内部人士，前提是我能找到这样的人并且愿意指导我。但实际上，各种各样的人都能提供帮助。

Orienting figures may need to feel confident of you before they can comfortably be candid. Being vouched for by a mutual acquaintance can be useful. Failing that, it can help to be able to say that someone known to both of you suggested the contact. The implied sponsorship of government or foundation funding for the project may also help.

在对方对你产生信任之前，关键人物可能需要先对你有所了解，才能坦诚相待。如果能得到共同熟人的担保，那就很有帮助。如果对方没有这样的担保，也可以说明是你们双方都认识的人推荐了你。此外，如果项目背后有政府或基金会的资助，也可能起到一定的作用。

But it can happen that people you would like to consult prove inaccessible to you; your calls are fielded by a lower-level staff member who turns you away. When this has happened to me, my response has been to think about getting the experience into my notes and to try again. When it keeps on happening, I try to be philosophical about being frozen out, do something else for a while, and then reconsider my strategy. But, in truth, the experience is hard on morale.

但有时，你想咨询的人却联系不上；你的电话会被级别较低的员工接听，然后被拒之门外。遇到这种情况时，我的应对方法是把这次经历记下来，然后再次尝试。如果这种情况反复发生，我会尽量坦然接受被冷落的事实，暂时去做点别的事情，然后再重新考虑策略。但说实话，这种经历确实很打击士气。

Sometimes there is no obvious orienting figure, or there is no need for one because the people to be interviewed are immediately apparent. In a study of a disaster there will be officials and professionals whose job it is to deal with the disaster and the people who are affected by it. Orientation may not seem necessary. Or it may happen that you simply cannot find someone to direct your efforts. How then should you proceed? Two principles suggest themselves: One principle is to start with people who are available to you and easy to interview, especially if having interviewed them will make you more informed and legitimized when you proceed to interview others. A second principle is to have your early interviews with people who are of marginal importance to the study so that if you make mistakes it won’t matter so much.

有时，并没有明显的指导人物，或者根本不需要指导人物，因为受访者显而易见。例如，在灾害研究中，会有官员和专业人员负责处理灾害及其受灾民众。在这种情况下，指导似乎并不必要。或者，你可能根本找不到人来指导你的工作。那么，你应该如何进行呢？以下两条原则值得考虑：第一条原则是，首先采访那些容易联系到且容易访谈的人，尤其是在采访这些人之后，如果你的访谈能让你掌握更多信息，并在你继续采访其他人时更具说服力。第二条原则是，先采访那些对研究而言并不重要的人，这样即使你犯了错误，也不会造成太大的影响。

How Large a Panel?

面板尺寸有多大？

In a study in which there are a great many potential informants it might seem as though interviewing could go on forever. In a study of the functioning of today’s divorce laws, with judges and lawyers and divorcees and their families all to be interviewed, when do you quit? When do you decide you have interviewed enough people? The best answer is that you stop when you encounter diminishing returns, when the information you obtain is redundant or peripheral, when what you do learn that is new adds too little to what you already know to justify the time and cost of the interviewing.

在一项研究中，如果潜在受访者众多，访谈似乎会永无止境。例如，在研究当今离婚法的运作情况时，需要采访法官、律师、离婚人士及其家人，那么何时才能停止？何时才能确定访谈人数已足够？最佳答案是：当访谈收益递减，获得的信息重复或无关紧要，新获得的信息对已有知识的贡献微乎其微，不足以抵消访谈所花费的时间和成本时，就应该停止。

Biographers, whose research by its nature requires a panel of informants, regularly have the problem of deciding when to stop interviewing. After having interviewed the occupational associates of the biographer’s subject, the subject’s close friends, the members of the subject’s immediate family, and the people who were close to the subject as a child, should the biographer continue with the college roommate, the distant cousin, the fleeting acquaintance? Even the most indefatigable biographer must call a halt somewhere. In general, when further inquiry will add little to the story, stop inquiring.

传记作家的研究本质上需要大量的受访者，因此他们经常面临何时停止采访的难题。在采访了传主的职业伙伴、挚友、直系亲属以及童年时期的亲近之人之后，传记作家是否应该继续采访大学室友、远房表亲或泛泛之交？即使是最不知疲倦的传记作家也必须适时止步。一般来说，当进一步的询问对故事本身贡献甚微时，就应该停止询问。

REPRESENTATIONAL SAMPLES

代表性样本

Suppose that we want to interview not a panel of people in peculiarly good positions to know but, rather, a sample of people who together can adequately represent the experiences of a larger group.

假设我们想要采访的不是一群特别了解情况的人，而是一群能够充分代表更大群体经验的人。

Probability Sampling for Qualitative Research

定性研究中的概率抽样

One approach is to develop a sample that can be argued on grounds of mathematical probability to be not too different from the population in which we are interested. If everyone in a population has the same chance of turning up in the sample, we have a probability sample.

一种方法是构建一个样本，根据数学概率论，该样本与我们感兴趣的总体不会有太大差异。如果总体中的每个个体出现在样本中的概率都相同，那么我们就得到了一个概率样本。

If the people who make up a probability sample are chosen in such a way that each choice is independent of every other choice, and the sample includes at least 60 respondents, then the sample is likely to be a fairly good representation of the population in the sense that every important characteristic of the population is likely to have one or more representatives in the sample. A sample of this sort and size will, 19 times out of 20, include at least one instance of any phenomenon that occurs at least 5% of the time in the larger population. (The probability that a one-time-in-twenty phenomenon will not appear at all in a simple random sample of size 60 is .046.) Larger samples are still more likely to provide adequate representation.3

如果概率样本中的个体选择方式使得每次选择都与其他选择相互独立，且样本至少包含 60 名受访者，那么该样本很可能能够较好地代表总体，因为总体的每个重要特征都可能在样本中得到一个或多个代表。这种类型和规模的样本，在 20 次中有 19 次会包含至少一个在总体中出现频率至少为 5% 的现象。（在 60 人的简单随机样本中，出现频率为 20 次中的一次现象完全不出现的概率为 0.046。）更大的样本更有可能提供充分的代表性。³

A sample can be a probability sample only if respondents are selected randomly. Random selection is not the same as haphazard selection. Random means, rather, that the members of the sample were selected by a procedure that could equally well have selected absolutely anybody in the population. One such procedure would be to choose names from a population list. For example, we could draw a sample of the community from the list of names in the telephone book. Our actual procedure might be to let a table of random numbers dictate page numbers, column numbers, and line numbers in the book. We would have to worry, though, about overrepresenting people who had multiple listings and about not representing at all those who had no phones or whose numbers were unlisted. As this example may suggest, designing a probability sample is a fairly specialized activity, and someone who hasn’t done it before might do well to consult a sampling statistician.

只有当受访者是随机选择的，样本才能称为概率样本。随机选择与随意选择不同。随机意味着样本成员是通过一种同样可以选中总体中任何一个人的方法选出的。一种方法是从总体列表中选择姓名。例如，我们可以从电话簿的姓名列表中抽取社区样本。我们实际的操作可能是让随机数表决定电话簿中的页码、列号和行号。但是，我们需要注意的是，对于拥有多个电话号码的人，样本可能被过度代表；而对于没有电话号码或电话号码未登记的人，样本则可能被完全忽略。正如这个例子所示，设计概率样本是一项相当专业的活动，没有相关经验的人最好咨询抽样统计学家。

Often, the list of names we have is limited to a company or a region. Can we generalize to people in other companies or regions? Yes, but not by claiming that the sample is likely, on grounds of statistical probability, to be representative. A sample can be a random sample only of the population from which it is drawn. If we want to generalize beyond that population, we must invoke other rationales.

通常，我们掌握的名单仅限于某个公司或地区。我们能否将结果推广到其他公司或地区的人群？可以，但不能仅仅因为统计概率就断言样本具有代表性。样本只能是其所属总体的随机样本。如果我们想将结果推广到该总体之外，则必须援引其他理由。

Samples That Attempt to Maximize Range

试图最大化范围的样本

We may not want a probability sample from a population even if we are able to obtain one. The larger a probability sample, the more likely it is that it will reproduce in miniature the population of cases from which it is drawn. Instances that occur frequently in the population will occur frequently in the sample. But if instances that occur frequently are very much like one another, the sample will be filled with near duplicates. Precisely because it replicates the population, a probability sample might produce more typical cases, and fewer atypical cases, than we need. We will be learning again and again about the same thing.

即使我们能够获得一个概率样本，我们也未必想要它。概率样本越大，它就越有可能在样本中近似地再现其所代表的总体。在总体中频繁出现的案例在样本中也会频繁出现。但如果频繁出现的案例彼此非常相似，那么样本中就会充斥着几乎完全相同的案例。正因为概率样本能够再现总体，它可能会产生比我们实际需要更多的典型案例，而产生更少的非典型案例。我们将一遍又一遍地重复学习同样的内容。

Rather than choose respondents randomly, and thus risk unwanted duplication in our sample, we may prefer to select respondents purposively so that we obtain instances of all the important dissimilar forms present in the larger population. We may further want each of the dissimilar forms represented about the same number of times, so that we have the same knowledge base for each. This kind of sample might be referred to as a sample chosen to maximize range.

与其随机选择受访者，从而导致样本中出现不必要的重复，我们可能更倾向于有目的地选择受访者，以便获得总体中所有重要差异形式的实例。我们可能还希望每种差异形式的出现次数大致相同，从而确保每种形式都拥有相同的知识基础。这种样本可以称为旨在最大化样本范围的样本。

We are particularly likely to want a sample chosen to maximize range rather than a probability sample if our sample will be small. If we plan to work with samples much smaller than 60 (samples of 30, say) we may not trust random selection to provide us with instances of significant developments that occur infrequently.

如果样本量较小，我们尤其倾向于选择能够最大化样本范围的样本，而不是概率样本。如果我们计划使用远小于 60 的样本（例如 30 个样本），我们可能不相信随机抽样能够提供那些发生频率较低的重大事件的实例。

With large samples we may choose to maximize range in order to avoid having too many instances of the same type, and with small samples we may choose to maximize range in order to ensure that our sample contains instances of infrequent types. In sum, whenever we conduct qualitative interview studies, we ought to consider sampling to achieve range as an alternative to random sampling. There are advantages to each approach to sampling. Random sampling will provide us with a picture of the population as well as of particular instances, and sampling for range will ensure that our sample includes instances displaying significant variation.

对于大样本，我们可以选择最大化样本范围，以避免出现过多同类型实例；而对于小样本，我们可以选择最大化样本范围，以确保样本包含不常见类型的实例。总之，在进行定性访谈研究时，我们应该考虑采用范围抽样作为随机抽样的替代方案。两种抽样方法各有优势。随机抽样可以让我们了解总体以及特定实例的情况，而范围抽样则可以确保样本包含具有显著差异的实例。

But if in sampling for range your aim is to obtain instances displaying significant variation, you must know in advance what might constitute significant variation and how to find the people who display it. Take, as an example, the problem of learning what the impact is of moving into a new community. You might consider any of the following suggestions: 4

但是，如果在范围抽样中，你的目标是获得展现显著差异的实例，那么你必须预先知道什么才算显著差异，以及如何找到展现这种差异的人群。例如，了解搬到新社区的影响。你可以考虑以下建议： 4

  1. Look for contrast in what may be significant independent variables. If you want to show that adaptation to geographical migration is dependent on the length of time available for planning, make sure you have in your sample instances where there was a good deal of anticipatory time and instances where there was little.
    寻找可能具有重要意义的自变量之间的对比。如果你想证明对地理迁移的适应程度取决于可用于规划的时间长短，请确保你的样本中既包含有充足规划时间的案例，也包含规划时间较短的案例。
  2. Look for contrast in what may be significant dependent variables. If you want to contrast those who have adapted to geographical migration and those who have not, include instances of each.
    寻找可能具有重要意义的因变量之间的对比。例如，如果您想对比那些已经适应地理迁移的人和那些尚未适应的人，请同时包含这两类人群的案例。
  3. Look for contrast in context. If you suspect that the experience of a newcomer is heavily dependent on the extent to which networks are already established in the community into which the newcomer moves, do some interviewing in a new development and some in a long-established neighborhood.
    寻找情境中的对比。如果你怀疑新来者的经历很大程度上取决于他们搬入社区中已有的社交网络的建立程度，那么不妨在新建社区和老牌社区分别进行一些访谈。
  4. Look for contrast in dynamics. If you want to show that one of the problems experienced by newcomer couples is that the husband is absorbed by the need to prove himself in his new workplace and so becomes emotionally unavailable to his wife, include in your sample couples in which the husband is unemployed or self-employed or in which the wife has the more demanding career.
    寻找家庭动态的对比。如果你想表明，新婚夫妇面临的问题之一是丈夫一心想在新工作中证明自己，从而在情感上疏远了妻子，那么你的样本夫妇中应该包括丈夫失业或自雇的夫妇，或者妻子职业压力更大的夫妇。

If you have a list of possible respondents to work from, you may be able to establish informal quotas that will maximize the heterogeneity of your sample in some respect. You can decide what sort of contrast you want among your respondents and, as you recruit from the list, give preference to the potential respondents whom you need to fill your quotas. 5 To know whether potential respondents have characteristics you want, you can include “filter” questions in the telephone calls you make to arrange for interviews. In our study of retirement, for example, we used the filter question “Might you retire within the next year or so?”
