如果您有一份潜在受访者名单，您可以设定非正式配额，从而在某些方面最大限度地提高样本的异质性。您可以决定希望受访者之间存在怎样的差异，并在从名单中招募受访者时，优先考虑那些能够满足配额要求的潜在受访者。为了了解潜在受访者是否具备您想要的特征，您可以在安排访谈的电话中加入“筛选”问题。例如，在我们关于退休的研究中，我们使用了“您是否会在未来一年左右退休？”这样的筛选问题。

One argument for generalizing to a larger population from a sample chosen to maximize range depends on being able to claim that the sample included the full variety of instances that would be encountered anywhere. If we find uniformities in our sample despite our having adequately represented the range of instances, then those uniformities must be general. If we find differences among types of instance, then those differences should hold in a larger population. We will not be able to say anything about the proportion of instances of different types in a larger population, since the proportion in our sample might be very different from the proportion elsewhere. But we can say what the various types are like, no matter where they appear.

从一个旨在最大程度涵盖各种情况的样本中得出推广到更大总体的一个论点，取决于我们能否声称该样本包含了任何地方可能遇到的所有实例类型。如果我们在样本中发现一致性，即使我们已经充分代表了各种实例，那么这些一致性必然具有普遍性。如果我们发现不同类型实例之间存在差异，那么这些差异也应该在更大的总体中成立。我们无法确定不同类型实例在更大总体中的比例，因为样本中的比例可能与其他地方的比例截然不同。但是，无论这些类型出现在何处，我们都可以描述它们的特征。

Convenience Sampling

便利抽样

The third approach to obtaining a sample of respondents, in addition to choosing them on a probability basis or choosing them to provide a useful range of instances, is to accept pretty much whomever we can get. This is a sample of convenience.

第三种获取受访者样本的方法，除了按概率抽样或选择样本以涵盖尽可能多的实例之外，就是接受任何我们能找到的人。这是一种便利抽样。

Some people who do qualitative research are willing to base their reports on informal interviews with friends, family, and chance acquaintances. Their examples are introduced with a phrase like “An acquaintance of mine told me that …” Nor is this the approach only of those who have no ambition to contribute to general understanding. In attempting to learn about a group difficult to penetrate—gypsies, migrant workers, the very rich—it can be a breakthrough to find any member of the group, any member at all, willing to serve as an informant and respondent.

有些从事定性研究的人愿意以与朋友、家人和偶然认识的人的非正式访谈为基础撰写报告。他们举例时通常会以“我的一位熟人告诉我……”这样的语句开头。这种方法并非只适用于那些无意增进公众理解的人。在试图了解难以渗透的群体——例如吉普赛人、外来务工人员或富豪——时，找到该群体中任何一位成员，哪怕只是一位愿意担任信息提供者和受访者的成员，都可能是一项突破。

Sometimes the kind of people wanted for study are unusual in a population and, in addition, not listed anywhere. In the paragraphs below I give some suggestions for nevertheless obtaining a sample. 6

有时，研究对象在特定人群中并不常见，而且也未在任何地方登记在册。以下段落中，我将提供一些获取样本的建议。

You may know a few people in the population you want to study. Start with those who are available to you and ask them for referrals. If you don’t know anyone in the population you want to study, ask for help from people you think are likely to know such people. Or tell all your friends and acquaintances that you want to find someone who could be instructive about your topic. This use of referrals to build a sample is described by Diane Ehrensaft, who wanted to interview parents who were sharing child-care responsibilities:

你或许认识一些你想研究的人群中的人。首先联系那些你能够接触到的人，请他们推荐合适的人选。如果你不认识任何你想研究的人群中的人，那就向你认为可能认识这类人的人寻求帮助。或者，你可以告诉所有的朋友和熟人，你想找一位对你的研究主题有启发性的人。黛安·埃伦萨夫特（Diane Ehrensaft）就曾描述过这种利用推荐来构建样本的方法，她当时想采访那些共同承担育儿责任的父母：

Through word of mouth and my own personal contacts, I began to generate a pool of people who fit the bill of two people, a man and a woman, sharing the position of primary parent in their family. I had no trouble finding potential couples to talk to. People told me eagerly about friends or friends of friends, and I soon found myself generating, both geographically and socially, an arena well beyond my own circles. 7

通过口口相传和我的私人关系，我开始建立起一个符合条件的夫妇群体，他们都是一对男女，共同承担家庭中的主要抚养责任。我很容易就找到了可以交谈的潜在夫妇。人们热情地向我推荐朋友或朋友的朋友，很快，我发现自己无论在地域上还是社会层面，都建立起了一个远远超出我自身社交圈的平台。

If the people you want to interview are likely to know others like themselves, you can ask them for referrals. Then the referrals can provide still further referrals. This technique is known as snowball sampling .

如果你想采访的人很可能认识和自己情况类似的人，你可以请他们推荐。然后，这些推荐人还可以提供更多推荐人。这种方法被称为滚雪球抽样。

Another method of locating respondents is to advertise for volunteers. Better still, you might arrange for a story about your study to appear in a newspaper. In a study of retirement I needed to interview women who had retired from administrative and managerial jobs. A story about the study and my desire to interview appropriate women appeared in a newspaper and brought several volunteers.

寻找受访者的另一种方法是刊登志愿者招募广告。更好的办法是，安排报纸刊登一篇关于你研究的报道。在一项关于退休的研究中，我需要采访一些从行政和管理岗位退休的女性。一篇关于这项研究以及我希望采访合适女性的报道刊登在报纸上后，吸引了几位志愿者。

You might find a congregating place for people of the kind you want to study. For example, if you want to learn about people who do something illegal, you may be able to find people in jail for the crime—although they will be, by definition, the ones who didn’t get away with it. That’s how Donald Cressey was able to learn about embezzling. 8

你或许能找到你想研究的那类人的聚集地。例如，如果你想了解那些从事违法活动的人，你或许能找到因犯罪入狱的人——尽管根据定义，他们是那些最终没能逃脱法律制裁的人。唐纳德·克雷西就是这样了解到了挪用公款的。

People who suffer from an affliction may have formed a support group. Leaders of support groups can suggest potential respondents and are also likely to be repositories of information regarding the condition. It is almost always a good idea to check an encyclopedia of associations to see if a group has been established that specializes in your concern. If the group is in your locale, you might be able to visit.

患有某种疾病的人可能会成立互助小组。互助小组的负责人可以推荐潜在的参与者，而且他们通常也掌握着关于这种疾病的信息。查阅协会名录，看看是否有专门针对您所患疾病的互助小组，几乎总是一个好主意。如果该小组就在您所在的地区，您可以去拜访一下。

Social agencies, schools, and hospitals can sometimes provide the kind of people you are interested in. To be sure, you will probably be required first to undergo the scrutiny of gatekeepers, research committees, and committees for the protection of human subjects. It helps to be on the staff or to work with someone on the staff. 9

社会机构、学校和医院有时可以提供你感兴趣的那类人。当然，你很可能首先需要接受把关人、研究委员会和人体受试者保护委员会的审查。如果能成为工作人员或与工作人员共事，会很有帮助。

These suggestions are not intended to minimize the ingenuity that may be needed to find appropriate respondents. For a pilot study of newcomers to the Boston area I started by asking the gas company for a copy of its most recent list of “turn-ons” and was told that the company guarded the list closely. It took the intercession of a university vice president to obtain the list, and I then discovered that it was several months out of date and thus useless as a list of people who had just moved in. I thought of contacting local newcomer clubs, but before doing so I made connection with a Welcome Wagon representative. She supplied me with names of newcomer couples in her area until the central office of her national organization reminded her that the information she was sharing was proprietary. Luckily, we had by then completed all the interviews we needed. 10

这些建议并非旨在降低寻找合适受访者所需的创造力。为了对波士顿地区的新居民进行试点研究，我首先向天然气公司索要了一份最新的“热门人群”名单，但被告知该公司对这份名单严加保密。最终，在一位大学副校长的斡旋下，我才拿到这份名单。然而，我发现这份名单已经过时好几个月了，因此对于刚搬来的居民来说毫无用处。我曾考虑联系当地的新居民俱乐部，但在那之前，我联系了一位“欢迎新居民”（Welcome Wagon）项目的代表。她向我提供了她所在地区的新居民夫妇名单，直到她所在全国性组织的总部提醒她，她分享的信息属于专有信息。幸运的是，那时我们已经完成了所有需要的访谈。

Arguments for the Generalizability of the Findings of Convenience Samples

关于便利样本研究结果普遍适用性的论证

A problem with all samples selected only because they are conveniently obtained is that we may not have good bases for generalization. With a probability sample, generalization is straightforward, based on mathematical argument. With a sample in which it has been possible to maximize range, it can be argued that instances of every important variation have been studied. With other sorts of samples other arguments must be relied on. Here are five arguments that might be advanced to justify the attempt to generalize from the findings of convenience samples—and one that should not be, although it sometimes is.

仅仅因为方便获取而选择样本，其问题在于我们可能缺乏良好的概括基础。对于概率样本，概括很简单，基于数学论证即可。对于能够最大限度涵盖范围的样本，可以说已经研究了所有重要变异的实例。而对于其他类型的样本，则必须依赖其他论证。以下列举了五个可能被用来证明从便利样本的研究结果中进行概括的论点——以及一个不应该被提出的论点，尽管它有时会被使用。

Respondents’ Own Assessments of Generalizability . Respondents may be able to judge the extent to which others in their situations behave similarly or differently and have the same or different experiences. Their appraisals are not conclusive. A respondent who says, “I’m like most other people I know in my situation” is not necessarily right. “Pluralistic ignorance”, in which people are like one another and don’t know it, certainly exists, and so does underestimating the way in which one is different. But knowledgeable appraisals may be more likely. The question to ask about a respondent’s appraisal is whether the respondent is in a position to know. I would trust an executive who says that most executives check around to learn the size of the end-of-the-year bonuses being given to others in order to know how to value their own; it is something an executive would be likely to observe. Sometimes respondents can offer evidence for their appraisals: they have talked with others in their situation about the topic or have observed others’ behavior with respect to it.

受访者对普遍性的评估。受访者或许能够判断与自己处境相同的人，在多大程度上表现得相似或不同，以及拥有相同或不同的经历。但他们的评估并非最终结论。例如，一位受访者如果说“我和我认识的大多数处境相同的人一样”，未必是正确的。“多元无知”——即人们彼此相似却不自知——确实存在，低估自身差异的情况也同样存在。但基于知识的评估可能更为常见。关于受访者评估的关键问题在于，他们是否具备了解情况的能力。如果一位高管表示，大多数高管都会四处打听其他人的年终奖金数额，以便评估自己的奖金价值，我会相信他；这是高管很可能会观察到的现象。有时，受访者可以为他们的评估提供证据：他们可能与处境相同的人讨论过这个话题，或者观察过其他人在这方面的行为。

Similarity of Dynamics and Constraints . Insofar as the dynamics of the group we study and the constraints to which they are subjected decide their behavior, we can expect the same behavior from any other group with the same dynamics and the same constraints. On this basis we might argue that what was learned about postdivorce father—child relationships from a study that was conducted in a New England city could be generalized to postdivorce father—child relationships throughout the country. The relationships, it could be argued, would involve the same emotions of parent and child and would be subject to the same constraints of postmarital life.

动态与约束的相似性。鉴于我们所研究群体的动态及其所受约束决定了他们的行为，我们可以预期任何其他具有相同动态和相同约束的群体也会表现出相同的行为。基于此，我们可以认为，从一项在新英格兰城市进行的研究中了解到的离婚后父亲与子女的关系，可以推广到全国各地的离婚后父亲与子女的关系。可以认为，这些关系涉及父母和子女相同的情感，并受到离婚后生活相同约束的影响。

Depth . An idea that may be intuitively appealing is that underneath the accidents of individuality lies an identity in structure and functioning among all members of our species. As Ralph Waldo Emerson put it, referring to an orator, “The deeper he dives into his privatest secretest presentiment—to his wonder he finds, this is the most … universally true.” 11

深度。一个可能颇具直觉吸引力的观点是，在个体差异的表象之下，我们物种的所有成员在结构和功能上都存在着共性。正如拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生在谈到一位演说家时所说：“他越深入探究自己最私密、最隐秘的预感，就越会惊奇地发现，这才是最……普遍真理。”

The problem, of course, is to know when we are dealing with a deep and presumably universal phenomenon. One guide might be to ask whether the phenomenon is necessary to the functioning of whatever it is we are studying or is closely linked to something necessary or is an expression of it. Yet we must be aware that we are working with theory, and we might be wrong.

当然，问题在于如何判断我们面对的是一种深刻且可能具有普遍性的现象。一个指导原则是：这种现象对于我们所研究对象的运作是否必要？是否与某种必要因素密切相关？或者是否是某种必要因素的体现？然而，我们必须意识到，我们是在运用理论，而我们的判断也可能出错。

The study of bereavement provides an example. We might assume that grief results from loss of a relationship of attachment, a relationship in which there is a sense of strong linkage between the self and the other, almost of being augmented by the other. We might also assume that both the capacity to form attachments and the emotions attending their loss are universal or nearly so. We would therefore believe that findings regarding the experience of grief would be generalizable, whatever the quality of the respondent sample. In contrast, we might suppose that mourning practices, the way people display their grief, are easily modified by time and place. We would, therefore, want a representative sample before generalizing about mourning practices. But it should be noted that our belief that we need a better sample for a study of mourning practices than for a study of grief depends on a theory regarding the nature of attachment, loss, and mourning.

对丧亲之痛的研究就是一个例子。我们可以假设，悲伤源于依恋关系的丧失，这种关系中自我与他人之间存在着强烈的联结感，几乎可以说是被他人所增强。我们还可以假设，形成依恋的能力以及伴随依恋丧失而来的情绪都是普遍存在的，或者几乎是普遍存在的。因此，我们认为，无论受访样本的质量如何，关于悲伤体验的研究结果都具有普遍性。相反，我们可以假设，哀悼行为，即人们表达悲伤的方式，很容易受到时间和地点的影响。因此，在对哀悼行为进行概括之前，我们需要一个具有代表性的样本。但需要指出的是，我们认为研究哀悼行为需要比研究悲伤本身更好的样本，这一观点是基于关于依恋、丧失和哀悼本质的理论。

Theory Independent of Qualifiers .

理论与限定词无关。

Akin to the argument based on the purported depth (and therefore universality) of whatever it is we are describing is the argument that there is no justification for questioning the exportation of a theory based on our sample. We might acknowledge that our sample is not representative but argue that there is no reason for the theory to be limited to the sample from which it was developed.

类似于基于我们所描述事物的所谓深度（以及由此而来的普适性）的论点，还有一种论点认为，没有理由质疑基于我们样本的理论的推广应用。我们或许会承认我们的样本不具代表性，但我们认为，理论没有理由局限于其所基于的样本。

Donald Cressey studied embezzlers in prison to learn about embezzling. His was hardly a representative sample of all embezzlers, since it included only those who had been caught and convicted. (But how else find a sample of embezzlers at all?) Despite this skewed sample, Cressey offered generalizations about the source of all embezzlement, not just unsuccessful embezzlement. He said that embezzling occurs when someone in a position to embezzle can justify violating others’ trust in order to solve a nonshareable problem. He argued that his theory could be applied to all embezzlement because it was inherently plausible, it was invariably consistent with his data, and—although he left this implicit—there was no reason his theory should be true only of imprisoned embezzlers. 12

唐纳德·克雷西研究了监狱中的挪用公款者，以了解挪用公款的成因。他的样本很难代表所有挪用公款者，因为他的研究对象仅限于那些被抓获并定罪的人。（但除此之外，又该如何找到挪用公款者的样本呢？）尽管样本存在偏差，克雷西仍然提出了关于所有挪用公款行为根源的概括性结论，而不仅仅是未成功的挪用公款。他认为，当有能力挪用公款的人能够为解决一个无法分担的问题而合理化其违背他人信任的行为时，挪用公款的行为就会发生。他辩称，他的理论可以应用于所有挪用公款行为，因为它本身就合情合理，与他的数据始终一致，而且——尽管他没有明确指出——他的理论并非只适用于被监禁的挪用公款者。

Corroboration from Other Studies . The findings and conclusions of other studies can sometimes buttress those of our qualitative interview study. They will not be able to corroborate every point of our study—if they could, our study would have been unnecessary. But the more we have of such corroboration for our findings, the more credible our findings become. This is especially the case when the results of a quantitative study can anchor a discussion based on qualitative interviewing. For example, a discussion of single parent overload might be anchored by a quantitative study’s findings regarding the disposable time available to parents in various types of households.

其他研究的佐证。其他研究的发现和结论有时可以佐证我们定性访谈研究的结论。它们不可能完全证实我们研究的每一个观点——如果可以，我们的研究也就没有必要了。但是，我们获得的佐证越多，我们的发现就越可信。当定量研究的结果可以为基于定性访谈的讨论提供依据时，这一点尤为重要。例如，关于单亲家庭负担过重的讨论，可以以一项关于不同类型家庭中父母可支配时间的定量研究结果为基础。

An Invalid Argument for Generalization from Convenience Samples

基于便利样本进行概括的论证是无效的

A sample that is not chosen randomly cannot be claimed to be representative even if some of its demographic characteristics match those of the country as a whole. One author described using snowball sampling to obtain a sample of respondents who, with a few exceptions, lived in West Coast urban areas. The author then argued that the sample should be taken as representative of a national population because it matched the national population on age at time of first marriage, number of children, length of marriage, and proportion divorced. However, absence of significant difference between a sample and a larger population on one or on a dozen characteristics does not make a sample representative of the larger population on characteristics that have not been examined. A snowball sample, for one thing, will always underrepresent those who have few social contacts and will therefore underrepresent every belief and experience that is associated with having few social contacts.

即使某些人口统计特征与全国总体相符，但并非随机抽取的样本也不能被认为是具有代表性的。一位作者描述了他如何运用滚雪球抽样法获得一个受访者样本，该样本除少数例外情况外，均居住在西海岸的城市地区。该作者随后认为，由于该样本在初婚年龄、子女数量、婚姻时长和离婚比例等方面与全国人口相符，因此应将其视为全国人口的代表。然而，样本与总体在某一或十几个特征上没有显著差异，并不意味着该样本在其他未考察的特征上也能代表总体。例如，滚雪球抽样法总是会低估那些社交活动较少的人群，因此也会低估与社交活动较少相关的各种信念和经历。

Comparison Cases

比较案例

In qualitative interview studies, anyone who has anything to teach us is a desirable interviewee. Often it is useful to interview at least a few people who might constitute comparison cases. In a study of men in responsible positions, we were several times misled by the filter questions we used to establish that a potential respondent was actually in a responsible job. As a result, we mistakenly selected into our sample men in occupations different from those we wanted to learn about. We interviewed the men anyway and found their contrasting experience to be instructive. And in a study of single parents, we intentionally interviewed people in intact marriages as a way of understanding better what we were being told by single parents.

在定性访谈研究中，任何能给我们带来启发的人都是理想的受访者。通常，采访一些可以作为对比案例的人是很有帮助的。在一项针对身居要职男性的研究中，我们曾多次被筛选问题误导，这些问题原本是为了确定潜在受访者是否真的担任要职。结果，我们错误地将一些从事与我们想要了解的职业不同的男性纳入了样本。尽管如此，我们还是采访了这些男性，并发现他们截然不同的经历很有启发意义。在另一项针对单亲父母的研究中，我们特意采访了一些婚姻状况完整的人，以便更好地理解单亲父母告诉我们的内容。

Should you have a full-scale comparison group? Often, it is all an investigator can do to collect information from an adequate sample of people in a situation; to also collect information from an adequate sample of people not in the situation can seem an unmanageable burden. It may also seem unnecessary. Why give time and energy to the study of people who by definition aren’t the people you want to learn about?

是否应该设立一个全面的对照组？通常情况下，研究者所能做的仅仅是收集到足够数量的处于特定情境中的人群的信息；而要再收集到足够数量的未处于该情境中的人群的信息，似乎会成为难以承受的负担。而且，这样做似乎也没有必要。为什么要花费时间和精力去研究那些本质上并非研究对象的人呢？

And yet, how can you be sure that phenomena you associate with the situation you are studying are in fact more frequent there than among people who are not in that situation? In studying single parents it appeared to me that their children were asked to do a great deal. It made sense that this would be linked to the understaffing of the single-parent home and to the special need the single parent would have for the children’s help. But, just to be sure, I did some interviewing of parents in two-parent homes. I discovered, to my surprise, that parents in two-parent homes expected their children to do the same sorts of chores that parents in single-parent homes expected their children to do. The difference wasn’t in the parents’ expectations, it was in the firmness of those expectations. Parents in two-parent homes would excuse their children from chores if the children had something else to do and would accept forgetfulness as an explanation for noncompliance. Parents in single-parent homes could not tolerate their children’s noncompliance. In the two-parent home parents wanted their children to help so that the children would learn to be responsible. In the single-parent home the parent needed the children to help because the parent could not manage otherwise. It took comparative data to make this clear.

然而，你如何确定你所研究的情境中出现的现象，在那种情境下确实比在非该情境人群中更为常见呢？在研究单亲家庭时，我发现他们的孩子似乎被要求做很多事情。这似乎与单亲家庭人手不足以及单亲父母对孩子帮助的特殊需求有关。但为了确保这一点，我采访了一些双亲家庭的父母。令我惊讶的是，我发现双亲家庭的父母期望孩子做的家务与单亲家庭的父母期望孩子做的家务并无二致。区别不在于父母的期望本身，而在于这些期望的坚定程度。双亲家庭的父母会因为孩子有其他事情要做而允许他们不做家务，并且会接受孩子因忘记而未完成家务的解释。而单亲家庭的父母则无法容忍孩子的不服从。在双亲家庭中，父母希望孩子帮忙，以便培养孩子的责任感。而在单亲家庭中，父母需要孩子帮忙，因为父母自己无力承担家务。这一点需要通过对比数据才能明确。

Judith Wallerstein is properly recognized for her contributions to our understanding of the stresses experienced by children following parental divorce. 13 But many of her readers have wondered whether children whose parents maintained intact marriages might not share some of these stresses and whether children whose parents are unhappily married might not experience still other stresses. Without comparison cases there is no way to be sure.

朱迪思·沃勒斯坦因其对我们理解父母离婚后儿童所承受压力的贡献而备受赞誉。但许多读者不禁会想，父母婚姻美满的孩子是否也会面临同样的压力？父母婚姻不幸的孩子是否也会经历其他压力？如果没有对比案例，我们无从得知答案。

An investigator who does not have comparison cases may argue, explicitly or implicitly, that a development in the group under study must be peculiar to that group because its presence outside the group has not been noted. Or the investigator may argue that the process leading to a special development is apparent, that the process could occur only in the group under study, or that members of the studied population affirm that they too have noticed that they are different in this special way. Any of these arguments can help, but none is likely to be as convincing as arguments based on comparative study. Is marriage better in couples who share parenting than in couples who do not? Diane Ehrensaft tries to answer this question affirmatively on the basis of her sample of shared-parenting couples. 14 But she did not have a comparison sample of marriages in which couples do not share parenting, so her argument comes close to being, “Well, their marriages look better.” She also says that if you consider the logic of the situation, the marriages would have to be pretty good or the couple couldn’t keep doing shared parenting. And there doesn’t seem to be a high divorce rate among them, although it’s hard to know. Without a comparison group, this is the best she can do.

缺乏对比案例的研究者可能会明确或隐含地论证，研究群体中出现的某种现象必然是该群体特有的，因为在其他群体中并未发现这种现象。或者，研究者可能会论证，导致这种特殊发展的过程是显而易见的，该过程只能发生在研究群体中，或者研究群体成员也证实他们注意到自身在这一特殊方面存在差异。这些论证都可能有所帮助，但没有一种比基于对比研究的论证更具说服力。共同抚养孩子的夫妻的婚姻是否比不共同抚养孩子的夫妻的婚姻更好？黛安·埃伦萨夫特试图根据她对共同抚养孩子的夫妻样本给出肯定的答案。但她没有不共同抚养孩子的夫妻的婚姻对比样本，因此她的论证更像是“嗯，他们的婚姻看起来更好”。她还说，从逻辑上讲，这些婚姻关系必须相当美满，否则夫妻双方不可能继续共同抚养孩子。而且，这些家庭的离婚率似乎并不高，尽管很难确定。由于没有对照组，她也只能给出这样的结论了。

Even if resources have already been stretched by the effort to obtain adequate representation of target cases, it is likely to be a good idea to include at least a few comparison cases. Statistical comparison may not be possible, but even so, the comparison cases can correct what would otherwise be a tendency to exaggerate the peculiarities of the sample that is the focus of the study.

即使为了获得足够的样本量来代表目标案例，资源已经捉襟见肘，但纳入一些对比案例仍然是明智之举。虽然可能无法进行统计比较，但对比案例可以纠正研究过程中可能出现的夸大研究重点样本特征的倾向。

Conceptually Important Cases

概念上重要的案例

Sometimes cases that occur infrequently should be sought out because they are significant conceptually. Take house husbands. I have occasionally presented findings from a study I conducted of occupationally successful men that dealt with, among other things, the division of household labor in their homes. I would report that these men operated from traditional understandings, though with flexibility, and that I imagined that other men did as well. Regularly, it seemed, someone in the audience would ask how I could maintain that position, given the existence of contented house husbands. “I know a man,” I would be told, “who stays home and takes care of the kids while his wife goes out to work. And he is perfectly happy with the arrangement.”

有时候，一些不常见的案例值得关注，因为它们具有重要的概念意义。以家庭主夫为例。我曾多次分享一项针对事业成功的男性所做的研究成果，该研究探讨了他们家庭中的家务分工等问题。我通常会指出，这些男性虽然在分工上遵循传统观念，但也具备一定的灵活性，而且我认为其他男性也是如此。然而，似乎总有人会问我，既然存在着一些心满意足的家庭主夫，我又如何能坚持这种观点呢？“我认识一个男人，”有人会这样告诉我，“他待在家里照顾孩子，而他的妻子则外出工作。他对这种安排非常满意。”

House husbands, men who devote themselves to child care and home maintenance while their wives work, are statistically unusual. In a random sample of a hundred families you might find two or three.15 But house husbands play a role in people’s thinking about family life, and if you are going to lecture on the division of marital labor, it is probably a good thing to have interviewed a few house husbands.

家庭主夫，即那些在妻子工作时专注于照顾孩子和料理家务的男性，在统计学上并不常见。随机抽取一百个家庭，可能只会找到两三个。<sup>15</sup> 但家庭主夫在人们对家庭生活的思考中扮演着重要角色，如果你要讲授婚姻中的劳动分工，采访几位家庭主夫或许会很有帮助。

I found two house husbands by asking around when attending conferences on “men’s issues.” I later met another house husband through personal acquaintances. I don’t pretend now to be an expert on this way of dividing domestic labor, but I do have real images in my mind when I talk about house husbands. Now if I am asked about house husbands, I can make clear my limited information but then describe the adaptations I have witnessed. I can say that each of the men I talked with had assimilated his roles and responsibilities to a sense of coping, of making things work, that struck me as masculine in style and that, in addition, each maintained a sense of being involved with the world outside the home: one as a writer, the second as a pioneer helping to establish a new form of masculinity, and the third as a former and future head of a small business who had decided with his wife that his wife’s greater earning power justified his staying home for now.

我在参加一些关于“男性议题”的会议时，通过四处打听认识了两位家庭主夫。后来，我又通过私人关系认识了另一位家庭主夫。我不敢说自己是这种家务分工方式的专家，但当我谈到家庭主夫时，脑海中确实浮现出一些真实的画面。现在如果有人问起家庭主夫，我可以坦诚地说明自己了解有限，然后描述我所观察到的他们的适应方式。我可以说，我交谈过的每位男士都将自己的角色和责任融入到一种应对困境、努力让一切运转起来的心态中，这种心态在我看来很有男子气概。此外，他们每个人都保持着与家庭之外世界的联系：一位是作家，第二位是帮助建立一种新型男性气质的先驱，第三位曾是一家小型企业的负责人，后来与妻子商量后认为，妻子更高的收入能力让他暂时留在家中是合理的。

An N of 1

N 为 1

Compared with survey research studies, qualitative interview studies collect more material from fewer respondents. Studies of a single case take this to an extreme. The single case may be advanced as valuable because it so effectively displays the complex interplay of particular circumstance and the regularities of the human condition. Furthermore, the density of detail possible in the presentation of the single case makes for drama and immediacy, which can foster an emotional level of understanding based on identification. Authors of studies of single cases may also want to generalize some of their observations. The justifications for generalizability they offer would be those offered for qualitative interview studies done with small convenience samples; for example, that the constraints the subject experienced and the motives the subject expressed were common to all those in the subject’s situation.

与调查研究相比，定性访谈研究从较少的受访者中收集更多资料。个案研究则将这一点发挥到了极致。个案研究之所以被认为有价值，是因为它能有效地展现特定情境与人类生存规律之间复杂的相互作用。此外，个案研究能够呈现丰富的细节，从而营造出戏剧性和即时性，这有助于基于认同感的情感层面理解。个案研究的作者可能还希望将某些观察结果推广到其他情境中。他们为推广性提供的理由与使用小样本便利样本进行的定性访谈研究类似；例如，受访者所经历的限制和所表达的动机对于所有处于类似情境中的人来说都是共通的。

To these arguments for the single case may be added the idea that the case displays a life significant in itself. Furthermore, insofar as the subject may have been witness to significant events, the subject may provide not only autobiographical material but also a valuable observer’s report.

除了上述支持个案的论点之外，还可以补充一点：该个案本身就展现了一个意义非凡的人生。此外，由于当事人可能亲历过重大事件，因此他/她不仅可以提供自传性材料，还可以提供宝贵的观察者报告。

Consider the book The Narrative of Hosea Hudson: His Life as a Negro Communist in the South , by Nell Irvin Painter. In it Painter presents edited and rearranged materials from dozens of interviews with a respondent who was “a black workingman in a southern city in midcentury.” More than that, he had been a union organizer, a member of the Communist party, a husband and father, and a man with his own ambition to write. His singularities weaken the extent to which he can be taken as exemplary of men in his situation, yet his story makes vivid the economic, social, and emotional problems confronting all black workingmen of that time and place.

不妨读读内尔·欧文·佩恩特所著的《霍西·哈德逊的自述：他在南方作为一名黑人共产主义者的生活》。书中，佩恩特对一位受访者进行了数十次访谈，并对其进行了编辑和重新整理。这位受访者是“20世纪中期南方城市的一名黑人工人”。不仅如此，他还曾是工会组织者、共产党员、丈夫和父亲，并且怀揣着写作的梦想。他的独特经历削弱了他作为同类人的典型代表的程度，但他的故事生动地展现了当时当地所有黑人工人所面临的经济、社会和情感困境。

One problem in dealing with the case study is to decide to what substantive frame it should be assigned. Helen and Everett Hughes raise this issue in their introduction to Helen Hughes’s interview-based life history of a female drug addict: “The story she [the informant] left can be read in a variety of ways: as a psychiatric case study, as an account of the use of narcotics in an American city, and so on. But beyond this, it is a story of one person’s journey through the city and of what that journey did to her.”16 The Hugheses here note three frames to which the case study may be assigned: personal pathology, narcotics user, urban dweller. Undoubtedly other frames could also be considered, such as “young woman without family or funds.” Perhaps we learn about issues within all these frames, but unless we have one frame clearly in mind, the lessons of the case tend to fade.

处理案例研究的一个难题在于如何确定其应归入哪个实质性框架。海伦·休斯和埃弗雷特·休斯在他们为海伦·休斯基于访谈撰写的女性吸毒者生平传记所作的引言中提出了这个问题：“她（线人）留下的故事可以从多种角度解读：精神病学案例研究、美国城市毒品使用情况的描述等等。但除此之外，它讲述的是一个人在城市中的旅程，以及这段旅程对她造成的影响。”<sup>16</sup> 休斯夫妇在此指出了该案例研究可能归入的三个框架：个人病理、吸毒者、城市居民。毫无疑问，其他框架也可以考虑，例如“没有家庭或资金的年轻女子”。或许我们能在所有这些框架下都了解到一些问题，但除非我们心中有一个清晰的框架，否则案例的启示往往会被模糊。

Plummer has remarked that case study research tends to be “the strategy of the poor—of the researcher who has little hope of gaining a large and representative sample from which bold generalization may be made.” 17 However, case research can absorb as much data-gathering effort and analytic time as would research based on larger samples. Case research is different primarily because it anchors its potential for generalization in the welter of detail of the single instance. Generalization can then become uncertain (and rest heavily on the theory we bring to the case), but in compensation we have the coherence, depth, development, and drama of a single fully understood life.

普卢默曾指出，案例研究往往是“穷人的策略——那些几乎没有希望获得足够大且具有代表性的样本，从而进行大胆概括的研究者的策略。”然而，案例研究在数据收集和分析时间方面可能与基于更大样本的研究一样耗费精力。案例研究的主要区别在于，它将概括的潜力建立在单一案例的丰富细节之上。因此，概括可能会变得不确定（并且很大程度上依赖于我们带入案例的理论），但作为补偿，我们拥有了对一个完整人生的连贯性、深度、发展性和戏剧性。

RECRUITING RESPONDENTS

招募受访者

Having decided on the people you want to interview, you must now gain their cooperation. How do you do it?

确定了采访对象之后，接下来你需要获得他们的合作。该如何做呢？

Sometimes a telephone call alone can be enough. There can be appeal in a request for an interview. People may welcome the chance to make their situation known or just to have a break in the day. People marooned at home tend to welcome interviewers. So do people with time on their hands, like the hospitalized or the retired. So may people in crisis, such as people going through marital separation, although this is chancy and may change for the same person from day to day. But most people, given adequate assurance about the legitimacy of the interviewer and the confidentiality of what they say, are willing to talk.

有时候，一个电话就足够了。提出面谈请求或许会很受欢迎。人们可能乐于有机会倾诉自己的处境，或者只是想在忙碌的一天中稍作休息。被困在家中的人往往欢迎采访者。那些有空闲时间的人，比如住院病人或退休人员，也同样如此。处于危机中的人，例如正在经历婚姻破裂的人，也可能愿意接受采访，尽管这种情况并不稳定，即使是同一个人，每天的想法也可能不同。但大多数人，只要得到充分的保证，确信采访者的身份合法，并且谈话内容会严格保密，都愿意开口。

On the other hand, interviewers may need the right sponsorship or topic or approach to avoid being turned down by people whose occupations have accustomed them to asking the questions, including physicians and the police. Indeed, all sorts of things, including geography, can increase the likelihood that a request for an interview will be turned down. In a study of the uses of planned environments such as museums and fairs, my first interviews were on the grounds of the Seattle World’s Fair. I found it easy there simply to stop people and ask them about their experiences. My clipboard was a sort of badge, identifying me as a person whose job entitled him to ask questions, and people seemed happy to talk to me. Doing the same thing in the same way at the New York World’s Fair a couple of years later, I found people much less willing to talk with me. New Yorkers, apparently, had learned to be skeptical of inquiring strangers—with or without clipboards. But I had no trouble conducting the same sort of interviews at a restored village not far from New York. It may be that in the small space of the restoration it was more evident that I had management approval.

另一方面，采访者可能需要合适的赞助、话题或方法，才能避免被那些因职业习惯而习惯于提问的人拒绝，例如医生和警察。事实上，包括地理位置在内的各种因素都会增加采访请求被拒绝的可能性。在一项关于博物馆和博览会等规划环境用途的研究中，我的首次采访是在西雅图世界博览会的场地内进行的。我发现在那里很容易就能拦住人们，询问他们的经历。我的记事板就像一枚徽章，表明我是一名有权提问的人，人们似乎也很乐意与我交谈。几年后，我在纽约世界博览会上以同样的方式进行采访时，发现人们远没有那么愿意和我交谈。显然，纽约人已经学会了对陌生人的询问保持怀疑——无论对方是否拿着记事板。但在离纽约不远的一个修复村庄里，我进行同样的采访却毫无困难。或许是因为在修复工作的小空间里，我获得管理层批准这一点显得更加明显。

A number of devices can increase the likelihood of recruiting people. We have already noted that it can help in establishing a relationship with an orienting figure in an informant study if you are able to name a mutual friend or colleague and say “So-and-so suggested I call you.” The usefulness of a vouching figure extends to members of representational samples. A sociologist found it easier to interview IV drug users after a member of his team who was himself a former drug user spread the message that the sociologist would be around and was all right.

许多方法可以提高招募人员的成功率。我们之前已经提到，如果你能说出一个共同的朋友或同事的名字，并说“某某建议我联系你”，那么在信息提供者研究中，与关键人物建立联系就很有帮助。这种担保人的作用也适用于代表性样本的成员。一位社会学家发现，在他团队中一位曾是吸毒者的成员向他们传达了这位社会学家会经常出现并且很安全的信息后，采访静脉注射吸毒者就变得容易多了。

There is a downside to the use of intermediaries that applies, though with less force, to the referrals of snowball sampling. The respondent’s presentation of self may be affected by his or her awareness of the intermediary’s sponsorship. This may be especially true if the intermediary helps arrange the interview.

使用中介机构也存在一些弊端，虽然程度较轻，但同样适用于滚雪球抽样法中的推荐。受访者可能会因为意识到中介机构的推荐而影响其自我呈现。如果中介机构协助安排访谈，这种情况尤其如此。

Sponsorship by impressive groups or by public figures does not have this drawback. Such sponsorship should, of course, be appropriate to the study if it is to be useful. For a study of businessmen, a business association would be appropriate; for a study of family life, a sponsoring group of priests, ministers, and rabbis. A grant from a government agency is usually viewed as testimony to legitimacy, as is a position at a university. Boards of advisers can serve, in part, as endorsers.

由知名团体或公众人物赞助则不存在这种弊端。当然，如果想要取得成效，此类赞助必须与研究内容相符。例如，如果研究对象是商人，那么商业协会的赞助就比较合适；如果研究对象是家庭生活，那么由牧师、神父和拉比组成的团体赞助则更为合适。政府机构的拨款通常被视为研究合法性的证明，大学教职亦是如此。顾问委员会也能在一定程度上起到支持作用。

In most of the studies I have done my only sponsorship has been whatever might be implied by government funding and university affiliation. It seemed to me not worth the time it would take to obtain anything more. But studies whose subject is likely to put off potential respondents might be helped by reassuring sponsorship.

在我所做的大多数研究中，我唯一的资助来源就是政府拨款和大学关系所带来的支持。我觉得没必要花费时间去争取更多资金。但是，如果研究主题可能会让潜在的受访者望而却步，那么更有保障的资助或许会有所帮助。

When my colleagues and I have tried to obtain the participation of respondents for a community sample of representatives, we have generally sent the potential respondents a letter explaining the study, arguing for the importance of their participation, and saying someone would telephone. Despite the letter, the call from my office to potential respondents often appeared to surprise them. One of the people working with me hit on the idea of starting the conversation with, “We sent you a letter last week. It could easily have gotten in with your junk mail, but do you happen to remember it?”

当我和同事们试图招募社区代表性样本的受访者时，我们通常会给潜在的受访者寄一封信，解释研究内容，阐述他们参与的重要性，并告知他们之后会有人打电话联系。尽管寄了信，但我办公室打来的电话似乎常常让他们感到意外。我的一位同事想出了一个好办法，可以这样开头：“我们上周给您寄了一封信。它可能被误判为垃圾邮件了，您还记得吗？”

A checklist of items the investigator might be prepared to tell respondents in a first phone call could include the following: who the investigator is (which ordinarily means what the investigator’s job or position is), the reasons for the study, the study’s sponsorship, how the potential respondent’s name was found, why the potential respondent was selected, what the purpose of the interview is, what will be asked of the respondent, whether confidentiality is guaranteed, and whether the interview will be tape-recorded. 18 It is sometimes useful to ask a few questions to decide whether a potential respondent meets a study’s eligibility requirements: is in the right age range or occupational bracket.

研究人员在首次电话沟通中可能需要告知受访者的信息清单可能包括以下内容：研究人员的身份（通常指研究人员的职业或职位）、研究目的、研究赞助方、如何找到潜在受访者、选择该潜在受访者的原因、访谈目的、将询问受访者哪些问题、是否保证保密性以及访谈是否会录音。 18 有时，询问一些问题有助于确定潜在受访者是否符合研究的资格要求：例如，是否在合适的年龄范围或职业类别中。

In a few studies, I have begun with a telephone call and told potential respondents that a descriptive letter would follow. In other studies I have simply telephoned, without any letter sent at any time. People who do survey research tell me that they prefer not to telephone for an appointment, since that makes it too easy for the respondent to refuse to see them. They would rather just show up. I doubt that just showing up would work for qualitative interviewing. But here, as elsewhere, if in a particular study it seems like a good idea, try it. How else can you learn what works?

在一些研究中，我先打电话联系潜在受访者，并告知他们之后会寄送一封说明信。而在另一些研究中，我只打电话，没有寄送任何信件。从事调查研究的人告诉我，他们更倾向于不打电话预约，因为这样受访者很容易拒绝见面。他们宁愿直接上门。我怀疑直接上门是否适用于定性访谈。但是，无论在哪里，如果在某个特定研究中，这种方法看起来不错，那就试试看。不然你又怎么能知道什么方法有效呢？

Where it is especially important to obtain an interview with a particular respondent it can make sense to engage in a concerted sales effort. A writer of books based on interviews wanted to interview me about loneliness, an issue on which I’d worked. The writer’s assistant called to tell me that the writer wanted to interview me and that some of the writer’s books and articles were being mailed to me. A few days later I received a package containing a paperback collection of the writer’s interviews, copies of magazine and newspaper reviews praising the writer’s books, and a copy of a magazine story about the writer. A couple of weeks later I received copies of two more of the writer’s interview collections. About two weeks after that I received a call from the writer, asking for the interview. I could hardly not agree.

如果采访某个特定受访者至关重要，那么采取有针对性的推销策略就显得尤为重要。一位以访谈为基础创作书籍的作家想就孤独这一我曾研究过的主题采访我。这位作家的助理打电话告诉我，作家想采访我，并且正在邮寄一些作家的书籍和文章给我。几天后，我收到一个包裹，里面装着一本作家访谈录的平装本、一些赞扬作家书籍的杂志和报纸评论，以及一篇关于作家的杂志报道。几周后，我又收到了两本作家访谈录的合集。大约两周后，我接到了作家的电话，邀请我接受采访。我欣然应允。

On another occasion an English journalist who wanted to interview me called from England for the appointment. Transatlantic calls get my attention, and I think I am in this regard typical. I wouldn’t go so far as to recommend that appointments with difficult-to-recruit respondents be made from a transatlantic telephone, but there is much to be said for letting respondents know that their participation will be valued.

还有一次，一位想采访我的英国记者从英国打来电话约我见面。跨大西洋的电话总能引起我的注意，我想我在这方面应该算是比较典型的。我并不建议用跨大西洋的电话来约那些难以招募的受访者，但让受访者知道他们的参与会被重视，这一点非常重要。

Also important in recruitment success is an ability to keep pitching the study until acceptance is obtained. In the study of occupationally successful men, we wanted to interview our respondents three times over the course of a couple of months. That was a lot to ask of busy men. We began by sending a letter to potential respondents selected on the basis of occupation from street lists of upper-income suburbs. Our interviewers then telephoned the men for appointments. A dozen or so efforts produced discouraging results: about two-thirds of those we contacted turned us down. After a few turndowns interviewers dreaded making the calls.

招募成功的关键还在于能否坚持不懈地推介研究，直到获得受访者的同意。在针对事业有成的男性的研究中，我们希望在几个月的时间里对受访者进行三次访谈。这对忙碌的男士来说要求很高。我们首先根据职业，从高收入郊区的街道名单中筛选出潜在的受访者，并向他们发送了邀请函。之后，我们的访谈员会打电话给这些男士预约访谈时间。十几次尝试的结果令人沮丧：我们联系的人中约有三分之二拒绝了我们的邀请。几次拒绝之后，访谈员开始害怕再打电话了。

If we had accepted this low response rate, we would have studied only men who were unusually friendly to the idea of being interviewed. I tried doing recruiting myself. My acceptance rate ran about 50%, but one acceptance for every two calls was still a low response rate. And I too was dispirited by the frequent rejection.

如果我们接受这样的低回复率，那么我们研究的对象就只是那些对接受采访异常友好的男性。我尝试过自己招募受访者。我的接受率大约是50%，但平均每打两次电话才有一个人接受，这仍然是一个很低的回复率。而且，我也因为频繁的拒绝而感到沮丧。

However, one staff member (I will call her Mrs. Adams) seemed to be doing fine with recruiting. She reported the astonishing acceptance rate of 80%. I asked her to show me how she did it.

然而，有一位员工（我姑且称她为亚当斯女士）在招生方面似乎做得非常出色。她报告说录取率高达80%，令人震惊。我请她向我展示一下她是如何做到的。

I role-played a potential respondent. When Mrs. Adams asked me if I would participate, I said I was too busy. Mrs. Adams seemed not to notice. She continued in a pleasant and engaging fashion to describe what the interview would cover. I said, “No, I’d rather not participate.” Mrs. Adams said, “Yes, of course, I understand, but I want to tell you why the study is being done and who is doing it.” And she went on to tell me about the sponsorship of the study and the kinds of questions that would be asked and how important it would be to have my perspective. She said that the interview would help establish the nature of the stresses in managerial and administrative work and might contribute to their amelioration. She said that I would find the interview interesting and that it would be held whenever and wherever suited me. By now I was intrigued by the study and flattered to be so wanted, as well as just a bit exasperated by being unable to escape. I said, “All right, let’s set a time.”

我扮演了一位潜在受访者的角色。当亚当斯夫人问我是否愿意参与时，我说我太忙了。亚当斯夫人似乎没有注意到。她继续以友好而引人入胜的方式描述访谈内容。我说：“不，我不想参与。”亚当斯夫人说：“是的，当然，我理解，但我想告诉你这项研究的目的和研究者是谁。”然后她接着告诉我这项研究的赞助方、将会提出的问题类型，以及我的观点有多么重要。她说，这次访谈将有助于了解管理和行政工作中的压力性质，并可能有助于缓解这些压力。她说我会觉得这次访谈很有趣，而且访谈的时间和地点都可以由我决定。这时，我对这项研究很感兴趣，也因为被如此需要而感到荣幸，但同时也因为无法推脱而感到有些恼火。我说：“好吧，那我们定个时间吧。”

Surprisingly, Mrs. Adams, although a demon recruiter, turned out not to be a very good interviewer. Her ability to seem responsive while continuing firmly on her own track, which made her a wonderful recruiter, produced difficulties for her as an interviewer. In recruiting she got people to see the world her way. In interviewing she tried to do the same thing. The transcripts of Mrs. Adams’s interviews showed her talking as much as did her respondents. She would continue with a line of questioning even when the respondent had begun to talk about something else. She would become impatient when a respondent hesitated and would supply what she believed to be the thought for which the respondent was searching; and, because she didn’t listen well, her suggestions could be way off the mark. After enough of this treatment, the respondent’s answers would become brief, but Mrs. Adams seemed not to notice.

令人惊讶的是，亚当斯夫人虽然是一位出色的招聘人员，却并非一位优秀的面试官。她那种看似积极回应却又固执己见的能力，使她成为一名优秀的招聘人员，但这却成了她面试的难题。在招聘中，她能让人们接受她的观点；在面试中，她也试图这样做。亚当斯夫人的面试记录显示，她自己说的话和受访者一样多。即使受访者已经开始谈论其他事情，她也会继续追问。当受访者犹豫不决时，她会变得不耐烦，并提出她认为受访者正在寻找的答案；而且，由于她不善于倾听，她的建议往往与受访者的意图相去甚远。在经历了足够多的这种对待之后，受访者的回答会变得简短，但亚当斯夫人似乎对此毫不在意。

Mrs. Adams and I had many a struggle before she accepted that it was undesirable to interrupt a respondent’s account. Once she accepted this principle, she became reluctant to redirect respondents at all, with the consequence that her respondents could wander into total irrelevance.

亚当斯夫人和我争论了很久，她才最终接受打断受访者陈述是不妥的这一观点。一旦她接受了这个原则，她就不愿再引导受访者，结果导致受访者的发言常常偏离主题，变得毫无意义。

And yet Mrs. Adams’s willingness to continue an interview despite the respondent’s indications that everything had already been said meant that several times she obtained important material other interviewers would have missed. The moral, I guess, is that in social research, as in life, never undervalue persistence.

然而，尽管受访者表示该说的都已经说完了，亚当斯夫人仍然坚持继续采访，这使得她多次获得了其他采访者可能会错过的重要信息。我想，这说明在社会研究中，就像在生活中一样，永远不要低估坚持的重要性。

# ↩

CHAPTER 3
PREPARATION FOR
INTERVIEWING

第三章 面试准备

WHAT DO YOU INTERVIEW ABOUT?

你们采访的内容是什么？

I was trying to think through how qualitative interviewers formulate the questions they include in their interviews when I had to break off to go to a lunch with a colleague who has since become a friend. My colleague does a fair amount of interviewing and is, I think, good at it. I decided that I would interview him about how he formulated his interview questions. I could at the same time monitor the source of my own questions.

我当时正在思考定性研究的访谈者是如何构思访谈问题的，这时我不得不中断思考，去和一位同事共进午餐，后来我们成了朋友。我的同事经常做访谈工作，而且我认为他做得不错。我决定采访他，了解他是如何构思访谈问题的。这样，我也可以同时反思自己访谈问题的来源。

While walking to the restaurant I could recognize in myself an almost kinesthetic sense of the material I needed for this chapter. I needed dense descriptions that would fully display the process of question formulation. This self-observation suggested that a first step in question formulation is a sense of what would be the right kind of information.

在去餐厅的路上，我隐约感觉到自己对本章所需素材有了近乎本能的感知。我需要详尽的描述，来充分展现问题构建的过程。这种自我观察让我意识到，问题构建的第一步是感知什么样的信息才是合适的。

A few minutes after we sat down to eat, and without much introduction, I asked my colleague how he went about learning from respondents. I was about to say that it might be good to talk about a specific incident, but he was already answering my question. However, he seemed to think I was interested not in the pedestrian issue of how he decided to ask this question or that one but rather in the deeper, more fundamental, issue of how he presented himself and his project to respondents. He said, “I show that I want to learn and that I’m worth teaching. That I know something, but not everything. So they can inform me, and I’ll understand.”

我们坐下吃饭几分钟后，我没怎么寒暄就问同事他是如何从受访者那里学习的。我正要说或许可以举个具体的例子，但他已经开始回答我的问题了。不过，他似乎觉得我感兴趣的不是他如何选择提问方式这种琐碎的问题，而是他如何向受访者展示自己和他的项目这种更深层次、更根本的问题。他说：“我会展现出我渴望学习，也展现出我值得被教导。我会让他们知道我懂一些，但并非无所不知。这样他们就能给我提供信息，而我也能理解。”

This was not what I needed to know. But I felt too uncomfortable to say, “How, exactly, do you work out what you will ask? Tell me about your most recent interview and how you did it.” In ordinary conversation it’s rude to pin people down by asking for specific incidents. So I asked the rather general question “How do you get to the questions you actually ask?” After a moment my colleague said, “I try to get to know the person. It isn’t like there’s just one question I’m going to ask.”

这并非我真正想知道的。但我不好意思直接问：“您究竟是如何决定要问什么问题的？跟我说说您最近一次面试的经历吧。”在日常对话中，追问具体事例是很不礼貌的。所以我问了一个比较笼统的问题：“您是如何想到要问的问题的？”过了一会儿，我的同事说：“我会先了解应聘者。我并不是只打算问一个问题。”

Again, not what I needed to know. Now I did ask, “How about the most recent interview you did?” And then, maybe because I wanted permission for my questioning, I added, “Could I ask about that? How you decided what you’d ask?”

这又不是我想知道的。于是我问：“您最近一次采访怎么样？”然后，也许是想征求一下提问的许可，我又问：“我可以问问那次采访吗？您是怎么决定要问什么问题的？”

Instead of answering my question, my colleague held it up for inspection. “That’s a good question,” he said. Then he thought about it. Then he told me a story: He had spent a lot of time with the head of a government agency, from whom he hoped to learn about the workings of the agency. He went to meetings with the man and regularly talked with him in the late afternoon. Finally, after one such talk, the official told him that he now understood what it was my colleague wanted to write about, that he could see that the story would be important and valuable. But he wasn’t going to let my colleague do the story because it would be an embarrassment to him and his agency. He liked my colleague and wished him well but would see to it that no one in his agency or anywhere else in government would cooperate with him. “And,” my colleague said to me, “that was the end of the enterprise.”

我的同事没有回答我的问题，而是把它举起来让我仔细查看。“问得好，”他说。然后他思考了一会儿，给我讲了一个故事：他曾花很多时间和一位政府机构的负责人待在一起，希望能从他那里了解该机构的运作方式。他经常和这位负责人开会，并在傍晚时分与他交谈。最终，在一次这样的谈话之后，那位官员告诉他，他现在明白了我的同事想写什么，他能看出这篇报道会很重要也很有价值。但他不会让我的同事写这篇报道，因为这会让他和他的机构蒙羞。他喜欢我的同事，也祝他一切顺利，但他会确保他所在机构或政府其他部门的任何人都不会与他合作。“然后，”我的同事对我说，“这件事就此结束了。”

I wondered if my colleague, in telling me this story, was also telling me that he didn’t want to be interviewed and would like to wish me well and send me off. Still, here we were at lunch, with another three-quarters of an hour before it would be time to return to our offices. I thought I would try once more. I noticed that I gave extra effort to being agreeable. I relaxed my voice and tried to make the next question casual, as though my questioning were no big deal, just that I happened to be working on a book about interview studies and found the issue interesting. I said, “I remember your saying, a while ago, that you were going to be doing some interviewing. Can you think about a specific interview? Maybe the one that was most recent. How did you work out what you would ask? Did you work out your questions in advance?”

我琢磨着，同事跟我讲这个故事，是不是也暗示他不想接受采访，只想祝我好运，然后送我离开。不过，我们当时正在吃午饭，离回办公室还有四十五分钟。我想再试一次。我注意到自己格外努力地表现得和蔼可亲。我放松了语气，尽量让下一个问题显得随意，好像我的问题无关紧要，只是碰巧我在写一本关于访谈研究的书，觉得这个问题很有意思。我说：“我记得你之前说过你要做一些访谈。你能回忆一下具体的访谈吗？比如最近的一次。你是怎么想好要问什么问题的？你事先准备好问题了吗？”

And now, for some reason, my colleague told me what I wanted to know. He said, yes, he could think of a specific interview. A week before our lunch he had interviewed someone for a book on which he was working. The morning of his interview he had listed the ten to twelve questions he wanted answered. He was able to list them because he knew, in general, the kind of information that would give his account substance. The questions he listed were the ones important to the book that he thought his respondent could answer.

不知为何，我的同事现在告诉我了我一直想知道的事情。他说，是的，他能想到一个具体的采访案例。就在我们午餐前一周，他为了正在撰写的一本书采访了一位受访者。采访当天早上，他列出了十到十二个他想了解的问题。他之所以能列出这些问题，是因为他大致知道哪些信息能为他的报道提供实质内容。他列出的这些问题对这本书至关重要，而且他认为受访者能够回答这些问题。

This incident seems to me to display the determinants of the questions we ask:

在我看来，这件事似乎揭示了我们所提问题的决定因素：

  1. The problem . Here my problem was to find out how interviewers work out what questions they will ask.
    问题在于，我如何弄清楚面试官是如何决定要问哪些问题的。
  2. A sense of the breadth and density of the material we want to collect . This is the substantive frame of the study plus a sense of the extent to which we want dense detail within it. We may want our materials to be extensive and definitive or neat and narrow or something else. I came to my meeting with my colleague with that almost kinesthetic sense of wanting dense description pretty much limited to the process of question formulation. I didn’t intend to learn, for example, whether my colleague’s interview practices had changed over the years. I was bringing a narrow substantive frame to my inquiry, but I wanted density within it.
    我们需要对想要收集的资料的广度和密度有所把握。这构成了研究的实质性框架，以及我们希望其中包含多少细节的程度。我们可能希望资料详尽而权威，也可能希望资料简洁而精炼，或者其他任何形式。我带着这种近乎本能的渴望去见我的同事，希望在提问过程中获得详尽的描述。例如，我并不打算了解同事的访谈方式这些年来是否有所改变。我带着一个较为狭窄的实质性框架进行研究，但我希望在这个框架内获得足够的细节。
  3. A repertoire of understandings based on previous work, study, awareness of the literature, and experience in living . That I was myself someone who did interviewing as part of his work made me a more informed and alert inquirer. For one thing, I understood the interview situation well enough to recognize that deciding what to ask about can be a problem.
    我积累了一套基于以往工作、学习、文献知识和生活经验的理解体系。我本人也曾从事访谈工作，这使我成为一个更加见多识广、反应敏捷的提问者。首先，我对访谈情境足够了解，能够意识到决定问什么问题本身就是一个难题。
  4. Pilot research . This was my first try at investigating how someone else formulated questions. Some of my fumbling might be chalked up to this being my first interview on this topic; I did not yet know what to ask and how to ask it. Had I done a second interview with another respondent, I’d have had a better idea of what to ask.
    试点研究。这是我第一次尝试调查别人是如何提出问题的。我的一些笨拙之处可能源于这是我第一次就这个主题进行访谈；我当时还不知道该问什么，也不知道该怎么问。如果我能对另一位受访者进行第二次访谈，我就会更清楚该问什么问题了。
  5. A sense of what will give substance to the eventual report . My colleague said he chose questions not only because he thought the respondent could answer them but, even more important, because he anticipated that the answers would give substance to his eventual report. 41
    他对最终报告的内容有所了解。我的同事说，他选择这些问题不仅是因为他认为受访者能够回答，更重要的是，因为他预料到这些答案将为他最终的报告提供实质性内容。<sup>41</sup>

The last consideration is perhaps the most important: The material we collect is of value insofar as it will contribute to a good report. But what would constitute a good report?

最后一点或许最为重要：我们收集的资料只有在有助于撰写一份好报告时才有价值。但什么样的报告才算好报告呢？

A GOOD REPORT

一份不错的报告

A good report would inform its audience about matters of importance to them. It would tell them about experiences that affect them, provide them with explanations for things that have puzzled them, and give them maps to situations they may enter. It would contribute to their competence, their awareness, or their well-being.

一份好的报告应该向读者传达对他们而言重要的信息。它会讲述影响他们的经历，解释他们困惑的事情，并为他们可能遇到的情况提供指导。它有助于提升他们的能力、认知或幸福感。

To do this, the report must go beyond mere provision of information; it must have form, so that its information can be grasped as a whole. A telephone book can be consulted, but not grasped. A good report should make sense as an entity as well as in its items of information; its parts should fit together; it should have coherence.

为此，报告不能仅仅提供信息；它必须结构完整，以便读者能够整体理解其中的信息。电话簿可以查阅，但无法真正理解。一份好的报告不仅其信息条本身要清晰易懂，整体也应如此；各个部分应该衔接流畅，逻辑连贯。

Coherence happens when the separate pieces of the study fit together so well that we move naturally from one to the next. There is a story or a line of argument or an integrative framework such that each piece of information is the right next one to have as we develop an understanding of an inclusive entity. This inclusive entity may be a story, with a beginning and an end, like the history of an innovative program in an organization, or it may be a functioning unit, like a family. If our report has coherence, our readers will recognize that each piece of the study is important to learn about because it contributes to their understanding of the whole.

当研究的各个部分衔接得如此完美，以至于我们可以自然而然地从一个部分过渡到下一个部分时，就体现出了连贯性。它包含一个故事、一条论证思路或一个整合框架，使得每一条信息都恰如其分地衔接起来，帮助我们逐步理解一个整体。这个整体可以是一个有始有终的故事，例如组织中一项创新项目的历史；也可以是一个运转良好的单元，例如一个家庭。如果我们的报告具有连贯性，读者就会意识到研究的每个部分都至关重要，因为它们共同构成了对整体的理解。

There are, in general, two approaches to achieving coherence: One, which uses passage through time to provide structure to the report, can be characterized as diachronic . The other, which makes no use of time and so must find some other basis for coherence, can be characterized as synchronic .

一般来说，实现连贯性有两种方法：一种是利用时间推移为报告提供结构，可以称之为历时性方法；另一种是不利用时间，因此必须寻找其他连贯性基础，可以称之为共时性方法。

DIACHRONIC REPORTS

历时性报告

Diachronic reports begin at the beginning and proceed from there. They may describe, for example, how young people leave the vicissitudes of adolescence to enter early adulthood or how stepparents move from wary role-playing to genuine family feeling. They tell stories in which things happen as time goes on.

历时性报告从最初开始，逐步展开。例如，它们可能描述年轻人如何走出青春期的迷茫，步入成年早期；或者继父母如何从谨慎的角色扮演转变为建立真正的家庭关系。它们讲述的是随着时间推移而发生的故事。

Diachronic reports may describe phases of development or change; for example, the phases of recovery from grief. They may consider the careers by which people achieve a particular end point; for example, arrival in a mental hospital or in an executive suite. Or they may focus on an event and its impacts beginning, say, with a tropical storm, noting the methods used by the weather bureau to predict its course, then moving to the experiences of sailors on ships caught in what has become a hurricane, then describing the impact of the storm’s winds on coastal towns, and on to the cleanups and insurance claims and stories of lucky survival.

历时性报告可以描述发展或变化的各个阶段；例如，从悲伤中恢复的各个阶段。它们可以探讨人们达到特定终点的职业历程；例如，进入精神病院或进入高管办公室。或者，它们可以聚焦于某个事件及其影响，例如，从一场热带风暴开始，记录气象局预测其路径的方法，然后讲述被困在已发展成飓风的风暴中的船只上的水手的经历，接着描述风暴的强风对沿海城镇的影响，最后讲述清理工作、保险索赔以及幸运幸存者的故事。

Diachronic reports sometimes provide explanation: why applicants chose this particular college or why a disaster occurred without forewarning. They can be responses to our desire to ask the retrospective question “How come that happened?” as well as the prospective question “What happened next?”

历时性报告有时会提供解释：例如，为什么申请者会选择这所特定的大学，或者为什么灾难会在毫无预警的情况下发生。它们既可以回应我们想要追问的回顾性问题“为什么会发生这样的事？”，也可以回应我们想要展望的未来问题“接下来发生了什么？”

Diachronic story lines that attempt to provide explanations have been called “accounting schemes.” 1 Suppose we want to explain why it is that some men achieve high business positions. We might include in our accounting scheme a description of the challenges the men confronted, their motivations to succeed, the resources they could call on, and how they finally won through. The story we would end up with would be one of men whose drive, intelligence, and luck brought them success.

试图提供解释的历时性叙事线索被称为“解释框架”。假设我们想解释为什么有些人能取得很高的商业地位。我们的解释框架可能会包含对这些人所面临的挑战、他们成功的动机、他们可以利用的资源以及他们最终如何取得成功的描述。最终，我们得到的故事将讲述的是一群凭借干劲、智慧和运气获得成功的人。

Alternative accounting schemes can almost always be devised. To explain why some men achieve success in business we might instead describe how these men learned the interpersonal and technical skills that later aided their rise. The story we could end up with would be one of the familial and educational influences that led to success.

几乎总能设计出其他的会计处理方案。为了解释为什么有些人能在商业上取得成功，我们不妨描述一下这些人是如何习得人际交往和技术技能的，而这些技能后来又帮助他们走向成功。最终，我们可能会得出这样的结论：家庭和教育因素共同促成了他们的成功。

Accounting schemes are not theories about how reality works. They are, rather, sets of categories waiting to be filled by fact. In consequence, accounting schemes are not to be judged as true or false. They should rather be judged by the extent to which they are useful in organizing what we have been told into a story that makes sense and that gives proper weight to the issues that we have learned from our interviewing are important. If we should find in the course of our interviews that a particular accounting scheme doesn’t work—the issues it suggests don’t seem important whereas other issues seem to matter a lot—then we ought to jettison the scheme. It isn’t useful enough.

会计模式并非关于现实运作方式的理论，而是一系列等待事实填充的类别。因此，我们不应评判会计模式的真假，而应根据其在多大程度上能够有效地将我们了解到的信息整理成一个合乎逻辑的故事，并恰当地强调我们从访谈中了解到的重要问题。如果在访谈过程中，我们发现某个会计模式并不适用——它所揭示的问题似乎并不重要，而其他问题却至关重要——那么我们就应该摒弃这个模式，因为它不够实用。

SYNCHRONIC REPORTS

同步报告

Synchronic reports attempt to achieve coherence without the armature of time. Generally, they do so by dividing whatever they are about into its significant sectors and moving in logical sequence from sector to sector. A report on the lives of successful men might begin with the sector of their work, since it provides a basis for their participation in the other sectors critical to their well-being. It might then describe the functioning of the men in the sector of marriage, and in their relationships with their children. It might then move outward to their relationships with other kin and to their friendships. In a similar way a report on an organization might describe the functioning of its various departments, perhaps beginning with its leadership, and moving then to the contributions, the internal problems, and the interdepartmental frictions of its operating units.

同步报告力求在不依赖时间框架的情况下实现连贯性。通常，它们通过将主题划分为若干重要部分，并按逻辑顺序逐一展开来实现这一目标。例如，一份关于成功人士生活的报告可能从他们的工作领域入手，因为工作是他们参与其他对其福祉至关重要的领域的基础。报告随后可能描述他们在婚姻领域以及与子女关系中的表现，并进一步扩展到他们与其他亲属的关系以及友谊。同样，一份关于某个组织的报告可能描述其各个部门的运作情况，或许可以从领导层入手，然后探讨各运营部门的贡献、内部问题以及部门间的摩擦。

Contributing to the coherence of synchronic reports can be themes or patterns that underlie developments in every sector. A report might attempt to show, for example, that each member of a family expresses the same unvoiced concern. Or a report might assert a logical connection among an organization’s sectors by arguing that one sector is basic to the others or that the sectors are linked by the flow of work.

有助于提高同步报告连贯性的因素包括贯穿各个领域发展的主题或模式。例如，一份报告可能试图表明，一个家庭的每个成员都表达了相同的未曾言明的担忧。或者，一份报告可能通过论证某个领域是其他领域的基础，或者各个领域通过工作流程相互联系，来阐明组织各领域之间的逻辑关系。

Sometimes synchronie stories are based on a functional approach. The aim in a functional approach is to explain how something works. 2 The approach requires seeing whatever is to be described—a family, a school, a company—as having goals that it seeks to achieve, or functional requisites that must be met if it is to survive. The members of these entities can also be described as having personal goals, in which event the analyst may be able to describe both the intermeshing and the conflict of personal and communal goals.

有时，同步性故事会基于功能主义方法。功能主义方法的目的是解释事物如何运作。这种方法要求将待描述的对象——例如家庭、学校或公司——视为拥有其力求实现的目标，或为了生存必须满足的功能性需求。这些实体的成员也可以被描述为拥有个人目标，在这种情况下，分析师或许能够描述个人目标和集体目标之间的交织与冲突。

One goal of any entity, in this way of seeing things, is self-maintenance: keeping on keeping on. Answering how self-maintenance is achieved could constitute one part of the story. If it is a family that is being described, this might mean giving attention to how funds are brought in and expended, how routines are maintained, and how the work of the family is done.

从这个角度来看，任何实体的目标之一都是自我维持：持续运转。而如何实现自我维持，则可以构成故事的一部分。如果描述的是一个家庭，这可能意味着要关注资金的来源和支出方式、日常作息的维持方式以及家庭成员的工作安排。

Every entity will have action goals, ends it wishes to achieve, as well as the goal of self-maintenance. An action goal for the family might be to launch its children into the larger society. A part of the story of a family might be a description of its efforts to achieve its action goals and its success or lack of success.

每个实体都会有行动目标，即希望达成的最终目标，以及自我维持的目标。例如，家庭的行动目标可能是将子女送入更广阔的社会。家庭故事的一部分可能就是描述其为实现行动目标所做的努力，以及这些努力的成败。

Some aspects of the entity could be taken as fixed for the period of the study. They might include, for example, the roles and relationships of members. The story could describe how these arrangements facilitate and impede goal attainment.

在研究期间，该实体的某些方面可以被视为固定不变的。例如，这些方面可能包括成员的角色和关系。研究报告可以描述这些安排如何促进或阻碍目标的实现。

The risk in synchronic reports is that they will lack a strong conceptual framework, and so will appear to be merely a collection of observations. True, stories that show how a system works can be interesting and may be what a particular study requires, but it is easier, all else being equal, to hold a reader’s attention with the sort of plot-unfolding story line that a diachronic approach makes possible. 3

共时性报告的风险在于缺乏强有力的概念框架，因此可能仅仅沦为观察结果的罗列。诚然，展现系统运作方式的故事可能引人入胜，也可能正是特定研究所需要的，但在其他条件相同的情况下，历时性研究方法所提供的情节展开式叙事更容易吸引读者的注意力。

FROM SUBSTANTIVE FRAME TO INTERVIEW GUIDE

从实质性框架到面试指南

Suppose the aim of our study is to learn about and report on the visitation experience of separated or divorced parents. As we think about the story we want to tell in our report, we find that we give it a diachronic form. We anticipate beginning with the parental relationships maintained by respondents when they were married. We would then trace the changes in the parents’ relationships with their children as the parents moved toward separation. We would describe what led the parents’ marriage to dissolve and what arrangements the parents made then for their children’s care. Finally, we would describe how the parents’ custody and visitation arrangements evolved over time.

假设我们研究的目的是了解并报告分居或离婚父母的探视经历。在构思报告内容时，我们发现应该采用历时性叙述方式。我们计划从受访者婚姻存续期间的亲子关系入手，然后追踪父母分居过程中与子女关系的变化，描述导致婚姻破裂的原因以及他们当时为子女抚养所做的安排，最后阐述父母的监护权和探视安排如何随时间演变。

We might have considered other frameworks for the report. We might have considered using a diachronic approach in which we would contrast the histories of visitation arrangements that produce repeated appeals to the court with the histories of visitation arrangements that seem more satisfactory to the parents. Or we might have considered using a synchronic strategy of contrasting the parents’ and children’s experience in conflict-free visitation arrangements with their experience in conflictladen visitation arrangements.

我们或许可以考虑采用其他报告框架。例如，我们可以采用历时性方法，对比那些导致反复上诉至法院的探视安排历史，以及那些父母似乎更满意的探视安排历史。或者，我们也可以采用共时性策略，对比父母和子女在无冲突探视安排中的体验，以及在充满冲突的探视安排中的体验。

But let us suppose that we have decided that our report will move from the parents’ early familial relationships to their relationships with their children after the ending of the parents’ marriage. Let us further suppose that our interests, experience, hunches, or preliminary work make us want to include as one area within the project’s substantive frame the level of parental investment in the children. One reason we might want to learn about parental investment is that we believe it can affect how the parents arrange custody and visitation.

但假设我们决定，报告将从父母早期的家庭关系转向他们婚姻结束后与子女的关系。再假设，我们的兴趣、经验、直觉或初步工作促使我们希望将父母对子女的投入程度纳入项目的主要框架。我们想要了解父母投入程度的原因之一可能是，我们认为它会影响父母如何安排监护权和探视权。

To develop information about parental investment, we must first decide the narrower components of the area about which we can question respondents. We also have to keep in mind that parental investment and its possible expressions could include enough topics to fill an interview all by itself, and if we want our interview to deal with other matters as well, we will eventually have to limit ourselves to the aspects of parental investment most relevant to custody and visitation. But let us begin by being inclusive. We might arrive at a list of topics-to-learn-about like the following:

为了收集有关父母投入的信息，我们首先必须确定可以向受访者询问的具体领域。我们还要记住，父母投入及其各种表现形式本身就足以构成一次完整的访谈内容，如果我们希望访谈还能涉及其他方面，最终就必须将范围限定在与监护权和探视权最相关的父母投入方面。但让我们先从涵盖面广的角度出发。我们可能会列出如下的待了解主题：

  1. The parent’s thoughts and feelings regarding the children when the children were born and on any later occasion when the parent became aware of emotional investment in the children.
    父母在孩子出生时以及之后任何父母意识到自己对孩子投入了情感的时候，对孩子的想法和感受。
  2. The parent’s present thoughts and feelings regarding the children, including fears, worries, hopes, gratifications.
    父母目前对孩子的想法和感受，包括恐惧、担忧、希望和满足感。
  3. The extent to which the parent’s planning and activities are organized around the parent’s relationships with the children. Are the children central or peripheral in the parent’s planning and activities?
    父母的计划和活动在多大程度上围绕着父母与子女的关系展开？子女在父母的计划和活动中是中心地位还是边缘地位？
  4. The extent to which the children play a role in the parent’s self-image and self-presentation.
    子女在父母的自我形象和自我呈现中扮演的角色程度。
  5. The parent’s thoughts and feelings when separated from the children.
    父母与子女分离时的想法和感受。

Each of the topics in the list suggests lines of inquiry that can be pursued with respondents. By listing these lines of inquiry we can construct a guide for the interviewer when exploring this area with a respondent. The listing of lines of inquiry might look like the following:

列表中的每个主题都提供了可以与受访者探讨的探究方向。通过列出这些探究方向，我们可以为访谈者构建一个指南，以便他们在与受访者探讨该领域时能够更好地进行交流。探究方向列表可能如下所示：

  1. Past thoughts and feelings . What were R’s [the respondent’s] thoughts and feelings regarding the children when the children were born? [Possible questions: “Can you remember when your child was born? Could you walk me through what your thoughts were? What your feelings were? Did you say anything to anyone? To the other parent? Do you remember when you first held the child? How did that happen? What went through your mind? What were your feelings?”] Was there a point where R really felt like a parent? What happened to produce this?
    过去的想法和感受。当孩子出生时，R（受访者）对孩子有哪些想法和感受？[可能的问题：“您还记得孩子出生时的情景吗？您能描述一下当时的想法和感受吗？您跟别人说过什么吗？跟另一位家长说过吗？您还记得第一次抱起孩子的情景吗？当时是怎么发生的？您当时在想什么？您的感受是什么？”] R 是否曾经真正感受到自己为人父母？是什么促使他产生这种感受？
  2. Current thoughts and feelings . Ask about occasions when R is with the children. What goes through R’s mind at such times? What are R’s feelings? Ask about most recent time R had worries about the children. What was the incident, what were the worries? Has R had fears in relation to the children? When? What did R fear? Has R had hopes? Ask about most recent time R was gratified by the children. What was the incident, what were the gratifications? Ask for times when R was dismayed or embarrassed by the children, when R was angry with them, when R felt burdened by them, when R was proud of them.
    当前的想法和感受。询问R与孩子们在一起时的情景。在这些时刻，R在想些什么？R的感受是什么？询问R最近一次担心孩子们是什么时候。发生了什么事？担心的是什么？R是否曾对孩子们感到恐惧？什么时候？R害怕什么？R是否抱有希望？询问R最近一次因孩子们而感到欣慰是什么时候。发生了什么事？欣慰之处是什么？询问R因孩子们而感到沮丧或尴尬、生气、感到负担或为孩子们感到骄傲的时刻。
  3. The children and R’s plans and activities . To what extent is R’s daily routine organized around the children’s needs and activities? Ask about R’s most recent workday and most recent weekend. How much are the children in R’s mind while R is at work? At other times? Does R have any impulse to telephone? What happens in telephone calls? In the most recent telephone call, what was said? Does R make a special occasion of the children’s birthdays, milestones at school? Ask about most recent such events.
    孩子们和R的计划和活动。R的日常安排在多大程度上围绕着孩子们的需求和活动？询问R最近一个工作日和最近一个周末的情况。R在工作时有多关心孩子们？其他时间呢？R是否有打电话的冲动？电话里都说了些什么？最近一次通话的内容是什么？R是否会特别庆祝孩子们的生日、在学校取得的成就？询问最近一次的此类活动。
  4. R’s self-image and self-presentation . Ask for incident when R has felt most like parent. Ask for most recent incident when R talked to friends or family about self as parent or about children. Was there such an incident in the last day or two? Is an incident of this sort frequent or infrequent?
    R的自我认知和自我呈现。询问R在什么时候感觉自己最像父母。询问R最近一次与朋友或家人谈论自己作为父母或孩子的情况。过去一两天内是否发生过此类事件？这类事件是经常发生还是很少发生？
  5. Separation from children . Ask R about times of separation from the children. How did the separation occur? What were R’s thoughts and feelings? Did R attempt to maintain contact by telephone? What were R’s feelings on rejoining the children?
    与子女分离。询问R与子女分离的经历。分离是如何发生的？R当时的想法和感受是什么？R是否尝试通过电话保持联系？R与子女重聚时有何感受？

The study’s substantive frame would, of course, require investigation of other areas as well as parental investment, including, at the least, the history of the parents’ visitation arrangements, the parents’ experience with the visitation arrangements, and the reactions of the children to the arrangements. For each of these other areas we would work out, just as we did here, the narrower issues and topics about which we might ask questions, and then work out lines of inquiry for the interview.

当然，这项研究的实质性框架除了父母的投入之外，还需要调查其他领域，至少包括父母探视安排的历史、父母对探视安排的体验以及孩子对这些安排的反应。对于这些其他领域，我们会像在这里一样，确定更具体的议题和主题，并据此制定访谈的调查方向。

It might be that interviewing in the area of parental investment would fill all the time set aside for a single interview and, to learn about other areas we would either have to narrow what we ask about in the area of parental investment or schedule more than a single interview with respondents. If we were devote an entire interview with respondents to discussing parental investment, the preceding list of topics might serve as an interview guide. If we intended to cover other areas as well in the interview, we could reduce the number of topics in our guide which deal with parental investment.

或许，围绕父母投资这一主题的访谈会占据我们为一次访谈预留的所有时间。为了了解其他领域，我们要么需要缩小父母投资领域的访谈范围，要么需要安排多次访谈。如果我们打算用一次完整的访谈来讨论父母投资，那么前面列出的主题可以作为访谈指南。如果我们还计划在访谈中涵盖其他领域，那么我们可以减少指南中与父母投资相关的主题数量。

An interview guide is a listing of areas to be covered in the interview along with, for each area, a listing of topics or questions that together will suggest lines of inquiry. The guide functions for the interviewer as a prompter might for an actor. If the interviewer is fully in control of the interview topics, the guide itself can remain unused. But if the interviewer begins to be uncertain about what questions might come next, or whether an area or a topic has been skipped, the guide is there to be consulted. The interview guide may also be consulted at the very end of an interview as a last check that everything has been asked.

面试指南是一份清单，列出了面试中需要涵盖的各个领域，每个领域都列出了一系列主题或问题，这些问题共同构成了提问方向。指南对于面试官的作用，就像提词器对于演员一样。如果面试官完全掌控了面试主题，指南本身可以不用。但如果面试官开始不确定接下来会问什么问题，或者某个领域或主题是否被遗漏，指南就派上了用场。面试指南也可以在面试结束时作为最后检查，确保所有问题都已提出。

One of the functions pilot interviews can perform is field testing a draft of the interview guide. A single pilot interview can suggest where a guide is overweighted or redundant and where it is skimpy, but three or four pilot interviews might be the minimum for safety. Even with such testing, the guide is likely to undergo modification as more is learned through interviewing about the area of the study.

试点访谈的功能之一是对访谈指南草稿进行实地测试。一次试点访谈即可发现指南中哪些内容过于冗赘或冗余，哪些内容过于简略，但为了确保万无一失，至少需要进行三到四次试点访谈。即使经过这样的测试，随着对研究领域的深入了解，指南仍可能需要进行修改。

The best guides list topics or lines for inquiry so they can be grasped at a glance, with just enough detail to make evident what is wanted. The guide may suggest specific questions to start discussion in important areas, but that isn’t necessary. Where the interviewer is thoroughly familiar with the study’s aims, guides can be sketchy, listing only topic headings. Where interviewers cannot make independent judgments regarding how best to direct their inquiry, as when the interviewers are not part of the investigative team, the interview guide must be developed in more detail. The amount of detail in the example above might be about right for an interview conducted by someone not fully aware of the study’s aims. But still more detailed and dense guides seem to me difficult to use in an interview setting. It wouldn’t do for an interviewer to have to say to a respondent, “Would you wait a moment while I read again what I’m supposed to ask?” 4

最佳的访谈指南会列出待问主题或要点，以便一目了然，并提供足够的细节来明确目的。指南可能会建议一些具体问题来开启重要领域的讨论，但这并非必要。如果访谈者对研究目标非常熟悉，指南可以简略一些，只列出主题标题即可。如果访谈者无法独立判断如何最好地引导提问，例如访谈者并非研究团队成员，则访谈指南必须更加详细。上述示例中的详细程度可能适合由不太了解研究目标的人员进行的访谈。但我认为，过于详细和繁复的指南在访谈环境中难以使用。如果访谈者不得不对受访者说：“请稍等片刻，让我再读一遍我应该问的问题好吗？”

When the guide is more fully detailed, interviewers may have to be cautioned not to shift from qualitative interviewing to survey-style interviewing in order to cover everything. Focusing closely on the guide, at the cost of attention to the respondent and the flow of the interview, is always a mistake. Some of my worst interviews have been produced by a conscientious attempt to cover the topics in a guide. Permitting the respondent to talk about what the respondent wants to talk about, so long as it is anywhere near the topic of the study, will always produce better data than plodding adherence to the guide. Even though the interviewer should try to cover the guide, the interviewer should be prepared to concentrate attention on matters on which the respondent is especially able to report, even at the cost of skimping on other matters.

当访谈指南内容更加详尽时，应提醒访谈员不要为了涵盖所有内容而从定性访谈转为问卷式访谈。过于注重指南而忽略受访者和访谈流程，始终是一个错误。我一些最糟糕的访谈，正是由于一丝不苟地试图涵盖指南中的所有主题而导致的。允许受访者谈论他们想谈论的内容，只要这些内容与研究主题相关，总是比死板地遵循指南更能获得高质量的数据。尽管访谈员应该尽量涵盖指南的内容，但也应该做好准备，将注意力集中在受访者特别擅长的方面，即使这意味着在其他方面有所疏漏。

Years ago, before tape recorders, when I was taking interviews in shorthand, the interview guide would be the last page of my shorthand book. Now it is a page or two on a clipboard. Sometimes, if I know an area well or if the interview is entirely exploratory, I do without a written interview guide, although I have one pretty well worked out in my mind. But I like to have a written guide available to me, even if I do not use it in the interview. It is there to provide preparation for the interview, before the interview begins, and it can be a checklist to be used at the end of an interview to ensure that nothing has been missed.

多年前，录音机还没普及的时候，我用速记做采访，采访提纲通常是速记本的最后一页。现在，它只是夹在写字板上的一两页。有时候，如果我对某个领域很熟悉，或者采访完全是探索性的，我就不会准备书面的采访提纲，尽管我脑子里已经有了相当完整的提纲。但我还是喜欢准备一份书面提纲，即使采访时不用。它的作用是在采访开始前进行准备，也可以在采访结束后作为检查清单，确保没有遗漏任何重要信息。

Here is a guide intended to direct the first of three interviews with occupationally successful men. It provides the basis for discussing the meaning of work and the nature of work stress in the men’s lives. 5

这是一份旨在指导对三位事业有成的男性进行首次访谈的指南。它为探讨工作的意义以及工作压力在这些男性生活中的性质奠定了基础。

  1. A DAY AT WORK
    工作中的一天
  4. TASKS AT WORK
    工作任务
  7. HOW R CAME TO THIS WORK
    R是如何得到这份工作的
  9. GRATIFICATIONS AND BURDENS OF WORK
    工作的满足感和负担
  1. RECOGNITION AND REWARDS
    表彰与奖励

This interview guide generally led to interviews of 2 hours or a bit less. Usually between four to six areas can be covered adequately in a 2-hour interview. If we want to cover more areas—or if one or more of the areas requires extensive discussion—we would probably do best to anticipate having more than a single interview session.

这份面试指南通常能将面试时间控制在两小时或略短一些。一般来说，两小时的面试可以充分涵盖四到六个方面。如果我们想涵盖更多方面，或者其中一个或多个方面需要深入探讨，那么我们最好预留出进行多次面试的时间。

QUANTITATIVE ITEMS

定量项目

Often, as I noted in chapter 1, there is good reason for including quantitative items in qualitative interviews. Quantitative items can help anchor a qualitative discussion. Without quantitative information we might have to make imprecise statements like “Many of our respondents felt their present circumstances to be undesirable.” With quantitative material we instead can say, “Asked to rate their present circumstances on a scale going from the best time in their lives to the worst, over 30% of respondents rated their present circumstances in the lower third of the scale.” The second is by far the stronger statement.
Furthermore, quantitative items—or, at any rate, items asked of everyone—make it easy to segment the population of respondents, for example, into those 40 and younger and those over 40, or into those who say their marriages are very good and those who say they are only good or fair. Quantitative items also can be a basis for further qualitative exploration. In the study of occupationally successful men I found that standardized questions about stress symptoms and depression symptoms provided a useful starting point for learning about times of stress and depression. At the end of the third interview we asked the men we were interviewing to respond to our symptom list. If in response to the item “Has there been a time in the last year when you felt low or depressed?” someone answered yes, the interviewer could then ask what was happening at the time. Important information often emerged.
I don’t like beginning qualitative interviewing by asking for census data (“What was your age at your last birthday?” and “Would you say you work at paid employment full-time, part-time, or not at all?”). It sets the wrong tone. Questions of this sort suggest that you want “just the facts, ma’am.” Once such an understanding is established, it becomes that much more difficult to establish that you want a full and detailed narrative account. But when an interview is over, it doesn’t hurt to ask for whatever census data you think may prove useful. It is then natural to say, “Could I ask a few more questions, about your age and the like?”

正如我在第一章中提到的，在定性访谈中加入定量项目往往是很有道理的。定量项目有助于为定性讨论提供依据。如果没有定量信息，我们可能只能做出一些不够精确的陈述，例如“许多受访者认为他们目前的处境并不理想”。而有了定量数据，我们就可以这样表述：“当被要求以人生最佳时期到最差时期来评价他们目前的处境时，超过30%的受访者将他们的处境评为较低等级。” 后一种表述显然更有力。此外，定量项目——或者至少是询问所有受访者的项目——便于对受访者群体进行细分，例如，将受访者分为40岁及以下和40岁以上两组，或者将他们认为婚姻非常美满的人和他们认为婚姻状况一般或尚可的人分为两组。定量项目还可以作为进一步定性探索的基础。在对事业成功的男性进行的研究中，我发现关于压力症状和抑郁症状的标准化问题，可以作为了解他们压力和抑郁时期的一个有效切入点。在第三次访谈结束时，我们会请受访者对我们的症状清单做出回应。如果有人对“过去一年中，您是否曾感到情绪低落或抑郁？”这个问题回答“是”，访谈者就可以进一步询问当时的情况。通常，一些重要的信息会由此浮现。我不喜欢在定性访谈开始时就询问人口普查数据（例如“您上次过生日时多大了？”以及“您目前从事的是全职、兼职还是完全没有工作？”）。这会奠定错误的基调。这类问题暗示着你只想了解“事实，女士”。一旦建立了这种认知，就很难再表明你想要的是完整而详细的叙述。但是，访谈结束后，询问一些你认为可能有用的人口普查数据也无妨。然后很自然地就会说：“我可以再问几个问题吗，比如您的年龄之类的？”

STANDARD GUIDES AND TAILORED GUIDES

标准指南和定制指南

A standard interview guide should do for interviews with respondents who are representative of a population. While each respondent may elaborate part of the interview in a way no other respondent does, this need not be anticipated in the guide. People who are informants on some part of an event, on the other hand, must be interviewed on what they know that no one else does. If you are interviewing a panel of informants, you will probably have to draft a new guide, with the particular respondent in mind, for each interview. And the interviewer should be prepared to drop the guide entirely if the interview takes an unexpected direction.

对于具有代表性的受访者，标准的访谈指南即可满足需求。虽然每位受访者在访谈中可能会以其他受访者不会的方式详细阐述某些内容，但这无需在指南中预先考虑到。然而，对于那些掌握事件部分信息的人，则必须就他们所了解的、其他人所不知道的信息进行访谈。如果您要访谈一组信息提供者，则可能需要为每次访谈专门为每位受访者拟定一份新的指南。此外，如果访谈朝着意料之外的方向发展，访谈者应做好完全放弃指南的准备。

EARLY INTERVIEWS AS LEARNING EXPERIENCES

早期面试作为学习经验

When we try to imagine developments in a situation we don’t know firsthand (such as what it is like to be a member of a submarine crew), we must adapt images from experiences we have had. We construct our initial understandings from the heroes, villains, and other characters who are members of our internal repertory company; the places we have been ourselves or have read about or have seen on television; and the plot developments our lives have taught us to anticipate. Our construction is never exactly right. When we actually interview someone in the situation, we inevitably discover that we didn’t understand fully, and perhaps not at all.

当我们试图想象自己并不了解的情况（例如潜艇艇员的经历）时，我们必须借鉴自身的经验来构建认知。我们最初的理解来源于我们内心深处的英雄、反派和其他角色；来源于我们亲身经历过、阅读过或看过的地方；来源于我们生活中习以为常的情节发展。然而，我们的理解永远无法完全准确。当我们真正采访身处其中的人时，我们最终会发现，我们之前的理解并不全面，甚至可能一无所知。

In virtually every new study I do I am thrilled by the surprise of things turning out to be different from my expectations and yet just the way they should be.
