Here the interviewer could have picked up the ethical issue or the self-restraint the respondent is describing, but that would probably have led the respondent to repeat what he’s already said about not wanting to put someone else at risk. Instead the interviewer makes explicit what may be the theme underlying much of what the respondent has been saying: no kids; being seen as suspect by friends and family; having no access to sexual relationships. The interviewer is, in effect, checking a hypothesis, while at the same time suggesting an issue for development. And the interviewer is also again establishing that he understands what the respondent is saying. Note that the interviewer offers his guess at the underlying theme in a tentative, “sounds like …” statement that the respondent can reject.

答辩人证实，他所说的正是那种被排斥的感觉。他现在明确地将这种感觉与他之前所说的只能看不能碰的说法联系起来。值得注意的是，现在答辩人不再像之前那样东拉西扯，而是条理清晰、情绪饱满地发言。他现在谈论的是对他来说至关重要的事情。

The respondent and the interviewer have together located what the respondent can best contribute to the study at this point in the respondent’s interview: a statement of how isolating it is to be HIV positive and how lonely it is to be so afflicted.

在受访者的访谈中，受访者和访谈员共同确定了受访者在此时此刻能为研究做出的最大贡献：陈述成为 HIV 阳性是多么孤立无援，以及遭受这种折磨是多么孤独。

The interviewer made a couple of mistakes in the course of this excerpt. He failed to recognize that the respondent had disclaimed any potentially romantic relationship and went ahead to ask for an instance; and he phrased an appropriate question in so open a fashion that the respondent entirely misinterpreted it. Nevertheless, the interviewer paid close and unfaltering attention not just to what the respondent was saying, but also to what might underlie what he was saying. Fairly quickly the interviewer found an important underlying issue that had been expressed in much of what the respondent had said and that had to be recognized if the respondent’s situation was to be understood. The interviewer’s recognition of this underlying issue was not only valuable for the study in its own right, but also strengthened the interviewing partnership.

在本次访谈中，访谈者犯了几个错误。他没有意识到受访者已经否认存在任何潜在的恋爱关系，仍然追问具体事例；而且，他提出的问题措辞过于开放，导致受访者完全误解。尽管如此，访谈者始终保持着高度的专注，不仅关注受访者的发言，也关注其言外之意。很快，访谈者就发现了一个贯穿受访者大部分发言的重要潜在问题，而这个问题必须被重视才能真正理解受访者的处境。访谈者对这一潜在问题的识别不仅对研究本身具有重要价值，也加强了访谈双方的合作关系。

EXAMPLES OF POOR INTERVIEWING

糟糕的面试案例

A bad interview can often be identified just from the look of a page of transcript: the ratio of words said by the respondent to words said by the interviewer will be nearly one to one. However, a preponderance of respondent material doesn’t guarantee a good interview. An interviewer can produce a bad interview not only by talking as much as the respondent but also by permitting the respondent to develop at length material of no value to the study.

一次糟糕的访谈往往只需浏览一下访谈记录就能发现：受访者发言的字数与访谈者发言的字数几乎是1:1。然而，受访者发言量大并不意味着访谈就一定好。访谈者不仅可以通过与受访者一样多的发言来制造糟糕的访谈，还可以通过允许受访者冗长地阐述与研究无关的内容来制造糟糕的访谈。

Bad interviews are more frequently of the sparse-response type than the runaway respondent type. Leading to the sparse responses, often, is what seems to be questioning by the interviewer that is unrelated to the respondent’s train of thought; instead, the interviewer’s questions are directed solely by the interview guide, or they express the interviewer’s own train of thought.

糟糕的访谈往往是回答稀疏型，而非回答失控型。导致回答稀疏的原因通常是访谈者提出的问题与受访者的思路无关；相反，访谈者的提问仅仅依据访谈提纲，或者表达的是访谈者自己的思路。

Interview III. An Interviewer with an Unshakeable Assumption

访谈三：一位抱持着不可动摇的假设的访谈者

In this first example of bad interviewing, the interviewer seems to be trying to control what she is being told. She has a preconceived notion of what the respondent ought to tell her, a notion she doesn’t permit the respondent to influence.

在第一个糟糕的面试例子中，面试官似乎试图控制受访者所说的话。她预先设定了受访者应该告诉她的内容，并且不允许受访者影响她的想法。

The general topic was relationships at work, and the interviewer was searching for instances of stressful relationships. The respondent had been talking about other members of his work group.

访谈主题主要是职场人际关系，面试官想了解受访者在工作中遇到的人际关系压力。受访者一直在谈论他所在工作团队的其他成员。

The respondent is now speaking in the generalized present. At this point it would make sense to accept where the respondent is and ask him to become concrete: “Could you tell me about the last meeting? Walk me through it?”

In this interview excerpt the interviewer was determined to get an interesting story of troubles with a coworker and refused to accept the respondent’s unwillingness or inability to come up with one. The interviewer also refused to accept the respondent’s indications of material he could develop comfortably. I find it remarkable that the respondent continued to be cooperative, despite the interviewer’s competing with him for the floor, disregarding his comments, and abruptly shifting topics.

for the respondent. Instead of pursuing this, the interviewer asks a leading question about what will now happen to the information about the respondent gained by his former coworker. One of the several problems in this excerpt is the extent to which the interviewer provided wordings for the respondent. When an interviewer introduces a phrase in a question (here the phrase is “and it kind of gets spread around”), then the phrase is the interviewer’s and not the respondent’s, even though the respondent may accept that phrase (“Yeah, it gets spread around”).

这段摘录中的几个问题之一是访谈者在多大程度上为受访者提供了措辞。当访谈者在问题中引入一个短语（这里是“而且它四处传播”），那么这个短语是访谈者的，而不是受访者的，即使受访者可能接受这个短语（“是的，它四处传播”）。

The same observation holds for this interviewer’s insistence, despite the respondent’s objections, on pursuing the theme of working to impress. Does this respondent really work to impress others? I would say no, not in the sense the interviewer intends. He wants recognition for his competence, but that’s different from being competent in order to gain recognition. However, the interviewer kept returning to this theme, and at a couple of points elicited very qualified agreement. But it would be wrong to accept this qualified agreement as validating the interviewer’s assumption.

同样的道理也适用于这位面试官，尽管受访者反对，他仍然坚持追问“努力给人留下深刻印象”这个话题。这位受访者真的努力是为了给别人留下深刻印象吗？我认为不是，至少不是面试官所指的那种程度。他渴望自己的能力得到认可，但这与为了获得认可而努力工作是两回事。然而，面试官反复提及这个话题，并且在某些时候获得了受访者非常谨慎的同意。但如果把这种谨慎的同意当作面试官假设的佐证，那就错了。

Interview V. Losing the Research Partnership

访谈五：失去研究伙伴关系

Despite the serious interviewing flaws in the two previous excerpts, the interviewer in each was able to maintain an interviewing partnership. When things really go badly, the research partnership is likely to be questioned by the respondent. The following example of bad interviewing is from an interview conducted by a student in a class on interviewing.

尽管前两个摘录中存在严重的访谈缺陷，但两位访谈者都能够维持良好的访谈合作关系。然而，当访谈真的出现严重问题时，受访者很可能会质疑这种合作关系。以下糟糕的访谈案例来自一位学生在访谈技巧课程中进行的访谈。

The student interviewer was concerned with identity formation among delinquents, an interesting issue for which qualitative interviewing would seem to be the appropriate data-gathering approach. The student hoped to demonstrate that criminal behavior stemmed from the development of a criminal identity and that one process leading to the development of a criminal identity was taking as a role model a figure from organized crime. The excerpt is from the student’s interview with a 17-year-old who had recently been convicted of theft. The 17-year-old has just said that organized crime figures had long been heroes of his.

这位学生访谈者关注的是青少年罪犯的身份认同形成问题，这是一个很有意思的议题，而定性访谈似乎是收集数据的合适方法。这位学生希望证明，犯罪行为源于犯罪身份的形成，而导致犯罪身份形成的一个过程就是以有组织犯罪人物为榜样。以下摘录自这位学生对一位近期因盗窃罪被定罪的17岁少年的访谈。这位17岁的少年刚刚表示，有组织犯罪人物长期以来都是他的偶像。

“权力”一词在我看来是另一个重要的线索。我猜测它表达了受访者在认知和情感上重视的某种东西。或许值得进一步探究。

I: How do you mean?

我：你这话是什么意思？

It’s going to be tough to get to the reason power is attractive, but maybe the respondent can describe the imagery associated with power. In general, it’s difficult to get respondents to explore cognitive and emotional complexes. Asked for elaboration, respondents are apt to state the complex in new words rather than provide its imagistic and emotional bases. Although the question “How do you mean?” can be a good one if a respondent is already in a scene (if this respondent had said, “The guy I was working for showed me he liked me”), here it’s too unfocused. The respondent can’t know whether the interviewer is asking for a definition (“What do you mean by power?”) or for an elaboration of the idea of power. A better question might

要探究权力为何具有吸引力并非易事，但或许受访者可以描述与权力相关的意象。一般来说，很难引导受访者深入探讨认知和情感上的复杂情结。当被要求详细阐述时，受访者倾向于用新的词语来描述这种情结，而不是提供其意象和情感基础。虽然如果受访者已经处于某种情境中（例如，如果这位受访者说“我当时的老板表现出他喜欢我”），“你的意思是？”这个问题可能不错，但在这里却显得过于笼统。受访者无法判断面试官是在询问权力的定义（“你说的权力是什么意思？”），还是在询问对权力概念的阐述。或许可以提出一个更好的问题。

have been “How did they show their power?”

一直以来的问题都是“他们是如何展现自己的力量的？”

R: They had the power to choose whether a person could live or die. They had the power to snap their fingers and people would do what they say.

R：他们有权决定一个人的生死。他们只需打个响指，人们就会听从他们的命令。

The respondent does provide some development of his idea of the crime bosses’ power. He conceives of the crime bosses as having not only a Godlike power of life and death but also a royal power of command. It would be important to move to concrete material now. One possibility would be to ask the respondent when he first became aware of the crime bosses’ power or first saw it displayed. The respondent’s stories would then show what images were indexed by his words. But also the interviewer should note that the response is a bit testy. Attention to the interviewing partnership might be in order.

受访者确实对犯罪头目的权力进行了一些阐述。他认为犯罪头目不仅拥有如同神明般的生杀大权，还拥有至高无上的指挥权。现在需要转向具体细节。一种方法是询问受访者何时首次意识到犯罪头目的权力，或者何时首次目睹其权力的展现。受访者的叙述将揭示他话语中暗示的意象。但访谈者也应注意到，受访者的回答略显急躁。因此，访谈者或许应该关注一下访谈伙伴之间的关系。

I: Like how? What do you have in mind?

我：比如怎样？你有什么想法？

This question, at this point, makes me think the interviewer was out of sync with the respondent. The respondent has just tried to answer “How do you mean?” by specifying the display of power he had in mind. Now the interviewer is again asking a kind of “How do you mean?” question.

此时此刻，这个问题让我觉得面试官和受访者的思路有些脱节。受访者刚刚试图通过具体说明他所理解的权力展现方式来回答“你的意思是？”这个问题。而现在，面试官又在问一个类似的“你的意思是？”的问题。

R: Come on, man. You know as much as I do. They don’t like somebody, they get one of their people in, they say go hit him in the head. Pretty soon he’s not around anymore. That’s all there is to it. They had that kind of power.

R：拜托，老兄。你跟我一样清楚。他们不喜欢谁，就派个人进去，命令他去揍他一顿。很快他就没戏了。就这么简单。他们就是有这种本事。

This is a rejection of “What do you have in mind?” Manifestly, the respondent rejects the interviewer’s pose of naïveté. But there is also in the respondent’s asperity an objection to a sense of artificiality in the interview, to

这是对“你有什么想法？”这个问题的拒绝。显然，受访者拒绝接受采访者装出的天真姿态。但受访者的尖刻态度中也包含着对采访中人为痕迹的反感。

the absence of genuine partnership. The level of the respondent’s asperity seems mild to me. Nevertheless, the respondent is questioning the assumptions of the interviewing partnership: “Come on, man. You know as much as I do.” The respondent goes on to provide an answer, but he has put the interviewer on notice that he is aware that the interviewer is playing a role and that he is made uncomfortable by it. And he refuses, at least for the moment, to provide anything more than a sketchy, if vivid, indication of what he has in mind.

缺乏真正的伙伴关系。在我看来，受访者的语气似乎并不激烈。然而，受访者质疑了访谈伙伴关系的假设：“拜托，老兄。你懂的跟我一样多。” 受访者继续回答，但他已经让访谈者意识到，他明白访谈者是在扮演某种角色，这让他感到不舒服。至少目前，他拒绝透露更多信息，只是粗略地、却生动地表达了他的想法。

There’s nothing irreparable here as yet. But note how the student interviewer’s failure to pick up markers, insistence on a particular line of thought, and, finally, unfocused response to the respondent’s reference to crime-boss power led the respondent to challenge the research partnership. The partnership may have been fragile to begin with—and certainly the student was courageous to undertake a tape-recorded interview with a 17-year-old who had recently been convicted of theft—but closer attention to the respondent’s thought and imagery and more concern for maintaining the interviewing partnership would almost surely have produced a better interview.

目前来看，这件事还没有什么不可挽回的。但请注意，这位学生访谈员未能注意到受访者的提示，坚持己见，最终对受访者提及的犯罪头目权力反应迟钝，导致受访者对研究合作关系提出质疑。这种合作关系或许一开始就比较脆弱——当然，这位学生敢于对一位近期因盗窃罪被定罪的17岁少年进行录音访谈，确实勇气可嘉——但如果他能更关注受访者的想法和意象，并更加重视维护访谈合作关系，几乎肯定能获得更好的访谈效果。

What is essential in interviewing is to maintain a working research partnership. You can get away with phrasing questions awkwardly and with a variety of other errors that will make you wince when you listen to the tape later. What you can’t get away with is failure to work with the respondent as a partner in the production of useful material.

访谈中最重要的是保持良好的研究伙伴关系。你可以容忍提问方式不当或其他一些错误，这些错误在之后回听录音时会让你感到尴尬。但你绝对不能容忍的是，在获取有效资料的过程中，未能与受访者建立伙伴关系。

# ↩

CHAPTER 5
ISSUES IN INTERVIEWING

第五章 面试中的问题

THE EFFECTS OF INTERVIEWING ON RESPONDENT AND INTERVIEWER

访谈对受访者和访谈者的影响

Qualitative interviews regularly bring the ordinarily private into view. What are the effects on the respondent and on the interviewer of the respondent’s sharing with the interviewer aspects of the respondent’s private life?

定性访谈经常会将原本属于隐私的话题带到公众视野。受访者向访谈者分享其私生活方面的信息，会对受访者和访谈者产生哪些影响？

WHAT IS IT LIKE TO BE A RESPONDENT?

作为受访者是一种怎样的体验？

Here is what two respondents, each a participant in the pilot study of people who are HIV positive, said about being interviewed. Both respondents were male and HIV positive; neither respondent had gone beyond high school.

以下是两位受访者（均为艾滋病毒感染者试点研究的参与者）对接受采访的描述。这两位受访者均为男性，且均为艾滋病毒感染者；两人均未接受过高中以上的教育。

I NTERVIEWER : What was it like to be interviewed?

采访者：接受采访的感觉如何？

R ESPONDENT : It was good to talk to somebody, finally. That’s one thing I haven’t done, is talk to many people about it. I’m getting something out of it.

受访者：终于能和人聊聊了，感觉真好。我之前很少跟人谈这件事。这次谈话让我受益匪浅。

I: How do you mean?

我：你这话是什么意思？

R: Well, see, there’s nobody that I can talk to in my life. There’s nobody whatsoever. I just don’t have nobody to talk to like that. I mean, even 121 though our conversations—it’s like you’re like listening. I mean, you ask questions, but you’re more listening. And that’s all sometimes I need. See, there’s nobody else that listens. I mean, you’re not saying one thing or another, you’re just listening. And that’s to me, that’s what I need sometimes. It’s probably what I needed for a long, long time. Or I wouldn’t be able to come in here so easily and just tell you about everything.

R：嗯，你看，我这辈子都没人能跟我倾诉。真的，一个都没有。我就是找不到人像那样跟我说话。我的意思是，即使是一对一的谈话——你就像是在倾听。我的意思是，你会问问题，但你更多的是在倾听。有时候，我需要的就只是这样。你看，没有其他人会这样倾听。我的意思是，你什么也不说，你只是在听。对我来说，这就是我有时候需要的。也许我很久很久以来都需要这种倾听。否则，我不可能这么轻松地来到这里，跟你倾诉一切。

One interpretation of this statement is that being interviewed interrupted the respondent’s oppressive isolation. It provided him with the opportunity to talk about urgent concerns to someone who listened closely and sympathetically. That the listener did nothing more—made no interpretations, offered no advice—did not matter. It was the talking and being listened to that counted.

对这句话的一种解读是，接受采访打破了受访者令人窒息的孤立状态。它让他有机会向一位认真倾听并表示同情的人倾诉迫切的担忧。倾听者没有做任何其他事情——没有做出任何解读，也没有提供任何建议——这并不重要。重要的是倾诉和被倾听本身。

To talk to someone who listens, and listens closely, can be valuable because one’s experience, through the process of being voiced and shared, is validated. Furthermore, it is useful to be able to formulate one’s experience and so to make sense of it.

与一位认真倾听的人交谈很有价值，因为通过表达和分享，个人的经历会得到认可。此外，能够梳理自己的经历并理解其意义也十分有益。

The second respondent offered only a brief response to the question about what it had been like to be a respondent. But in that brief response he made evident the cathartic value of talking:

第二位受访者对作为受访者的感受这个问题只作了简短的回答。但在这简短的回答中，他清楚地表明了倾诉的宣泄价值：

I: What has it been like, talking?

我：谈话感觉如何？

R: I haven’t had no problem with it. Some days I got something on my mind maybe, and … well, it drains some of the pressure out of me.

R：我倒没觉得有什么问题。有时候我可能心事重重，然后……嗯，这能帮我释放一些压力。

I have several times been a respondent in a qualitative interview. When the interview went well, I found afterward that in the areas covered in the interview I made more sense to myself. It’s not that I had been puzzled by myself before, but I hadn’t given systematic attention to the issues I discussed in the interview. Furthermore, I was pleased to have had someone’s uninterrupted attention for a while. I liked having a sympathetic listener. I found it confirming to have what I said treated as legitimate and valuable. I liked feeling that my accounts were useful. When the interview ended I was reminded of how rarely in my life I can talk about my experiences in something other than a condensed, allusive, or generalized fashion. Spinning out a detailed, coherent story just isn’t done in conversations with friends and intimates, nor is it likely that an attempt to do so would be uninterrupted.

我曾多次参与定性访谈。每次访谈进行得很顺利，事后我都会发现，在访谈涉及的领域，我对自己的理解更加透彻了。并非我之前对自己感到困惑，而是我没有系统地思考过访谈中提到的那些问题。此外，我很高兴能得到他人一段时间的专注倾听。我喜欢有位善解人意的倾听者。我的发言被认可、被重视，这让我感到很欣慰。我喜欢这种感觉，觉得自己的叙述是有用的。访谈结束后，我意识到，在生活中，我很少有机会能完整地讲述自己的经历，除非是简略、含糊或概括性的描述。在与朋友和亲密之人的对话中，我很难完整地讲述一个详尽连贯的故事，即使尝试这样做，也很难不被打断。

Although my situation is far less pressured, far less distressing, than the situation of someone who is HIV positive, the value of being interviewed seemed the same for me as for the two HIV-positive men. I believe the value of being interviewed is much the same for most respondents.

虽然我的处境远没有艾滋病毒感染者那么艰难，压力也小得多，但对我而言，接受采访的价值似乎与那两位艾滋病毒感染者并无二致。我相信，对大多数受访者来说，接受采访的价值也大致相同。

In large measure, interviewing provides respondents with an opportunity to talk about matters of emotional importance while remaining at an emotional middle distance: close enough to the emotions to experience them but distant enough to maintain self-control. 1 The alliance with the interviewer, which is an aspect of the research partnership, can provide helpful support as a respondent explores matters that had been confusing, distressing, or painful. The respondent’s task—to describe in a coherent fashion what happened—requires the respondent to maintain control over the memories and feelings even as he or she experiences them anew. The result is likely to be that the respondent becomes somewhat more comfortable with matters the respondent had previously felt troubled by. 2

在很大程度上，访谈为受访者提供了一个机会，让他们能够谈论具有重要情感意义的事情，同时保持一定的情感距离：既足够接近这些情绪以便体验它们，又足够远以保持自我控制。与访谈者的联盟是研究伙伴关系的一个方面，它能够为受访者探索那些曾经令他们困惑、痛苦或难过的事情提供有益的支持。受访者的任务——以连贯的方式描述所发生的事情——要求受访者即使在重新体验这些记忆和感受时，也要保持对它们的控制。其结果很可能是，受访者能够对之前令他们感到困扰的事情感到更加自在。

The risks to respondents in qualitative interviewing are not usually significant. One risk is a consequence of the time-limited nature of the interviewing relationship. When there is a series of interviews and the respondent is socially isolated (as a single parent might be), the respondent may feel let down when the interviewing ends. But terminating a series of interviews probably doesn’t leave the lonely respondent worse off than before the interviewing began, and precautions can be taken against the respondent’s experiencing too severe a sense of loss. The respondent can be told in advance how many meetings are planned, and the last meeting can include a summing up to help the respondent achieve closure on the experience. And it may be possible to send the respondent a copy of a project publication.

定性访谈中受访者面临的风险通常并不显著。其中一个风险源于访谈关系的时效性。当访谈分为多个阶段，而受访者又处于社会孤立状态（例如单亲父母）时，访谈结束后，受访者可能会感到失落。但结束一系列访谈可能不会让孤独的受访者比访谈开始前境况更糟，而且可以采取一些预防措施，避免受访者产生过深的失落感。例如，可以提前告知受访者计划的访谈次数，并在最后一次访谈中进行总结，帮助受访者为整个访谈经历画上句号。此外，还可以考虑向受访者发送一份项目出版物。

Institutional review boards set up for the protection of human subjects sometimes worry about an interviewer shaking up a respondent’s defenses and weakening his or her integration. They imagine a respondent reacting like Captain Queeg during his cross-examination, becoming all nervous tic and jittery incoherence. I suppose this is theoretically possible, but I have never known it to happen. It seems to me unlikely to happen if only because virtually all respondents will have successfully defended their character organization against severe onslaughts—such as those launched by an angry spouse—and will have little trouble dealing with the much lesser threat an interview may pose.

为保护受试者而设立的机构审查委员会有时会担心访谈者会动摇受访者的防御机制，削弱其人格完整性。他们设想受访者会像奎格船长在接受交叉询问时那样，变得神经质、语无伦次、紧张不安。我承认理论上存在这种可能性，但我从未见过这种情况发生。在我看来，这种情况发生的可能性很小，原因很简单：几乎所有受访者都曾成功地抵御过来自愤怒配偶的猛烈攻击，维护了自身的人格结构，因此他们应对访谈这种程度较轻的威胁应该不成问题。

It is possible that interviewing may cause someone to reflect on his or her life and, in consequence, make changes. A respondent in a study of single parents, after interviews in which she described her rather barren life, decided she had become entirely too reliant on her mother. Soon thereafter, despite her mother’s opposition, she embarked on a relationship with a married man. She and her mother became estranged. For a couple of months the relationship with the man was sustaining, but then the man returned to his wife and the woman became depressed. The woman thought being interviewed had contributed to her shift in life organization, but she said that she thought she would have rebelled against her mother sooner or later anyway.

访谈可能会促使人们反思自己的人生，并因此做出改变。在一项针对单亲父母的研究中，一位受访者在访谈中描述了自己略显单薄的生活后，意识到自己对母亲的依赖已经到了极致。不久之后，尽管母亲反对，她还是与一位已婚男子开始了交往。她和母亲的关系也因此疏远。与这位男子的交往最初几个月让她感到慰藉，但后来男子回到了妻子身边，这位女士陷入了抑郁。她认为访谈促使她改变了生活方式，但她也表示，即便没有访谈，她迟早也会反抗母亲。

On a very few occasions in my experience a respondent indicated that he or she regretted having talked too freely in the interview. Once, in an interview marked by close rapport, a woman employed in the design world talked freely about the sexual lives of her associates. She later called my office to ask that the sections of the tape containing those comments be erased. I erased the sections. In another instance a respondent withdrew from a study and demanded that his tapes be sent to him because his wife was outraged by his candor about their marriage. I sent the tapes and did not use his material in the study. In each of these cases the interview obviously had created transient discomfort.

在我以往的经验中，受访者表示后悔在访谈中过于畅所欲言的情况极为罕见。有一次，在一次气氛融洽的访谈中，一位从事设计行业的女士畅谈了她同事的性生活。之后她打电话到我的办公室，要求删除录音中包含这些内容的片段。我照做了。还有一次，一位受访者退出了研究，并要求将录音寄给他，因为他的妻子对他在访谈中坦诚谈论他们的婚姻感到非常愤怒。我寄出了录音，并且没有在研究中使用他的素材。在这两起案例中，访谈显然都给受访者带来了短暂的不适感。

My associates and I have found that respondents may be concerned that they will be identifiable in our publications. One man, head of a family business, was worried that we would describe him so precisely that he would lose anonymity. We reassured him that we wouldn’t, and we didn’t; in our report, for one thing, we omitted that his was a family business. Another man gave us an account of his marriage that contained potentially embarrassing material. He asked that if we quoted from his interview we not give any clues to his identity. We did quote from his interview, but gave no information at all about his age or occupation.

我和我的同事发现，受访者可能会担心在我们的出版物中暴露他们的身份。一位家族企业负责人担心我们会对他进行过于详细的描述，从而失去匿名性。我们向他保证不会，而且我们也确实没有这样做；例如，在我们的报告中，我们省略了他经营家族企业的信息。另一位男士向我们讲述了他的婚姻经历，其中包含一些可能令他尴尬的内容。他要求，如果我们引用他的采访内容，请不要透露任何关于他身份的线索。我们确实引用了他的采访内容，但完全没有提供关于他的年龄或职业的任何信息。

In most studies I’ve done, a few respondents have been dealing with a current upset, such as a recent marital separation or a recent diagnosis of serious illness, and the interviewing uncovers their distress. It isn’t possible at that point to remain the unobtrusive research interviewer. Rather, you have to acknowledge the respondent’s distress and, for a time, simply sit and listen and permit the person to feel whatever he or she feels. Such occasions impose on an interviewer a responsibility for providing a supportive presence, a role the interviewer may not have expected. But, as Saint-Exupéry’s Little Prince pointed out, such are the risks of entering someone else’s life.

在我做过的大多数研究中，总会有一些受访者正经历着一些困扰，例如最近分居或被诊断出患有重病，而访谈过程会揭示出他们的痛苦。此时，你不可能再像以前那样保持不加干预的访谈员身份。相反，你必须正视受访者的痛苦，并暂时静静地倾听，允许他们表达自己的感受。这种情况赋予了访谈员提供支持性陪伴的责任，而这或许是访谈员始料未及的。但是，正如圣埃克苏佩里的《小王子》中所指出的那样，这就是介入他人生活所要承担的风险。

Does an interviewer have the right to ask a respondent about potentially painful material? If that is what the study is about, then the answer is “of course.” The respondent should have agreed in advance to the topic of the interview, and the interviewer always is responsible for being considerate in questioning and listening. If the study has another focus but the respondent has provided a marker—“Let’s see, I accepted early retirement a couple of months after my divorce”—the interviewer is being invited to ask about the matter—“Your divorce?”—and probably should. If the matter is relevant to the study but the interviewer is uncertain whether the respondent wants to discuss it, the interviewer could first ask, “Is this something you would feel all right talking about?” 3

访谈者是否有权询问受访者可能涉及的敏感话题？如果研究本身就是关于这个话题的，那么答案当然是“当然”。受访者应该事先同意访谈主题，而访谈者始终有责任在提问和倾听时保持体贴。如果研究的重点另有其他，但受访者已经提供了相关信息——例如，“嗯，我离婚几个月后就接受了提前退休”——那么访谈者就被引导去询问此事——“你的离婚经历？”——而且很可能应该这样做。如果该话题与研究相关，但访谈者不确定受访者是否愿意讨论，那么访谈者可以先问：“您觉得谈论这件事可以吗？”

WHAT IS IT LIKE TO SIT AND LISTEN?

静静地坐着聆听是一种怎样的体验？

There isn’t any one reaction I have to listening to respondents. Sometimes I leave an interview exhilarated; at other times an interview is only an interview, an afternoon’s task. To be sure, even in the latter case I am likely to feel privileged to have been admitted into someone else’s private experience.

我对受访者的回答并没有固定的反应。有时，访谈结束后我会感到振奋；有时，访谈仅仅是一次访谈，一个下午的工作而已。当然，即便在后一种情况下，我仍然会感到荣幸，能够有机会了解他人的私人经历。

Occasionally, an interview is engaging enough for me not only to feel in tune with the other person’s rhythm of speaking and thought but to see the world through the other person’s eyes. At such times I feel myself to be split, with one part functioning professionally, asking questions and monitoring responses, while another part is identified with the respondent. Identification can become so strong that I feel my contact with my own core self has been loosened. I remain aware, of course, that I am with the respondent as an interviewer, but the world in which I live is replaced, temporarily, by the respondent’s.

有时，访谈会让我完全沉浸其中，不仅能感受到对方说话和思考的节奏，还能透过对方的视角看待世界。此时，我感觉自己仿佛分裂了，一部分人以专业人士的身份提问、观察对方的回答，另一部分人则与受访者融为一体。这种融合有时会变得如此强烈，以至于我感觉与自身核心的联系都变得松动了。当然，我始终意识到自己是以访谈者的身份与受访者在一起，但我原本的世界暂时被受访者的世界所取代。

After the ending of any interview that has been engaging, I am likely to be a bit disoriented, the way someone might be on emerging from a movie. On the drive back to the office I may take a wrong turn and go in a direction I hadn’t intended. But instead of being impatient and frustrated I am likely to feel as though I need the extra time to return from the respondent’s world to my own.

每次精彩的访谈结束后，我都会有些恍惚，就像刚看完电影一样。开车回办公室的路上，我可能会走错路，去到意料之外的方向。但我不会感到不耐烦或沮丧，反而会觉得需要一些时间，才能从受访者的世界回到自己的世界。

At some point in every study in which I have done interviewing, I have found a respondent’s account so evocative of developments in my own life or of my own concerns that I am flooded with thoughts or feelings. I then try as best I can to allow my thoughts and feelings to enter my awareness, while continuing to attend to the respondent, as a way of better understanding him or her. Later I try to summon the thoughts and feelings so that I can better assimilate them, or at least become accustomed to them.

在我参与的每一项访谈研究中，总会有那么一些时刻，受访者的叙述与我自身的生活经历或担忧产生了强烈的共鸣，令我思绪万千，难以自拔。这时，我会尽力让自己的思绪和感受进入意识层面，同时继续关注受访者，以此更好地理解他/她。之后，我会尝试梳理这些思绪和感受，以便更好地消化吸收，或者至少逐渐适应它们。

My aim is to enable myself to emotionally understand someone’s account without allowing my attention to be captured by my own feelings and thoughts. When we interview on an issue that is painful for respondents and when their accounts are likely to elicit sympathetic pain in us, it is almost necessary that we achieve this kind of neutralization. In a study of bereavement, for example, the interviewer should try to get to the point where he or she can hear about—and witness—the pain that follows a husband’s death, or a wife’s, or a child’s, and understand it and respond to it while neither becoming a distanced spectator nor being flooded by personal experiences, associations, and feelings. This sort of neutralization is not callousness; rather, it is a state in which the interviewer can understand emotionally while still attending to the respondent and the interview.

我的目标是让自己能够在情感上理解他人的叙述，同时又不让自身的情感和想法左右我的注意力。当我们访谈的对象是令受访者感到痛苦的话题，而他们的叙述很可能引发我们内心的共鸣时，我们几乎必须做到这种情感中立。例如，在丧亲研究中，访谈者应该努力做到能够倾听并见证丈夫、妻子或孩子去世后所承受的痛苦，理解并回应这种痛苦，同时既不成为一个疏离的旁观者，也不被个人的经历、联想和感受所淹没。这种情感中立并非冷漠无情；相反，它是一种访谈者能够在情感上理解受访者的同时，仍然关注受访者和访谈本身的状态。

Interviewing is, for me, usually tiring. I find that it takes energy to maintain an unswerving attention. It requires energy to get into sync with the respondent’s way of thinking while remaining alert to what isn’t being said. It requires energy for me to monitor my own reactions, to judge whether the material is vivid enough, to keep in mind the issues about which I hope to learn, to maintain a sense of how I am doing with time, and to remember to check the tape recorder’s view meter to be sure the recorder is working. I can’t do too many interviews in a day. Three strikes me as a lot; two would be better.

对我来说，采访通常很累人。我发现要保持全神贯注需要耗费大量精力。要跟上受访者的思路，同时还要留意他们言外之意，这同样需要精力。我还要时刻注意自己的反应，判断素材是否足够生动，牢记想要了解的问题，把握好时间，还要记得查看录音机的播放进度条，确保录音机正常工作。我一天不能进行太多采访。三个就太多了，两个比较合适。

Some interviews leave me feeling washed out. Some leave me feeling perplexed, wondering if I managed them properly. I may be uncertain about the way the interview developed or feel bad about walking away from someone whose life is difficult. Whenever any of this happens, I want to talk to someone; when I have a partner on the project, I try to talk with that person about what happened. If there’s no one to talk to, I can manage, but it’s better to have someone to talk to.

有些访谈让我感觉精疲力竭。有些则让我感到困惑，怀疑自己是否处理得当。我可能不确定访谈的进展情况，或者因为不得不离开那些生活艰难的人而感到内疚。每当出现这种情况，我都想找人倾诉；如果项目有合作伙伴，我会尽量和他/她沟通。如果没有人可以倾诉，我也能应付，但最好还是有人可以交流。

I am always gratified if an interview has gone well. The interview will then have been a good experience in itself, and in addition I know that I have usable material on the tape. Sometimes, after an interview has gone well, I find myself believing that I am good at what I do and, in consequence, am pleased with myself. By the same token, after a bad interview I feel awful.

如果面试进行得很顺利，我总是会感到欣慰。面试本身就是一次很好的经历，而且我知道录音带里会有可用的素材。有时候，面试成功后，我会觉得自己很擅长这份工作，因此会感到很自豪。同样，面试失败后，我会感觉很糟糕。

I have had my share of bad interviews. I think especially of interviews where I have been clumsy, a respondent has been ungiving, and my clumsiness and the respondent’s obduracy each exacerbated the other. In an interview that is going badly I fumble for questions, try to remind myself of the interview’s objectives, phrase badly the questions I come up with, and begin to feel acutely uncomfortable. I leave such an interview frustrated and self-doubting, sure that the interview produced little of value. I am likely to wonder whether I have not stumbled into the wrong line of work.

我经历过不少糟糕的面试。我尤其记得那些面试，当时我笨手笨脚，面试官又很固执，而我的笨拙和对方的固执互相加剧了彼此的糟糕表现。在糟糕的面试中，我会手忙脚乱地想问题，努力回忆面试的目标，却总是措辞生硬，开始感到非常不自在。这样的面试结束后，我会感到沮丧和自我怀疑，确信这次面试毫无价值。我甚至会怀疑自己是不是选错了职业。

But even with the occasional failure, there is much I gain from the experience of interviewing. I can find myself so absorbed by the issues of the interview that I suspend awareness of myself. I am in that state that Csikszentmihalyi calls “flow”: I am totally in the interview, aware of it and nothing more. 4 Or an interview can suddenly become so rich in material the study needs that it is as if I have struck the mother lode. (It is at such moments that I feel compelled to check that the tape recorder is working.) In a sizable proportion of the interviews I’ve done I have felt that I was being given personal instruction in some sector of living, for example, how to be a parent or how to function despite adversity. At such times I have felt doubly privileged: privileged to be permitted into the respondent’s life and privileged again for the opportunity to learn.

即使偶尔会失败，我仍然能从访谈中获益良多。我有时会完全沉浸在访谈内容中，以至于忘记了自己。我进入了齐克森米哈里所说的“心流”状态：我完全投入到访谈中，只意识到访谈的存在，除此之外别无其他。或者，访谈内容会突然变得如此丰富，仿佛挖掘到了金矿。（正是在这种时刻，我才会不由自主地检查录音机是否正常工作。）在我做过的相当一部分访谈中，我感觉自己仿佛在接受关于生活某些方面的个人指导，例如如何为人父母，或者如何在逆境中生存。在这样的时刻，我感到双重的荣幸：荣幸能够进入受访者的生活，以及荣幸能够从中学习。

INTERVIEWER RESPONSIBILITIES

面试官职责

While interviews are extremely unlikely to introduce pain or trouble in respondents’ lives, they may well elicit in respondents an awareness of pain they had pushed out of their consciousness. A woman who worked for me as an interviewer was disturbed when her respondent, also a woman, suddenly began crying because she was reminded by the interview of how disappointing her life had been. But neither the interview nor the interviewer was responsible for the respondent’s sadness and tears, Nor should the interviewer’s relationship to the respondent have been changed by their display. It should have continued to be a partnership based on mutual respect, concerned with producing information useful to research.

虽然访谈极不可能给受访者的生活带来痛苦或困扰，但它很可能会唤起受访者内心深处那些他们一直刻意压抑的痛苦。我的一位女访谈员就曾感到不安，因为她的一位受访者（也是一位女性）在访谈中突然哭泣起来，因为访谈让她想起了自己生活中那些令人失望的经历。然而，受访者的悲伤和泪水并非访谈本身或访谈员的责任，访谈员与受访者之间的关系也不应该因此而改变。这种关系应该继续保持，建立在相互尊重的基础上，共同致力于获取对研究有用的信息。

Often, when a respondent is flooded by emotion, the interviewer’s respect for the respondent is best expressed by just sitting quietly. When the respondent gives evidence of being back in touch, the interviewer might ask, “Is it all right to go on?” or might say something that indicates understanding, such as “It must have been hard going for you, these past weeks” or “It sounds like anniversaries are hard.” The interviewer should offer such comments as a professional who is working with the respondent. It would be wrong for the interviewer to step out of role and say, as might a solicitous friend, “You just have to think of the future.” Not only is this statement out of keeping with the interviewer’s role, but it also suggests a reluctance to listen. And with a truly serious hurt or loss, an attempt at good advice can be felt as a minimization of how dreadful was the respondent’s experience.

通常，当受访者情绪激动时，面试官表达尊重最好的方式就是保持安静。当受访者表示已经恢复联系后，面试官可以问：“可以继续吗？”或者说一些表示理解的话，例如“过去几周您一定很难熬”或“周年纪念日听起来很艰难”。面试官应该以专业人士的身份，以与受访者合作的视角来表达这些感受。如果面试官脱离角色，像一位关心受访者的朋友那样说“你只需要考虑未来”，那就不合适了。这种说法不仅不符合面试官的身份，也暗示着不愿倾听。对于真正遭受重创或失去亲人的人来说，任何试图提供建议的行为都可能被他们视为轻视其痛苦经历。

It would also be wrong for the interviewer to try to comfort by saying “I know how hard it can be” or, worse, “I’m sure it will be better in time.” The interviewer has been granted no right to attempt to modify the respondent’s feelings. Nor should the interviewer become evaluative, not even approvingly evaluative, as by saying “It’s brave of you to keep going” or “I admire your ability to keep going.” The interviewer is a work partner, not a therapist, not a friend, not an appraising audience. It is appropriate for the interviewer to indicate, by his or her manner, “Yes, I understand the seriousness and painfulness of what you are reporting.” The interviewer might be able to say, with sympathy, “That’s too bad.” Beyond this the interviewer does best to convey a middle distance in response to the respondent’s feelings, in touch with them and responsive to them, but not overwhelmed by them.

面试官试图安慰受访者，比如说道“我知道这有多难”，或者更糟糕的是说“我相信时间会治愈一切”，都是不恰当的。面试官无权试图改变受访者的感受。面试官也不应该进行评价，哪怕是赞许式的评价，例如说“你坚持下来真勇敢”或“我很佩服你坚持下去的能力”。面试官是工作伙伴，不是心理咨询师，不是朋友，也不是评判者。面试官恰当的做法是通过自己的态度表明：“是的，我理解您所讲述事情的严重性和痛苦。”面试官可以带着同情说：“那太糟糕了。”除此之外，面试官最好对受访者的感受保持一种适度的距离，既要理解他们的感受，也要对他们的感受做出回应，但不要被他们的感受所左右。

There is no reason for an interviewer to feel guilty about intruding on a respondent’s grief or sorrow. It’s not the talking that hurts. Yes, sometimes people who are grieving want to distract their minds so that they can gain respite from their distress. But if they are aware of the interview’s topic, they are likely to be prepared to talk about the loss. Still, the interviewer should bear in mind that sensitivity, tact, and respect for the respondent, always important, are essential with a respondent who displays pain.

采访者无需为打扰受访者的悲伤或痛苦而感到内疚。真正伤人的并非谈话本身。的确，有时悲伤的人会想要转移注意力，以求从痛苦中解脱。但如果他们事先了解访谈主题，他们很可能愿意谈论失去亲人的感受。尽管如此，采访者仍应谨记，对于正在经历痛苦的受访者，保持敏感、得体和尊重至关重要。

Once, while interviewing a respondent, a lawyer who had retired from a distinguished career, I was asking about his current activities when he said, in passing, that he was dealing with some unexpected personal problems. This was, of course, a marker, and I picked it up. He then said that 5 or 6 weeks earlier his wife had left him. Then he stopped and sighed. After a moment’s silence I asked how it had happened. The man then talked about his wife’s long-unexpressed anger at having been his taken-for-granted spouse and how his traveling to collect an honor had been for her, unbeknownst to him, a last straw. The information was valuable for the study. It demonstrated how isolating was the double loss of work and spouse, even for a widely respected man. Talking about the loss was also, I think, helpful to the respondent.

有一次，我在采访一位退休律师时，询问他目前的近况。他曾是一位杰出的律师，退休前事业有成。他无意间提到自己正面临一些意想不到的个人问题。这当然是一个信号，我立刻察觉到了。接着，他说五六周前妻子离开了他。说着说着，他停顿了一下，叹了口气。沉默片刻后，我问他事情的经过。他这才谈起妻子长期以来对他视而不见的愤怒，以及他出差领奖这件事，在他不知情的情况下，成了压垮她的最后一根稻草。这些信息对研究很有价值。它表明，即使对于一位备受尊敬的人来说，失去工作和伴侣的双重打击也会让人感到多么孤立无援。我认为，谈论这段经历对受访者本身也很有帮助。

Of course, we should not be so single-minded in pursuit of data that we encourage respondents to decompensate, to shift their defenses so that they become less capable of effective functioning. Indeed, we; ought to call a halt to interviewing if it ever appears that a respondent is decompensating. I suppose an instance of this might be a respondent telephoning us, the day after the first of an intended series of interviews or bereavement, to say that as a result of the interview he had been unable to sleep and intended to stay home from work. But I have never known this to happen, and I have interviewed people who were pretty fragile.

当然，我们不应一味追求数据，以至于鼓励受访者情绪失控，改变防御机制，从而降低其有效工作的能力。事实上，如果发现受访者情绪失控，我们应该立即停止访谈。例如，受访者在计划进行的一系列访谈的第二天，或者在经历丧亲之痛后，可能会打电话告诉我们，由于访谈，他彻夜难眠，打算请假在家休息。但我从未遇到过这种情况，而我访谈过的受访者中不乏一些身体非常脆弱的人。

In a study of case management I interviewed formerly hospitalized mental patients. My respondents were men and women who had been diagnosed as schizophrenic, paranoid, or brain damaged. With only a few exceptions, each had sufficient clarity to tell me how case managers had helped or had failed to help. None suffered anything more than transitory discomfort as a result of participating in the interview.

在一项关于个案管理的研究中，我采访了一些曾住院治疗的精神病患者。受访者包括被诊断患有精神分裂症、妄想症或脑损伤的男性和女性。除少数例外，每位受访者都能清晰地告诉我个案管理人员是如何帮助他们或未能帮助他们的。参与访谈后，所有受访者都只感到短暂的不适，没有其他不适。

This is not to say that the interviewing never unsettled these respondents. A man in his mid-thirties, living in supervised housing, had until a few months earlier lived with his family. But when I introduced the topic of how it had happened that he had moved from his family into supervised housing, the man produced a sound like an air-raid siren, piercingly loud and unvarying in pitch, followed by a staccato burst of words whose sequence made no sense whatsoever. Then he began to sigh deep, rasping sighs. Then, again, the air-raid siren, followed by the words, followed by the sighs. The episode lasted a couple of minutes in all. Then the man was quiet. Then, in a normal voice, he returned to the interview as though nothing had happened. We talked a bit more about his current housing, and I again asked about the family events that had preceded his move into supervised housing. There was a moment’s silence, and then the man went into the sequence of siren noise, word salad, and sighing. At that point I decided to ask no more direct questions about events in his family.

这并非说访谈从未让受访者感到不安。一位三十多岁的男子住在监管住房里，几个月前还和家人住在一起。但当我问及他为何从家人身边搬进监管住房时，他发出了一声如同空袭警报般的刺耳声音，音调始终不变，随后是一连串语无伦次、毫无逻辑的词语。接着，他开始发出深沉而沙哑的叹息。然后，警报声再次响起，接着是说话，接着又是叹息。整个过程持续了几分钟。之后，他安静了下来。然后，他用正常的语气重新开始访谈，仿佛什么都没发生过。我们又聊了一会儿他目前的住所，我再次询问了他搬进监管住房之前发生的家庭变故。一阵沉默之后，那人开始发出类似警笛的声响，语无伦次，还不停地叹气。这时，我决定不再直接询问他家里的情况。

In another interview in that study a woman insisted, whenever the interview made her uncomfortable, that she had given birth to a child from her forehead. I’m sure her delusion had symbolic meanings, but I decided that learning what they were would not contribute to an evaluation of case management. Instead, when the woman began describing her baby’s emergence from her forehead, I would try, gently, to return her to her experience with her case manager.

在那项研究的另一次访谈中，一位女士每当访谈让她感到不舒服时，都会坚持说她从额头上生下了一个孩子。我确信她的这种妄想有其象征意义，但我认为了解这些意义对评估个案管理并无助益。因此，每当这位女士开始描述她的孩子从额头里“诞生”的情景时，我都会尝试温和地引导她回到与个案经理的对话中。

As these two respondents demonstrated, even formerly hospitalized mental patients who are still severely troubled have effective ways of guarding their integrity. I feel confident that being interviewed did no harm to either of these two respondents. Nor did it harm a paranoid respondent who refused to believe I was really an interviewer, several other respondents whose region of clarity was limited, nor the quite extraordinary respondent who seemed as sane as anyone but had become adapted to life as a mental patient.

正如这两位受访者所展现的那样，即使是曾经住院治疗、如今仍饱受精神困扰的精神病患者，也有有效的方式来维护自身的尊严。我相信，接受采访并没有对这两位受访者造成任何伤害。同样，对于那位不相信我是采访者的妄想症患者、其他几位思维模糊的受访者，以及那位看似理智却已适应精神病患者生活的非凡受访者来说，采访也没有造成任何伤害。

I have also interviewed troubled adolescents and, again, feel confident that the interviews were not harmful to them. Most welcomed the interview. I do remember one boy who was thoroughly distrusting, but he dealt with whatever threat he believed the interview posed by limiting his responses to the most laconic. I finally said something like “You seem to be sort of uncomfortable, like you’re not sure you like being interviewed.” At this he brightened and said I was right. I congratulated myself on getting through to him and said, “What is it that doesn’t feel comfortable? Like, is it just talking about things, or something else?” The young man hesitated, then his face set, and he said, “I don’t know,” and that was the end of it. He wasn’t benefited by being interviewed, but I don’t think he was hurt either.

我也采访过一些问题少年，同样地，我确信这些采访对他们并无害处。大多数人都欢迎采访。我记得有个男孩非常不信任我，但他用最简短的回答来应对他认为的采访带来的威胁。最后，我开口说：“你好像有点不自在，好像不太喜欢接受采访。”他听了这话，精神一振，说我说得对。我暗自庆幸自己成功说服了他，然后问道：“是什么让你感到不自在呢？是单纯的谈话，还是别的什么原因？”他犹豫了一下，然后脸色凝重，说道：“我不知道。”采访就此结束。他并没有从采访中受益，但我认为他也没有受到伤害。

Janet Malcolm suggests that interviewing is inherently duplicitous. She generalizes from a particular instance in which a writer ingratiated himself with a subject in order to obtain material that he later used to discredit the subject. (To be sure, the subject had already been discredited by a conviction for murder.) Malcolm characterizes all journalists—her argument can be extended to anyone who interviews—as confidence men, skilled at establishing relationships of apparent warmth and trust so they can obtain information that they will later use for their own purposes. The result, she says, is that respondents feel, at the very least, misled. 5

珍妮特·马尔科姆认为，采访本质上就是一种欺骗。她以一个具体案例为例进行概括：一位作家为了获取素材，先是讨好受访者，然后利用这些素材诋毁受访者。（当然，受访者此前已因谋杀罪被定罪，名誉扫地。）马尔科姆将所有记者——她的论点可以推广到任何采访者——都描述为骗子，他们擅长建立表面上的热情和信任关系，从而获取信息，以便日后用于自身目的。她说，其结果是，受访者至少会感到被误导。

This can be true, but I think it need not be and should not be. The relationship established with respondents should be exactly what it purports to be—a research partnership. Beyond this, I think interviewers should ensure that respondents are not hurt because of their cooperation. Unlike physicians, interviewers have no responsibility to benefit the people they talk with, but, like physicians, they do have a responsibility to do no harm.

这或许属实，但我认为并非如此，也不应该如此。与受访者建立的关系应该名副其实——是一种研究伙伴关系。除此之外，我认为访谈员应该确保受访者不会因配合访谈而受到伤害。与医生不同，访谈员没有义务让受访者受益，但与医生一样，他们也有责任避免造成伤害。

Respondents are very unlikely to be harmed simply by participating in a research interview. Indeed, as I have noted, the chances of their being benefited by the interview are much greater than the chances of their being harmed. But they can be hurt by confrontation with a view of themselves that they feel to be injurious or by making available to others potentially discrediting information.

受访者仅仅参与研究访谈不太可能受到伤害。事实上，正如我之前提到的，他们从访谈中获益的可能性远大于受到伤害的可能性。但是，如果他们被迫面对自己认为有害的观点，或者将可能损害自身声誉的信息泄露给他人，则可能会受到伤害。

It is an expression of the interviewer’s responsibility, quite apart from its importance as technique, to be nonjudgmental, even when that goes against the interviewer’s grain. Furthermore, the interviewer has no mandate to help respondents understand themselves. This means, among other things, that the interviewer should refrain from making connections for respondents that the respondents have not made for themselves and from suggesting motivations for the respondents’ behavior that the respondents have not themselves considered.

除了技巧的重要性之外，保持不带评判的态度也是访谈者的责任所在，即便这种态度与访谈者的本性相悖。此外，访谈者没有义务帮助受访者理解自己。这意味着，访谈者不应替受访者建立他们自己没有建立的联系，也不应暗示受访者行为背后的动机是他们自己没有考虑过的。

The interviewer must, of course, respect the commitment to confidentiality. Nothing a respondent says to the interviewer should be leaked to others in the respondent’s world, nor should the respondent’s interview materials be available to anyone outside the study. Nothing reported from the study, in print or in a lecture, should permit identification of respondents.

当然，访谈者必须尊重保密承诺。受访者对访谈者所说的任何内容都不得泄露给受访者圈子里的其他人，受访者的访谈材料也不得提供给研究之外的任何人。研究报告（无论是印刷版还是讲座版）均不得泄露受访者的身份信息。

We have, I think, one further responsibility to our respondents. In any study we have an obligation to our sponsors (government or foundation or university or our own bank account), to our field, and to ourselves to produce the most useful report possible. We have the same obligation to our respondents. We have engaged them in a partnership in which they are expected to do their best to provide the study with observations. It is our responsibility to make their lessons known.

我认为，我们对受访者还有另一项责任。在任何研究中，我们都对资助方（政府、基金会、大学或我们自己的资金）、研究领域以及我们自身负有义务，力求撰写出最有价值的报告。我们对受访者也负有同样的义务。我们与他们建立了合作关系，他们理应尽最大努力为研究提供观察结果。我们有责任将这些观察结果公之于众。

CONFIDENTIALITY DILEMMAS

保密困境

We guarantee respondents confidentiality. Indeed, we put the guarantee into our consent forms. Furthermore, one element of the implicit research partnership we establish with a respondent is a commitment that the respondent will not be damaged because of his or her participation in the interview. Are there any circumstances in which an interviewer could nevertheless be justified in passing on interview information to whoever might be the appropriate authorities—the police, the respondent’s psychiatrist, a state agency for the protection of children? Suppose the respondent confesses behavior that is criminal? Should the respondent be reported to the police? What if the respondent is homicidal? Or suicidal? What if the respondent is harming others? What if the respondent is harming children?

我们保证受访者的隐私。事实上，我们在知情同意书中明确写入了这项保证。此外，我们与受访者建立的隐性研究伙伴关系的一个要素是，我们承诺受访者不会因参与访谈而受到任何损害。那么，在哪些情况下，访谈员可以合理地将访谈信息传递给相关机构——例如警方、受访者的精神科医生或儿童保护机构？如果受访者承认自己有犯罪行为呢？是否应该向警方举报？如果受访者有杀人倾向呢？或者自杀倾向呢？如果受访者正在伤害他人呢？如果受访者正在伤害儿童呢？

I have never interviewed anyone who gave me reason to believe he or she planned a homicide or suicide or was involved in child abuse. If I had, I believe I would have made an effort to contact appropriate authorities. I have interviewed people engaged in criminal behavior, including several who were engaged in illegal drug use, a few who were involved in occasional theft from retail stores, and one man who a year before our interview had committed armed robberies. (The man was a drug user who had been desperate for money.) I did not report any of these respondents to the police and would have resisted efforts to make their interview reports available as evidence against them. I hope I am not vulnerable to charges as an accessory after the fact, but I think in those cases I could responsibly honor my pledge of confidentiality.

我从未采访过任何让我觉得有理由相信其计划谋杀或自杀，或参与虐待儿童的人。如果我采访过这样的人，我相信我会尽力联系相关部门。我采访过一些有犯罪行为的人，包括几名吸毒者、几名偶尔在零售店行窃的人，以及一名在采访前一年犯下持械抢劫罪的男子。（这名男子吸毒，当时急需用钱。）我没有向警方举报这些受访者，并且会抵制任何将他们的采访记录作为不利于他们的证据的做法。我希望自己不会因事后从犯而被起诉，但我认为在那种情况下，我能够负责任地履行我的保密承诺。

More difficult was the problem posed by a woman respondent who was HIV positive. She said that all her life, from the time she was a child, she had been treated brutally by men. Contracting HIV from a boyfriend was only the most recent instance. Now she wanted to get even with the whole male sex. She visited barrooms every evening to pick up men with whom she could have intercourse, in the hope that she would infect them. The woman’s sister had already reported her to a public health agency, mostly because she wanted the woman stopped before she was hurt by some man she had tried to infect. The public health agency did nothing.

更棘手的是一位感染了艾滋病毒的女性受访者提出的问题。她说，从孩提时代起，她就一直遭受男性的虐待。从男友那里感染艾滋病毒只是最近一次。现在，她想报复所有男性。她每天晚上都去酒吧勾搭男人，试图与他们发生性关系，希望把病毒传染给他们。这位女性的姐姐已经向公共卫生机构举报了她，主要是因为她想阻止她，以免她被自己试图传染的男人伤害。但公共卫生机构却什么也没做。

In our final interview I learned the woman was no longer seeking revenge through sex. She had met a man who had become her steady boyfriend and who remained with her even after he was told—by that same sister—that she was HIV positive. (His first reaction was to yell at the woman and, I think, push her around.) If in our final interview the woman had reported continuing her campaign to spread HIV among men, I would have told her to stop. I can’t believe that would have done much good, but I would have told her anyway. I also would have discussed her report with the head of the clinic where she was being treated, with the thought of devising some way to interrupt her behavior.

在最后一次访谈中，我了解到这位女士不再试图通过性来报复。她遇到了一个男人，两人成为了稳定的男友，即使在她姐姐告诉他她感染了艾滋病毒之后，这个男人仍然和她在一起。（他的第一反应是冲着这位女士大吼大叫，而且我认为他还推搡了她。）如果这位女士在最后一次访谈中提到她仍在继续向男性传播艾滋病毒，我会劝她停止这种行为。我不认为这样做会有多大作用，但我还是会劝她。我还会和她就诊诊所的负责人讨论她的报告，希望能找到一些方法来阻止她的行为。

Until the woman herself resolved the issue, the problem of what to do with information that a respondent was trying to spread HIV infection to others was the most difficult dilemma I have faced in a lifetime of interviewing. But there were two other respondents in that pilot study who also raised issues of intervention. One was an HIV-positive woman, an IV drug user and an alcoholic, who blithely reported that she had passed along her hypodermic needle to an acquaintance. The respondent had known what she was doing; she had told the recipient to “wash it out good.” In the interview she offered the rationalization that the acquaintance probably was already infected. I was appalled and indicated concern, but I did not tell her she should never again pass on a needle she had used. Nor did I take this information to the clinic where she was being treated. The second instance was a woman whose husband was HIV positive who was deliberately exposing herself to the risk of contracting the disease. Again I was appalled, and again indicated concern, but did not say she should stop.

在她自己解决这个问题之前，如何处理受访者试图将艾滋病毒传播给他人这一信息，是我一生访谈生涯中最棘手的难题。但那项试点研究中还有另外两位受访者也提出了干预的问题。其中一位是艾滋病毒感染者，她既是静脉注射毒品者又是酗酒者，她轻描淡写地告诉我，她把自己的注射器转给了熟人。这位受访者明知故犯，她告诉对方“好好清洗一下”。在访谈中，她辩解说，那位熟人可能已经被感染了。我感到震惊，并表示担忧，但我没有告诉她以后绝对不能再把用过的针头转给别人。我也没有把这个信息告诉她所在的诊所。第二个例子是一位丈夫是艾滋病毒感染者的女性，她故意让自己暴露在感染风险之中。我同样感到震惊，并再次表示担忧，但我也没有劝她停止这种行为。

These dilemmas develop at the intersection of two governing principles. We have, usually explicitly, bound ourselves to respect the confidentiality of what we are told. We have also, usually implicitly, bound ourselves to respect the integrity of our respondents, including their right to their decisions and behaviors. These commitments are on the side of inaction. On the other side are our responsibilities as citizens to prevent harm by our respondents both to themselves and to others. Generally, we respect our pledges to respondents, but there can be circumstances under which we would not. An interviewer who was convinced by a respondent that the respondent intended to kill someone, and had the gun with which to do it, would be required, under law, to do whatever might be necessary to stop the intended crime, including placing a call to the police.

这些困境源于两项基本原则的交汇。我们通常明确承诺尊重受访者所透露信息的保密性。同时，我们也通常默认承诺尊重受访者的尊严，包括他们自主决定和行为的权利。这些承诺倾向于不作为。另一方面，作为公民，我们有责任防止受访者对自己和他人造成伤害。一般来说，我们会履行对受访者的承诺，但在某些情况下，我们可能不会这样做。例如，如果受访者让访谈员确信其意图杀人，并且持有作案枪支，那么根据法律规定，访谈员有义务采取一切必要措施阻止犯罪行为，包括报警。

It might seem that dilemmas associated with confidentiality could be avoided by noting in the consent form the conditions under which confidentiality will be breached. A statement might be made in the consent form that a serious threat to adult life or to the well-being of children would justify suspension of the investigator’s commitment to confidentially. In fact, some research review boards require such statements.

似乎只要在知情同意书中注明违反保密义务的条件，就能避免与保密相关的困境。例如，可以在知情同意书中声明，如果成年人的生命或儿童的福祉受到严重威胁，研究者可以暂停履行保密义务。事实上，一些研究审查委员会确实要求做出此类声明。

Noting in the consent form that confidentiality may not be absolute can help, but it will not fully resolve the problem. If an interview produces evidence of a threat to the well-being of the respondent or others, the investigator would still be required to assess the threat’s credibility. If the investigator believes the threat to be genuine and yet unlikely to be implemented, should action to forestall it nevertheless be taken, to be on the safe side? Issues of judgment remain, no matter what’s in the consent form: Just how credible is the threat? Is useful action to forestall it possible? What would be the cost to the respondent and to the study of any action undertaken? What are the possible costs of inaction?

在知情同意书中注明保密性可能并非绝对，会有所帮助，但并不能彻底解决问题。如果访谈中发现受访者或其他人的人身安全受到威胁，调查员仍然需要评估该威胁的可信度。如果调查员认为威胁真实存在但不太可能实施，为了安全起见，是否仍应采取措施予以防范？无论知情同意书中如何规定，判断的问题依然存在：威胁的可信度究竟如何？是否有有效的防范措施？对受访者和研究而言，采取任何行动的成本是什么？不采取行动的潜在代价又是什么？

Problems of this sort are, fortunately, rare, but when they arise they are likely to have no easy solution. Nor does there seem to be any general method for their resolution. Rather, as would be true in other situations where the behavior required by one governing moral principle is contrary to the behavior required by another governing moral principle, decision can only be arrived at on a case-by-case basis.

幸运的是，这类问题并不常见，但一旦出现，往往难以轻易解决。似乎也没有什么通用的解决方法。正如其他情况下，当一项道德原则所要求的行为与另一项道德原则所要求的行为相冲突时，也只能根据具体情况逐案处理。

RESEARCH INTERVIEWING AND THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

研究访谈和治疗干预

The techniques of qualitative interviewing may seem uncomfortably close to constituting psychotherapy unsought by the respondent. An interviewer with whom I once worked told me that she had become conscience stricken when one of her respondents said, “I’m talking to you like I would to my therapist.” My colleague worried that, unknowing and unbidden, she had blundered into the realm of therapy.

定性访谈的技巧似乎与受访者未主动寻求的心理治疗过于接近，令人不安。我曾经的一位同事告诉我，当一位受访者说“我跟你说话的方式就像跟我的心理治疗师说话一样”时，她感到非常内疚。我的同事担心，自己不知不觉地、未经允许地踏入了心理治疗的领域。

There are obvious resemblances between the research interview and therapeutic interviewing. The research interviewer resembles a therapist by encouraging the respondent to develop thoughts and memories, by eliciting the respondent’s underlying emotions, and by listening closely to the respondent’s utterances. How different, then, is the respondent from a patient when the respondent provides what would otherwise be private observations, thoughts, and feelings? And how different from therapeutic results are the results of participation in a research interview when respondents leave the research interview more comfortable with themselves? Is qualitative interviewing really therapeutic interviewing motivated by research needs?

研究访谈与治疗性访谈之间存在明显的相似之处。研究访谈者如同治疗师一般，鼓励受访者展开思考和回忆，引导受访者表达其潜在的情感，并认真倾听受访者的陈述。那么，当受访者提供原本属于个人隐私的观察、想法和感受时，他们与患者之间究竟有何区别？当受访者在研究访谈后感到更加自在时，其结果与治疗效果又有何不同？定性访谈真的是一种出于研究需要而进行的治疗性访谈吗？

There are several ways in which qualitative interviewing is different from therapeutic interviewing. First, the aims and practices of research interviewing and of therapeutic interviewing are different. In therapeutic interviewing the functioning of the patient is the object of concern. Whatever the therapist does is, or should be, motivated by the aim of helping the patient. Patients understand that their talking is a means to their improvement. In order to help, therapists may do much more than simply listen closely: they may also provide interpretations of the patient’s behavior, advice on the patient’s choices in life, and explorations of the patient’s thoughts and feelings about the therapeutic relationship. In research interviewing, on the other hand, the interviewer’s questioning is motivated by the aim of eliciting information useful to a study. The respondent is a partner in developing the research information. The interviewer is without license to produce change in the respondent’s functioning and has no right to give interpretations or advice. It would not be proper for a research interviewer to suggest connections between the respondent’s verbalizations when the respondent has not already made them. It was improper, for example, for a student interviewer to follow a young woman’s report of liking young men who were active! in sports with the question “Is your father active in sports?”

定性访谈与治疗性访谈在几个方面有所不同。首先，研究性访谈和治疗性访谈的目的和实践方式不同。在治疗性访谈中，关注的是患者的功能状态。治疗师所做的一切都是为了帮助患者，或者说应该如此。患者明白，他们的倾诉是改善自身状况的一种手段。为了帮助他们，治疗师可能做的远不止是认真倾听：他们还可能对患者的行为进行解读，就患者的生活选择提供建议，并探索患者对治疗关系的想法和感受。另一方面，在研究性访谈中，访谈者的提问是为了获取对研究有用的信息。受访者是研究信息生成的合作伙伴。访谈者无权改变受访者的功能状态，也无权提供解读或建议。研究访谈员在受访者尚未明确表达相关观点的情况下，暗示受访者的言语之间存在联系是不恰当的。例如，一位学生访谈员在一位年轻女性表示喜欢积极参与体育运动的年轻男性后，紧接着问“你父亲积极参与体育运动吗？”就是不恰当的。

Second, the material elicited during research interviewing and therapeutic interviewing is different. Therapists are likely to encourage patients not only to talk about their internal states but also to find sources in earlier life for current images and feelings. And a therapist is likely to want the patient to explore these matters until the patient has dealt with them adequately. The research interviewer is much more likely to want to hear about scenes, situations, and events the respondent has witnessed. The interviewer in a qualitative research study will want respondents to talk about their internal states only if this would be useful for the study. Once the interviewer has obtained the information needed by the study, the area of a respondent’s internal state would not be revisited.

其次，研究访谈和治疗性访谈中获取的信息有所不同。治疗师不仅会鼓励患者谈论他们的内心状态，还会鼓励他们从过往经历中寻找当前意象和感受的根源。治疗师通常会希望患者深入探索这些问题，直到他们能够充分处理为止。而研究访谈者则更倾向于了解受访者亲身经历的场景、情境和事件。在定性研究中，访谈者只有在受访者谈论其内心状态对研究有益时，才会邀请他们参与。一旦访谈者获得了研究所需的信息，就不会再进一步探讨受访者的内心状态。

Third, the interview relationship is different for the researcher and the therapist. Therapists are responsible to patients for helping them improve in functioning. Because the patient looks to the therapist for help, the therapist will almost surely become an authoritative figure in the patient’s life and thoughts. In contrast, the research interviewer is a partner in information development. The interviewing relationship is defined as one of equals, although interviewer and respondent have different responsibilities. And while therapists remain for some time important figures in the lives of patients, interviewers are ordinarily recognized by respondents as transient figures in their lives.

第三，研究者和治疗师的访谈关系截然不同。治疗师对患者负有责任，帮助他们改善功能。由于患者寻求治疗师的帮助，治疗师几乎必然会成为患者生活和思想中的权威人物。相比之下，研究访谈者是信息收集的合作伙伴。访谈关系被定义为平等关系，尽管访谈者和受访者承担着不同的责任。而且，治疗师在患者的生活中会长期扮演重要角色，而受访者通常认为访谈者只是他们生活中的过客。

Finally, the patient pays the therapist for the therapist’s help. The interviewer is paid not by the respondent but by the study. Indeed, the respondent may also be compensated by the study; at the very least, the respondent is likely to be thanked by the interviewer for the interview.

最后，患者会向治疗师支付费用。访谈员的报酬并非来自受访者，而是来自研究机构。事实上，受访者也可能从研究机构获得补偿；至少，访谈员可能会对受访者表示感谢。

IF A RESPONDENT HAS NEED OF CLINICAL SERVICES

如果受访者需要临床服务

What if someone you talk with is so troubled that you feel psychiatric help is desirable? If respondents themselves indicate an interest in clinical services, there is not much of a problem. It is a good idea to have available a list of services, including therapists and social agencies, to be given to people who ask for referrals. But absent such a list, you can always tell respondents that you will check with colleagues and get back to them.

如果你遇到一位情绪非常低落、让你觉得有必要寻求精神科医生帮助的人，该怎么办？如果受访者本身就表示对临床服务感兴趣，那就没什么大问题。最好准备一份服务机构清单，包括治疗师和社会服务机构，以便提供给那些寻求转介的人。但如果没有这样的清单，你也可以告诉受访者，你会咨询同事后再回复他们。

It is when a respondent doesn’t indicate an interest in clinical services but you think they are needed anyway that you may have a problem. Although it is not your place to make diagnoses or judgments regarding who might be benefited by therapy or counseling or other services, if your respondent, on the way to sitting down with you for the interview, were to trip on the rug and be injured, you would of course call for emergency treatment. Similarly, if the respondent gives the kind of evidence of need that any fellow citizen would respond to, you should respond as a fellow citizen. For example, after an interview with a new widower who is baffled by his inability to manage his household, you could mention that homemaker services may be available.

如果受访者并未表示对临床服务感兴趣，但您认为他们仍然需要这些服务，那么您可能就遇到问题了。虽然您无权诊断或判断谁可能受益于治疗、咨询或其他服务，但如果受访者在来与您面谈的路上被地毯绊倒受伤，您当然会立即寻求紧急救治。同样地，如果受访者表现出的需求是任何公民都会关注的，您也应该以公民的身份给予帮助。例如，在面谈一位因无法管理家务而感到困惑的新丧偶男子后，您可以提及或许可以获得家政服务。

But people who do a great deal of research interviewing can go through their careers without meeting more than a handful of situations in which they think it right to make an unrequested referral or offer unsolicited advice. More often they run into situations where the right thing to do isn’t evident. I once interviewed a couple whose marriage was clearly troubled. They both described loud quarrels, frightening to the children and disturbing to themselves. The husband, after he and I completed our interview, asked me what I thought about his family. I said I thought all families, including his, had strengths and vulnerabilities. I waited for him to say more about what he had in mind, but he didn’t. So I left.

但那些从事大量调研访谈的人，在其职业生涯中可能只会遇到寥寥几例需要主动推荐他人或提供建议的情况。更多时候，他们遇到的情况是，如何做才是明智之举并不明显。我曾经采访过一对婚姻明显出现问题的夫妇。他们都描述了激烈的争吵，这不仅吓坏了孩子，也让他们自己感到不安。采访结束后，丈夫问我对他的家庭有何看法。我说我认为所有家庭，包括他的家庭，都有其优势和不足。我等着他进一步阐述他的想法，但他没有。于是，我离开了。

It is not all that unusual for respondents to want to know the interviewer’s reactions to them or to their situation just to be reassured that they are doing well enough. If I can offer that kind of reassurance without being false or patronizing, I will do so. If I can’t, I will retreat into generalities, as I did here. Perhaps in this case nothing more was being asked for. But as I remember the ending of that interview, I suspect that the man did want something more. Maybe he wanted a referral for counseling or at least a judgment on whether he and his wife should have counseling. Maybe I should have found a way to ask if that was what he had in mind. I still wonder what I should have done.

受访者想知道面试官对他们或他们处境的反应，只是为了确认自己一切都好，这并不罕见。如果我能在不虚伪或居高临下的情况下给予这种安慰，我会这样做。如果做不到，我就会像这次一样，泛泛而谈。也许在这种情况下，他并没有提出更多要求。但回想起那次面试的结尾，我怀疑他其实想要更多。也许他想要一份咨询转介，或者至少想知道他和妻子是否应该接受咨询。也许我应该找个机会问问他是否是这个意思。我至今仍在思考我当时应该怎么做。

MATCHING INTERVIEWERS TO RESPONDENTS

将访谈员与受访者进行匹配

A few years ago it was fashionable among reviewers of proposals for the funding of qualitative interview studies to want interviewers matched to intended respondents, at least in race and possibly in sex and social background as well. There were two reasons given for the desirability of such compatibility: acceptance of the interviewer by the respondent and a greater likelihood that the interviewer would be able to understand.

几年前，在审阅定性访谈研究项目资助申请书时，评审专家们普遍希望访谈员与受访者相匹配，至少在种族上要匹配，性别和社会背景也可能要匹配。这种匹配的必要性主要体现在两个方面：受访者更容易接受访谈员，以及访谈员更有可能理解受访者。

One way to phrase this issue is to ask to what extent it is necessary for the interviewer to be an insider in the respondent’s world in order to be effective as an interviewer. Studies of survey interviewing have shown that respondents do use observable characteristics of the interviewer, including the interviewer’s skin color, dress, demeanor, age, and sex, to guess where they might find common ground. Their judgment in this respect then affects the opinions and attitudes they voice. But we can’t be sure whether interviewer characteristics would also affect the sort of detailed report of witnessed events that is the more usual concern of qualitative interviewing. My guess is that even if a respondent had a tendency to slant a description of an event in order to win the interviewer’s approval, the interviewer could reduce that tendency by obtaining full detail.

这个问题的一种表述方式是：为了有效开展访谈，访谈者在多大程度上需要了解受访者的处境？调查访谈研究表明，受访者确实会利用访谈者的可观察特征，例如肤色、着装、举止、年龄和性别，来猜测彼此的共同点。他们在这方面的判断会影响他们表达的观点和态度。但我们无法确定访谈者的特征是否也会影响到定性访谈中通常关注的那种对目击事件的详细描述。我的猜测是，即使受访者为了赢得访谈者的认可而倾向于歪曲事件描述，访谈者也可以通过获取完整的细节来减少这种倾向。

In any case, it is difficult to anticipate what interviewer attributes will prove important to a respondent and how the respondent will react to them. Nell Painter, a black academic woman of clearly middle-class background, found when establishing an interviewing relationship with Hosea Hudson, a radical black man of rural Southern working-class background, that the attribute that mattered to the respondent was her politics:

总之，很难预料访谈者的哪些特质对受访者来说会很重要，以及受访者会如何回应这些特质。内尔·佩恩特是一位出身中产阶级的黑人女学者，她在与霍西亚·哈德森（一位来自美国南方农村工人阶级的激进黑人）建立访谈关系时发现，对受访者来说最重要的特质是访谈者的政治立场：

When he asked about my politics I feared that would mean the end of our work together, for although I admired his long years of dedication to radical change in the face of opposition, I had to admit that I was only a Democrat. To my surprise, Hudson was greatly relieved. His worry was not that I might be a liberal, but that I might belong to one of the groups he calls “left-splinter,” such as the Socialists Workers Party. 6

当他问起我的政治立场时，我担心我们的合作就此结束，因为尽管我钦佩他多年来不畏强权、致力于激进变革，但我不得不承认，我只是个民主党人。令我惊讶的是，哈德森如释重负。他担心的不是我可能是个自由主义者，而是我可能属于他所谓的“左翼分裂派”，比如社会主义工人党。

There are so many different interviewer attributes to which a respondent can react that the interviewer will surely be an insider in some ways, an outsider in others. When I interviewed men who were IV drug users, I was an outsider to the drug culture but an insider to the world of men. When I interviewed a woman who was an IV drug user living in a shelter and also the mother of two children, I was an outsider to the world of women, drug users, and women’s shelters, but an insider to the concerns of parents.

受访者会对访谈者的各种特质做出反应，因此访谈者在某些方面肯定是圈内人，在另一些方面又是圈外人。当我采访静脉注射毒品的男性时，我对毒品文化来说是圈外人，但对男性的世界来说却是圈内人。当我采访一位住在收容所、同时也是两个孩子的母亲的静脉注射毒品女性时，我对女性、吸毒者和妇女收容所的世界来说是圈外人，但对为人父母者的担忧来说却是圈内人。

I have generally found it better to be an insider to the milieu in which the respondent lives, because it is easier then for me to establish a research partnership with the respondent. But some of my most instructive interviews have been good just because I was an outsider who needed instruction in the respondent’s milieu. I was once instructed in the art of car stripping by a respondent who found me, as he put it, a little lame in my understanding of his hustle. For a similar reason I was told in detail about the functioning of a “shooting gallery” and the reasons for the willingness of addicts to use house needles—something an insider might not have asked about. Also, respondents sometimes talk more openly to outsiders not only because the outsiders seem to appreciate tutelage but also because outsiders don’t share the values that would make them condemn those aspects of the respondents’ behavior that an insider would recognize as failing insider norms.

我通常发现，如果我是受访者生活环境的内部人士，研究效果会更好，因为这样更容易与受访者建立研究伙伴关系。但我的一些最有启发性的访谈恰恰是因为我是局外人，需要了解受访者的生活环境。我曾经被一位受访者指导过汽车拆解技巧，因为他觉得我对他的“营生”了解得有点浅薄。出于类似的原因，我还详细地了解过“注射室”的运作方式，以及吸毒者愿意使用私自针头的原因——这些都是内部人士可能不会问到的问题。此外，受访者有时会更愿意与局外人交流，这不仅是因为局外人似乎很感激指导，还因为局外人并不认同那些会让内部人士谴责受访者行为的价值观，而这些行为在内部人士看来却是违背了内部规范的。

It may well be possible to be so much of an outsider that respondents decide they cannot talk to you because you could never understand or cannot be trusted or do not know how to ask. Charles Briggs writes that different settings require that interviewing be done in different ways, and the proper way to ask questions must be mastered if there is to be an interview at all. But my experience, limited to be sure, is that learning how to be instructed is among the first things one learns in a new setting. 7 And investigators, though they may begin as thoroughgoing outsiders, are likely in time to learn from their study how to manage to interview. 8 Robert Merton concludes after careful consideration that both insiders and outsiders can make unique and valuable contributions to an understanding of situations. 9 My own view is that a reasonably proficient qualitative interviewer can establish an effective research partnership with a very wide range of respondents. 10

完全有可能因为与受访者格格不入而导致他们觉得无法与你交谈，因为你根本无法理解他们，或者他们不信任你，或者你不知道该如何提问。查尔斯·布里格斯写道，不同的环境需要不同的访谈方式，如果想要进行访谈，就必须掌握正确的提问方法。但我的经验（当然，经验有限）是，在新的环境中，学习如何接受指导是人们首先要学习的事情之一。 7 研究者虽然一开始可能是彻头彻尾的局外人，但随着时间的推移，他们很可能从研究中学会如何进行访谈。 8 罗伯特·默顿经过深思熟虑后得出结论：内部人士和外部人士都能为理解各种情况做出独特而宝贵的贡献。 9 我个人认为，一位具备相当能力的定性访谈者可以与各种各样的受访者建立有效的研究伙伴关系。 10

What I give in the following paragraphs is an account of my own experiences, as I am aware of them, in relation to four bases frequently considered for deciding insider or outsider status in research interviewing.

以下段落将根据我所了解的情况，对我自己在研究访谈中经常考虑的四个决定内部人或外部人身份的依据进行描述。

SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS

社会经济地位

I have found that when my niche on the socioeconomic ladder was higher than that of my respondent’s, because I was a college professor and the respondent was a blue-collar worker or on welfare, it was usually easy to establish a good research partnership. All it took was ordinary considerateness, together with full and respectful attention within the interview. When I was inferior in social standing to someone in a different field, as when my respondent was someone highly successful in business or medicine, our being in different fields seemed to reduce the relevance of our relative ranking.

我发现，当我的社会经济地位高于受访者时——比如我是大学教授，而受访者是蓝领工人或领取福利金——通常很容易建立良好的研究合作关系。这只需要基本的体贴，以及在访谈中给予充分且尊重的关注。而当我的社会地位低于其他领域的人时——比如我的受访者是商界或医学界的成功人士——我们身处不同领域似乎会降低我们相对地位的重要性。

I have found it most difficult to interview highly successful people in academic or professional fields not too different from mine. In one such interview I found myself, without consciously intending to, repeatedly making reference to my own achievements. I mentioned, for example, that I had once taught at the respondent’s university; I also noted that I was the principal investigator of the study and that I had done successful work in the past. It is not unusual for men to assert their own merits in early interchanges with someone whom they respect, but it was no way for me to go about establishing an interviewing partnership; the competitive element was too obtrusive. This particular interview went badly. I suspect that similar issues, on my side and on the side of respondents, have troubled other interviews I’ve had with people in or near my own field.

我发现，采访那些在学术或专业领域与我相差不远的、成就斐然的人士非常困难。在一次这样的采访中，我发现自己无意间反复提及自己的成就。例如，我提到我曾在受访者所在的大学任教；我还提到我是这项研究的首席研究员，并且过去也取得过一些成功。男性在与自己尊敬的人初次交流时强调自身价值并不罕见，但这对我来说却不利于建立良好的采访关系；这种竞争性的倾向太过明显。那次采访进行得并不顺利。我怀疑，类似的问题，无论是我自身还是受访者，都困扰着我在其他与我领域或相近领域人士的采访中。

I think it may be undesirable to be an occupational insider because issues of competition are difficult to suspend. Furthermore, confidentiality is a problem. Can you really be trusted to keep the information to yourself? Might not the interview provide material for gossip, maybe introduced by the comment, “I once interviewed him …”? And even if the information goes nowhere else, you have it and you are a potential colleague or competitor. Just as you probably should avoid interviewing people in your own family—talking with them frankly is a different matter—you probably should avoid interviewing people who are or may become colleagues. An exception to this would be if your study requires such interviews; even then I would be cautious.

我认为，成为业内人士可能并不可取，因为竞争问题很难避免。此外，保密性也是个问题。你真的能做到保守秘密吗？采访会不会成为八卦的素材，比如有人会说“我曾经采访过他……”？即使信息没有泄露出去，你也掌握了这些信息，而你本身就是潜在的同事或竞争对手。正如你最好避免采访自己的家人一样——与他们坦诚交谈是另一回事——你也应该避免采访那些现在是或将来可能成为同事的人。除非你的研究需要进行此类采访，否则我不会轻易妥协。

RACE AND ETHNICITY

种族和民族

It seems like common sense that it would be better for the interviewer to be of the same race and, if possible, of the same ethnic background as the respondent. My own experience has been that here common sense is mostly wrong. Racial and ethnic differences, insofar as the respondent can infer these, may perhaps play a role in a respondent’s initial reaction to the interviewer, but my experience has been that once an interview takes hold, these differences have little effect on the quality of the interviewing partnership. They become like a difference in height: there, but unimportant.

人们通常认为，面试官最好与受访者属于同一种族，如果可能的话，最好是同一族裔背景。但我的经验是，这种常识往往并不适用。种族和族裔差异，如果受访者能够感知到的话，或许会影响他们对面试官的最初反应，但我的经验是，一旦面试正式开始，这些差异对面试质量的影响微乎其微。它们就像身高差异一样：存在，但无关紧要。

I speak as someone who is white who has interviewed people who are in other racial groups and as someone who is Jewish who has interviewed people of other religious and ethnic groups. Only on rare occasions has my religion or ethnicity seemed even relevant. Once, when I was starting out, a respondent who did not recognize me as Jewish described his own sharp negotiating as justified because his victim was Jewish. I remained an attentive interviewer. More recently, a respondent who was a retired minister quizzed me about my religion with an eye toward recruiting me to his faith. This happened after the interview had ended and seemed manageable enough. That’s about it, as instances where religion or ethnicity seemed to matter.

我以白人的身份采访过其他种族的人，也以犹太人的身份采访过其他宗教和族裔的人。我的宗教或种族背景似乎只在极少数情况下才会产生影响。有一次，在我刚入行的时候，一位受访者没认出我是犹太人，却认为他咄咄逼人的谈判策略是合理的，因为他的“受害者”是犹太人。但我依然保持了专注的采访态度。最近，一位退休牧师询问了我的宗教信仰，意图拉拢我加入他的教派。这件事发生在采访结束后，当时我觉得还好处理。宗教或种族背景似乎起作用的情况也就这些了。

SEX

性别

Most often, it seems to me, men can interview women with the same success they would have in interviewing men, and women can interview men with the same success they would have in interviewing women. There is some belief in the field that women do better as interviewers with both men and women. Certainly, women are more often chosen as confidants by men as well as by other women. But among the very good interviewers with whom I have worked there have been both men and women, and good interviewers remain good interviewers irrespective of the sex of the respondent. Also, it has seemed to me, the great majority of respondents can form a good research partnership with an interviewer of either sex.

在我看来，大多数情况下，男性采访女性的成功率与采访男性的成功率相同，女性采访男性的成功率也与采访女性的成功率相同。业内有一种观点认为，女性作为访谈者，无论面对男性还是女性，都表现得更好。当然，男性和其他女性都更倾向于选择女性作为知己。但我合作过的优秀访谈者中，既有男性也有女性，而且优秀的访谈者无论面对的是受访者的性别，依然是优秀的访谈者。此外，在我看来，绝大多数受访者都能与任何性别的访谈者建立良好的研究合作关系。

However, difficulties do sometimes appear in cross-sex interviewing that express themselves as respondent or interviewer discomfort. When interviewing women of about my age, I am often aware—and suspect that the woman is also aware—that while our relationship will under no circumstance become a sexual one, still it can be imagined that it could. This awareness, no matter how peripheral to attention, can make the research partnership more cautious. But even if it should have the effect of making the partnership more engaging, this would be no less a problem: an interviewer who feels drawn to a respondent can feel encouraged to be more present and more interactive than is entirely desirable. Similarly, a respondent can be encouraged by a relationship with an interviewer that has begun to seem intriguing to be more concerned with interaction with the interviewer than with memories and observations. But in reality any hope that might develop in an interview for a continued relationship can only lead to disappointment and confusion. If an interviewer becomes aware of a developing personal interest within an interview, an interest of the sort that is usually preliminary to a continuing relationship, it is the interviewer’s responsibility to cool it. Nothing good comes from using such an interest to enliven an interview.

然而，在异性访谈中，有时确实会出现一些困难，表现为受访者或访谈者的不适感。在访谈与我年龄相仿的女性时，我常常意识到——而且我怀疑她们也意识到了——虽然我们的关系绝不会发展成性关系，但这种可能性仍然存在。这种意识，无论多么细微，都会使研究伙伴关系更加谨慎。但即便它能使伙伴关系更加投入，这本身也并非问题：如果访谈者对受访者产生好感，就会受到鼓励，更加投入，互动也更加频繁，而这并非完全可取。同样，如果受访者与访谈者之间开始建立起某种联系，他们可能会更关注与访谈者的互动，而不是回忆和观察。但实际上，任何在访谈中萌生的建立关系的希望，最终都只会导致失望和困惑。如果访谈者在访谈过程中察觉到自己对受访者产生了个人兴趣，而这种兴趣通常是发展长期关系的先决条件，那么访谈者有责任将其扼杀在萌芽状态。利用这种兴趣来活跃面试气氛并不会带来任何好处。

It is possible for women who are interviewers to be challenged by male respondents who want to test the women’s sexual accessibility. My impression from women who have worked with me is that such challenges occur infrequently, but, as I noted in chapter 3, I do not think interviewers should take any risk whatsoever of assault. It seems to me only sensible for an interviewer to trust, and act on, even vague intuitions. A feeling of discomfort is reason enough to avoid an interview situation or, if one is in it, to end it.

女性面试官可能会遇到男性受访者试图试探她们的性开放程度的情况。据我与合作过的女性同事反映，这种情况并不常见。但是，正如我在第三章中提到的，我认为面试官不应该冒任何遭受性侵犯的风险。在我看来，面试官应该相信并运用哪怕是模糊的直觉。感到不适就足以构成避免面试的理由，如果已经身处面试之中，则应该立即结束面试。

AGE

年龄

When I began interviewing I was a young man often interviewing men and women much older than I. Now most respondents are younger than I am. Age does make a difference in the nature of the relationship that is established. When I was the younger I often took the role of someone less experienced than the respondent. Now I more often take the role of someone widely experienced, although not necessarily in the area of the interview. But in either case my stance has been that of someone who can be talked to, and, young and old, I have tried to listen attentively. The content of the interviews seems to me to be no different.

我刚开始做访谈员的时候还很年轻，经常采访比我年长很多的男士和女士。现在大多数受访者都比我年轻。年龄确实会影响我们之间建立的关系。年轻的时候，我常常扮演经验不如受访者的人的角色。现在，我更多地扮演经验丰富的人的角色，尽管不一定是在访谈领域。但无论年龄大小，我的态度始终是平易近人，无论受访者是年轻人还是老年人，我都努力认真倾听。在我看来，访谈的内容并没有什么不同。

INTERVIEWING DIFFICULTIES

面试困难

PROBLEM RESPONDENTS

问题受访者

Most respondents are cooperative and easy to work with. Some respondents present one or another sort of challenge.

大多数受访者都很配合，容易合作。但也有一些受访者带来了这样或那样的挑战。

The Unresponsive Respondent

无回应的答辩人

The respondent who is unresponsive may not be convinced that candor is without risk. Or the respondent may just feel that there is no potential profit in participating in the interview and therefore no point in cooperating with it. The result is a sequence like the following, from an interview in the study of occupationally successful men:

不愿配合的受访者可能并不相信坦诚相待没有风险。或者，他们可能只是觉得参与访谈没有任何潜在好处，因此没有必要配合。以下是针对职业成功男性的一项访谈调查中出现的情况：

I NTERVIEWER : What’s it been like for you, raising your children?

采访者：你觉得养育孩子是什么感觉？

R ESPONDENT : Well, I suppose you don’t have to worry about running out of aggravations.

答辩人：嗯，我想你不用担心会没有烦心事了。

I: Could you tell me about the most recent time when you might have felt an aggravation?

我：您能告诉我您最近一次感到烦躁不安的时候是什么时候吗？

R: That’s just a manner of speaking. Really, things are just fine.

R：那只是说话方式而已。实际上，一切都很好。

Maybe the interviewer should have shown more appreciation of the humor in the respondent’s initial response. Maybe the interviewer’s follow-up question was too abrupt. Maybe the interviewer would have been more successful with “What are the kinds of things you have in mind that might supply you with aggravations?” But there’s no reason to believe the respondent would not have deflected any query. A respondent who doesn’t want to respond isn’t going to become cooperative because of a question’s wording.

或许面试官应该更欣赏受访者最初回答中的幽默感。或许面试官的后续问题过于唐突。或许面试官如果问“您认为哪些事情会让您感到烦恼？”会更有效。但没有理由相信受访者不会回避任何问题。一个不想回答的受访者不会因为问题的措辞而变得配合。

The Respondent Determined to Present a Particular Picture
