答辩人决心呈现某种特定图景。

A man I interviewed in the study of retirement was anxious to have me believe that he had been an outstanding success as a businessman. This may have been the case, although he was so determined to have me believe it that I was led to wonder. When I asked for incidents that would display the highs of his business career, he became evasive. Every effort I made to elicit the daily experience of running a business was misunderstood or sidestepped. A pump-priming comment I made—“It sounds like you were carrying a lot of responsibility”—elicited only annoyance. No matter how I tried, I couldn’t get specifics. I gave the interview about an hour and at the end of that time felt that I had learned little. I couldn’t see how a second interview would make things better and didn’t try to schedule one.

我在一项关于退休的研究中采访了一位男士，他急于让我相信他是一位非常成功的商人。也许事实的确如此，但他如此执着于此，反而让我产生了怀疑。当我请他举例说明他事业上的辉煌成就时，他却闪烁其词。我试图了解他日常经营企业的经历，但他要么误解我的意思，要么避而不谈。我开了个玩笑——“听起来你肩负着很多责任”——结果却只换来他的不耐烦。无论我如何努力，都无法得到具体的细节。我花了大约一个小时进行采访，但结束后感觉收获甚微。我看不出第二次采访会有什么帮助，所以没有安排第二次。

I don’t know if this respondent wanted to convince me of something that was counterfactual, but he acted as though he did. When a respondent wants you to believe something that is different from what actually happened, the respondent is likely to avoid providing detail and to frustrate your efforts to elicit detail. My policy in such situations is to keep plugging away for concreteness until I’m convinced further effort is pointless. If problems seem to exist primarily in one area, I will search for a study-relevant area in which the respondent is willing to be candid. If the respondent insists on remaining general, I may try saying something like “We really need stories that will show us what was happening—the more concrete and detailed, the better” or “I wonder if there’s a specific incident you could describe, because then we can see what happens.” But if the respondent doesn’t have detailed stories to tell and doesn’t want to admit it, this urging won’t work either.

我不知道这位受访者是否想说服我接受一些与事实不符的说法，但他表现得好像是这样。当受访者想让你相信一些与实际情况不同的事情时，他们很可能会回避提供细节，并阻挠你获取细节的努力。在这种情况下，我的策略是坚持不懈地追问，直到我确信继续努力毫无意义为止。如果问题似乎主要集中在某个方面，我会寻找与研究相关的、受访者愿意坦诚相待的领域。如果受访者坚持保持笼统，我可能会尝试说：“我们真的需要一些能展现当时情况的故事——越具体、越详细越好”，或者“我想知道您是否可以描述一个具体的事件，这样我们就能了解发生了什么。”但如果受访者没有具体的故事可讲，也不愿承认这一点，那么这种劝说也无济于事。

A respondent who wants to avoid an issue in an area of the research may be as difficult. I was in the early phase of an interview with a physician about his retirement when it became evident that he had been asked to resign his hospital appointment. There was some hint in what he was saying that he had become unreliable, maybe that he had botched a procedure. A colleague’s vulnerability to a malpractice suit was alluded to and then dropped. As I pressed for detail about the reasons for the respondent’s retirement, I could see his edginess increase. Although I then moved to an area where I thought he would be more comfortable, he wanted to be told again what the study was about and where I was from and who would know what he said. For the rest of the interview he was tense. He didn’t relax until I said that I thought the questions I had brought with me had been adequately explored and that I wanted to thank him. His interview provided usable material, but it wasn’t a good interview.

如果受访者想要回避研究领域中的某个问题，那他可能同样难以应付。我曾与一位医生就他的退休事宜进行访谈，当时访谈尚处于初期阶段，但很快我就意识到他已被医院要求辞职。他的话语中隐隐透露出他变得不可靠，或许是某个手术出了差错。他曾提及一位同事可能面临医疗事故诉讼，但随后又避而不谈。当我追问他退休的具体原因时，我能感觉到他的紧张情绪日益加剧。尽管我随后将话题转移到我认为他会更自在的领域，但他还是反复强调这项研究的内容、我的背景以及谁会知道他所说的话。在接下来的访谈中，他一直处于紧张状态。直到我表示我认为我提出的问题已经得到了充分的探讨，并向他表示感谢，他才放松下来。他的访谈虽然提供了一些有用的素材，但整体而言，这是一次并不成功的访谈。

People Whose Feelings Are Raw

情感脆弱的人

In a study of bereavement we called widows and widowers within weeks of the death of their husbands and wives to arrange for an interview. If our call was answered by a relative acting as a caretaker, we would be sent away, sometimes fiercely: what right did we have, they wanted to know, to intrude at such a time? But when it was the widow or widower who answered our call, we often were welcomed. For the most part, the new widows and widowers were grateful for someone to talk to. Although their feelings were raw and their pain immediately at hand, the great majority found talking to be helpful.

在一项关于丧亲之痛的研究中，我们在配偶去世后的几周内致电丧偶人士，安排访谈。如果接电话的是负责照护的亲属，我们会被打发走，有时甚至会遭到粗暴对待：他们质问我们有什么权利在这种时候打扰他们？但如果是丧偶人士本人接听电话，我们通常会受到欢迎。大多数情况下，这些新丧偶的人都很感激有人可以倾诉。尽管他们悲痛欲绝，但绝大多数人都觉得倾诉很有帮助。

When grief is new and pain intense, people need both to let their distress be known and to gain relief from the distress by pushing it away. So people want sometimes to be able to talk, sometimes not to have to talk. An interviewer—as a stranger who is understanding, indeed professional; concerned yet dispassionate; and able to listen without offering either report-limiting sympathy or a palliative formula—is exactly the right person to talk to. Usually people organize themselves so they are ready to talk during the interview. They then take other times for distraction from awareness of their loss.

当悲伤来袭，痛苦难耐时，人们既需要倾诉自己的痛苦，又需要通过逃避来缓解这种痛苦。因此，人们有时渴望倾诉，有时却又不想开口。一位访谈者——作为一位理解他人、专业且不带偏见的陌生人，既关心他人又保持客观冷静，能够倾听而不提供任何可能限制倾诉的同情或安慰剂——正是最合适的倾诉对象。通常，人们会在访谈过程中调整好状态，做好倾诉的准备。之后，他们会利用其他时间来分散注意力，暂时忘记失去亲人的痛苦。

If I Weren’t in This Situation, You Wouldn’t Want to Interview Me

如果我不是身处这种境地，你肯定不会想采访我。

Sometimes the interview is a reminder to the respondent that he or she is in a category of people who have been hurt or who are, for some other regrettable reason, special. I once interviewed a widow whose husband had been an important political figure. She felt that if her husband were still alive not only would I not be seeing her in the course of a study of bereavement but she would perhaps not even be accessible to me for an interview of any kind. And also she felt that if we were having this interview while her husband was still alive, my manner would have been deferential rather than sympathetic. The respondent was able to describe these feelings; by doing so she was instructive about the social effects of bereavement.

有时，访谈会提醒受访者，他们属于遭受过伤害或因其他一些令人遗憾的原因而显得特殊的人群。我曾采访过一位寡妇，她的丈夫曾是一位重要的政治人物。她觉得，如果她的丈夫还活着，我不仅不会在丧亲研究的过程中见到她，甚至可能根本无法接受任何形式的采访。她还觉得，如果是在她丈夫还活着的时候进行这次访谈，我的态度会是恭敬而非同情。这位受访者能够描述这些感受；她的描述也让我们对丧亲的社会影响有了更深刻的理解。

THE PRESENCE OF OTHERS

他人的存在

Having others present in an interview’s setting always affects what can be asked and what will be reported. Often, the best way to deal with the situation is to include everyone present in the interview. At least then their contributions to what is said will be more nearly evident.

在访谈过程中，其他人的在场总会影响到提问的内容和最终的记录。通常，最好的办法是让所有在场人员都参与到访谈中来。至少这样一来，他们各自的发言就能更清晰地呈现出来。

For example, I began an interview of a retired physician with his wife silently in the background. The physician was maintaining that he felt happily occupied despite a much-reduced work schedule. He clearly was not only reporting to me but also arguing with his wife, although I had no idea what the argument was about. When I asked the physician’s wife what she thought about what her husband was saying, she said that he didn’t have a reduced work schedule at all, that he was still working 10-hour days, only now he wasn’t getting nearly the income he had gotten when he worked those long hours in his practice. He had given up his medical building office, to be sure, but he continued to treat patients from an office in the home. She said her husband could easily cut back his hours if he wanted to but he was determined to fill his time with work.

例如，我开始采访一位退休医生时，他的妻子在旁边默默地听着。这位医生坚持说，尽管工作时间大幅减少，但他仍然感到生活充实而快乐。他显然不仅在向我汇报情况，还在和妻子争论，但我完全不知道他们在争论什么。当我问医生的妻子对丈夫的说法有何看法时，她说丈夫的工作时间根本没有减少，他仍然每天工作10个小时，只是现在的收入远不如以前在诊所长时间工作时那么高了。诚然，他放弃了在医疗大楼的办公室，但他仍然在家里的办公室里继续为病人看病。她说，如果她丈夫想的话，他完全可以减少工作时间，但他决心要把所有时间都用来工作。

The joint interview provided information about the tensions that could be introduced into the marriage of retired men should the men define their retirement as bringing their work lives home. Had I been able to interview the respondent without his wife in the background, I might or might not have obtained a useful interview, But given that the respondent’s wife was there, it was better to include her.

这次联合访谈让我了解到，如果退休男性将退休定义为把工作带回家，他们的婚姻可能会因此产生哪些紧张关系。如果我能在没有他妻子在场的情况下单独采访他，或许能获得一些有用的信息，也或许不能。但既然他妻子在场，让她参与进来就更好了。

INTERVIEWING FAILURES

面试失败案例

Sometimes respondents decide that they are being oppressed by the interview. And sometimes this is true. Being asked repeatedly for concrete instances can be experienced as badgering. Not being understood by an interviewer can be experienced as a kind of nonacceptance, and it is easy to become irritated or angry in response.

有时受访者会觉得面试过程让他们感到压抑。有时确实如此。被反复追问具体事例会被视为骚扰。如果面试官不理解自己，可能会被视为一种不被接纳，从而很容易产生恼怒或愤怒的情绪。

Respondents who begin being uncomfortable may ostentatiously check their watch, ask how many more questions you have, or just stop talking. In one instance in our study of occupationally successful men, a respondent fell asleep during an interview. I am grateful that I was not the interviewer, although I hope I would not have let the interview get to this pass. Going to sleep was the respondent’s final move in a contest between him and the interviewer over who would control the interview.

感到不自在的受访者可能会故意看表，问你还有多少问题，或者干脆停止说话。在我们对一些事业成功的男性进行的研究中，就有一个受访者在访谈过程中睡着了。我很庆幸自己不是那个访谈者，但我希望自己不会让访谈发展到这种地步。睡着是这位受访者在与访谈者争夺访谈主导权的较量中的最后一招。

Sooner or later every interviewer encounters a bad interview, an interview in which no matter what the interviewer does, the respondent does not provide usable material. Interviews that go badly have occurred less and less often as I have become more experienced. Nevertheless, I would guess that one interview in fifteen or twenty is a failure. When I have had an interview failure, my first reaction has been that it was my fault. Often enough, I have found much to criticize in my approach. But usually a bad interview, like a good one, is jointly produced by interviewer and respondent.

每个面试官迟早都会遇到糟糕的面试，无论面试官如何努力，受访者都无法提供有效信息。随着经验的积累，糟糕的面试发生的频率越来越低。尽管如此，我估计每十五到二十次面试中，大约会有一次失败。每当面试失败时，我的第一反应往往是反思自己的问题。很多时候，我都能从自己的面试方法中找到许多需要改进的地方。但通常来说，一次糟糕的面试，就像一次成功的面试一样，是面试官和受访者共同作用的结果。

In one interview that went badly, the respondent appeared skeptical about the interview to begin with. He wanted to talk about his situation, partly to get a grip on it, but he didn’t want to lose control of the discussion. I don’t think he started off determined to reject the interview, although that is what he came to.

在一次不太成功的访谈中，受访者一开始就对访谈抱有怀疑态度。他想谈谈自己的处境，部分原因是想理清思路，但他又不想失去对谈话的控制。我认为他一开始并没有打算拒绝访谈，尽管最终他确实这么做了。

The respondent had had a distinguished career and now was retired. He lived by himself, separated from his wife. He sometimes visited his former firm when the firm had open meetings, although he then sat silently through the meetings. He had no financial problems. He presented his current life as ideal, without stress, with all the time in the world for hobbies and reading. It struck me as bleak.

这位受访者曾有过辉煌的职业生涯，如今已退休。他独自生活，与妻子分居。他有时会在公司召开公开会议时回访，但总是默默地参加会议。他没有经济问题。他把自己现在的生活描述得非常理想，没有压力，有大把的时间可以发展爱好和阅读。在我看来，这简直是悲惨。

The interview began with the respondent answering questions briefly, although thoughtfully. But when I tried to get him to elaborate on a response, he replied that he had already answered the question. When I said it was important for us to have a sense of the events of his retirement, he responded by wondering what I could possibly make of his words. He said that people are each unique, living unique lives, and that you can’t generalize from what any one person tells you. I didn’t want to get into defending the study, but not defending it may have been a kind of defensiveness too, an unwillingness to take his objections seriously. Anyway, I asked more questions. The respondent began allowing his attention to wander. I don’t think he looked at his watch, but he shuffled in his chair in a way that suggested he was bored. Then, in case I had missed the body language, he told me he was bored. Then he said that he thought the kind of work I was doing was useless and that he didn’t see any reason to participate further. I thanked him for his time and left.

访谈开始时，受访者虽然回答问题很简短，但思路清晰。当我试图让他详细阐述某个回答时，他却说他已经回答过了。我说了解他退休后的经历很重要，他却反问我，我到底能从他的话里得出什么结论。他说，每个人都是独一无二的，过着独一无二的生活，你不能仅凭一个人的讲述就妄下结论。我不想为这项研究辩护，但或许不辩护本身也是一种自我保护，一种不愿认真对待他反对意见的态度。总之，我继续追问。受访者开始走神。我想他没看表，但他挪动了一下身子，似乎有些无聊。然后，为了确保我没听出他的肢体语言，他告诉我他很无聊。接着，他又说他觉得我做的工作毫无意义，他觉得没有必要继续参与下去。我感谢他抽出时间，然后离开了。

I decided later that I should have attempted to strengthen the interviewing partnership by focusing on the respondent’s former work. But when I listened to the tape of the interview, I found that I had tried doing that. The respondent had brightened briefly but then had gone silent again. That was the worst interview I have had in the last fifty or so I have done, and maybe the worst interview I’ve ever had.

后来我意识到，我应该尝试通过关注受访者的过往工作来加强访谈关系。但当我听了访谈录音后，发现我其实已经尝试过了。受访者的情绪短暂地有所好转，但随后又陷入了沉默。那是我近五十次访谈中最糟糕的一次，或许也是我经历过的最糟糕的一次。

What to Do When an Interview Is Going Badly

面试不顺利时该怎么办

It isn’t hard to tell when an interview is going badly. Neither the respondent nor you is relaxed. The respondent may indicate discomfort or resistance or antagonism by lapses in attention or sparse responses or outright challenges. Even without this, you are likely to be uncomfortable. You can’t get engaged by the interview. You find it hard to listen closely to the respondent. You aren’t in touch with the respondent’s account, limited as it is. Your questions are awkward. You fail to ask the respondent to extend a description or give detail for an incident, although usually you would do this almost automatically. You flounder. The interview takes on a survey research quality: you ask a question, and then the respondent gives a brief response and waits for the next question. You are painfully aware of how little the interview is producing and yet feel unable to rescue it.

不难判断访谈是否进行得不顺利。受访者和你都无法放松。受访者可能会通过注意力不集中、回答寥寥或直接质疑来表现出不适、抵触或敌意。即使没有这些表现，你也可能感到不自在。你无法投入到访谈中。你发现自己很难认真倾听受访者的讲述。你无法理解受访者有限的叙述。你的问题显得笨拙。你没有要求受访者扩展描述或提供事件细节，尽管通常你会几乎是下意识地这样做。你不知所措。访谈变得像调查问卷一样：你问一个问题，然后受访者简短地回答，等待下一个问题。你痛苦地意识到访谈毫无成效，却又无力挽救。

What can you do? If it is the first few minutes of the interview, you might simply continue in the hope that you and the respondent will become more at ease. But if the interview has been going as long as 5 minutes, and the respondent indicates discomfort, you ought to try to strengthen the research partnership. You might check that the respondent understands and accepts the study’s assumptions. A pause in questioning to discuss the study’s aims can make it easier for the respondent to ask for further information. You might search for an area of easy rapport; the area of the respondent’s work will often do. You should make every effort to follow the respondent’s lead in deciding what to talk about, so long as it is within hailing distance of the study’s substantive frame (as the interviewer did in the second interview in chapter 4). More than anything else, you should attend closely to both text and subtext of the respondent’s statements.

你能做什么？如果访谈才刚刚开始几分钟，你可以继续进行，希望你和受访者都能放松下来。但如果访谈已经持续了5分钟，而受访者表现出不自在，你应该努力加强研究合作关系。你可以确认受访者是否理解并接受研究的假设。暂停提问，讨论研究目的，可以让受访者更容易提出更多信息。你可以寻找一个容易建立融洽关系的话题；受访者的工作领域通常是一个不错的选择。你应该尽力跟随受访者的引导来决定谈话内容，只要这些内容与研究的实质框架密切相关（就像第四章第二次访谈中的访谈者那样）。最重要的是，你应该仔细聆听受访者话语的字面意思和弦外之音。

A way of dealing with ungiving respondents that I haven’t tried, but have been told by other investigators is effective, is to say, “It is important for us that the people we talk with give us complete accounts of their observations or experiences in the area of the study. Is this something you feel you can do?” If this can be said so that it isn’t confrontational, it might make it easier to obtain useful materials.

我还没试过，但其他研究人员告诉我，对付不愿配合的受访者的一种有效方法是：对受访者说，“对我们来说，受访者完整地讲述他们在研究领域的观察或经历非常重要。您觉得您能做到吗？” 如果措辞得体，避免对抗，或许更容易获得有用的资料。

My own practice, if an interview is going badly and nothing seems to be working and yet I do not want to give up entirely, is to end the interview before the respondent begins to think about ending it, and set another appointment. To justify returning, I name some topics still to be discussed. Back at the office I talk to a colleague about the problems in the interview or at least think about how to approach the next interview.

如果面试进行得不顺利，似乎什么方法都行不通，但我又不想完全放弃，我的做法是在受访者开始考虑结束面试之前就结束面试，并安排下一次时间。为了证明下次面试的必要性，我会列出一些还有待讨论的话题。回到办公室后，我会和同事讨论面试中遇到的问题，或者至少思考一下如何更好地进行下一次面试。

With some respondents, nothing can be done. It may be that the particular match of interviewer and respondent is wrong. Or it may be that the respondent will always refuse to provide usable information, or is unable to. Some people play their lives close to their chests and will never show their hand, no matter the circumstance. Chalk it up to experience. Everyone has some bad interviews. It is not essential for a study that every interview be illuminating. If this respondent does not provide information about some phenomenon, then another will. It’s a shame to lose the opportunity to learn from a respondent, and a bad interview is a loss for the study. But the loss is virtually never fatal.

对于某些受访者，我们无能为力。或许是访谈者和受访者的匹配度有问题。又或许受访者始终拒绝提供有效信息，或者根本无法提供。有些人对自己的生活讳莫如深，无论在什么情况下都不会轻易表露心迹。就当是积累经验吧。每个人都会遇到一些糟糕的访谈。研究并非一定要每次访谈都富有启发性。如果这位受访者无法提供关于某种现象的信息，总会有其他受访者提供。错失从受访者那里学习的机会固然可惜，一次糟糕的访谈对研究来说也是一种损失。但这种损失几乎不会造成致命的后果。

ISSUES OF VALIDITY: DO RESPONDENTS TELL THE TRUTH, THE WHOLE TRUTH, AND NOTHING BUT THE TRUTH?

有效性问题：受访者是否说了真话、全部真话、只说真话？

How much of what a respondent tells you can you believe? And how much is left out?

受访者所说的话有多少可信？又有多少被隐瞒了？

A while ago I was a respondent being interviewed by a skillful and sympathetic interviewer about the history of a research training program I had helped organize. I wanted the interviewer’s project to succeed and wanted to provide her with whatever information I had. And yet as I described the early days of the program, I observed myself slide over incidents that had been important at the time, because describing them would have made evident the frictions that had developed among the program’s staff. Here I was, determined to be a good respondent and to describe exactly how it had all happened, and I was being less than candid. My justification to myself was that I didn’t want to compromise other people’s privacy nor to rehash old quarrels. Nor was I entirely happy with my own part in the conflicts of those long ago days. I dropped one or two markers to indicate that the program had had its problems, and had the interviewer asked me to say more about them, I would have. She didn’t, and so I let them be. But what an incomplete report I provided!

不久前，我接受了一位技巧娴熟、富有同情心的访谈员的采访，内容是关于我曾协助组织的一个研究培训项目的历史。我希望访谈员的项目能够顺利进行，也想尽我所能地提供信息。然而，在描述项目初期的情况时，我发现自己有意忽略了一些当时很重要的事件，因为如果描述这些事件，就会暴露出项目工作人员之间产生的摩擦。我当时一心想做一个好受访者，如实描述事情的来龙去脉，结果却有所隐瞒。我给自己的理由是，我不想泄露他人的隐私，也不想重提旧事。而且，我对当年自己在那些冲突中所扮演的角色也并不完全满意。我略微提及了一两点，表明项目确实存在一些问题，如果访谈员要求我详细说明，我也会继续说下去。但她并没有，所以我也就作罢了。然而，我提供的这份报告却如此片面！

I was also struck by the gaps in my memory. These, for all I know, may have been more significant. I could not remember how a critically important proposal had gotten written, although almost certainly I had done most of the writing. I vividly remembered going to Washington to seek further funding after the program had completed its first years, and my unsatisfactory encounter there with a representative of a granting agency. Perhaps defending a program that had become emotionally important to me was a more memorable event than writing a proposal for a program that did not yet exist. But it was surprising to me that I could provide detailed information about the one event and no information about the other.

我也注意到自己记忆中的空白。就我所知，这些空白或许更为重要。我记不起一份至关重要的提案是如何撰写出来的，尽管几乎可以肯定大部分内容都是我写的。我清楚地记得，在项目启动几年后，我去华盛顿寻求后续资金，以及在那里与一位拨款机构代表令人失望的会面。或许，为一个对我来说意义非凡的项目辩护，比为一个尚未存在的项目撰写提案更令人难忘。但令我惊讶的是，我能详细回忆起前一件事，却对后一件事毫无印象。

Cooperative respondents asked about a past no longer much thought about will probably display, as I did, oases of vivid memories within a desert of uncertainty. They are likely also to display, as I did, unwillingness to make all their memories accessible. On the other hand, they may, again as I did, provide markers to the elided material that an attentive interviewer can recognize.

那些被问及一段不再常想起的往事的合作受访者，很可能会像我一样，在茫茫的记忆荒漠中闪烁着鲜活的回忆。他们也可能像我一样，不愿将所有记忆都诉诸笔端。另一方面，他们或许也会像我一样，提供一些线索，帮助细心的访谈者辨识出那些被刻意回避的记忆。

There was one thing I did not do in my responses to that interview: I did not invent events that had not occurred. Indeed, I felt no temptation to invent anything—not a role for myself I hadn’t played nor a success for the program it hadn’t had. I think this too is likely to be the case for most respondents in most studies: what is reported may be spotty, but little will be invented. The lying respondent happens less often than people who don’t do interviewing may imagine. For one thing, it’s difficult to maintain a counterfactual reality when being pressed to provide detailed descriptions of events. And why should anyone want to do it?

在那次采访中，有一件事我没有做：我没有捏造任何未曾发生过的事情。事实上，我丝毫没有想要捏造任何事情的冲动——无论是我扮演过的角色，还是项目取得过的成功。我认为大多数受访者在大多数研究中的情况也大致如此：他们所报告的内容可能存在一些瑕疵，但很少会捏造事实。撒谎的受访者比那些不做采访的人想象的要少得多。首先，当被要求详细描述事件时，很难维持一种反事实的现实。而且，谁又会想这么做呢？

But while we as interviewers can anticipate that we will be told the truth, we cannot assume that we will be told the whole truth nor the 148 precise truth. If respondents want to keep from us events or behaviors or a sector of their lives, there is every reason to believe that they can succeed. While it would be difficult for respondents to produce the circumstantial detail and corroborating incident necessary to make an invented reality seem plausible, it is very easy for them not to report something—and to give no indication that there is something not being reported.

但是，虽然作为访谈者，我们可以预期受访者会告诉我们真相，但我们不能假定他们会告诉我们全部真相，也不能假定他们会告诉我们精确的真相。如果受访者想对我们隐瞒某些事件、行为或生活片段，我们完全有理由相信他们能够成功。虽然受访者很难提供必要的细节和佐证事件来使虚构的现实显得合情合理，但他们却很容易隐瞒某些事情——而且不会透露任何信息。

There are some kinds of events that we are unlikely to hear about unless we have established an interviewing relationship in which there is extraordinary trust. People will not endanger themselves to contribute to social research. In our interviewing of occupationally successful men we were told of no incidents in which our respondents embezzled from their employers, although we heard of incidents in which others had embezzled. It seems to me unlikely that we had in our sample only men who were aware of others’ dishonesty and none who were dishonest themselves.

有些事情，除非我们与受访者建立了高度信任的访谈关系，否则我们不太可能了解。人们不会为了参与社会研究而让自己身处险境。在我们采访一些事业有成的男性时，虽然我们听说过其他人挪用公款的案例，但受访者中没有一人提及自己曾挪用雇主的钱财。在我看来，我们的样本中只有知晓他人不诚实行为的男性，而没有一个自己不诚实的男性，这种可能性似乎不大。

Nor can we be sure we will be told the precise truth. The vagaries of respondent memory make for reports in which some observations are crystal clear while others are obscured or distorted or blocked. Respondents also may shade their responses to present a positive picture of themselves. This seems to me most likely in a first interview; in later interviews a respondent, more confident of acceptance, may provide corrective information. One respondent, an HIV-positive IV drug user, in a first interview described breaking a syringe against the wall when importuned by a friend to share it; in a subsequent interview he described another occasion when he agreed to share his needle. He wasn’t lying in his first story. It really happened—or maybe came close to happening. But it wasn’t until the later interview that he presented the more mixed picture.

我们也不能确定自己会听到确切的真相。受访者记忆的不确定性导致报告中有些观察结果清晰明了，而另一些则模糊不清、扭曲变形或被刻意忽略。受访者也可能为了展现自己积极的一面而对回答进行润色。在我看来，这种情况最有可能发生在第一次访谈中；在之后的访谈中，受访者可能因为更有信心接受采访而提供更正信息。一位艾滋病毒感染者，同时也是一名静脉注射吸毒者，在第一次访谈中描述了他被朋友恳求共用注射器时，将注射器摔在墙上的经历；在随后的访谈中，他又描述了另一次他同意与朋友共用针头的情况。他第一次讲述的故事并没有撒谎。这件事确实发生过——或者说，差点就发生了。但直到后来的访谈，他才呈现出更为复杂的情况。

Shading responses to present a positive picture of the self is especially likely when respondents are asked about opinions, attitudes, appraisals, evaluations, values, or beliefs. These can express an identity appropriate to the situation of the interview as much as something more stable. Asked by a friend to comment on the future of an institution the respondent is involved in—for example, a company or university—the respondent might express his mood of the moment; with an interviewer, the respondent might be more thoughtful and analytic.

当被问及观点、态度、评价、价值观或信仰时，受访者尤其容易通过调整回答来展现积极的自我形象。这些回答既可以表达一种符合访谈情境的身份认同，也可以反映一种更为稳定的自我认知。例如，如果朋友请受访者评价其参与的机构（如公司或大学）的未来，受访者可能会表达当时的情绪；而面对面试官，受访者则可能更加深思熟虑、分析透彻。

Information is context dependent—that is, shaped in part by the interview situation—when it is free of anchors in observations of events. Generalizations from experiences also tend to be context dependent because they depend on weightings of what may be discordant observations. A question like “Is your relationship with your sister good or not so good?” can have many true responses, including those indicating that the two get on well enough, that the two have a barely submerged rivalry, and that the two stopped talking for a year after the sister disputed a will. If we are seen as a friendly stranger, we may be told that the relationship is amicable, which is true. If we are seen as a sympathetic listener, interested in the respondent’s disappointments, we may hear that the sister is not to be fully trusted, also a true response.

当信息脱离了对事件的观察作为锚点时，它就具有情境依赖性——也就是说，它在一定程度上受到访谈情境的影响。从经验中得出的概括也往往具有情境依赖性，因为它们取决于对可能存在矛盾的观察结果的权重。例如，“你和你姐姐的关系好还是不好？”这个问题可能会有很多真实的回答，包括两人相处融洽、两人之间存在着一种隐隐的竞争关系，以及姐姐对遗嘱提出异议后两人一年没有联系。如果我们被视为友好的陌生人，我们可能会听到她们关系友好，这当然是事实。如果我们被视为善解人意的倾听者，对受访者的失望感兴趣，我们可能会听到她们的姐姐不太值得信任，这也是一个真实的回答。

While questions about concrete incidents—such as “What happened when you and your sister were last together?”—may be answered from more than one perspective, they are less likely to be modifiable by the interviewing context. Thus, we will obtain more reliable information and information easier to interpret if we ask about concrete incidents than we will if we ask about general states or about opinions.

虽然关于具体事件的问题——例如“你和你妹妹上次在一起时发生了什么？”——可以从多个角度回答，但它们受访谈情境的影响较小。因此，与询问一般情况或观点相比，询问具体事件能让我们获得更可靠、更易于理解的信息。

Despite all the ways in which interview material can be problematic, richly detailed accounts of vividly remembered events are likely to be trustworthy. Nor does apparent inconsistency always demonstrate invalidity. After all, people can act in inconsistent ways or maintain inconsistent feelings. Business partners, for example, can be both grateful and resentful. A respondent who in a second interview describes an attitude toward a partner contradictory to an attitude described in a first interview may in both interviews have been telling the truth. 11

尽管访谈材料可能存在各种问题，但对记忆犹新的事件进行详尽描述通常值得信赖。表面上的矛盾也并非总是意味着无效。毕竟，人们的行为或情感可能前后矛盾。例如，商业伙伴可能既感激又怨恨。如果受访者在第二次访谈中对合作伙伴的态度与第一次访谈中的态度相矛盾，那么他在两次访谈中可能都说了真话。

Sometimes we can check on the validity of a respondent’s account by interviewing other respondents. Occasionally, there are records we can look to for corroboration. 12 But for the most part we must rely on the quality of our interviewing for the validity of our material. Ultimately, our best guarantee of the validity of interview material is careful, concrete level, interviewing within the context of a good interviewing partnership.

有时我们可以通过采访其他受访者来核实受访者陈述的真实性。偶尔，我们也可以查阅记录以寻求佐证。但大多数情况下，我们必须依靠访谈质量来保证资料的有效性。归根结底，确保访谈资料有效性的最佳方法是在良好的访谈合作关系下，进行细致、具体、深入的访谈。

# ↩

CHAPTER 6
ANALYSIS OF DATA

第六章 数据分析

Most investigators let analysis slide until the advent of an “analysis phase.” Anselm Strauss, in Qualitative Analysis for Social Scientists , his manual on analysis in the style of “grounded theory,” 1 and Miles and Huberman, in their more eclectic Qualitative Data Analysis , consider this bad practice. They urge that analysis begin as soon as there is data collection. Miles and Huberman observe that the more investigators have developed understandings during data collection, the surer they can be of the adequacy of the data collection and the less daunting will be the task of fully analyzing the data. 2

大多数研究者往往等到所谓的“分析阶段”才开始进行分析。安塞尔姆·施特劳斯在其著作《社会科学家的定性分析》（一本关于“扎根理论”式分析的手册）中，以及迈尔斯和胡伯曼在其著作《定性数据分析》（内容更为广泛）中，都认为这种做法是不妥的。他们敦促研究者在数据收集之初就应立即开始分析。迈尔斯和胡伯曼指出，研究者在数据收集过程中获得的理解越多，就越能确信数据收集的充分性，从而更容易完成数据分析。

Despite the unquestionable merits of this view, a conspiracy of forces regularly impedes early analysis. During the interviewing phase the investigator must deal with all the demands of obtaining the data: recruiting the respondents, conducting the interviews, getting them transcribed, deciding whether the right information is being collected, and returning to conduct more interviews. Nor can the investigator escape awareness that when the interviewing is finally over, not only will all the data be at hand but there will be uninterrupted weeks or months available for their analysis. Undoubtedly the investigator will develop insights, speculations, and small-scale theories beginning with the first pilot interview or before. But it is likely to be only after interviewing has ended that the investigator can give full attention to analysis and writing.

尽管这种观点无疑具有其合理性，但诸多因素的相互作用常常阻碍早期分析。在访谈阶段，研究者必须应对获取数据的所有需求：招募受访者、进行访谈、转录访谈记录、判断收集的信息是否正确，以及返回进行更多访谈。研究者也无法忽视这样一个事实：当访谈最终结束时，不仅所有数据都已准备就绪，而且还会有数周甚至数月的时间可供分析。毫无疑问，研究者会在第一次试点访谈甚至更早的时候就形成一些见解、推测和初步理论。但很可能只有在访谈结束后，研究者才能全身心投入到分析和写作中。

Although analysis and writing can be separated from data gathering, they cannot be separated from each other. The kind of report that will be written and the kind of analysis that will be done must be decided jointly. Each implies the other. If the report is to be a set of case studies of respondents, then each respondent’s material must be organized and interpreted separately; conversely, if each respondent’s materials are organized and interpreted separately, the only report possible is a set of case studies.

尽管分析和撰写可以与数据收集分开进行，但它们彼此密不可分。报告的撰写方式和分析方法必须共同决定，二者相辅相成。如果报告是一系列受访者的案例研究，那么每位受访者的资料都必须单独整理和解读；反之，如果每位受访者的资料都单独整理和解读，那么最终的报告也只能是一系列案例研究。

We can identify four different approaches to analysis and reporting. The four approaches represent the different combinations of decisions regarding, first, whether the report will focus on issues or on cases and, second, what is to be the report’s intended level of generalization.

我们可以识别出四种不同的分析和报告方法。这四种方法代表了关于以下两个方面的不同决策组合：第一，报告将侧重于议题还是案例；第二，报告的概括程度。

Analysis and reporting can deal either with issues as they are learned about from respondents or with the respondents themselves: they can, for example, deal with the effect being forced to retire has on feelings of worth, using relevant materials from all respondents; or with particular respondents and how they happened to retire, and what were their subsequent experiences, perhaps including their feelings of worth. We can call the first approach “issue-focused” and the second “case-focused.” 3

分析和报告可以针对从受访者那里了解到的问题进行处理，也可以针对受访者本身进行处理：例如，可以利用所有受访者的相关资料，探讨被迫退休对自我价值感的影响；或者针对特定受访者，探讨他们退休的原因以及之后的经历，其中可能包括他们的自我价值感。我们可以将第一种方法称为“问题导向型”，将第二种方法称为“案例导向型”。

Analysis and reporting can also either remain on the level of respondents’ reports or be generalized from their reports: they can, for example, deal with the effects of retirement on the particular administrators and professionals who were respondents in the study, or they can use what was learned in the study to consider the effects of retirement on all or most former administrators and professionals. We can call the first the “level of the concrete,” the second the “level of the generalized.”

分析和报告既可以停留在受访者报告的层面，也可以从他们的报告中进行概括：例如，可以探讨退休对参与研究的特定管理人员和专业人员的影响，也可以利用研究成果来考察退休对所有或大多数前管理人员和专业人员的影响。我们可以将前者称为“具体层面”，后者称为“概括层面”。

When the report is issue focused and generalized, we have the usual sociological account. When the report is issue focused and concrete, we have the usual historical or journalistic account. When the report is case focused and concrete, we have the usual case studies of individuals. When the report is case focused and generalized, we have typological description. Later in this chapter I give descriptions of reports in each of these modes.

当报告聚焦于某个议题并进行概括时，我们通常会看到社会学式的叙述。当报告聚焦于某个议题并进行具体分析时，我们通常会看到历史或新闻报道式的叙述。当报告聚焦于某个具体案例并进行具体分析时，我们通常会看到个案研究式的叙述。当报告聚焦于某个案例并进行概括时，我们通常会看到类型学式的描述。本章稍后将分别对每种类型的报告进行描述。

No matter the level or focus of the final report, there is no single tried-and-true method of analysis or strategy for presentation of findings. Investigators have different styles, studies different requirements, audiences different needs. Consider only the extent to which the investigator’s voice is present. Studs Terkel’s books present respondent’s voices, one after the other, without editorial interruption, 4 Daniel Levinson’s Seasons of a Man’s Life presents theory and generalized observation interrupted by heavily interpreted case materials. 5 In some chapters of Elliot Liebow’s Talley’s Corner the only voice presented is the author’s; in others, passages of interview, of dialogue, and of group conversation provide a sense of the reality that underlies Liebow’s observations. 6 Any of these might serve as a model, but they would be different models. 7

无论最终报告的层级或侧重点如何，都没有一种万无一失的分析方法或研究结果呈现策略。研究者的风格各异，研究的要求也不同，受众的需求也各有差异。我们只需考虑研究者的声音在报告中出现的程度即可。斯塔兹·特克尔（Studs Terkel）的著作逐一呈现受访者的声音，没有编辑的干预；丹尼尔·莱文森（Daniel Levinson）的《男人的一生》（Seasons of a Man’s Life）则以理论和概括性的观察为主，穿插着大量经过诠释的案例材料；埃利奥特·利博（Elliot Liebow）的《塔利角》（Talley’s Corner）在某些章节中只呈现了作者的声音；而在另一些章节中，访谈、对话和小组讨论的段落则展现了利博观察背后的现实。这些都可以作为参考范例，但它们各自都是不同的范例。

In one respect all good reports, despite wide variation in style, are similar: they tell a coherent story. They provide a line of argument, or an image of how it all works, such that material presented early in the report prepares the reader for material that will appear later and later material draws on the earlier. The reader, at the end, can grasp the report entire.

从某种意义上说，所有优秀的报告，尽管风格各异，却都具有相似之处：它们都讲述了一个连贯的故事。它们提供了一条论证思路，或者描绘了整个过程的运作方式，使得报告开头呈现的内容为后续内容做好铺垫，而后续内容又相互呼应。最终，读者能够全面理解整份报告。

The kind of story the investigator can tell must be consistent with the kind of data that has been collected. As I noted in chapter 3, a coherent story may be achieved either by the diachronic strategy of describing movement through time or by the synchronic strategy of describing the integration of elements at a moment in time. A report whose subject is single parents might begin with the way in which people become single parents, go on to describe how they manage to meet the problems they encounter, and then assess the benefits and stresses of single-parent life. Alternatively, it might move from sector to sector within single-parent life, describing first the way single parents organize their households and then their relationships with their children and so on. One of these strategies of presentation will almost surely have been anticipated when the interview guide was developed, and it would be difficult now to move to the other. In other respects, however, the investigator is likely to be able to choose how the data should be presented, and so how it should be analyzed.

研究者能够讲述的故事类型必须与所收集的数据类型相一致。正如我在第三章中所述，连贯的故事可以通过两种策略实现：一是描述时间进程的历时性策略，二是描述某一特定时刻各要素整合的共时性策略。例如，一份以单亲父母为主题的报告可以从人们如何成为单亲父母入手，进而描述他们如何应对遇到的问题，最后评估单亲生活的益处和压力。或者，报告也可以从单亲生活的各个方面入手，首先描述单亲父母如何安排家庭事务，然后描述他们与子女的关系等等。在制定访谈指南时，几乎可以肯定已经预料到其中一种呈现策略，现在很难再转向另一种。然而，在其他方面，研究者通常可以选择数据的呈现方式，从而选择数据的分析方法。

In the following pages I shall discuss first what might be involved in issue-focused analyses and then what might be involved in case-focused analyses. In my discussion of issue-focused analyses I will begin with the generalized level, because the analytic issues are clearer there; in my discussion of case-focused analyses I will begin with concrete description, because this provides an introduction to the problems of generalizing from individual cases.

在接下来的篇幅中，我将首先探讨议题导向分析可能涉及的内容，然后探讨案例导向分析可能涉及的内容。在讨论议题导向分析时，我将从概括层面入手，因为在这个层面上分析问题更为清晰；在讨论案例导向分析时，我将从具体描述入手，因为这有助于引出从个案中进行概括所面临的问题。

ISSUE-FOCUSED ANALYSIS

问题聚焦分析

What I believe is the most frequent social science approach to presenting the findings of a qualitative interview study is to describe what has been learned from all respondents about people in their situation. An analysis whose aim is issue focussed would concern itself with what could be learned about specific issues—or events or processes—from any and all respondents. Some respondents might contribute more to the analysis, others less. The analyst would become like the medical specialist who is interested in livers, not in particular patients, except that the analyst would be concerned with more than a single set of issues.

我认为，社会科学中最常见的呈现定性访谈研究结果的方法是，描述从所有受访者那里了解到的关于他们所处境况的人们的信息。而以问题为导向的分析则会关注从所有受访者那里了解到的关于特定问题、事件或过程的信息。有些受访者可能对分析贡献更大，有些则贡献较小。分析者就像一位关注肝脏而非特定病人的医学专家，只不过这位分析者关注的不仅仅是一组问题。

An issue-focused description is likely to move from discussion of issues within one area to discussion of issues within another, with each area logically connected to the others. A report about people who retired might begin with a discussion of how the retirement occurred (an area). In the discussion it might consider the different impacts of being pushed out of one’s job, retiring to gain freedom from the job, and retiring for reasons of health (specific issues). The next area to be discussed might be early reactions to retirement. This area would, of course, have its own issues. Then would follow still other areas, again each with its own issues. The whole would together describe the retirement experience in a number of areas for the group the respondents represented.

以问题为中心的描述通常会从一个领域内的问题讨论到另一个领域内的问题讨论，每个领域都与其他领域逻辑相连。例如，一份关于退休人员的报告可能会从讨论退休是如何发生的（一个领域）开始。在讨论中，报告可能会考虑被迫离职、为了获得工作自由而退休以及因健康原因退休等不同情况的影响（具体问题）。接下来要讨论的领域可能是退休初期的反应。当然，这一领域本身也会涉及一些问题。之后还会涉及其他领域，每个领域也都有其自身的问题。最终，报告会从多个方面描述受访者所代表群体的退休经历。

There are four distinct analytic processes involved in producing an issue-focused analysis of interview material. These are coding, sorting, local integration, and inclusive integration. Early in the analysis, coding is likely to predominate; later, local and inclusive integration may absorb the most energy and attention. But all analytic processes occur throughout the analysis. Coding is intended to provide the materials for sorting and integration, but sorting and integration can also raise questions for further coding.

对访谈材料进行以议题为中心的分析涉及四个不同的分析过程：编码、分类、局部整合和包容性整合。在分析初期，编码可能占据主导地位；后期，局部整合和包容性整合可能占据更多精力。但所有分析过程贯穿整个分析过程。编码旨在为分类和整合提供素材，而分类和整合本身也可能引发需要进一步编码的问题。

CODING

编码

The idea in coding is to link what the respondent says in his or her interview to the concepts and categories that will appear in the report.

编码的理念是将受访者在访谈中所说的话与报告中将出现的概念和类别联系起来。

Suppose that in analyzing data on retirement we read in the transcript of an interview with a retired surgeon the following comment: “I started the process of retiring several years ago when I began winding down my practice and cut out the major surgery and went just to doing minor surgery.” We could code this—that is, link it to concepts and categories—by noting that it is an instance of (1) preparation for retirement in which there is movement to the periphery of the occupation; (2) withdrawal from tasks of high responsibility, tension, skill, and visibility; (3) unclear regarding the source of the pressure to retire; and (4) more a change in work routine than a change in identity as a physician. How we code it depends on our theoretical assumptions and the research interests we bring to the project.

假设在分析退休数据时，我们在一位退休外科医生的访谈记录中读到以下评论：“几年前，我开始逐步减少工作量，不再做大型手术，只做小型手术，那时我就开始着手退休了。”我们可以对这段话进行编码——即将其与相关概念和类别联系起来——指出它体现了以下几个方面：（1）为退休做准备，逐渐淡出医疗行业；（2）退出高责任、高压力、高技能、高曝光度的工作；（3）退休压力来源不明；（4）与其说是医生身份的改变，不如说是工作方式的改变。我们如何进行编码取决于我们的理论假设以及我们对该项目的研究兴趣。

Some coding categories we bring to our studies before ever knowing what the interviews will produce. We plan to use them because they are related to the problem we hope to study, as an aspect of the problem or an explanation for it or a consequence of it. Others we bring with us as readinesses to interpret respondents’ comments in one way or another. The readinesses come from our training, our reading, our life experiences, and our general understandings. When I code a respondent’s description of night sweats as an expression of stress, my coding comes from my having learned to attribute a particular meaning to this particular symptom. Many codings seem to be immediately plausible abstractions from respondents’ statements. For example, the respondent statement “We don’t agree on the children’s bedtimes, but I’m the one who has to deal with them” might be coded “conflict over children resolved by reference to domain responsibility.”

有些编码类别是我们事先设定的，甚至在了解访谈结果之前就已经准备好的。我们之所以计划使用这些类别，是因为它们与我们希望研究的问题相关，可能是问题的某个方面、对问题的解释，或是问题的结果。另一些编码类别则是我们预先设定的，用于以某种方式解读受访者的评论。这些预设来源于我们的培训、阅读、生活经验和一般认知。例如，当我将受访者对盗汗的描述编码为压力的一种表现时，我的编码就源于我已学会将这种特定症状赋予特定的含义。许多编码似乎是对受访者陈述的直接抽象。例如，受访者的陈述“我们对孩子的就寝时间意见不一致，但最终由我来处理”可以被编码为“通过明确责任范围解决的育儿冲突”。

I find myself coding automatically as I read interview transcripts. The code categories I use, at least initially, are efforts to capture the interview material. I don’t try to make sense of every “meaning unit”—every utterance that provides a complete thought—nor of every sentence or paragraph. But as I go through the material I do ask myself what I am seeing instances of, what I am learning about, and what questions the material raises.

我发现自己在阅读访谈记录时会不自觉地进行编码。我使用的编码类别，至少在最初阶段，是为了尽可能地捕捉访谈内容。我并不试图理解每一个“意义单元”（即每一个表达完整思想的语句），也不试图理解每一个句子或段落。但在阅读过程中，我会问自己：我看到了哪些实例？我从中了解到了什么？这些材料又引发了哪些问题？

I generally write my codings, along with formulations or speculations, in the margins of the transcripts I am working with. Later, I go back over my marginal notes. If they still make sense, I dictate them into a tape recorder, together with the interview excerpts on which they are based, to be transcribed as background notes. I am likely to use the formulations in these notes as I develop chapter drafts, but I may not. However, once I have dictated the notes, I remember their formulations at least in outline and can carry them in my mind and review them and think about how to test them or develop them. I am likely, too, to return again to the interview excerpts in the notes to reconsider whether they truly support the codings I have made.

我通常会将编码、一些概括或推测写在正在处理的访谈记录的空白处。之后，我会重新查看这些空白笔记。如果它们仍然有意义，我会将它们连同所依据的访谈摘录一起录入录音机，作为背景笔记。我可能会在撰写章节草稿时用到这些笔记中的概括，但也可能不会。不过，一旦我把笔记录了下来，至少就能记住它们的概要，并能将它们记在脑子里，随时回顾，思考如何检验或完善它们。我也可能会再次翻阅笔记中的访谈摘录，重新思考它们是否真的支持我所做的编码。

Fairly early in a study, if I am doing issue-focused analysis, I shift from reading and coding transcripts of interviews to reading and coding “excerpt files.” These are collections from many interviews of excerpts dealing with the same issue. I say more about excerpt files in the next section.

在研究初期，如果我进行的是议题聚焦分析，我会从阅读和编码访谈记录转向阅读和编码“摘录文件”。这些摘录文件收集了多次访谈中围绕同一议题展开的摘录。下一节我会详细介绍摘录文件。

As I make decisions regarding whether instances fit my coding categories, I find it necessary to further specify what I mean by the categories. Thus, the coding category is developed and defined through interaction with the data. Take the category “snares responsibility for home maintenance,” which was one of the categories in my study of occupationally successful men. One man said that he fully shared household responsibility and performed many of the household tasks, except at those times when his professional work load became heavy. When his professional work load became heavy, he would ask his wife to take over the entire responsibility of the home, and he believed it was her place to do so. I then realized that I meant by “shared responsibility” a responsibility for home maintenance that was understood by the couple to be shared not just when other responsibilities permitted it but always.

在判断某些案例是否符合我的编码类别时，我发现有必要进一步明确这些类别的含义。因此，编码类别是通过与数据的互动而发展和定义的。以“承担家庭维护责任”这一类别为例，这是我在对事业成功的男性进行研究时使用的类别之一。一位男士表示，他完全承担家务，并负责许多家务，除非他的工作量过大。当工作量过大时，他会请妻子承担全部家务，并且他认为这是妻子应尽的责任。这时我意识到，我所说的“共同承担责任”指的是夫妻双方都理解的共同承担家庭维护责任，这种责任并非仅仅在其他责任允许的情况下才需要共同承担，而是始终如此。

Coding of this sort cannot be delegated to a research assistant. Coding is thinking about the material, and the thinking should be that of whoever will be responsible for the report. This is not to say that others cannot help. It is almost always useful to be able to talk about codes, and having others code the same material can be a good basis for such talk.

这类编码工作不能委托给研究助理。编码需要对材料进行思考，而这种思考应该由最终负责撰写报告的人来完成。但这并不意味着其他人不能提供帮助。能够讨论代码几乎总是很有帮助的，而让其他人对相同的材料进行编码可以为这种讨论奠定良好的基础。

When do you stop coding? Only when you stop reading transcripts—and that may not be until the final report is completed. But there is a change in the character of coding as a study progresses. By the end of the analysis phase the investigator should more and more see the data fitting into already established codes. While the point is never reached where new material can no longer enrich codings, toward the end of the analysis there should be few important phenomena that significantly extend or deepen or qualify codings.

何时停止编码？只有当你停止阅读访谈记录时才会停止——而这可能要等到最终报告完成之后才会发生。但随着研究的推进，编码的性质也会发生变化。在分析阶段结束时，研究者应该越来越能看出数据与已建立的编码相吻合。虽然永远不会达到新材料无法再丰富编码的地步，但在分析后期，应该很少有重要的现象能够显著扩展、深化或修正编码。

SORTING

排序

Before the advent of computers and word-processing programs there was a standard approach to the analysis of interview transcripts and other qualitative data: Make second copies of transcripts and notes. Put the first copies away, to serve as an archive. Label file folders with the titles of the sections of the report, the chapters, or chapter sections. Cut up the second copies of the material into topical units corresponding to the labels on the file folders. File each excerpted topical unit in its proper folder. If folders become too full, divide the materials by subtopics and sort into new folders.

在计算机和文字处理程序出现之前，分析访谈记录和其他定性数据的标准方法是：制作访谈记录和笔记的副本。将副本妥善保存，作为档案。在文件夹上贴上报告各部分、章节或章节标题的标签。将副本材料按主题单元剪裁，每个主题单元对应一个文件夹。如果文件夹已满，则按子主题对材料进行分类，并整理到新的文件夹中。

The result is a set of folders containing excerpts from cases, each folder holding a category of material. What happens next with the material is, first, “local integration,” in which the material of the file folder is interpreted, and, second, “inclusive integration,” in which the collection of file folders is organized into a coherent sequence.

最终形成一系列文件夹，每个文件夹包含案例摘录，每个文件夹对应一个材料类别。接下来对这些材料的处理分为两部分：首先是“局部整合”，即对文件夹中的材料进行解读；其次是“整体整合”，即将所有文件夹整理成一个连贯的序列。

The cutting and sorting into file folders, which is the traditional approach to qualitative analysis, can now be done by computer wordprocessing programs. Instead of literally cutting up interviews and putting the snippets into appropriate file folders, the analyst at a computer electronically moves material from an interview file or a file of notes into an appropriate excerpt file. Then the excerpt file can be printed out as needed.

传统的定性分析方法是将访谈记录剪切并整理到文件夹中，而现在，计算机文字处理程序可以完成这项工作。分析人员无需再像以前那样将访谈记录剪切并放入相应的文件夹中，而是通过电脑将访谈记录或笔记文件中的材料电子化地移动到相应的摘录文件中。然后，可以根据需要打印出摘录文件。

As I noted, in doing issue focused analysis I find it more satisfactory to code from excerpt files than from full interviews. If an initial excerpt file becomes too bulky, I can break it into smaller excerpt files dealing with narrower topics. If it is too narrow to start with—this doesn’t often happen—I can amalgamate it with other excerpt files.

正如我之前提到的，在进行以问题为中心的分析时，我发现从摘录文件中进行编码比从完整的访谈记录中进行编码更为有效。如果初始摘录文件过于庞大，我可以将其拆分成处理更细分主题的较小摘录文件。如果一开始就过于狭窄——这种情况并不常见——我可以将其与其他摘录文件合并。

In analyzing material from the study of occupationally successful men for one section of a chapter on fathering, I began with an except file of expressions of paternal investment in children. That turned out to be too thick to deal with. So I divided it into several more narrowly focused excerpt files: one dealt with indications of pride in the children, another with instances of dealing with crises, another with instances of acting in a paternal role in sports or discipline or character formation, and so on. I then coded each of these files (by writing in the margins of transcript pages) and dictated the codes and exemplary excerpts for later transcription.

在分析一篇关于父亲角色的章节中某个部分所研究的职业成功男性的资料时，我最初整理了一份关于父亲对子女投入的摘录文件。但这份文件太厚，难以处理。于是，我将其拆分成几个主题更明确的摘录文件：一个文件记录父亲对子女的自豪感，一个文件记录父亲处理危机的实例，还有一个文件记录父亲在体育运动、管教或性格塑造等方面扮演父亲角色的实例，等等。然后，我给每个文件都做了编码（在转录页的空白处做标记），并口述了这些编码和示例摘录，以便后续转录。

I find it most efficient to produce excerpt files only as I need them. If the interviews provide a great deal of material regarding an issue, I will not require that the excerpt file contain it all. An excerpt file that runs to 80 pages of single-spaced text, with wide enough sampling from the interviews to make me confident the interview materials are adequately represented, strikes me as good enough and about all I will want to work through.

我发现最有效的方式是只在需要时才生成摘录文件。如果访谈内容提供了大量关于某个议题的资料，我不会要求摘录文件包含所有内容。一份80页单倍行距的摘录文件，只要包含足够广泛的访谈内容样本，足以让我确信访谈资料得到了充分的体现，对我来说就足够了，也基本满足我的需求。

While I haven’t found it possible to have others help me in coding, I have found that others can help in making up an excerpt file. Sometimes the decisions they make about what belongs in a file aren’t exactly the decisions I would make, but ordinarily they are good enough. I can always add to or subtract from the file if I want to.

虽然我还没找到其他人帮我编写代码的方法，但我发现他们可以帮我创建代码摘录文件。有时候，他们对文件内容的选择可能和我不太一样，但通常来说，他们的选择已经足够好了。如果需要，我可以随时对文件进行增删。

The use of a computer in making up excerpt files makes for greater flexibility in managing data. It is easier with a computer file than with sheets of paper in an actual file folder to break a too inclusive file into narrower files or to amalgamate too thin files. Furthermore, the computer excerpt file can be printed out to provide a set of passages from interviews to be read and coded, formatted in any way you like. Computer programs exist whose aim is to facilitate the coding and sorting of interview material. While their use is not without problems—including the need to invest time in mastering them and the risk that, once mastered, they will dictate the direction of the analysis—they can further facilitate analytic work. 8

使用计算机创建摘录文件可以更灵活地管理数据。与使用纸质文件相比，计算机文件更容易将内容过多的文件拆分成内容较少的文件，或合并内容过少的文件。此外，计算机摘录文件可以打印出来，提供一系列访谈摘录，供阅读和编码，并可根据需要进行任何格式设置。目前有一些计算机程序旨在简化访谈材料的编码和整理工作。虽然使用这些程序并非没有问题——例如需要投入时间学习，以及一旦掌握，程序可能会主导分析方向——但它们确实可以进一步促进分析工作。

LOCAL INTEGRATION

本地一体化

The codings of the material in an excerpt file constitute a statement of what we believe the material tells us. We now need to find a way of organizing and integrating our observations and understandings in each section of the report. This I call local integration. I find myself beginning to do this as soon as any interview materials show up and continuing it all the way through the study, although it becomes a focus of my effort only when I am involved in producing the final report.

摘录文件中材料的编码构成了我们对材料内容的理解。现在，我们需要找到一种方法，将我们在报告各部分中的观察和理解进行组织和整合。我称之为局部整合。我发现自己一旦开始处理任何访谈材料，就会着手进行局部整合，并贯穿整个研究过程，尽管只有在撰写最终报告时，它才会成为我工作的重点。

One way to achieve local integration is simply to summarize the excerpt file and its codings: Here is what is said in this area, and this is what I believe it to mean. We might first summarize the main line of the material: what most respondents say. Then we could turn to the material that does not fit in the main line, the variants, and summarize them. If there are too many variants, our definition of what constitutes the main line is unsatisfactory and we need to move to a more inclusive formulation.

实现本地化整合的一种方法是简单地概括摘录文件及其编码：这部分内容是这样说的，以及我认为它的含义是这样。我们可以先概括材料的主线：即大多数受访者的说法。然后，我们可以转向那些不符合主线的内容，即变体，并对其进行概括。如果变体过多，则说明我们对主线的定义不够完善，我们需要采用更包容的表述方式。

An example of summarizing the main line and its variants might be taken from bereavement project material dealing with widowers who were parents of small children. Here we could summarize material dealing with the fathers’ reliance on their mothers or their sisters or on female housekeepers or, in a few instances, their mothers-in-law. We could then summarize as cases that did not fit the main line the stories of fathers who did not at all rely on women to help them care for their children. We would try to provide enough material about the main line so that our summary made sense to the reader, and it also made sense that this should be the most frequent development. We would also try to explain why cases that did not fit the main line were different. We might note, for example, that the fathers who did not rely on women to help them care for their children had older children or had decided to stay home from work for a time.

我们可以以丧偶父亲（育有幼儿）的丧亲关怀项目资料为例，总结主流模式及其变体。例如，我们可以总结这些父亲依赖母亲、姐妹、女管家，或者在少数情况下依赖岳母的案例。然后，我们可以将那些完全不依赖女性照料孩子的父亲的故事，作为不符合主流模式的案例进行总结。我们会尽量提供足够的主流模式相关资料，使读者能够理解我们的总结，并明白这才是最常见的模式。我们还会尝试解释不符合主流模式的案例有何不同。例如，我们可以指出，那些不依赖女性照料孩子的父亲，要么孩子年龄较大，要么决定暂时在家照顾孩子。

A theory that makes sense of the materials is preferable to a descriptive summary of main lines and variations. I find myself developing, from the very beginning of the study, “minitheories,” hypotheses whose aim is to make sense of material dealing with specific issues or material within a particular sector. As the study progresses I retain those that are supported by the data and drop those that are not, almost without noticing that I am doing so.

比起对主要脉络和变奏的描述性总结，能够解释材料的理论更为可取。我发现自己从研究伊始就开始构建“微型理论”，即旨在理解涉及特定议题或特定领域材料的假设。随着研究的深入，我会保留那些有数据支持的理论，舍弃那些没有数据的理论，几乎是无意识地进行着这样的选择。

Early in my study of occupationally successful men I found myself developing a minitheory about the meaning for the men of challenge at work. The theory was attractive to me because it made a connection that I thought valid between two things that weren’t obviously connected: the men’s zest for challenge and their frequent stress at work. The minitheory was that the men viewed challenge at work as a test of their worth and responded by mobilization of their energy and attention. They relaxed their energy and attention if they met the challenge successfully—indeed, they then felt good about themselves. If they didn’t meet the challenge successfully, however, they remained mobilized. This persisting mobilization was exactly work stress. Further, the men’s jobs consisted of meeting challenges, one after another. This was what the men wanted. Such a job gave them maximum opportunity to test themselves and gain the pleasure of self-approbation. But it also made it likely that sooner or later they would run into a challenge they could not meet, and so experience work stress.

在早期对事业成功的男性进行研究时，我逐渐形成了一个关于工作挑战对他们意义的微型理论。这个理论吸引我的地方在于，它将两个看似无关的事物联系起来，而我认为这种联系是合理的：男性对挑战的热情和他们频繁的工作压力。这个微型理论认为，男性将工作中的挑战视为对自身价值的考验，并通过调动精力和注意力来应对。如果他们成功应对挑战，就会放松下来——事实上，他们会因此感到自我肯定。然而，如果他们未能成功应对挑战，他们就会保持高度集中状态。这种持续的集中状态正是工作压力。此外，这些男性的工作本身就包含着接踵而至的挑战。这正是他们所追求的。这样的工作让他们有最大的机会去检验自己，并获得自我认可的愉悦感。但这同时也意味着，他们迟早会遇到无法应对的挑战，从而感受到工作压力。

I liked this minitheory because it explained a lot, fit with the interview material, and had an aesthetically pleasing neatness. Almost all the excerpted materials corroborated it. A few men did seem to have nonchallenging work, but they didn’t like it or didn’t respect it. So even material off the main line could be assimilated to the minitheory. I began extending the minitheory, adding to it ideas such as that successfully met challenge could augment self-confidence and so make the next challenge less daunting.

我喜欢这个微型理论，因为它解释了很多问题，与访谈内容吻合，而且结构清晰简洁，赏心悦目。几乎所有摘录的材料都印证了这一点。确实有一些男性从事的工作似乎并不具有挑战性，但他们要么不喜欢这份工作，要么不尊重它。因此，即使是偏离主线的内容也可以被纳入这个微型理论。我开始扩展这个微型理论，并添加了一些观点，例如成功应对挑战可以增强自信心，从而使下一个挑战不再那么令人畏惧。

But while this minitheory offered one basis for the integration of a good deal of material in the area of work, it didn’t deal with other material adequately, or at all. This included, for example, material on the importance of teamwork, on work as a kind of play, and on the importance of recognition. In these other sectors I had to develop other minitheories about men’s investments in work.

虽然这个微型理论为整合工作领域的大量素材提供了一个基础，但它对其他素材的处理却不够充分，甚至完全忽略了。例如，这包括关于团队合作的重要性、工作作为一种游戏以及认可的重要性等素材。在这些其他领域，我不得不发展出关于男性在工作中投入的其他微型理论。

When I turned to still other sectors of men’s lives, including their marriages and their relationships with their children, I had to develop new bases for local integration. This meant working with new excerpt files and new codings, from which I could develop new summaries and try to develop new minitheories. When I came to write chapters for the book that was the eventual project report the summaries and minitheories became the armatures of the chapters.

当我将目光转向男性生活的其他领域，包括他们的婚姻和亲子关系时，我必须为本地化研究建立新的基础。这意味着我需要处理新的摘录文件和新的编码，从中提炼出新的摘要，并尝试构建新的微型理论。最终，当我为这本最终成为项目报告的书籍撰写章节时，这些摘要和微型理论便成为了各章节的框架。

If a minitheory seems both plausible and potentially useful, I try to verify it. If there is interview material I haven’t included in the excerpt file, I might now consult it. If I know of relevant literature, I without fail examine it. But if, after having done this, the truth value of a particular minitheory seems to me high, that is, if it is well supported by the interview material and in addition makes sense, then I go on to the next excerpt file. My anticipation is that as minitheories become organized into more embracing theories, the truth value of the minitheories will be enhanced.

如果某个微型理论看起来既合情合理又有潜在用途，我会尝试验证它。如果摘录文件中缺少我未收录的访谈资料，我现在可能会查阅这些资料。如果我知道相关的文献，我一定会仔细研读。但是，如果经过这些步骤后，我认为某个微型理论的真值很高，也就是说，如果它得到了访谈资料的充分支持，并且本身也合情合理，那么我就会继续处理下一个摘录文件。我预期，随着微型理论逐渐被整合为更全面的理论，它们的真值也会随之提升。

INCLUSIVE INTEGRATION

包容性融合

Local integration brings coherence and meaning to excerpt file materials and their codings. Inclusive integration knits into a single coherent story the otherwise isolated areas of analysis that result from local integration.

本地整合使摘录的文件材料及其编码具有连贯性和意义。包容性整合则将原本因本地整合而产生的孤立分析领域编织成一个连贯的整体。

The problem in inclusive integration is to develop a framework that will include all the analyses the investigator wants to report, moves logically from one area to the next, and leads to some general conclusion. An initial framework for the report is likely already to have been outlined in the course of developing the interview guide. But that first framework will probably now require further development, or even fundamental revision, given the need to incorporate within it the understandings realized by the interviewing and analysis.

包容性整合的难点在于构建一个框架，该框架能够涵盖研究者希望报告的所有分析，逻辑清晰地从一个领域过渡到下一个领域，并最终得出总体结论。在制定访谈指南的过程中，报告的初步框架可能已经形成。但鉴于需要将访谈和分析中获得的理解纳入其中，该初步框架现在可能需要进一步完善，甚至进行根本性的修订。

It may be useful for me to review how I came to the framework I used in a report on single parents. 9 My aim in that study was to describe the life experience of custodial parents after the turmoil of separation and divorce had subsided. I anticipated a report in which I would describe the structure and functioning of the single-parent household, with the idea that this would help make sense of the problems single parents encountered. The interview guide, in consequence, focused on the tasks of daily life in single-parent households and how single parents managed them, the single parents’ relationships with their children and with others, what the single parents saw as the problems of their lives, and how they coped with those problems.

回顾一下我在一份关于单亲家庭的报告中所使用的框架的构建过程或许对我有所帮助。 9 在那项研究中，我的目标是描述单亲父母在分居和离婚的动荡过后，其子女的监护人的生活经历。我设想撰写一份报告，描述单亲家庭的结构和运作方式，希望这能帮助理解单亲父母遇到的问题。因此，访谈提纲主要围绕单亲家庭的日常生活任务以及单亲父母如何应对这些任务、单亲父母与子女及其他人的关系、单亲父母认为生活中存在的问题以及他们如何应对这些问题展开。

In analyzing the interview material, I focused first on what seemed to me the two core areas of my intended report. One was the parent’s relationships with the children, which provided the “structure” of the single-parent household. Here I noted, among other things, that in singleparent households children were likely to be treated as junior partners in household management. My other core area of analysis was how things got done in the single-parent household—how the household functioned. I described here, among other things, how employed parents might have even quite young children do some household chores.

在分析访谈材料时，我首先关注了我认为与报告主题密切相关的两个核心领域。一是父母与子女的关系，这构成了单亲家庭的“结构”。我注意到，在单亲家庭中，孩子往往被视为家庭管理中的次要角色。我的另一个核心分析领域是单亲家庭的日常运作方式——家庭如何运转。我描述了，即使是年幼的孩子，在职父母也可能会让他们承担一些家务。

At this point it seemed to me that the report in which I presented these analyses should begin with how single-parent households developed. I now did further analysis, comparing the experiences with marital dissolution of my largely divorced sample with the experiences of bereavement of a small number of widowed respondents. I hadn’t initially intended to include widowed single parents, but had interviewed a few anyway, and now I found I could use the materials of their interviews. It also seemed to me that I needed to follow descriptions of my core areas with material describing the personal life of the single parent, including relationships with other adults and issues of loneliness and of sexuality. The interviews had collected information on these issues, and I now proceeded with their analysis.

此时，我认为我所作的分析报告应该从单亲家庭的发展历程入手。于是，我进一步分析，将我样本中大部分离异人士的婚姻破裂经历与少数丧偶受访者的丧亲经历进行比较。我最初并没有打算纳入丧偶的单亲父母，但还是采访了一些，现在我发现可以利用他们的访谈资料。此外，我认为在描述核心领域之后，还需要补充一些关于单亲父母个人生活的内容，包括他们与其他成年人的关系、孤独感以及性方面的问题。访谈已经收集了关于这些问题的信息，现在我继续进行分析。

It was only when I had produced about half the report that I worked out how the report should conclude, although that was something I had worried about as soon as I began to write. What seemed an appropriate conclusion was to identify what were the problems faced by single parents and how they coped with them. I found that the interviews had collected the needed information, and again I was able to proceed with analysis in the area.

直到我完成了报告的一半左右，才最终确定报告的结尾，尽管从一开始写作我就对此感到担忧。我认为合适的结尾是找出单亲父母面临的问题以及他们如何应对这些问题。我发现访谈已经收集到了所需的信息，因此我得以继续进行这方面的分析。

As I look back, it seems to me that much of the work developing the report’s story line took place away from my desk, as I repeatedly considered what would constitute a satisfactory report. This strikes me as the way I have customarily developed the framework for a report. Very early in the study I had a general idea of what issues I would eventually discuss. This sense of the issues to be discussed gave shape to the interview guide and later suggested the core areas for analysis. On achieving local integration in the core areas, I could then think further about what might be the shape of the final report and what materials should precede and follow the core areas. But the final framework wasn’t entirely in place until I had finished the report.

回想起来，我觉得报告叙事结构的构建工作大部分是在办公桌之外完成的，因为我一直在反复思考一份合格的报告应该包含哪些内容。这似乎正是我构建报告框架的惯常方式。在研究初期，我就对最终要探讨的问题有了大致的构想。这种对议题的把握为访谈提纲奠定了基础，并最终确定了分析的核心领域。在核心领域实现本地化整合之后，我才能进一步思考最终报告的结构，以及核心领域前后应该包含哪些材料。但直到报告完成，最终的框架才算完全成型。

Other investigators with whom I have worked seem to have proceeded in roughly the same way I did. They, too, began with a rather sketchy framework, developing it further as they went along, but did not have everything in place until they had their report nearly done.

其他与我共事的调查人员似乎也采取了与我大致相同的方法。他们也都是先从一个比较粗略的框架开始，然后随着调查的深入不断完善，但直到报告接近完成时，所有细节才最终确定下来。

VISUAL DISPLAY

视觉显示

Many researchers find visual display of the elements of their story a valuable means of achieving both local integration and inclusive integration. Miles and Huberman recommend diagrams on paper, with lines linking related issues, to display graphically the conceptual framework of the final report. 10 Becker suggests putting data and memos about the data on file cards that can then be spread on a large flat surface and arranged and rearranged until they achieve a logical sequence. 11 Agar suggests finding an empty classroom full of blackboards on which can be drawn maps of concepts and their interrelations. 12

许多研究人员发现，将研究内容以可视化的方式呈现，是实现本地化和包容性融合的有效途径。迈尔斯和胡伯曼建议在纸上绘制图表，用线条连接相关问题，以图形化的方式展示最终报告的概念框架。贝克尔建议将数据和相关备忘录写在卡片上，然后将卡片铺在大的平面上，反复排列调整，直到形成逻辑顺序。阿加尔建议找一间空教室，教室里要有黑板，可以在黑板上绘制概念图及其相互关系。

I don’t much use visual display myself, although I do often make tentative lists of chapters or chapter sections in what I believe to be logical order. But visual display as a way of achieving local or inclusive integration is so often recommended that researchers who are just beginning to work with qualitative interview material might want to see whether this approach works for them.

我本人不太常用视觉展示，虽然我经常会根据自己的理解，按逻辑顺序列出章节或章节节选的初步清单。但由于视觉展示作为一种实现本地化或包容性整合的方法经常被推荐，因此刚开始使用定性访谈材料的研究人员或许可以尝试一下这种方法是否适合他们。

A GENERALIZED ISSUE-FOCUSED REPORT

一份以问题为重点的综合报告

Most studies of family life have been based on interviews. Other methods don’t work nearly as well in capturing family life: adequate observation of families is intrusive and time consuming, and family records such as letters, diaries, and photographs tend to be sparse and to emphasize the ceremonial. Interviews, however, can obtain information not only about family events but also about the ordinarily unvoiced perceptions and emotions that underlie family dynamics. Mirra Komarovsky’s Blue-Collar Marriage 13 is among the earliest of the studies to ask how a type of family or type of marriage worked, although still earlier interview-based studies of families had examined how families dealt with the Great Depression and how men and women responded to divorce. 14

大多数家庭生活研究都基于访谈。其他方法在捕捉家庭生活方面远不如访谈有效：对家庭进行充分的观察既费时又费力，而信件、日记和照片等家庭记录往往稀少，且侧重于仪式性内容。然而，访谈不仅可以获取家庭事件的信息，还可以获取通常不为人知的、隐藏在家庭动态背后的感知和情感。米拉·科马罗夫斯基的《蓝领婚姻》是最早探讨某种家庭或婚姻类型如何运作的研究之一，尽管更早的基于访谈的家庭研究已经考察了家庭如何应对大萧条以及男女如何应对离婚。

Komarovsky interviewed husbands and wives in 58 blue-collar marriages. Her aim was to learn how blue-collar marriages were different from other marriages and thus how social class affects marriage. Her eligibility criteria for respondents required that, in addition to being married, they be white native-born Protestants, without any college education, and with the husband in a blue-collar occupation. She also wanted respondents to be currently raising children. She obtained the names of her couples from a city directory, from membership lists of Protestant churches, and, in two instances, from recommendations by other respondents.

科马罗夫斯基采访了58对蓝领夫妇。她的目的是了解蓝领婚姻与其他婚姻有何不同，以及社会阶层如何影响婚姻。她对受访者的资格要求是：除了已婚之外，他们必须是白人、土生土长的新教徒，没有大学学历，并且丈夫从事蓝领工作。她还希望受访者目前正在抚养子女。她从城市名录、新教教堂的成员名单中获取了这些夫妇的姓名，并在两个案例中，通过其他受访者的推荐获得了他们的信息。

Two 2-hour interviews were held with wives, and a third 2-hour interview with the husband. The interviews were for the most part qualitative, “within a carefully worked out guide,” but also included questions and checklists to be asked of everyone. Komarovsky did not do much tape-recording: her study was conducted before tape recorders were common household equipment, and she thought that her respondents would be made uncomfortable by them. Instead, her interviewers were required to take detailed notes.

研究人员对妻子进行了两次时长两小时的访谈，并对丈夫进行了第三次时长两小时的访谈。访谈主要采用定性方法，“遵循精心设计的访谈提纲”，但也包含一些需要询问所有受访者的问题和清单。科马罗夫斯基并没有进行大量的录音：她的研究是在录音机尚未普及的年代进行的，她认为录音会让受访者感到不自在。因此，她要求访谈员做详细的笔记。

Some of the codings of responses appear to be immediately plausible categorizations of respondents’ comments. For example, husbands were asked “How does marriage change a man’s life?” and wives were asked the parallel question “How does marriage change a woman’s life?” Komarovsky used the coding “escape from home” to characterize responses like these:

有些回答的编码似乎是对受访者评论的直接合理的分类。例如，丈夫被问到“婚姻如何改变男人的生活？”，妻子也被问到类似的问题“婚姻如何改变女人的生活？”。科马罗夫斯基使用“逃离家庭”这一编码来描述类似这样的回答：

He’s got his own place and he’s boss. With my mother, I had to come home when she said or I wouldn’t get anything to eat. Now I can come and go whenever I like. [ A husband’s comment ]

他有自己的房子，他说了算。以前跟我妈住的时候，她让我回家我就得回家，不然就没饭吃。现在我可以想来就来，想走就走。[丈夫的评论]

One reason I got married at sixteen was to get away from home…. They would tell us kids that they stayed together for our sakes—that made us feel real good. [ A wife’s comment ] 15

我十六岁结婚的原因之一就是想离开家……他们会告诉我们这些孩子，他们是为了我们才维持婚姻的——这让我们感觉很好。[妻子的评论] 15

Other codings seem to be expressions of interest Komarovsky brought to the study. Thus, couples were assessed on the extent to which their marriage was close or distant and on the extent to which the spouse was a friend, even when closeness and distance weren’t directly discussed by the spouses. In addition to “closeness,” codes dealing with adequacy of marital communication and with level of marital happiness appear to have been brought to the study by Komarovsky.

其他编码似乎体现了科马罗夫斯基对这项研究的兴趣。因此，即使夫妻双方并未直接讨论亲密或疏远的程度，研究人员也会评估他们的婚姻关系亲密或疏远的程度，以及配偶作为朋友的程度。除了“亲密程度”之外，科马罗夫斯基似乎还为这项研究引入了与婚姻沟通是否充分以及婚姻幸福程度相关的编码。

Still other codings seem to be neither a priori categories nor immediate inferences from responses. These are possibly the most interesting. They include “the pull of the male clique,” which in Komarovsky’s view “retarded the domestication or the marital socialization of the husband.” This coding, and others like it, must have come from a good deal of thought about the meaning of responses.

还有一些编码似乎既非先验类别，也非对回答的直接推断。这些编码或许最为有趣。例如，“男性小团体的吸引力”，在科马罗夫斯基看来，这种吸引力“阻碍了丈夫的驯化或婚姻社会化”。这种编码以及其他类似的编码，必然是经过对回答含义的深入思考而得出的。

The sequence of material presented in Komarovsky’s book begins with a description of the respondents and proceeds to the respondents’ motivations for marriage, the division of labor in their marriages, their marital communication, and the relative power of the two spouses in the marriage. It then proceeds to kin ties, economic and occupational issues, the couples’ use of leisure, and, finally, the implications of the findings. Sorting of materials was undoubtedly done within this structure and probably was straightforward.

科马罗夫斯基著作中呈现的材料顺序首先描述了受访者，然后探讨了他们的结婚动机、婚姻中的劳动分工、夫妻沟通以及夫妻双方在婚姻中的相对权力。接下来，论述了亲属关系、经济和职业问题、夫妻的休闲活动，最后总结了研究结果的意义。毫无疑问，材料的整理是按照这一结构进行的，而且可能相当直接。

Local integration may well have absorbed most analytic time and energy. Each chapter seems to have been treated almost as a separate study. Chapter 5, “The Marriage Dialogue: Expectations,” begins by setting out the problem to which it will attend: Do working-class husbands and wives share the desire and expectation of middle-class husbands and wives that their marriages will be relationships of communicative intimacy? The data used to answer this question came primarily from respondents’ reactions to vignettes describing problems in marital communication and answers to questions about the qualities of a good husband and wife.

本地化分析或许占据了大部分的分析时间和精力。每一章似乎都被视为一项独立的研究。第五章“婚姻对话：期望”开篇便提出了本章要探讨的问题：工人阶级夫妇是否像中产阶级夫妇一样，渴望并期望他们的婚姻能够建立在沟通亲密的关系之上？用于回答这个问题的数据主要来自受访者对描述婚姻沟通问题的短文的反应，以及他们对关于好丈夫和好妻子应具备的品质的回答。

The chapter reports that couples who shared middle-class ideals regarding intimacy were likely to be better educated. If not, the wives were better educated and the husbands aspired to upward social mobility. Other blue-collar couples, however, are presented as happy despite little talk that could be called intimate. To show how such a marriage might work, Komarovsky presents a case study of a husband and wife who were happy although noncommunicative. Komarovsky’s conclusion is that while working-class marriages of a certain sort display the communicative ideals of middle-class marriages, other working-class marriages do not—and they aren’t necessarily unhappy.

本章指出，那些在亲密关系方面持有中产阶级理想的夫妇往往受过更好的教育。即便并非如此，妻子也往往受过更好的教育，而丈夫则渴望向上流动。然而，其他一些蓝领夫妇尽管鲜少进行可以称之为亲密的交流，却依然幸福美满。为了说明这种婚姻模式的运作方式，科马罗夫斯基举了一个案例研究，讲述了一对夫妻虽然缺乏沟通，却依然幸福美满的故事。科马罗夫斯基的结论是，虽然某些类型的工人阶级婚姻展现出中产阶级婚姻中沟通的理想，但其他类型的工人阶级婚姻则不然——而且这些婚姻也并非一定不幸福。

Komarovsky achieves local integration in this chapter by posing and then resolving the question of intimacy in working-class marriages. She first proposes a minitheory about which of her respondent couples would display communicative intimacy and then presents material that illustrates and supports the minitheory. She then presents further material that suggests necessary qualifications in the minitheory. Other chapters display the same movement from problem statement to minitheory, to supporting data, to qualifications, and finally, to conclusions. Most chapters could stand alone as sector reports.

科马罗夫斯基在本章中通过提出并解决工人阶级婚姻中的亲密关系问题，实现了本土化的整合。她首先提出了一个关于哪些受访夫妇会展现出沟通型亲密关系的微型理论，然后呈现了例证和支持该微型理论的材料。接着，她又提供了进一步的材料，指出了该微型理论中必要的修正。其他章节也呈现出同样的结构：从问题陈述到微型理论，再到佐证数据、修正，最后得出结论。大多数章节都可以作为独立的行业报告。

Komarovsky accomplishes inclusive integration by leading the reader from the early days of a couple’s marriage and the couple’s division of marital labor to what appears to be her primary concern, the closeness of the present marriage. That occupies the bulk of the book. At the end, chapters are added on economic and occupational issues as they may affect a couple’s marriage and on how couples use leisure. A final chapter, “Theoretical and Methodological Conclusions,” is intended to wrap up the whole thing.

科马罗夫斯基通过引导读者从一对夫妇婚姻初期及其分工入手，逐步过渡到她似乎最为关注的当下婚姻亲密关系，从而实现了包容性的整合。这部分内容占据了本书的大部分篇幅。在书的结尾，她又增加了关于经济和职业问题如何影响夫妻婚姻以及夫妻如何利用休闲时间的章节。最后一章“理论与方法论结论”旨在为全书画上句号。

How good was Komarovsky’s analysis? It was certainly good enough to enable her to influence thinking about working-class marriage and about the problems, as well as benefits, of presumably supportive relationships with friends and kin. (Komarovsky calls the wife’s continued closeness to her mother “the working-class marriage triangle.”)

科马罗夫斯基的分析究竟有多出色？她的分析无疑足以影响人们对工人阶级婚姻以及与亲友之间看似相互扶持的关系所带来的问题和益处的思考。（科马罗夫斯基将妻子与母亲的持续亲密关系称为“工人阶级婚姻三角”。）

Maybe more could have been learned about the lives of the husbands and wives had there been less focus on marital communication and less reliance on checklists. There is almost nothing on courtship. Sex is discussed, but there is little discussion of love and affection. There is surprisingly little about children and the problems of parenting: about all there is appears in a section where Komarovsky notes that parents sometimes quarreled over how the children should be raised.

如果少一些对婚姻沟通的关注，少一些对清单的依赖，或许我们能更深入地了解夫妻的生活。书中几乎没有提及恋爱过程。虽然讨论了性，但很少谈及爱情和情感。令人惊讶的是，书中对孩子和育儿问题的着墨也少得可怜：仅有的几处提及是在科马罗夫斯基指出父母有时会因为如何养育孩子而争吵的章节中。

More than the most authors of qualitative studies, Komarovsky is concerned with quantification. She regularly reports the proportion of cases that had particular characteristics: that, for example, exhibited communicative distance. Because the sample was not representative of any meaningful universe, the proportions cannot be taken as estimates of anything; they are only descriptive of Komarovsky’s sample. Still, reporting proportions does suggest the strength with which the sample supports generalizations, and it gives the reader reason for confidence in the probity of the analysis.

与大多数定性研究的作者相比，科马罗夫斯基更注重量化。她经常报告具有特定特征的案例比例，例如，表现出沟通距离的案例。由于样本并不代表任何有意义的总体，这些比例不能被视为任何估计值；它们仅仅是对科马罗夫斯基样本的描述。尽管如此，报告比例确实表明了样本对概括性结论的支持力度，并让读者有理由相信分析的严谨性。

In a few respects, the study’s methods place the study in an earlier era of qualitative work. Quotations have the choppy quality that comes from being based on notes rather than tape recordings. There is a pervasive concern with demonstrating that there is legitimacy in qualitative work even though it may appear less scientific than large-scale surveys. And the data gathered included, at least for my taste, too much material regarding expectations and reactions to hypothetical vignettes and not enough regarding ongoing life. But the analysis is thoughtful and thorough, and if the resulting picture is not as vivid as it might be, it is thoroughly credible.

在某些方面，这项研究的方法使其更接近早期定性研究的水平。引文由于基于笔记而非录音，显得不够流畅自然。尽管定性研究可能不如大规模调查那样科学严谨，但研究者仍然非常注重证明其合法性。而且，至少在我看来，收集到的数据中关于对假设情景的预期和反应的内容过多，而关于日常生活的内容则相对较少。不过，分析过程严谨细致，即便最终呈现的图景不够生动，也依然具有很强的可信度。

AN ISSUE-FOCUSED REPORT AT THE LEVEL OF CONCRETE MATERIAL

一份聚焦具体问题的报告

An example of how concrete excerpts can be organized to tell a story is provided by Ronald Fraser’s Blood of Spain . Fraser’s aim was to weave a history of the Spanish Civil War not from the perspective of its leaders but, rather, from the perspective of the ordinary people swept up in it. He conducted more than three hundred interviews in order to, in his words, “describe the major contours of the war through eye-witness narration.” 16

罗纳德·弗雷泽的《西班牙之血》一书就是一个很好的例子，它展示了如何组织具体的摘录来讲述一个故事。弗雷泽的目标是，不是从领导人的视角，而是从卷入这场战争的普通民众的视角来叙述西班牙内战的历史。他进行了三百多次采访，用他自己的话说，就是“通过目击者的叙述来描绘这场战争的主要轮廓”。

Although Fraser does not tell us his analytic methods, he must have coded his interview responses for the time in the war they referred to, the particular region they gave information on, and whether their perspective was Republican or Nationalist. His sorting would then have been straightforward: collect materials by time and, within time, by event. Local integration would require that he work out what descriptions he would give of the historical context and how he would introduce the interview materials; how much space he would give particular perspectives; which interview excerpts he would quote and which he would paraphrase; and when he would enter the report in his own voice and when he would have respondents speak. Inclusive integration would have been a matter of organizing events temporally.

尽管弗雷泽没有告诉我们他的分析方法，但他肯定对访谈内容进行了编码，编码依据包括访谈中提及的战争时期、受访者提供信息的具体地区，以及他们的立场是共和派还是民族主义派。这样一来，他的分类工作就非常简单：先按时间收集资料，再按同一时间点的事件进行分类。本地化整合则要求他事先构思好如何描述历史背景、如何引入访谈资料、如何分配篇幅来阐述特定观点、哪些访谈摘录需要直接引用、哪些需要转述，以及何时用自己的语言叙述报告内容，何时让受访者发言。包容性整合则意味着按时间顺序组织事件。

Fraser begins his book with interview excerpts describing the years before the war, when Spain was governed by the Left. He sketches the opposition to the government by business leaders, the military, and the church and shows the hatred and fear that existed between the classes. Then he tells us how the war started, through interviews with those who had participated in the uprising of army units in Morocco in July, 1936. He uses further interview excerpts to display the reaction in mainland Spain to the news of the uprising.

弗雷泽在书中以访谈摘录开篇，描述了战前西班牙左翼执政时期的情形。他勾勒出商界领袖、军方和教会对政府的反对，展现了阶级之间存在的仇恨和恐惧。随后，他通过对参与1936年7月摩洛哥军队起义者的采访，讲述了战争的起因。他还引用其他访谈摘录，展现了西班牙本土对起义消息的反应。

Throughout the book Fraser places his interview excerpts and paraphrasings within their historical context. The historical context, in turn, is illuminated by the interview excerpts. His style may be suggested by the following paragraph from the book, in which he describes the resignation of one leftist government and the formation of another:

在整本书中，弗雷泽都将他的访谈摘录和转述置于历史背景之中。反过来，访谈摘录也阐明了历史背景。他的写作风格可以从书中以下段落中窥见一斑，他在这段文字中描述了一个左翼政府的辞职和另一个左翼政府的组建：

In the evening the government resigned. A new government … was formed. To a Left Republican school teacher, Regulo Martinez, the new government seemed a prudent move…. But the people took the news badly. “Even members of my own party—Azana’s party—began tearing up their membership cards. The masses wanted revenge, revolution. They threw caution to the wind; courage and resolution were the order of the day …”

当晚，政府辞职。新政府……成立了。对于左翼共和党教师雷古洛·马丁内斯来说，新政府的成立似乎是一个明智之举……但民众对此反应强烈。“就连我所在的党——阿扎纳的党——的成员也开始撕毁他们的党员证。群众想要复仇，想要革命。他们抛开一切顾虑；勇气和决心成了当时的准则……”

Eraser’s style provides a “you are there” sense of the disorganization that accompanied the early days of the war, the breakdown in civil order, the excitement and hope of participating in heroic action, and the pervasive blindness on both sides to the misery the war would bring.

埃拉瑟的风格营造了一种“身临其境”的感觉，展现了战争初期混乱的局面、社会秩序的崩溃、参与英勇行动的兴奋和希望，以及交战双方对战争将带来的苦难的普遍视而不见。

Fraser goes on to describe, in the same way, the early days of the war, in which battles sprang up between isolated units distant from the larger forces and everywhere people acted on thin information and often mistaken surmise. As his story moves on to the full-scale war, Fraser presents excerpts from respondents that describe the callousness of leaders, the advent of atrocity and counteratrocity, the many casually ordered deaths, and the fewer narrow escapes. In passing, Fraser reproduces published materials of the time, including a full-page announcement from a rightwing newspaper pleading for the confidence of readers.
