Finally, Fraser describes the end of the war and the advent of the Franco government.

弗雷泽继续以同样的方式描述了战争初期的情况：孤立的部队远离主力部队，各自为战，人们的行动往往基于片面的信息和错误的猜测。随着故事进入全面战争阶段，弗雷泽引用了一些受访者的证词，描述了领导人的冷酷无情、暴行和反暴行的出现、许多随意下令的杀戮以及少数侥幸逃脱的案例。弗雷泽还顺带引用了当时的出版物，包括一份右翼报纸刊登的整版公告，恳求读者给予信任。最后，弗雷泽描述了战争的结束和佛朗哥政府的建立。

The book does wonderfully well in providing a sense of the experience of the Spanish Civil War for a reader removed from it in time and space. It may, perhaps, give disproportionate space to the vivid. This bias is understandable; the ordinary does not hold our attention. Nevertheless, there is enough in the book to make evident the torn texture of daily life and the numbed reality of a daily round carried on against a backdrop of catastrophe.

这本书出色地展现了西班牙内战的种种经历，即使读者身处遥远的时空之外，也能感同身受。或许，它对生动鲜活的描写着墨过多。这种倾向可以理解；平凡的事物往往难以吸引我们的注意力。然而，书中也足以展现战争背景下，人们日常生活的支离破碎，以及日复一日麻木不仁的现实。

CASE-FOCUSED ANALYSIS

案例聚焦分析

CONCRETE CASES

具体案例

Feature stories in newspapers and magazines regularly begin with an account of a particular case. Our interest is much more likely to be attracted by the concrete and particular than by the abstract and general. And we understand the concrete more easily: we can identify with actual people and immediately grasp real situations whereas the abstract and general requires us to understand in a more secondary way.

报纸和杂志上的专题报道通常以具体案例开篇。我们更容易被具体、具体的事件吸引，而不是抽象、笼统的话题。而且，我们更容易理解具体的事情：我们可以与真实的人物产生共鸣，并立即把握真实的情境；而抽象、笼统的话题则需要我们进行更深层次的理解。

What concrete case studies of individuals do superbly is make the reader aware of the respondents’ experience within the context of their lives: this is what it is like to be this person in this situation. Case studies take readers into respondents’ lives.

案例研究最出色的地方在于，它能让读者了解受访者在特定生活情境下的经历：这就是这个人身处这种境况的感受。案例研究带领读者走进受访者的生活。

In addition, case studies regularly imply generalizations, although without assurance of their validity. Readers take from case studies a sense of the case as exemplary, with general lessons to teach. They believe themselves to be learning not just about particular people but about people who are like them, not just about particular situations but about a class of situations.

此外，案例研究通常包含概括性的结论，尽管这些结论的有效性无法保证。读者从案例研究中得出的结论往往具有代表性，可以从中汲取普遍经验。他们认为自己不仅在了解特定人物，也在了解与他们相似的人群；不仅在了解特定情境，也在了解一类情境。

Because investigators, as well as readers, grasp concrete cases more easily than abstract models, constructing case studies can be useful even in an issue-focused analysis. I have found that when I am unable to work out a persuasive conceptual scheme or unsure of what to emphasize in achieving local integration or inclusive integration, I am helped by putting together the materials of an individual case. I gain from the experience of case construction a more immediate understanding of the situation of respondents, and I can then more easily imagine how that situation might be presented and explained. For example, my first step in the analysis of data dealing with single parents’ lives was to construct two extensive case studies. With them at hand, I could see how central was the issue of vulnerability to overload.

由于研究人员和读者都更容易理解具体案例而非抽象模型，因此即使在以问题为导向的分析中，构建案例研究也十分有用。我发现，当我无法构建一个令人信服的概念框架，或者不确定在实现本地融合或包容性融合时应该强调什么时，收集个案资料会很有帮助。通过构建案例，我能更直接地了解受访者的处境，从而更容易地想象如何呈现和解释这种情况。例如，在分析有关单亲父母生活的数据时，我的第一步是构建两个详尽的案例研究。有了这些案例研究，我就能清楚地看到，单亲父母容易超负荷的问题是多么重要。

Producing a case study begins with sorting. Material that deals with the same issue must be brought together no matter where the material originally appeared in the interview transcripts. The material is then organized into a story of that issue. In the single-parent study, “fights with children” was one grouping of material. Integrating is likely to be done in two stages: a first stage of bringing together material into coherent scenes—the case-study parallel to the local integration of an issue-focused analysis—and a second stage of inclusive integration, in which scenes are linked into a coherent story. The investigator may also want occasionally or regularly to introduce a “voice-over,” that is, a paragraph or page of commentary in which the reader is told what the case materials mean or what general processes they illustrate.

案例研究的撰写始于整理。无论素材最初出现在访谈记录的哪个位置，只要涉及同一主题，都必须将其汇集在一起。然后，将这些素材组织成一个关于该主题的故事。在单亲家庭研究中，“与子女争吵”就是其中一组素材。整合通常分两个阶段进行：第一阶段是将素材整合为连贯的场景——案例研究中这类似于以问题为中心的分析的局部整合——第二阶段是包容性整合，即将各个场景连接成一个连贯的故事。研究者可能还会不时或定期地加入“旁白”，即一段或几页的评论，向读者解释案例素材的含义或它们所揭示的一般过程。

It takes me several drafts to arrive at an organization of interview material I feel presents a case properly. In my first drafts of a case study I include too much; I want to preserve respondents’ words, as if I were a curator of language. Only as I read and reread the material can I see where points are being made, what is superfluous, and where the argument has begun to veer off the track. New drafts are likely to suggest additional voice-overs, or better ones. At the end I will have to do a final editing to eliminate redundancies, straighten out the story line, and ensure that the case reads as well as it can. A good case study may make a reader believe that putting it together was easily done, but I have not found this to be true.

我需要反复修改才能最终整理出一份我认为能够恰当呈现案例的访谈材料。在案例研究的初稿中，我往往会加入过多的内容；我希望尽可能保留受访者的原话，就像我是语言的策展人一样。只有反复阅读这些材料，我才能分辨出哪些是重点，哪些是多余的，以及论证何时开始偏离主题。新的草稿往往会让我想到需要添加或改进旁白。最后，我还要进行最终编辑，删除冗余内容，理顺叙事思路，确保案例尽可能流畅易读。一篇优秀的案例研究可能会让读者觉得它很容易完成，但我发现事实并非如此。

An interesting question is the extent to which the investigator who constructs a case study intends from the beginning of the analysis to illustrate a particular conception or provide support for a particular theory. My guess is that most often the investigator’s understanding and the developing organization of the case material interact. The investigator’s preconceptions help to decide the initial organization of the material, but then the material forces modification of the investigator’s thinking, which then leads the investigator to revise the organization of materials, and so on for several iterations.

一个有趣的问题是，研究者在构建案例研究时，从分析之初就打算阐明某种特定概念或支持某种特定理论，这种意图究竟有多大？我的猜测是，研究者的理解与案例材料的逐步组织往往相互影响。研究者的先入之见有助于确定材料的初始组织方式，但随后材料本身会促使研究者修正其思路，进而修改材料的组织方式，如此反复多次。

In the two examples given here of the case-study approach, the investigators make different choices regarding explicit generalization. Oscar Lewis, in an introduction to his cases, proposes that from them one can infer the grand, inclusive hypothesis that the lives described in the book were shaped by a “culture of poverty.” Ronald Blythe is more circumspect in his treatment of case material. But he too seems to have a more general story in mind for which he intends his study to provide an instance: that the organization of society structures and constrains individual lives, but the human spirit, given the least opportunity, will break through the limitations that social organization imposes.

在本文列举的两个案例研究方法案例中，研究者在明确的概括性结论方面做出了不同的选择。奥斯卡·刘易斯在其案例的引言中提出，从这些案例中可以推断出一个宏大的、包容性的假设，即书中描述的生活是由一种“贫困文化”塑造的。罗纳德·布莱斯在处理案例材料时则更为谨慎。但他似乎也怀有一个更为普遍的设想，并希望通过他的研究来阐释这一设想：社会组织塑造并限制了个人生活，但只要给予人类精神最微小的机会，就能突破社会组织所施加的限制。

TWO CASE-FOCUSED REPORTS AT THE LEVEL OF CONCRETE MATERIAL

两份以具体材料为层面的案例分析报告

In Children of Sanchez: Autobiography of A Mexican Family , Oscar Lewis presents the autobiographies of the four children of Jesus Sanchez, a restaurant worker in Mexico City. 17 Lewis edited and rearranged segments of his interview transcripts so that the lives of his respondents are told by the respondents themselves. He begins the book by having Jesus Sanchez describe coming to Mexico City to make a life for himself. He ends the book with Jesus Sanchez speaking of his present life as an older man who has succeeded, finally, in obtaining title to a dwelling of his own. Between this beginning and end, Lewis has the children describe their lives—in the first section, their childhoods; in the second, their early adulthoods; in the third, their current lives.

在《桑切斯家的孩子们：一个墨西哥家庭的自传》一书中，奥斯卡·刘易斯呈现了墨西哥城餐馆员工赫苏斯·桑切斯的四个孩子的自传。刘易斯编辑并重新编排了访谈记录的部分内容，使受访者能够亲自讲述他们的生活。本书以赫苏斯·桑切斯讲述他来到墨西哥城闯荡人生的经历开篇，并以他晚年终于拥有自己房产的现状作结。在开头和结尾之间，刘易斯让孩子们分别讲述他们的生活——第一部分是他们的童年；第二部分是他们的青年时期；第三部分是他们现在的生活。

Lewis’s editing is intentionally novelistic. The first of the children to be presented is Manuel, the oldest. The excerpt from Manuel’s interviews that Lewis chooses as Manuel’s introduction has the quality of an early memory, like the beginning of Joyce’s Portrait of the Artist As a Young Man . But it also sets the stage for what follows.

刘易斯的编辑手法刻意营造出小说般的风格。首先出场的是孩子们中的老大曼努埃尔。刘易斯选择的曼努埃尔访谈摘录作为曼努埃尔的引言，这段文字如同早期记忆一般，如同乔伊斯《青年艺术家画像》的开头。但它也为接下来的故事埋下了伏笔。

I was eight years old when my mother died. I was asleep on a mat on the floor next to my brother Roberto. My little sisters, Consuela and Marta, slept on the bed with my Mama and Papa.

我八岁那年母亲去世了。当时我睡在地板上的垫子上，旁边是哥哥罗伯托。我的妹妹康苏埃拉和玛尔塔则和爸爸妈妈一起睡在床上。

Here we are introduced all at once, in the space of three sentences, to the main characters, to the poverty that defines them, and to the mother’s death that was the tragic beginning of their lives with a father we later see to be brusque and resentful. We are also introduced to what will be the dominant tone of all the narratives: a flat, matter-of-fact description of intensely emotional events.

短短三句话，我们就一下子认识了主要人物，了解了他们所处的贫困环境，以及母亲的去世——这悲剧开启了他们与父亲共同生活的序幕，而我们后来发现，父亲性格粗暴，充满怨恨。同时，我们也感受到了贯穿所有叙事的主旋律：一种平铺直叙、不加修饰的描述，讲述着那些充满强烈情感的事件。

The last sentence of this first section of Manuel’s account is a statement of the event that ended his childhood: “That’s how we got married: I had just turned fifteen and she was nineteen.” By his marriage, Manuel established himself as an adult despite his age. Consider how much control of his material Lewis needed to be able to find just the right quotations with which to begin and end this section.

曼努埃尔叙述的第一部分最后一句话，描述了结束他童年的那件事：“我们就是这样结婚的：我刚满十五岁，她十九岁。” 通过婚姻，曼努埃尔尽管年纪尚小，却已确立了自己成年人的地位。想想路易斯需要对素材多么精通，才能找到恰到好处的引文来开头和结尾。

Lewis next introduces Roberto, the younger brother, who will describe recurrent problems with the law. The quotation with which Lewis has him introduce himself is “I started stealing things from my own house when I was small.” The theme of thieving is presented at once.

接下来，路易斯介绍了弟弟罗伯托，他将讲述自己屡次触犯法律的经历。路易斯让他自我介绍时引用了一句话：“我从小就开始偷自己家里的东西。” 盗窃的主题由此展开。

The end-of-childhood statement that Lewis gives Roberto, with which Lewis ends the first section of Roberto’s narrative, is “Then I joined the army, first because I wanted to be a soldier, but most of all, because it was getting impossible for me at home.” And so we learn of another way of establishing adulthood.

刘易斯在罗伯托叙述的第一部分结尾，用一句话宣告了罗伯托的童年结束：“然后我参军了，首先是因为我想当兵，但最重要的是，因为我在家里的日子越来越难熬。” 由此，我们了解到另一种确立成年的方式。

While maintaining the autobiographical form, Lewis was able to introduce descriptions of the social institutions that structured low-income Mexican life. Here, for example, is Manuel on seeking admission to the United States to work as a migrant laborer:

在保持自传体形式的同时，刘易斯还融入了对构成墨西哥低收入人群生活的社会制度的描述。例如，以下是曼努埃尔寻求进入美国以从事移民劳工工作的经历：

We got in line [in front of the U.S. Customs House] and waited. There were people from all ends of the Republic, all dirty, in rags, and starving.… Everybody was anxious to get through; I understood their desperation because I felt the same way.

我们在美国海关大楼前排队等候。那里聚集了来自全国各地的人，个个衣衫褴褛，脏兮兮的，饥肠辘辘……每个人都急切地想要通过；我理解他们的绝望，因为我也感同身受。

Then the squeezing and pushing began.… The shoving got worse. I was standing between two big guys, and when I was being smothered and felt myself walled in, I grabbed the two of them around their necks and pulled myself up.… The Immigration Office was at the height of a flight of stairs. Well, these guys began going up the stairs with me hanging from them; otherwise I wouldn’t have made it.…

然后就开始了挤压和推搡……推搡越来越厉害。我站在两个大块头中间，感觉快要窒息，被挤得动弹不得，于是我抓住他们的脖子，把自己拉了上去……移民局在楼梯顶端。结果，这两个家伙带着我一起往楼上爬；不然我肯定上不去……

When I reached the office, I got nervous. We were all convinced that the Immigration Officer knew who was lying and who wasn’t.… Then, “Thank God and the Holy Mother,” I said to myself, “I think they are going to let me in.” …

到了办公室，我开始紧张起来。我们都确信移民官能分辨出谁在撒谎，谁在说谎……然后，我对自己说：“感谢上帝和圣母玛利亚，我想他们会放我进去的。”……

Always, in reading autobiographical accounts, we give some attention to the credibility of the narrator. Especially do we do this when narrators talk about themselves. Because Lewis presents the views of four siblings, we hear not only the self-appraisals of each but the appraisals made of them by their siblings. After hearing Roberto deprecate himself, it is instructive to have his brother, Manuel, tell us, “Roberto was really very noble, the most noble in the family.”

在阅读自传时，我们总会关注叙述者的可信度。尤其当叙述者谈论自己时，更是如此。由于路易斯呈现了四兄妹的观点，我们不仅能听到他们各自的自我评价，还能听到兄弟姐妹对他们的评价。在听到罗伯托贬低自己之后，他的兄弟曼努埃尔告诉我们：“罗伯托其实非常高尚，是家里最高尚的人。” 这句话颇具启发意义。

The last words of the book are the ruminations of Jesus Sanchez about the meaning of his life. Lewis proposes in his introduction that the message of his book is the way the culture of poverty works to prevent people from rising. But the final statement of Jesus Sanchez suggests that his story may have a different message. Here are the words with which Children of Sanchez ends:

本书的结尾是耶稣·桑切斯对人生意义的沉思。路易斯在引言中提出，本书的主旨在于揭示贫困文化如何阻碍人们向上流动。但耶稣·桑切斯的最后陈述表明，他的故事或许蕴含着不同的信息。以下是《桑切斯的孩子们》的结尾：

I struggled and worked day and night to establish my home, a poor home, as you can see, but I have my happy moments with my grandchildren. It is first for God and then for my grandchildren that I’m on my feet, plugging away.… I hope God will allow me to be with them until they can earn their own living.… I want to leave them a room, that’s my ambition; to build that little house, one or two rooms or three so that each child will have a home and so they can live there together.… It will be a protection for them when I fall down and don’t get up again.

我日夜辛劳，努力建立起我的家——一个简陋的家，正如你所见——但我与孙辈们在一起的时光无比幸福。我首先是为了上帝，其次是为了我的孙辈们，我才如此坚持不懈地努力……我祈求上帝让我陪伴他们，直到他们能够自食其力……我渴望为他们留下一间房子，这是我的愿望；我想建一座小房子，一间、两间，或者三间，让每个孩子都能拥有一个家，让他们可以一起生活……当我跌倒再也爬不起来时，这将是他们的庇护。

This final speech of Jesus Sanchez suggests that the book is not about poverty as much as it is about fathers and children. The book’s title— The Children of Sanchez , not The Lives of Members of a Poor Family —suggests that Lewis may have recognized this. Although many stories may be found in the book, the one that is for me the most compelling is Sanchez’s story of how he came to Mexico City as a young man in search of a better life, rapidly became the father to four children by his wife and to other children by another woman, provided for his children and raised them—while bitterly resenting having to do so—and discovered at the end that his children’s lives, filled with troubles about which he knew little and yet in some fundamental way shaped by him, and the lives of his children’s children, had become the ultimate justification for all his struggles.

赫苏斯·桑切斯的这段最后演讲表明，这本书与其说是关于贫困，不如说是关于父子关系。书名——《桑切斯的孩子们》，而非《一个贫困家庭的成员的生活》——暗示路易斯或许也意识到了这一点。尽管书中包含许多故事，但对我而言，最引人入胜的是桑切斯的故事：他年轻时来到墨西哥城寻求更好的生活，很快便与妻子育有四个孩子，又与另一位女性育有子女。他养育子女，尽管内心充满怨恨，却依然竭尽全力。最终，他发现，孩子们的生活——尽管他知之甚少，却在某种程度上受他影响——以及子孙后代的生活，成为了他所有奋斗的最终意义。

Ronald Blythe, in his Akenfield: Portrait of an English Village , presents many more voices than does Lewis, none of them extensively and some only briefly. He is concerned less with the events that made up the lives of his respondents than with their personalities and their place in the life of his village. 18 In a long excerpt, for example, one of the village’s bell ringers talks about his obsession with ringing: “You have to be bitten by the bug. You have to be smitten. If you are a real ringer you think about bells morning, noon and night, and you only live for the next time you can have a go at them.”

罗纳德·布莱斯在其著作《阿肯菲尔德：英国乡村肖像》中呈现的声音比刘易斯的多得多，但每个人的叙述都不深入，有些甚至只是寥寥数语。他关注的与其说是受访者生活中发生的事件，不如说是他们的个性和他们在村庄生活中的地位。例如，在一段较长的摘录中，村里的一位敲钟人谈到了他对敲钟的痴迷：“你必须对此着迷。你必须深深地爱上它。如果你是一个真正的敲钟人，你从早到晚都在想着钟，你活着就是为了下一次敲钟的机会。”

Early in the book, a man, aged 71, remembers leaving the village for the battles of World War I: Gallipoli and the battles in France. Another man, aged 80, talks about the Armistice. Both had been underpaid farm workers before they enlisted, and both returned to find conditions no better. There was a strike, bitter and inconclusive. A bit later in the book, retired officers and gentlemen are introduced to give their different views, and the class structure emerges. This is the way Blythe shows us how the personal and the social intermesh.

书的开头，一位71岁的老人回忆起当年离开村庄奔赴第一次世界大战战场——加里波利和法国战役——的情景。另一位80岁的老人则讲述了停战协定签署时的情景。两人在参军前都是收入微薄的农场工人，而战后回到家乡，发现生活境况并未改善。当时爆发了一场激烈的罢工，最终以失败告终。书中后半部分，一些退休军官和绅士登场，讲述了他们不同的观点，阶级结构也由此显现。布莱斯正是通过这种方式，向我们展现了个人与社会是如何相互交织的。

Blythe frequently introduces other material in addition to the interviews: he offers his own observations of a pub evening; he gives excerpts from the log book of the village school, beginning in 1875; he gives the local version of the Rumpelstiltskin legend, transcribing it in the local dialect; and he offers brief essays as introductions to interviews. He is willing to include anything—whatever scenes caught his eye, whatever thoughts came to his mind—that might deepen the picture of the village.

除了访谈内容，布莱斯还经常穿插其他材料：他分享自己对某个酒吧夜晚的观察；摘录了村里学校自1875年起的日志；用当地方言转述了鲁姆普尔斯蒂尔特金的传说；他还撰写短文作为访谈的引言。他乐于收录任何内容——任何吸引他眼球的场景，任何涌上心头的想法——只要能丰富对这个村庄的描绘。

The result, one reviewer said, is “sociology written by a poet.” Blythe offers a few generalizations about English life, but these are context for the lives he presents rather than the point of his work. His aim is to tell his readers what life is like in the small and, by extension, in the large. The impulse seems to be like that underlying Thornton Wilder’s Our Town : to capture the tragedy of the ordinary. At the very end, after having considered the many rhythms of the village, Blythe allows its grave digger to muse:

一位评论家称，其结果是“诗人笔下的社会学”。布莱斯对英国生活做了一些概括性的描述，但这些描述只是他所呈现的生活的背景，而非作品的重点。他的目的是告诉读者，小家庭的生活是什么样的，并由此延伸到大家庭的生活。这种创作冲动似乎与桑顿·怀尔德的《我们的小镇》有着异曲同工之妙：捕捉平凡生活中的悲剧。在结尾，在细致描绘了村庄的种种节奏之后，布莱斯让掘墓人陷入沉思：

I have no family, none at all. No one in all the world is my relation. I never did read a lot. I never could give my mind to it. I talk too much, that is my failing. I come into contact with many people at a serious time, so I have picked up serious conversation. What most folk have once or twice in a lifetime, I have every day. I want to be cremated and my ashes thrown in the air. Straight from the flames to the winds, and let that be that.

我没有家人，一个也没有。这世上没有任何亲人。我从来不怎么读书，也从来没能专心致志地读过。我话太多，这是我的缺点。我经常在严肃的场合接触很多人，所以练就了一身严肃的谈吐。大多数人一生中可能只有一两次的经历，我却每天都要面对。我希望死后火化，骨灰撒向天空。从烈焰中直接飞向风中，就此结束。

These final words of the grave digger are also Blythe’s final words: “Straight from the flames to the winds, and let that be that.” So very many things can be done with a concrete case study—even the composition of a long prose poem.

掘墓人的遗言也是布莱斯的遗言：“从烈焰中直接奔向风中，就此结束吧。”一个具体的案例研究可以做很多事情——甚至可以创作一首长篇散文诗。

Because Blythe says nothing about his analytic methods, we must guess how he put this case study together. My guess is that he sorted, arranged, and rearranged his case materials, probably several times, until he found a sequence that made a compelling story. He may have done this in his mind, but I think it more likely he shuffled pages on a table. Levi-Strauss is reputed to have said that if he had a card table big enough he could figure out all of France. 19 There’s much to be said for a large flat surface when trying to generate a coherent story from case material.

由于布莱斯并未提及他的分析方法，我们只能猜测他是如何整理出这份案例研究的。我的猜测是，他反复整理、排列、再重新排列案例材料，可能不止一次，直到找到一个能够构成引人入胜的故事的顺序。他或许是在脑海中完成这项工作的，但我认为更有可能的是，他直接在桌子上翻阅资料。据说列维-斯特劳斯曾说过，如果他有一张足够大的牌桌，他就能弄清楚整个法国的情况。 19 在试图从案例材料中构建一个连贯的故事时，一张宽阔的平面确实大有裨益。

TYPOLOGIES AS GENERALIZATIONS FROM CONCRETE CASES

从具体案例中概括出的类型学

A way of generalizing from concrete cases while yet retaining their holistic character is to introduce types. Description of a type suggests that a common core has been identified within a set of particular cases and now is being named. The investigator, in presenting the type, is saying to the reader, “Here is the underlying structure, the skeleton of the case, unencrusted by the idiosyncrasies of specific instances, and here is a model of the dynamic that sets its parts in motion.”

在保留具体案例整体特征的同时进行概括的一种方法是引入类型。对类型的描述表明，在特定案例中已经识别出一个共同的核心，并对其进行命名。研究者在介绍类型时，实际上是在告诉读者：“这就是案例的底层结构，是案例的骨架，它没有被具体实例的特质所掩盖；这就是驱动案例各部分运转的动态模型。”

The type embraces many cases in a single framework. By invoking a type, the investigator need not describe first this particular case of, say, a young upwardly mobile couple of middle income and then that particular case of a young upwardly mobile couple of middle income and then the next, but can instead describe, all at once, “The young upwardly mobile couple of middle income.”

这种类型在一个框架内涵盖了许多案例。通过引入类型，调查人员无需先描述某个特定案例（例如，一对收入中等的年轻向上流动夫妇），然后再描述另一个特定案例（例如，一对收入中等的年轻向上流动夫妇），然后再描述下一个案例，而是可以一次性描述“这对收入中等的年轻向上流动夫妇”。

Investigators often tell readers what they think is essential in a type by the name they give it. Suppose we believed that what was essential about young upwardly mobile couples of middle income was that they were doing everything in their power to achieve social success. We might communicate this by naming them “young strivers.” We could then propose that this essential characteristic was responsible for much of the behavior of our respondents. We could therefore call on it to explain, among other things, the frequency with which they maintained dual careers and their determination to send their children to the best schools.

研究者常常通过给某一类型人群命名来告诉读者他们认为该类型人群的本质特征。假设我们认为，中等收入、积极向上、渴望成功的年轻人夫妇的本质特征是他们竭尽全力追求社会成功。我们可以用“年轻的奋斗者”来表达这一点。然后，我们可以提出，这一本质特征解释了受访者的大部分行为。因此，我们可以用它来解释，例如，他们为何经常从事双职工家庭，以及他们为何决心将子女送入最好的学校。

This view of types is close to the biological idea of species. One type is different from another in the same way an oak is different from an elm; there is a difference in kind. If it is a single type that is being described—the suburban family or the American housewife—the underlying idea is of a single inclusive species. But often a typology made up of several types is identified. Cuber and Harroff, for example, identified five types of marriage among the affluent: “conflict-habituated,” “devitalized,” “passive-congenial,” “vital,” and “total.” Each of these is equivalent to a subspecies within the inclusive species of marriage of affluent couples. 20

这种类型观与生物学中的物种概念非常接近。一种类型与另一种类型之间的区别，就像橡树与榆树之间的区别一样；它们之间存在着本质区别。如果描述的是单一类型——例如郊区家庭或美国主妇——那么其基本概念就是一个包含所有类型的单一物种。但通常情况下，人们会识别出由多种类型组成的类型体系。例如，库伯和哈罗夫识别出了富裕人群中的五种婚姻类型：“冲突习惯型”、“活力缺失型”、“被动和谐型”、“活力型”和“完全型”。每一种都相当于富裕夫妇婚姻这一包含所有类型的物种中的一个亚种。

We can use our model of the type to report, in a fashion similar to the local integration of issue-focused data analysis, the main line of our interview material and the variations from the main line. We would first describe what we believe to be true of the group as a whole and then turn to its usual expression and variations from that. For example: “While all young strivers are limited in the time they can give to being with friends, their responses differ. Most accept that they will see friends less often than they would like. But one couple arranged with two other couples to have potluck dinner together, children included, every other weekend, with each couple serving as hosts in turn. And a second couple each summer arranged to take a vacation home with another couple, not always the same one.”

我们可以使用这种类型的模型，以类似于本地化问题导向数据分析的方式，报告访谈材料的主线及其变体。我们首先描述我们认为该群体整体的普遍特征，然后转向其通常的表达方式及其变体。例如：“虽然所有年轻有为的人与朋友相处的时间都有限，但他们的反应各不相同。大多数人接受与朋友见面的频率不如预期。但有一对夫妇与其他两对夫妇安排每隔一个周末一起享用带孩子的聚餐，每对夫妇轮流担任东道主。还有一对夫妇每年夏天都会安排与另一对夫妇（不一定是同一对）一起度假。”

Types can be constructed of anything that could serve as the subject for case studies—not just individuals but also relationships, families, organizations, and more. Gerhardt, in a study of dialysis patients, found it useful to construct two idealized “patient careers,” one leading to invalidism and the other to a return to normal or near-normal life. 21

任何可以作为案例研究对象的事物都可以被归类——不仅包括个人，还包括人际关系、家庭、组织等等。格哈特在一项针对透析患者的研究中发现，构建两种理想化的“患者生涯”很有帮助：一种导致残疾，另一种则恢复正常或接近正常的生活。

Types are effective ways of communicating images that then are easily incorporated into thinking. Indeed, types can be seductive in their capacity to simplify thought. It is easier to picture in one’s mind the single parent than the range of family arrangements and living situations that would be found by a survey of single parents—although it is the range of family arrangements that is the reality.

类型是传递图像的有效方式，这些图像很容易被纳入思考之中。事实上，类型之所以具有简化思维的能力，是因为它具有诱惑力。人们更容易在脑海中想象单亲家庭的形象，而不是通过单亲家庭调查所发现的各种家庭结构和生活状况——尽管现实情况恰恰相反。

The Epistemological Status of Types

类型的认识论地位

Where do types come from? Are they inferences from observations or are they conceptual inventions? Arguments can be made for each view.

类型从何而来？它们是观察的推论，还是概念的创造？这两种观点都有其道理。

When most people invoke a type, they imply that the types captures essentials shared by all the instances it embraces. People who talk about “deadbeat dads,” for example, have in mind a way of acting toward a family left behind that they believe is common to a group of irresponsible divorced fathers. The essentials that are believed to mark the type presumably have been inferred from examination of instances. To the extent this is the case, types are anchored in reality.

当大多数人提及某种类型时，他们指的是这种类型概括了所有此类案例的共同本质特征。例如，谈论“不负责任的父亲”的人，指的是他们认为一群不负责任的离异父亲对待留守家庭的普遍行为方式。人们认为构成这种类型的本质特征，很可能是通过对案例的考察而推断出来的。如果情况确实如此，那么这种类型就扎根于现实。

What is often unclear, however, when a type is thought of as a classification based on essentials, is how one is to know in any particular instance whether the essentials are there. Is Madame Bovary an instance of the neurotic type or just a victim of romantic novels? How can we judge whether Madame Bovary’s behavior is essentially neurotic or not? The difficulties of deciding in any given case on the presence of inferred essentials may suggest that types would be better defined by the observables themselves rather than inferences from the observables. Then we could decide whether Madame Bovary was or was not an instance of the neurotic type by considering whether she displayed such observables as nervous tics or unjustified fears.

然而，当人们将某种类型视为基于本质特征的分类时，往往难以确定的是，在特定情况下，如何判断这些本质特征是否存在。包法利夫人是神经质类型的典型例子，还是仅仅是浪漫小说中的受害者？我们如何判断包法利夫人的行为本质上是否具有神经质的特征？在任何特定案例中判断是否存在推断出的本质特征都存在困难，这或许表明，与其从可观察的特征中推断，不如直接用可观察的特征来定义类型更为合适。这样，我们就可以通过考察包法利夫人是否表现出诸如神经性抽搐或无端恐惧等可观察的特征，来判断她是否属于神经质类型。

A second approach to typing, then, would be to define a member of a type by a conjunction of one or more significant characteristics. For example, a “young striver” would be someone in the right part of the age range (between 25 and 35), with the right marital status (married), the right occupation (middle-class), and a high score on a rating scale of desire for upward mobility. We could leave open the question of whether the observables (between 25 and 35, married, middle-class occupation, rating scale score) are causes or expressions of some underlying essential. Some might hold that the conjunction of observable characteristics locates an unobservable essential (such as conformist striving) with more or less success. But others might hold that the conjunction is the type, period.

因此，第二种类型划分方法是通过一个或多个显著特征的组合来定义某一类型成员。例如，“年轻奋斗者”指的是年龄在25至35岁之间、婚姻状况符合要求（已婚）、职业属于中产阶级，并且在向上流动意愿评分量表上得分较高的人。至于这些可观察的特征（25至35岁、已婚、中产阶级职业、评分量表得分）究竟是某种潜在本质的成因还是表现，我们可以留待进一步探讨。有人认为，这些可观察特征的组合或多或少地反映了某种不可观察的本质（例如循规蹈矩的奋斗）。但也有人认为，这些特征的组合本身就是类型，仅此而已。

Defining a type in terms of observables can be helpful for the work of classification. (It is the approach taken by the American Psychiatric Association’s Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders .) Insofar as it is unsatisfactory, it is because there is something odd about proposing a special name and implying a special set of dynamics for individuals who differ only slightly from others. Could someone be almost neurotic but not quite? Once we admit that, yes, this is a possibility, we suggest that we are imposing typological thinking on what are actually continua.

根据可观察特征来定义类型有助于分类工作。（美国精神病学会的《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》就采用了这种方法。）然而，这种方法的不足之处在于，为那些与他人仅有细微差别的个体赋予一个特殊的名称，并暗示其具有一套特殊的动态特征，这本身就有些奇怪。一个人是否可能接近神经质，但又不完全是呢？一旦我们承认这种可能性，就等于承认我们正在将类型学的思维强加于实际上是连续体之上的事物。

This brings us to the third meaning of types, in addition to their identifying essentials and their representing a conjunction of characteristics: types, no matter their source, are conceptualizations, mental constructs. Whether they have been inferred from real instances or not, they are themselves only imagery, theories in the form of models of people or families or institutions.

这就引出了类型的第三个含义，除了其识别本质特征和代表多种特征的组合之外：类型，无论其来源如何，都是概念化、心理建构。无论它们是否源于真实案例，它们本身都只是意象，是以人物、家庭或机构模型形式呈现的理论。

This is the construction Weber would have us make of types. He proposed that we treat types as pure conceptualizations, with no necessary match in any real instance. Their purpose is to help us grasp our empirical cases by providing us with coherent models of what would exist if essential elements of the cases were in pure, idealized, form. We can then understand actual cases by comparing them with the conceptual template provided by the type. We note where the cases match the type and where they do not. And we can understand the dynamics of an individual case by understanding those of the ideal type and then considering how much the individual case is a modification of the ideal type. 22

这就是韦伯希望我们构建的类型。他提出，我们应该将类型视为纯粹的概念化，它们在任何实际案例中都不一定存在对应关系。类型的目的是帮助我们理解经验案例，为我们提供连贯的模型，展现如果案例的基本要素以纯粹的、理想化的形式存在，将会是什么样子。然后，我们可以通过将实际案例与类型提供的概念模板进行比较来理解它们。我们注意到案例与类型相符的地方以及不符的地方。我们可以通过理解理想类型的动态，然后考虑个案在多大程度上是对理想类型的修正，来理解个案的动态。

The Weberian approach is appealing. And, yes, we do use types in our thinking and in that sense all types are conceptualizations. But beyond this the Weberian view has limited application. The types we use in the reports of our studies are almost always intended to be descriptive of our data. Even when they are presented as idealizations, they are idealizations of a state real instances are thought to approach. Consider the typology of the “other-directed” character type and the “inner-directed” character type in The Lonely Crowd . 23 Although the types were idealized, they were used descriptively to suggest how the America of its time had changed, and readers certainly interpreted them as descriptive of the characters of real people.

韦伯的理论很有吸引力。的确，我们在思考中会运用类型，从这个意义上讲，所有类型都是概念化的。但除此之外，韦伯的观点适用范围有限。我们在研究报告中使用的类型几乎总是旨在描述我们的数据。即使它们被呈现为理想化，它们也只是对现实实例所接近的一种理想状态的描述。以《孤独的人群》中的“外向型”和“内向型”性格类型为例。尽管这些类型是理想化的，但它们被用来描述当时美国社会的变化，读者也确实将它们解读为对真实人物性格的描述。

My own view of the matter is that types are almost always generalizations from observed instances or at least purport to be. If the instances have been well observed and the types capture important dynamics, they can be a powerful device for explaining how things happen. They also can offer vivid imagery even when there is no evidence for the theories they imply. A commonly used typology of personal functioning classifies people, on the basis of their birth dates, as Libras or Geminis or any of ten other types. This classification is believed by many to make individual behavior understandable and to an extent predictable. There is, of course, no evidence whatsoever to support the theory. In general, types and typologies are a valuable resource in data analysis, but they should be treated with caution.

我个人认为，类型几乎总是对观察到的实例进行概括，或者至少表面上如此。如果这些实例观察得当，且类型能够捕捉到重要的动态特征，那么它们就可以成为解释事物发生方式的有力工具。即使没有证据支持它们所隐含的理论，它们也能提供生动的形象描述。一种常用的个人功能类型学根据出生日期将人分为天秤座、双子座或其他十种类型。许多人认为这种分类能够使个人行为变得易于理解，并在一定程度上进行预测。当然，没有任何证据支持这种理论。总的来说，类型和类型学是数据分析中宝贵的资源，但应该谨慎使用。

An Example of Generalized Case-Focused Analysis

一个通用案例聚焦分析的例子

In The Gamesman: Winning and Losing the Career Game , 24 Michael Maccoby attempted to present portraits of the managerial types who direct large American businesses. Working from structured and unstructured interviews with 250 managers from 12 major companies, Maccoby identified four character types: “gamesmen,” “craftsmen,” “jungle fighters,” and “company men.” The types differed in motivations, goals, resources, and ways of treating others, but what was most important for Maccoby was that they approached their managerial jobs in different ways. The gamesman treated work as a gamelike challenge, the craftsman as a set of technical problems, the jungle fighter as a conflict to be won, and the company man as an opportunity for service.

在《游戏玩家：职业生涯的成败》一书中，迈克尔·麦科比试图描绘美国大型企业管理者的典型形象。他通过对来自12家大型企业的250位经理进行结构化和非结构化访谈，总结出四种性格类型：“游戏玩家”、“工匠”、“斗士”和“公司人”。这些类型在动机、目标、资源和待人接物的方式上各不相同，但对麦科比而言，最重要的是他们对待管理工作的态度截然不同。“游戏玩家”将工作视为一场游戏般的挑战，“工匠”将其视为一系列技术难题，“斗士”将其视为一场必须赢得的冲突，“公司人”则将其视为服务他人的机会。

Maccoby describes in detail how each of his four types of business leader functioned in the business environment. He also provides case studies to suggest the kinds of people he classified into each of his types and the kinds of business environments in which each type might do well. Because he thought gamesmen would be the managerial style of the future, he gave a good deal of space to describing a respondent whom he characterized as a “creative gamesman.”

麦科比详细描述了他提出的四种商业领袖类型在商业环境中的运作方式。他还提供了案例研究，以说明他将哪些类型的人归入每种类型，以及每种类型可能擅长的商业环境。由于他认为“博弈者”将是未来的管理风格，因此他用了相当多的篇幅来描述一位他称之为“富有创造力的博弈者”的受访者。

Where did Maccoby’s types come from? Maccoby reports that he based the typology on his study of the managers’ self-descriptions, augmented by their responses to Rorschach ink blots and descriptions of them provided by their colleagues. Maccoby describes his approach in this way:

麦科比的类型划分源于何处？麦科比表示，他的类型划分基于对管理者自我描述的研究，并辅以他们对罗夏墨迹测验的反应以及同事对他们的描述。麦科比这样描述他的研究方法：

Once we had scored [the respondents] in terms of dynamic character traits, different types began to emerge as distinct from one another in terms of the individual member’s overall orientation to work, values, and self-identity. We eventually came to name four main psychological types in the corporate techno-structure: the craftsman, the jungle fighter, the company man, and the gamesman. These are “ideal types” in the sense that few people fit the type exactly and most are a mixture of types. But in practically every case, we were able to agree on which type best described a person, and the individual and his colleagues almost always agreed with our typing, (p. 37).

在根据动态性格特征对受访者进行评分后，不同类型的人开始显现，他们在工作态度、价值观和自我认同方面存在显著差异。最终，我们将企业技术结构中的主要心理类型归纳为四种：工匠型、实战型、公司型和博弈型。这些是“理想类型”，因为很少有人完全符合某种类型，大多数人都是多种类型的混合体。但在几乎所有情况下，我们都能就哪种类型最能描述一个人达成一致，而且受访者及其同事几乎总是认同我们的分类结果（第37页）。

Maccoby alludes to three analytic processes in this paragraph. The first process was perceiving a typology among the different groupings of scores respondents had been given on such traits as aggression and intellectuality. Theories of personality may have played a role in the interpretation of the observed clusterings, but chances are a certain amount of inspiration also entered in. We have to guess, because we aren’t told exactly how the typology was developed.

麦科比在本段中提到了三个分析过程。第一个过程是识别受访者在诸如攻击性和智力等特质上所获得的不同分数分组之间的类型学。人格理论可能在解释观察到的聚类结果中发挥了作用，但很可能也融入了一些灵感。我们只能猜测，因为文中并未明确说明这种类型学是如何构建的。

The second analytic process was the naming of the emergent types. Here Maccoby clearly sought words that would accurately communicate each type’s essential nature. Implicit is a theory of individual functioning in which some single self-other outlook determines social behavior. Actually, the types proved too broad for many analyses, and at several points Maccoby had to introduce subtypes. Craftsmen were divided into the “dutiful,” who were driven and hierarchical, and the “receptive,” who were more life-loving and democratic. Jungle fighters were subspeciated into “lions,” who terrorized, and “foxes,” who manipulated. As I noted, one gamesman was a “creative” gamesman; presumably, others were not.

第二个分析过程是对涌现出的类型进行命名。显然，麦科比在此寻求能够准确传达每种类型本质特征的词语。内隐理论是一种关于个体功能的理论，该理论认为某种单一的自我-他人视角决定了社会行为。实际上，这些类型对于许多分析而言过于宽泛，麦科比不得不多次引入亚型。工匠被分为“尽职型”，他们积极主动且等级分明；以及“接纳型”，他们更热爱生活且更民主。丛林战士又被细分为“狮子型”，他们恐吓他人；以及“狐狸型”，他们善于操纵。正如我所指出的，一位玩家是“创造性”的玩家；想必其他玩家并非如此。

The third analytic process to which Maccoby refers in the quoted section was the assignment of individuals to one of the four types. Although Maccoby first notes that few people precisely fit a single type, he then says that there was agreement by respondents and their colleagues regarding the type to which respondents were closest. It seems to me that Maccoby is waffling a bit on the epistemological status of his types. On the one hand he describes the types as inferential, developed from a study of diagnostic material. He asserts that in practically every case managers could be fit into one type or another and that there was agreement regarding the typing. But in introducing the types, Maccoby described them as ideal types, which real instances might approach but should not be expected to match.

麦科比在引文中提到的第三个分析过程是将个体归入四种类型之一。尽管麦科比首先指出很少有人能完全符合单一类型，但他随后又表示，受访者及其同事对于受访者最接近的类型达成了一致。在我看来，麦科比在阐述其类型的认识论地位时有些含糊其辞。一方面，他将这些类型描述为推断性的，源于对诊断材料的研究。他断言，几乎所有个案管理人员都可以归入某种类型，并且对于类型划分也达成了一致。但在介绍这些类型时，麦科比又将它们描述为理想类型，现实案例可能接近这些类型，但不应期望它们完全一致。

One test that Maccoby’s typology passed with flying colors was acceptance by its readers. The Gamesman made the best-seller list. Most reviews were positive. Those that were not were critical of Maccoby’s view of the managers rather than of the methods he used in his study. One reviewer, for example, speculated that, given the time they were able to take from their work to participate in the study, Maccoby’s managers were second-stringers rather than real leaders. Another reviewer thought the managers banal and uninteresting. But all reviewers accepted Maccoby’s typology as valid. For a time, at least, the book was influential in business circles.

麦科比的管理者类型学经受住了读者的广泛认可，这无疑是它最成功的一次考验。《博弈者》一书荣登畅销书榜单，且大多数评论都给予了积极评价。少数持批评态度的评论主要针对麦科比对管理者的看法，而非他研究的方法。例如，一位评论者推测，考虑到参与研究的管理者们能够抽出大量时间，他们或许只是二流人才，而非真正的领导者。另一位评论者则认为这些管理者平庸乏味。但所有评论者都认可麦科比的管理者类型学的有效性。至少在一段时间内，这本书在商界产生了深远的影响。

THE DEMONSTRATION OF CAUSATION

因果关系的论证

In qualitative interview studies the demonstration of causation rests heavily on the description of a visualizable sequence of events, each event flowing into the next. In Children of Sanchez we can see how the tensions in the Sanchez home, together with the values of the society in which he lived, pushed Manuel into independent adulthood at age 15. In Blood of Spain we can follow the widening impact of garrison revolts into first skirmishes and then war. In Blue-Collar Marriage we can see the ways that mutual trust and respect, plus a secure marital partnership, can produce contentment in a marriage in which there is little apparent companionship. And in The Gamesman we can see how managerial styles affect organizational cultures.

在定性访谈研究中，因果关系的论证很大程度上依赖于对一系列可可视化的事件的描述，每个事件都环环相扣，环环相扣。在《桑切斯的孩子们》中，我们可以看到桑切斯家庭的紧张氛围，以及他所处社会的价值观，如何促使曼努埃尔在15岁时就独立生活。在《西班牙之血》中，我们可以追踪驻军叛乱的影响如何从最初的小规模冲突演变为最终的战争。在《蓝领婚姻》中，我们可以看到，相互信任和尊重，加上稳固的婚姻关系，如何在缺乏明显陪伴的婚姻中带来满足感。而在《赌徒》中，我们可以看到管理风格如何影响组织文化。

The description of a visualizable sequence of events differs from the approach of quantitative studies as a way of demonstrating causation. Quantitative studies support an assertion of causation by showing a correlation between an earlier event and a subsequent event. An analysis of data collected in a large-scale sample survey might, for example, show that there is a correlation between the level of the wife’s education and the presence of a companionable marriage. In qualitative interview studies we would look for the process through which the wife’s education or factors associated with her education express themselves in marital interaction.

对一系列可可视化的事件进行描述，与定量研究论证因果关系的方法有所不同。定量研究通过展示先前事件与后续事件之间的相关性来支持因果关系的断言。例如，对大规模抽样调查中收集的数据进行分析，可能会发现妻子的教育水平与婚姻关系是否和谐之间存在相关性。而在定性访谈研究中，我们会探究妻子的教育水平或与其教育相关的因素如何在婚姻互动中体现出来。

A search for the visualizable process that led from one event to the next can be one of the directing forces in an interview. At the end of many interviews the investigator can offer, with some confidence, a description of how some aspect of the respondent’s life or situation came to be. If the same sort of description fits a series of respondents, the investigator can feel justified in proposing a more general statement as a hypothesized minitheory. Each new interview can then be a test, the results of which will support the minitheory, discredit it, or, most likely, require that it be augmented or qualified.

在访谈中，探寻事件间可可视化的关联过程，可以成为指导访谈的方向之一。经过多次访谈，研究者可以较为自信地描述受访者生活或处境中某些方面是如何形成的。如果类似的描述适用于一系列受访者，研究者便可提出一个更普遍的假设性微型理论。每一次新的访谈都可以成为一次检验，其结果将支持、否定或（更有可能）要求对该微型理论进行补充或修正。

One idea of how to establish causal connections using qualitative interview material no longer has much currency. This was the idea that an invariable sequence must be found in the material, that is, that determinant A must always be followed by consequent B and consequent B must always be preceded by determinant A. Robert Cooley Angell, in The Family Encounters the Depression , and Donald Ray Cressey, in Other People’s Money , were among those in the social sciences who tried to find a process in their materials that was present each and every time. Angell hoped to show that income loss in families that were initially poorly integrated would always end in familial disintegration whereas in betterintegrated families income loss could be taken in stride. He ultimately gave up on this hypothesis; some families that looked bad to begin with were nevertheless able to pull themselves together. Cressey did find an invariant association between certain potentially causal elements, including the embezzler’s ability to find some way of justifying what he was doing, and ultimate embezzlement. But, by and large, invariable associations aren’t to be found, not in interview data any more than in survey research.

一种利用定性访谈材料建立因果关系的方法如今已不再流行。这种方法认为，必须在材料中找到一个不变的顺序，也就是说，决定因素A之后必然是结果B，而结果B之前必然是决定因素A。罗伯特·库利·安吉尔（Robert Cooley Angell）在其著作《家庭遭遇大萧条》（The Family Encounters the Depression）以及唐纳德·雷·克雷西（Donald Ray Cressey）在其著作《别人的钱》（Other People’s Money）中，都曾试图在他们的材料中找到一个始终存在的流程。安吉尔希望证明，对于最初融合度较差的家庭来说，收入损失总是会导致家庭解体；而对于融合度较高的家庭来说，收入损失则可以被轻松应对。但他最终放弃了这一假设；一些起初看似糟糕的家庭最终还是能够重整旗鼓。克雷西确实发现某些潜在因果因素之间存在不变的关联，例如挪用者能够找到某种方式为自己的行为辩解，以及最终的挪用行为。但是，总的来说，无论是在访谈数据中还是在调查研究中，都很难找到不变的关联。

However, a process does not have to be invariable in order to be causal. There are always extraneous factors that can modify the direction of a particular process. All that is necessary to show that a process may be causal is to make evident how it moves from cause to consequence. Blood of Spain shows that news of the garrison revolts in Morocco led to battles elsewhere in Spain, although such battles did not happen everywhere. It is a distinct problem—albeit a most important one—to identify the factors that can impede, redirect, or facilitate a causal process.

然而，一个过程并非必须一成不变才能具有因果关系。总有一些外部因素会改变特定过程的方向。要证明一个过程可能具有因果关系，只需阐明它如何从原因发展到结果即可。《西班牙之血》表明，摩洛哥驻军叛乱的消息引发了西班牙其他地区的战斗，尽管并非所有地方都爆发了此类战斗。识别能够阻碍、改变或促进因果过程的因素，是一个截然不同却又至关重要的问题。

In chapter 2 I pointed out that qualitative interview studies regularly lack comparison groups; it’s hard enough to study the group of interest without taking on the study of another group. I also suggested that it is often desirable nevertheless to do some limited interviewing of comparison respondents. Here let me note that we quite often can make comparisons within the sample we are studying. Komarovsky had within her study the comparison groups of couples who had completed high school and couples who had not. And although she had limited her study to people who were raising children, she could ask her respondents to tell her about their preparental lives. Her respondents could, in a way, serve as their own comparisons. On the other hand, if Komarovsky had wanted to consider the possible effects of the working-class status that all her respondents shared, she would have needed at least a few comparison cases from the middle class.

在第二章中，我指出定性访谈研究通常缺乏对照组；研究目标群体本身就已十分困难，更何况还要研究其他群体。我还建议，尽管如此，对一些对照组受访者进行有限的访谈往往是可取的。在此，我想指出，我们通常可以在研究样本内部进行比较。科马罗夫斯基的研究中就设置了高中毕业夫妇和未毕业夫妇作为对照组。虽然她的研究对象仅限于正在抚养孩子的家庭，但她可以询问受访者在为人父母之前的经历。从某种意义上说，她的受访者本身就可以作为比较对象。另一方面，如果科马罗夫斯基想要考察所有受访者共同的工人阶级身份可能产生的影响，她至少需要一些来自中产阶级的比较案例。

Respondents often have beliefs regarding causal processes, but they must be treated cautiously. The returned veterans of Blythe’s Akenfield blamed the landowners for the hard times they experienced on their return from war, but the landowners too were caught in an economic downturn that affected them all. Potential causal factors outside respondents’ observational fields cannot be referred to by them. 25

受访者通常对因果过程持有某种信念，但必须谨慎对待。布莱斯镇阿肯菲尔德的退伍老兵将他们战后归咎于地主，认为地主们造成了他们战后生活的艰难，但地主们也同样受到经济衰退的影响。受访者无法提及他们观察范围之外的潜在因果因素。

Caution in the treatment of respondents’ causal explanations should be extended to respondents’ explanations of their own behavior. People tend not to be fully aware of their emotions and their motivations. This does not mean that their self-reports have to be disregarded. Rather, they should be treated as likely to be incomplete.

在对待受访者对因果关系的解释时，应同样谨慎，这种谨慎也适用于受访者对其自身行为的解释。人们往往无法完全意识到自己的情绪和动机。但这并不意味着他们的自我报告必须被忽略，而是应该被视为可能存在不完整之处。

Nevertheless, we do well to attend to respondents’ descriptions of causation in social developments as well as in themselves. Often, they have identified at least part of the dynamics that have produced events. Some respondents may be especially worth attending to because they were close to the decision-making process or to some other development that set events in motion, or are especially perceptive or thoughtful. We will, of course, have to treat what these respondents tell us as suggestions to be investigated further, but they may point us in the right direction.

尽管如此，我们仍应重视受访者对社会发展及其自身因果关系的描述。他们往往至少能识别出部分促成事件发生的动态因素。有些受访者尤其值得关注，因为他们可能接近决策过程，或与推动事件发展的其他因素密切相关，又或者他们本身就具有敏锐的洞察力或深思熟虑的思维。当然，我们必须将这些受访者的反馈视为需要进一步调查的建议，但它们或许能为我们指明正确的方向。

I think we ultimately have to judge the validity of our identification of a causal process by considering all of our evidence together. We have to weigh the nature and density of the interview information supporting the identification; consider whether we have negative cases and, if we do, whether we have plausible explanations for them; and determine whether there are other bases for support or, on the other side, reasons for doubt.

我认为，最终我们必须综合考虑所有证据来判断我们对因果过程的识别是否有效。我们必须权衡支持这一识别的访谈信息的性质和详实程度；考虑是否存在反例，如果有，我们是否有合理的解释；并确定是否存在其他支持依据，或者是否存在令人怀疑的理由。

SUMMARY

概括

Certain analytic processes show up in every analysis of the data of qualitative interview studies: sorting the data, achieving local integration, achieving inclusive integration. In analyses intended to generalize regarding issues, coding is also important. In a typological analysis, the characterization of types is crucial.

在所有定性访谈研究的数据分析中，都会出现一些特定的分析过程：数据整理、局部整合和包容性整合。在旨在概括问题的分析中，编码也至关重要。在类型学分析中，类型的界定是关键所在。

Each analytic approach has strengths and drawbacks. The generalized approaches, both issue-focused and case-focused, contribute to our understanding on the level of theory. The approaches that provide us with concrete materials, again both issue-focused and case-focused, enlarge our experience and provide us with a basis for developing our own inferences.

每种分析方法都有其优势和不足。概括性的方法，无论是聚焦于问题还是聚焦于案例，都有助于我们从理论层面理解问题。而那些提供具体材料的方法，同样也是聚焦于问题和聚焦于案例的方法，则能拓展我们的经验，并为我们构建自身的推论奠定基础。

Causal explanation can be found in the products of every analytic approach, issue-focused and case-focused, concrete and generalized. Its demonstration rests on empirical and logical grounds that are different from those of a survey or an experimental study, but it need be no less a contribution to our understanding for that.

无论采用何种分析方法，无论是针对具体问题还是个案，无论是具体分析还是概括分析，都可以在分析结果中找到因果解释。虽然其论证基于经验和逻辑基础，不同于调查或实验研究，但它对我们理解的贡献却毫不逊色。

# ↩

CHAPTER 7
WRITING THE REPORT

第七章 撰写报告

GETTING STARTED

入门

By the time a study has reached the phase in which writing is its investigator’s primary concern, it will have amassed a great deal of material. The study’s file cabinets are likely to contain—in addition to the interview transcripts and excerpt files—codings of transcripts, descriptions of minitheories, data supporting the minitheories, summaries of the literature, and lists of questions to be answered, together with some answers to the questions. There may also be outlines and drafts of chapters or papers. Despite all this—maybe because of all this—it can be hard for the investigator to know where to start the report.

当一项研究进展到以写作为主要任务的阶段时，它已经积累了大量的资料。研究的文件柜里除了访谈记录和摘录文件外，很可能还包含访谈记录的编码、微理论的描述、支持微理论的数据、文献综述、待解答的问题清单以及部分答案。此外，可能还有章节或论文的提纲和草稿。尽管如此——或许正因为如此——研究者往往难以确定报告的切入点。

A first effort might be to reconsider the questions that motivated the study and how they have been answered. This may in itself provide an outline for a brief report. But it may be that answering the study’s initial questions will use only a small part of the information that has been gathered. Or the study’s initial questions may no longer seem of central importance, after all that has been learned.

首先，可以尝试重新审视这项研究的出发点以及研究是如何解答这些问题的。这本身或许就能为撰写一份简要报告提供思路。但或许，解答研究最初的问题只需要用到已收集信息的一小部分。又或许，在掌握了所有信息之后，研究最初的问题可能不再那么重要了。

If the investigator has already given a good deal of effort to analysis, the results of the analysis should provide the material for a report. All that may be necessary is their organization, development, and presentation. On the other hand, the investigator may have postponed full scale analysis until a decision was made on what was to be reported. In either event, but especially in the latter, the investigator may be uncertain about where to begin.

如果调查人员已经投入大量精力进行分析，那么分析结果应该足以撰写报告。他们可能只需要对这些结果进行整理、阐述和呈现。另一方面，调查人员可能为了确定报告内容而推迟了全面的分析。无论哪种情况，尤其是在后一种情况下，调查人员可能都不确定从何入手。

Here are some exercises that may be useful preparation for beginning a report. None are necessary, but one or two of them may help the investigator make a start.

以下是一些有助于撰写报告的练习。这些练习并非必须，但其中一两项或许能帮助调查人员着手开展工作。

BEGINNING WITH THE CONCRETE

从混凝土开始

What stories do you have to tell? Write down all the stories you can think of that strike you as interesting enough to hold an audience’s attention. Now sort the stories so they achieve a sequence. (It could help, if you’re not using a word processor, to put each story on its own index card.) If you now tell a reader your stories in the sequence you have developed, augmenting them with appropriate introductions and lesson drawing, you’ll have a report. If there are gaps, you should now be able to see what has to be added.

你有什么故事要讲？把你所有能想到的、觉得足够有趣、能吸引听众的故事都写下来。现在，把这些故事按顺序排列。（如果你不用文字处理软件，可以把每个故事写在单独的索引卡片上。）现在，按照你整理好的顺序，把这些故事讲给读者听，并配上合适的引言和插图，你就能得到一份报告。如果报告里有遗漏，你应该能看出需要补充哪些内容。

A variant of this is to identify exemplary respondents, develop their interviews into case studies, and then put the case studies in logical sequence. You might now note what can be learned from each case study. Having done this, you might think about the best way of communicating these lessons. Do you want to leave your case materials as is? Or do you want to retain the “caseness” of your material but generalize to a typological report? Or do you want to emphasize the issues the cases display by developing an issues-focused report?

另一种方法是找出优秀的受访者，将他们的访谈内容整理成案例研究，然后将这些案例研究按逻辑顺序排列。现在，您可以记录下每个案例研究中可以学到什么。完成这项工作后，您可以思考如何最好地传达这些经验教训。您想保留案例材料原样吗？还是想保留材料的“案例性”，但将其概括为类型学报告？或者您想通过撰写一份以问题为中心的报告来强调案例所揭示的问题？

A third possibility is that you might write about your own experience in doing the study. (Although this could be hard if you haven’t been keeping a diary.) You might start with your preconceptions, describe how you went about learning, and end with what you now know.

第三种方法是，你可以写下自己参与这项研究的经历。（不过，如果你没有写日记的话，这可能会比较困难。）你可以从你的先入为主的观念开始，描述你是如何进行学习的，最后总结你现在所了解到的知识。

BEGINNING WITH THE GENERAL

从将军开始

In developing your interview guide you almost surely thought about how you might present findings. This would especially be the case if you relied on an accounting scheme to develop the guide. Return to the guide now and imagine a generalized respondent. For every issue raised in the guide, sketch how this generalized respondent would deal with it. If you now develop your sketch and add supporting materials, you have the skeleton of a report. Now go back to the interview data so that you can decide where you will introduce real instances, including those that exemplify the main line of your findings and those that are variants of it.

在制定访谈提纲时，你几乎肯定考虑过如何呈现访谈结果。如果你是依据某种统计方案来制定提纲，那就更是如此。现在回到提纲，想象一个典型的受访者。针对提纲中提出的每一个问题，设想一下这位典型的受访者会如何处理。如果你现在完善你的设想并添加佐证材料，你就得到了报告的框架。现在回到访谈数据，决定在哪里引入真实案例，包括那些能够体现你主要研究结果的案例，以及那些与主要研究结果相关的案例。

Another approach would be to list your findings—all of them. Imagine you are to present them to an audience. Which do you start with? How do you connect them? What would make them into a coherent story rather than a listing of items?

另一种方法是列出你的所有发现。想象一下你要向听众展示这些发现。你会从哪些发现开始？如何将它们联系起来？怎样才能使它们成为一个连贯的故事，而不是一堆罗列的项目？

You might compare your actual findings with those you anticipated when you began the study. After all, when you began your study you were in the position of the ordinary well-informed person. What do you know, now that the study is done, that you didn’t know then? This should tell you where your study will be instructive to its likely reader. Now think about how to organize what you have to report and how to back it up with evidence. The result should be an outline of your report.

你可以将实际发现与研究开始时的预期进行比较。毕竟，研究开始时，你只是一个对情况有所了解的普通人。现在研究完成了，你又了解到了哪些当时不知道的信息呢？这应该能帮助你了解研究对潜在读者的指导意义。接下来，思考如何组织报告内容，以及如何用证据支撑你的论点。最终，你应该能得到一份报告提纲。

BEGINNING WITH THE MIX OF MATERIAL

从材料混合开始

You might take printouts of all the analytic material you have developed in your study, including memoranda, notes, and especially instructive interview excerpts, and sort them by topic. Now try to summarize the sortings. For each sorting, attempt to integrate what you have by finding an underlying dynamic, or some way in which everything expresses a common theme. Or search for a way in which everything adds to the understanding of an important outcome. This done, search for a way of integrating the themes or stories you developed for each sorting.

你可以将研究中收集到的所有分析材料打印出来，包括备忘录、笔记，尤其是一些有启发性的访谈摘录，并按主题进行分类。现在，尝试总结这些分类结果。对于每一种分类，尝试将你收集到的内容整合起来，找到一个潜在的动态，或者找到所有内容都表达共同主题的方式。或者，寻找所有内容如何共同有助于理解某个重要结论。完成这些步骤后，尝试将你为每一种分类提炼出的主题或故事整合起来。

Or you might review the literature on your topic. What is it that other investigators are interested in? Can your study speak to their interests? What is it that people believe? Does your study provide corroboration? Or does it require that some general belief be revised? Work out how you will develop your argument, the order in which you will make your points, and how you will bring in your evidence.

或者你可以查阅相关文献。其他研究者感兴趣的是什么？你的研究能否回应他们的兴趣？人们普遍持有的观点是什么？你的研究能否提供佐证？或者它是否需要修正某些普遍的观点？仔细思考你将如何展开论证，如何安排论点的顺序，以及如何引入证据。

FIRST DRAFTS

初稿

My own experience is that I begin to write the report before I get to the end of any of these preparatory exercises. And almost always I begin with chapter 1, even if the really important material won’t show up for another 50 pages. It may be that I need the sense of pushing the manuscript ever forward. However, I generally leave the introduction, where I tell the reader what the report is about, to the very last—when I know myself.

就我个人经验而言，我往往会在完成任何准备工作之前就开始撰写报告。而且我几乎总是从第一章开始，即便真正重要的内容要到五十页之后才会出现。或许我需要这种不断推进报告进度的感觉。不过，我通常会把引言——也就是向读者介绍报告内容的部分——留到最后写，等到我最了解自己的时候再写。

I try to do my first draft quickly, to assure myself that I have all the parts. And then, as I note later in this chapter, I rewrite. In the course of writing and rewriting, a number of issues may arise having to do with the way in which material is presented. The remainder of this chapter deals with what I think are the more important of these issues.

我尽量快速完成初稿，以确保所有内容都已涵盖。然后，正如我在本章后面提到的，我会进行修改。在写作和修改的过程中，可能会出现一些与材料呈现方式相关的问题。本章的剩余部分将探讨我认为其中较为重要的几个问题。

TO WHAT AUDIENCE IS THE REPORT DIRECTED?

这份报告的目标读者是谁？

How you present your material may depend on the audience you want to reach. Here are some thoughts about audiences.

你呈现内容的方式可能取决于你想要触达的受众。以下是一些关于受众的思考。

ACADEMIC AUDIENCES

学术受众

Academic audiences are likely to want first to be told how the report will add to their knowledge or understanding. The report must justify its demand on their time. You may have to argue that the report will teach them something new and important.

学术读者通常首先想知道这份报告将如何增进他们的知识或理解。报告必须证明其占用他们时间是值得的。你可能需要论证这份报告将教会他们一些新的、重要的知识。

Academic readers are likely to accept as valid the material of the interviews. Case studies, if they contribute to an understanding of an important area, are likely to be accepted with no further scrutiny. Inferences, generalizations, interpretations, and theory, on the other hand, are likely to be examined closely.

学术读者通常会认可访谈内容的有效性。案例研究如果有助于理解某个重要领域，则往往无需进一步审查即可被接受。而推论、概括、解释和理论则更有可能受到严格审查。

Academic readers have high standards for credibility. They are likely to think about comparison groups. Some of them will be skilled in devising alternative interpretations. Generalizations beyond your sample may make them uncomfortable. They will want to know your justification for generalizing.

学术读者对可信度要求很高。他们很可能会考虑比较组。有些读者擅长提出不同的解释。超出样本范围的概括可能会让他们感到不安。他们会想知道你进行概括的理由。

Should you advance an argument about the way things are, based on your interview material, your task is not only explication but advocacy. The analysis of your data led you to a conclusion; now you have to convince your readers. You must play fair with your evidence, but you also must develop your reasons for coming to your conclusion. If you think something is likely to be true, but you’re not sure, all of that is worth saying. Try to get to the heart of the matter; academic audiences will not quite join with Diaghilev in demanding that they be astonished, but they do want to go beyond superficials.

如果你要根据访谈资料提出关于现状的论点，你的任务不仅是阐释，更是论证。数据分析让你得出结论；现在，你必须说服读者。你必须公正地运用证据，同时也要阐明得出结论的理由。如果你认为某件事很可能是真的，但又不确定，那么这些都值得一提。努力抓住问题的核心；学术界的读者或许不会像佳吉列夫那样要求他们感到震惊，但他们确实希望超越表面现象。

Quantitative support for key points is helpful. One of the strengths of Recovery from Bereavement , my book with Colin Parkes, was that key points were supported by counts and correlations. We were able to report, for example, what proportion of our sample who early on displayed strong pining later failed to recover from grief. Although we didn’t have many tables in the book, the fact that we had tables for key points helped the entire report gain acceptance.

对关键论点进行量化分析很有帮助。我和科林·帕克斯合著的《从丧亲之痛中恢复》一书的优势之一在于，关键论点都得到了统计数据和相关性分析的支持。例如，我们可以报告样本中早期表现出强烈思念之情的人，后来有多少人未能从悲伤中恢复过来。虽然书中表格不多，但关键论点的表格形式有助于整份报告获得认可。

PROFESSIONAL AUDIENCES

专业观众

Professional audiences are likely to be concerned with the applicability of your report. Professionals must stay informed of current understandings in their fields and be able to implement what is currently endorsed as good practice. They will want a report that contributes to their competence.

专业读者可能会关注报告的适用性。专业人士必须了解各自领域的最新研究成果，并能够将当前公认的最佳实践付诸实践。他们希望获得一份有助于提升自身能力的报告。

Professionals are a bit less likely than academics to ask for conclusive evidence. Although they will want to be assured that credible evidence supports the conclusions of the report, they are ordinarily less concerned than academics that it all be displayed or at least be obtainable. They will care most about whether the report helps them do their work.

专业人士比学者更不倾向于要求提供确凿的证据。虽然他们也希望确保报告的结论有可靠的证据支持，但他们通常不像学者那样关心所有证据是否都已公开展示或至少易于获取。他们最关心的是报告是否能帮助他们完成工作。

CLIENTS WHO HAVE COMMISSIONED THE STUDY

委托开展这项研究的客户

Client groups tend to want diagnoses and recommendations. They have come to you, ordinarily, with a problem in their organization or in their program. They want to know what is going wrong and, even more, how to make it right.

客户群体通常希望得到诊断和建议。他们来找您，通常是因为他们的组织或项目存在问题。他们想知道哪里出了问题，更重要的是，如何才能解决问题。

Vividness is valuable, as is completeness. The arguments for recommendations should be spelled out, as should be the possible costs of implementing them. The client group ordinarily will not demand extensive evidence for assertions, although they will want to know that sound evidence exists and, in general terms, what it is. A methods section describing how the study was done may be essential, even if it is unlikely to be read closely.

生动性和完整性都非常重要。建议的论据应该详细阐述，实施这些建议可能产生的成本也应如此。客户群体通常不会要求提供大量证据来支持他们的主张，但他们会想知道是否存在可靠的证据，以及这些证据的大致内容。即使不太可能被仔细阅读，描述研究方法的章节也可能至关重要。

Controversy produced by the conclusions of a report is not infrequent. Indeed, you should assume that a report that is in any way critical of any sector of a client organization or of any program that has loyal backers within the client organization will become controversial. The credibility of the findings and conclusions of the report are then likely to be attacked, and you should be sure that good evidence is available and should present it fully and clearly. And if you suspect that your report is likely to stir controversy within the client group, you should give serious thought to strategies for presenting the report. You might also discuss such strategies with figures within the client group who might help in the report’s presentation.

报告结论引发争议并不罕见。事实上，任何对客户机构的任何部门或任何在客户机构内部拥有忠实支持者的项目提出批评的报告，都必然会引发争议。报告的调查结果和结论的可信度很可能会受到质疑，因此您务必确保掌握充分的证据，并完整、清晰地呈现这些证据。如果您怀疑报告可能会在客户群体内部引发争议，则应认真考虑报告的呈现策略。您还可以与客户群体内部一些可能在报告呈现方面提供帮助的人士讨论这些策略。

THE GENERAL READER

普通读者

Interview-based studies can be of genuine interest to a general audience if they offer enough opportunity for insight into the lives of others to involve and instruct a casual reader.

如果访谈研究能够提供足够的机会让普通读者深入了解他人的生活，从而吸引和指导他们，那么这类研究就能真正引起普通读者的兴趣。

A general audience is likely to be more interested in being informed than in being presented with support for one hypothesis or another. Although a general audience may be concerned with issues of credibility, it will not be as critical as an academic audience. Members of a general audience are more apt to respond positively than would an academic audience to a succession of anecdotes and interview excerpts. Indeed, the loosely attributed anecdote about “a person I know” would be acceptable as evidence only by a general audience.

普通大众更感兴趣的是获取信息，而不是被灌输某种假设的证据。虽然普通大众也可能关注可信度问题，但他们的批判性远不及学术界人士。与学术界人士相比，普通大众更容易对一系列轶事和访谈摘录做出积极回应。事实上，只有普通大众才会接受“我认识的人”这样来源不明的轶事作为证据。

One image of the typical member of a general audience is someone you meet at a party who is at first only mildly interested in your topic. Your listener is intelligent enough but with no special need for the information you can provide. You can assume that your listener’s attention will stray if you become boring.

普通听众的典型形象可以想象成你在聚会上遇到的那种人，他起初对你的话题只有淡淡的兴趣。你的听众虽然足够聪明，但对你提供的信息并没有特别的需求。你可以预料到，如果你的演讲变得枯燥乏味，听众的注意力就会转移。

General readers, like other readers, require the best thought and the clearest writing of which the investigator is capable. They should not be written down to. It may be inadvisable to use specialized language, but it is important to make available all that you know. What you write should be as full and rich as you can make it.

普通读者和其他读者一样，需要研究者尽其所能地进行深入思考和清晰写作。写作时不应降低标准。使用专业术语或许不妥，但务必将你所掌握的知识全部呈现给他们。你的文章应该尽可能详尽丰富。

CAN YOU WRITE FOR MORE THAN ONE AUDIENCE?

你能为多个读者群体写作吗？

The density of information, careful review of findings, and systematic citation of literature that would satisfy an academic audience might make a report too heavy and slow-moving for a general reader. A client report, as well as a report intended for a professional audience, would almost surely focus on questions specific to its audience’s concerns. It’s hard to write a report for more than one audience.

一份报告如果信息密集、对调查结果进行仔细审查，并系统地引用文献，虽然能够满足学术读者的需求，但对于普通读者来说可能过于冗长乏味。客户报告以及面向专业人士的报告，几乎肯定会侧重于与其受众密切相关的问题。很难为多个受众撰写一份报告。

Yet occasionally a report does succeed in reaching both a general audience and a more specialized one; Children of Sanchez, Blood of Spain , and The Gamesman are examples. An investigator hoping to achieve the like might be best advised to try for a report so interesting and so valuable that it will attract a general audience, while members of other audiences will make allowances for its not being directed solely to them. Thus, if you write for the intelligent layman and the report is important enough, others will read it too.

然而，偶尔也会有报告能够同时吸引普通读者和专业读者，例如《桑切斯的孩子们》、《西班牙之血》和《赌徒》。希望达到类似效果的调查人员最好撰写一份既有趣又有价值的报告，使其能够吸引普通读者，而其他读者也会理解报告并非专门针对他们。因此，如果你为有一定知识的普通读者写作，并且报告内容足够重要，那么其他人也会阅读它。

TO WHAT EXTENT DO YOU ENTER AS A FIGURE IN THE REPORT?

您在报告中以数字形式输入的程度如何？

To what extent do you introduce your own experience in the report? Do you remove yourself entirely, except as someone presenting and interpreting the reports of respondents? Or do you describe for the reader your problems in data collection, your encounters with respondents, and your understanding of their responses as they were made? The first approach provides the reader with the information you obtained, but neglects the issue of how you obtained it. John Van Maanen calls this the “realist” style, in his discussion of rhetorical styles in the social sciences. The second approach shares with the reader the experiences you had in producing the report. Van Maanen calls this the “confessional” style. 1

您在报告中会在多大程度上引入自己的经历？您是否完全置身事外，仅仅作为受访者报告的呈现者和解读者？或者，您是否会向读者描述数据收集过程中遇到的问题、与受访者的互动以及您对他们回答的理解？第一种方法向读者提供了您获得的信息，但忽略了您是如何获得这些信息的。约翰·范·马南在其关于社会科学修辞风格的讨论中，将这种方法称为“现实主义”风格。第二种方法则与读者分享了您在撰写报告过程中的经历。范·马南将这种方法称为“自白式”风格。

The realist style is generally written in what Van Maanen calls “didactic deadpan,” that is, an even-voiced, self-confident presentation of fact. The investigator may describe his or her own experience in an introduction but after that the investigator appears only to set a scene or comment on a statement, like the stage manager in Our Town . Should the investigator take over to tell the respondents’ stories, paraphrasing and summarizing respondents’ interviews, it is still the respondents who are the only actors.

现实主义风格通常采用范·马南所说的“说教式冷面”，即以平和的语调和自信的口吻陈述事实。研究者可能会在引言中描述自己的经历，但之后，研究者就只出现来交代背景或对某个陈述进行评论，就像电影《我们的小镇》中的舞台监督一样。即使研究者接手讲述受访者的故事，转述和总结受访者的访谈内容，最终的主角仍然是受访者。

In the realist style the investigator remains an invisible, dispassionate observer, even when the report deals with material of great emotional intensity. Here is how Glaser and Strauss describe what they learned from interviews with nurses about working with the families of patients dying at home:

在现实主义风格中，调查者始终保持着一种隐形、冷静的观察者形象，即便报告涉及极具情感冲击力的素材。以下是格拉泽和施特劳斯对他们通过访谈护士，了解她们如何与在家临终病人的家属相处的描述：

In the typical lingering death at home, the closer to the end, the more difficult the care becomes for the family members. The amount of deterioration and the work it entails are not easy for them to imagine unless they have experienced such deaths previously. Consequently, the nurse almost inevitably finds herself stepping up the number of her visits during this phase of dying: “Toward the end you generally have to start going in more frequently, and this gives you an idea the end is near.” 2

在家中常见的临终关怀中，越接近生命终点，家属的照护就越困难。除非亲身经历过，否则他们很难想象病情恶化的程度以及由此带来的种种负担。因此，护士几乎不可避免地会在临终阶段增加探访次数：“临近终点时，你通常需要更频繁地探访，这让你意识到生命即将走到尽头。”

This is the traditional style of report writing, and the approach most like that used in the physical sciences. A chemist would hardly interrupt a description of a chemical reaction to describe how he had gone about obtaining test tubes. Nor do Glaser and Strauss interrupt their narrative to tell the reader how they presented themselves to the nurses they inter viewed, what their problems were in eliciting descriptions of disturbing experiences, or what their own reactions were.

这是传统的报告写作风格，也是与物理科学领域最为相似的写作方法。化学家几乎不会在描述化学反应时突然中断，去解释他是如何获得试管的。格拉泽和施特劳斯也没有在叙述中插入他们如何向采访的护士们介绍自己，他们在引导她们描述令人不安的经历时遇到了哪些困难，或者他们自己的反应是什么。

But with increasing frequency investigators in the social sciences are including in their reports their experiences in conducting the studies. They present not only the story of one or more respondents but also the story of the investigation—if not the problems it encountered, then how it felt to conduct it and what decided them on the research choices they made. They may describe their reactions when they met their respondents and how further acquaintance with respondents affected their feelings about them.

但社会科学领域的研究人员越来越频繁地在报告中分享他们开展研究的经验。他们不仅讲述一位或多位受访者的故事，也讲述整个研究过程——即便不提及遇到的问题，也会描述研究过程中的感受以及他们做出研究选择的决定因素。他们可能会描述初次见到受访者时的反应，以及与受访者进一步了解后，他们对受访者的看法发生了怎样的变化。

Writing in this confessional style makes it possible for investigators to introduce novelistic devices. They can, for example, describe their response to a setting as a way of suggesting the emotional tensions within it. Here is how Arlie Hochschild, in her study of two-job marriages, introduces a couple for whom overload had led to marital strain: “When I entered the Livingstons’ home, I noticed a half-empty trellis standing ready to support a frail, outreaching bougainvillea with leaves of brilliant crimson. A window was cracked. The paint was peeling.” 3

这种自白式的写作风格使得研究者能够运用小说式的叙事手法。例如，他们可以通过描述自己对某个环境的反应来暗示其中蕴含的情感张力。以下是阿莉·霍克希尔德（Arlie Hochschild）在其关于双职工婚姻的研究中，对一对因工作过载而导致婚姻紧张的夫妇的描述：“当我走进利文斯顿家时，我注意到一个半空的棚架，原本用来支撑一株纤弱而伸展的三角梅，它的叶子是鲜艳的深红色。窗户裂了，油漆也剥落了。”

This confessional style of presentation permits investigators to confide in the reader their developing understanding of a respondent’s character or circumstance. They can engage the reader’s interest by introducing story elements such as witnessing a tense interchange between a husband and wife. The confessional style permits the investigator to include in the report anecdotes that would otherwise be restricted to dinner table conversation. It can help make the report a good read. Beyond that, it can make the report more useful.

这种坦诚的叙述方式允许调查人员向读者倾诉他们对受访者性格或处境的逐步理解。他们可以通过引入故事元素来吸引读者的兴趣，例如目睹夫妻间紧张的对话。坦诚的叙述方式也允许调查人员在报告中加入一些通常只存在于餐桌谈话中的轶事。这不仅能使报告更具可读性，还能提升报告的实用价值。

Here is an example of how the confessional mode provides an additional dimension to observations. It is from Maren Carden’s qualitative interview study of feminist movements of the late 1960s and early 1970s. By describing her concerns with her own dress she illuminates the ways dress signaled identity in the groups she was learning about.

以下示例展示了自述模式如何为观察增添新的维度。该示例出自玛伦·卡登（Maren Carden）对20世纪60年代末至70年代初女权运动的定性访谈研究。通过描述她对自身着装的担忧，她阐明了着装在她所研究的群体中如何象征身份认同。

In my manner, dress, and general behavior I tried to fit into my surroundings without violating my own integrity. For example, I wore informal sweaters and skirts for Women’s Liberation meetings but did not wear the near-universal jeans or slacks because I feel uncomfortable in them. When interviewing several people on one day I would often wear the same knitted dress to meet someone from WEAL [Women’s Equity Action League] and someone from Women’s Liberation. For the WEAL interview, I would add a gold pin and slightly dressy shoes—the sort of outfit in which I might lecture; for the Women’s Liberation interview, I would add a sweater and change to plain shoes—the sort of outfit I might wear to go to a movie. 4

在举止、穿着和日常行为方面，我努力融入周围环境，同时又不违背自己的原则。例如，参加妇女解放运动的会议时，我会穿休闲的毛衣和裙子，但不会穿几乎人人都穿的牛仔裤或休闲裤，因为我觉得那样不自在。如果一天要采访好几个人，我通常会穿同一件针织连衣裙去见妇女权益行动联盟（WEAL）的人和妇女解放运动的人。采访妇女权益行动联盟的人时，我会加一枚金胸针和略显正式的鞋子——就像我演讲时穿的那种装束；采访妇女解放运动的人时，我会加一件毛衣，换上朴素的鞋子——就像我去看电影时穿的那种装束。

Issues of credibility are for the most part the same in a consistently realist presentation and in one that now and again adopts the confessional mode. But the report in the confessional mode makes an additional argument for credibility through its inclusion of first-person material. The reader is encouraged to adopt an identification with the author that, in turn, fosters suspension of disbelief.

在始终如一的现实主义叙述和偶尔采用自白式叙述的叙述中，可信度问题大体相同。但自白式叙述通过纳入第一人称材料，为可信度提供了额外的论据。读者被引导去认同作者，从而更容易接受作者的观点。

USING EXCERPTS AS ILLUSTRATION AND AS EVIDENCE

以摘录作为例证和证据

Excerpts from interviews can do more than simply enliven a report, though this alone might be enough to justify their use. Excerpts also provide evidence for our assertions: “What I said is true; here it is in this quotation.” They provide examples of the words and images respondents use and a sense of the lives that underlie our findings. They foster identification with respondents and facilitate understanding of their points of view. They show the particular forms of general phenomena. But presenting excerpts is hardly problem free. We always select from our files of materials a small part to present. And we almost always edit. Each of these processes deserves examination.

访谈摘录的作用远不止于为报告增添活力，尽管仅凭这一点就足以证明其合理性。摘录还能为我们的论断提供证据：“我说的是真的；这段引文就是明证。”它们展现了受访者使用的词语和意象，以及我们研究结果背后所反映的生活情境。它们有助于读者与受访者产生共鸣，并理解他们的观点。它们展现了普遍现象的具体表现形式。然而，呈现摘录并非一帆风顺。我们总是从资料库中挑选一小部分进行展示，而且几乎总是会进行编辑。这些过程都值得深入探讨。

SELECTION OF RESPONDENTS TO QUOTE

选择受访者进行引用

It is a matter of common sense to select the quotation that makes the point in as strong a fashion as possible. It is, however, important to check that the quotation is representative in the sense that a member of Congress is supposed to be representative, that is, that it forcefully presents what is widely shared. Respondents whose material makes a different point should then be given their own representatives.

选择能够最有力地阐明观点的引语是常识。然而，重要的是要确保引语具有代表性，正如国会议员应该具有代表性一样，也就是说，引语必须有力地表达了普遍认同的观点。如果答辩人提出的观点不同，则应为其提供不同的代表。

Some report writers provide a string of quotations from different respondents, each saying about the same thing, as a way of demonstrating to the reader that they are playing fair. I don’t see the point in this strategy. If the reader doesn’t trust you, providing half a dozen quotes instead of one isn’t going to make a difference. When I come to these pages of snippets, I read one or two and skip the rest. It would be better to provide a couple of quotations and then indicate the proportion of respondents who say something similar.

有些报告撰写者会引用不同受访者的一系列话，而这些话的内容都大同小异，以此向读者表明他们秉持公平公正的原则。我不明白这种做法的意义何在。如果读者不信任你，提供六七个引语并不会起到任何作用。当我看到这些堆砌片段的报告时，我通常只会读一两个，然后跳过其余部分。更好的做法是只提供几个引语，然后指出有多少受访者持有类似的观点。

Most of the quotations I eventually use come from the notes I developed reading interview transcripts or excerpt files. Occasionally, I will give a good deal of time to developing at length a particularly instructive story in the respondent’s words, and will then actually quote only a part of the story in my report. Occasionally, too, I will realize only in the writing of the report the need for an illustrative quotation, and then if I do not remember a respondent who said something appropriate, I will check the nearest transcript in a drawer full of them or scan the excerpt files in my computer. If I find an illustrative quotation easily, I am reassured that what I am reporting is generally true.

我最终引用的大部分内容都来自我阅读访谈记录或摘录文件时所做的笔记。有时，我会花大量时间，根据受访者的原话，详细梳理一个特别有启发性的故事，然后在报告中只引用其中的一部分。有时，我也会在撰写报告的过程中才意识到需要引用一些例证性的内容，这时，如果我记不起哪个受访者说过合适的话，我就会翻阅抽屉里最近的访谈记录，或者扫描电脑里的摘录文件。如果我能轻易找到合适的例证性内容，我就能确信我所报告的内容总体上是真实的。

While quotations are useful, the report writer should be aware that they require the reader to shift attention from the writer’s voice to a new voice. Doing this several times in a few pages can be fatiguing for the reader. A high ratio of text to interview excerpt can help.

虽然引用很有用，但报告撰写者应该意识到，这需要读者将注意力从作者的叙述转移到另一种叙述方式上。在短短几页内多次这样做会让读者感到疲劳。提高正文与访谈摘录的比例有助于缓解这种情况。

A few long excerpts are preferable to listings of snippets. However, if longer excerpts are used in an issue-oriented report, readers are likely to want them interrupted now and again by text that tells them the point being made. Excerpts should forward an argument. If they don’t, they should be dropped. An excerpt whose contribution to the text is mysterious risks losing the reader.

比起罗列片段，少量较长的摘录更为可取。然而，如果在以议题为导向的报告中使用较长的摘录，读者可能希望时不时地被一些文字打断，以阐明摘录的要点。摘录应当有助于论证。如果摘录对正文的贡献不明，则应删除。如果摘录对正文的贡献令人费解，则可能导致读者流失。

HOW SHOULD QUOTATIONS BE EDITED?

引用应该如何编辑？

Blauner distinguishes between two philosophies in the treatment of interview excerpts: the “preservationist” and the “standardized.” The first would present the original speech in such a way as to reproduce the sounds on the tape as accurately as possible. The second would remain true to the words and meanings of the original but would accept editing that made the excerpt easier for a reader to grasp. 5

布劳纳区分了两种处理访谈摘录的理念：“保留主义”和“标准化”。前者力求尽可能准确地还原录音带中的声音，从而呈现原始讲话。后者则忠于原文的措辞和含义，但会进行一些编辑，使摘录更容易被读者理解。

The Preservationist Approach

保护主义方法

There are two arguments for the preservationist approach. The first is that speech communicates not only the dictionary meanings of its words but also the speaker’s feelings, including the speaker’s passions and uncertainties. 6 The thought here is that every element in a respondent’s expression—including the respondent’s hesitancies, nonstandard grammatical constructions and pronunciations, and circuitous rather than straightforward narrative—has value as communication. As Catherine Riessman has put it, “Speech that has been ߢcleaned upߣ to be more readable loses important information.” 7

支持保留原文的观点有两个论点。首先，言语不仅传达词语的字典释义，还传达说话者的感受，包括其激情和不确定感。 6 这里的观点是，说话者表达中的每一个要素——包括其犹豫、非标准的语法结构和发音，以及迂回而非直白的叙述——都具有沟通价值。正如凯瑟琳·里斯曼所说，“为了更易读而‘清理’的言语会丢失重要的信息。” 7

The second argument for the preservationist approach is that speech is a presentation of self and that changing speech misrepresents both the respondent’s personality and the respondent’s place in society. As Van Maanan says, standardizing respondents’ speech turns all respondents into “mannerly, pleasant, rational, and down-to-earth chaps who speak the King’s English remarkably well.” 8

支持语言保护主义的第二个论点是，语言是自我表达的一种方式，改变语言会歪曲受访者的个性及其社会地位。正如范·马南所说，规范受访者的语言会将所有受访者变成“举止得体、和蔼可亲、理性务实、能说一口流利标准英语的绅士”。

Both these arguments hold that only the original speech, pristine and without any editorial change, can adequately represent the respondent’s meanings and self. Anything else distorts. In the preservationist view it would be best if the reader could hear the original speech, with its pitch and sounds. Next best is to render these into words on a page with as much fidelity as possible. Anything less is playing with the evidence, no matter how benign the intent.

这两种观点都认为，只有未经任何编辑改动的原始演讲才能充分代表受访者的意图和自我认知。任何其他改动都会造成扭曲。在保存论者看来，最好的做法是让读者能够听到原始演讲，包括其音调和语调。其次，尽可能忠实地将这些内容以文字形式呈现在纸上。任何低于此标准的做法都是在篡改证据，无论其初衷多么良善。

The Standardized Approach

标准化方法

The argument for standardizing respondent quotations is that nonstandardized speech distracts from content. A too faithful rendering of respondent dialect, instead of enriching a quotation, may strike the reader as mannered and annoying. Almost surely the reader will have to puzzle out the respondent’s meaning instead of being able to understand it immediately. According to this view, speech needs to be cleaned up to be readable. Furthermore, nonstandard speech suggests an uneducated respondent. Such speech may therefore encourage the reader to disregard or disparage what the respondent says.

支持规范受访者引语的理由是，不规范的语言会分散读者对内容的注意力。过于忠实地呈现受访者的方言，非但不能丰富引语，反而可能让读者觉得矫揉造作、令人厌烦。读者几乎肯定需要费力琢磨受访者的意思，而无法立即理解。根据这种观点，为了便于阅读，语言需要进行规范化处理。此外，不规范的语言会让人觉得受访者缺乏教育。因此，这样的语言可能会促使读者忽视或贬低受访者的言论。

The Usual Compromise

通常的妥协

Generally, investigators in the social sciences make those modifications in the quotation excerpts they present that they believe make the excerpts easier to grasp but that they are certain have no effect on the respondent’s meaning. They are likely to permit themselves to eliminate words, sentences, and paragraphs—and also, most of the time, their own questions—in order to achieve a more compact statement. They will bring together in one place material dealing with the same issue that originally appeared in different sections of the interview transcript. They will standardize the slurrings of colloquial speech: “I was gonna” would be rendered as “I was going to.” But never is a word changed, never is a word supplied.
