通常，社会科学研究者在引用摘录时，会进行一些他们认为更易于理解但又不会影响受访者原意的修改。他们可能会删减词语、句子甚至段落，而且大多数情况下还会删掉自己的问题，以使表述更加简洁。他们会将原本分散在访谈记录不同部分的、涉及同一主题的材料整合在一起。他们会规范口语中的含糊不清之处，例如将“I was gonna”改为“I was going to”。但他们绝不会更改任何一个词，也绝不会添加任何词。

In a book on how journalistic aims intersect with ordinary understandings, Janet Malcolm describes a more liberal practice in editing taped statements. Her editing takes revision for coherence and grace far beyond anything anyone in the social sciences would have the wish or the skill to do. She introduces her own connectives (“and this, too,” “since”), regularly straightens out her respondent’s grammar and syntax, and not only condenses but sharpens her respondent’s argument. Her defense is that we are always translating speech into English: “Our ear takes it in as English, and only if we see it transcribed verbatim do we realize it is a kind of foreign tongue.” According to Malcolm, a written quotation should be just such a translation, now produced by the report writer rather than by a listener. It is only necessary for the report writer to be sure that the translation is faithful to the subject’s thought and characteristic mode of expression. 9

在探讨新闻目标如何与日常理解交织的一本书中，珍妮特·马尔科姆描述了一种更为自由的录音编辑实践。她的编辑对连贯性和流畅性的修改远远超出了社会科学领域任何人的意愿或能力。她会添加自己的连接词（例如“而且，还有这个”、“因为”），经常纠正受访者的语法和句法，并且不仅精简，还强化了受访者的论点。她的辩护理由是，我们始终在将口语翻译成英语：“我们的耳朵将其视为英语，只有当我们看到逐字转录的文本时，才会意识到它是一种外语。” 马尔科姆认为，书面引述也应该如此，只不过现在是由报道撰写者而非听众完成的。报道撰写者只需确保翻译忠实于受访者的思想和特有的表达方式即可。

So much assumption of editorial prerogative strikes me as going much too far. Quotation marks do not indicate that this is what the respondent meant , they indicate that this is what the respondent said . The reader is being misled when an investigator rephrases a respondent’s statements and then attributes the rephrasing to the respondent. It is one thing to standardize word use and drop out repetitions, but it is quite another to provide as the respondent’s statement a much more literate and pointed and effective translation. Not only is the character of the respondent changed—the respondent made into someone whose competent use of language implies a more general competence—but the respondent’s thoughts become less clouded than they were in reality, less blurred by other thoughts. Incidents are described more starkly.

如此多的编辑特权在我看来实在太过分了。引号并非表示这是受访者的意思，而是表示这是受访者所说的话。当调查人员改写受访者的陈述，然后又将改写的内容归于受访者名下时，读者就受到了误导。规范用词、删除重复是一回事，但以更文雅、更精辟、更有效的译文来冒充受访者的陈述则是另一回事。这不仅改变了受访者的形象——受访者被塑造成一个语言运用娴熟、能力出众的人——而且受访者的思路也变得比实际情况更加清晰，不再受其他想法的干扰。事件的描述也更加鲜明。

Perhaps the much milder sort of editing that seems to me customary in social science could also be attacked as changing the respondent’s presentation of self. But I think the rule that words should never be supplied is one defense against this, and the effort to retain the respondent’s phrasings is another. And there is much to be said for making the respondent’s statements accessible to the reader. While I strongly believe that if the words aren’t the respondent’s, they shouldn’t be attributed to the respondent, I also believe that absolutely literal transcription of a respondent’s words can interfere with understanding them.

或许，社会科学领域中常见的、程度较轻的编辑方式也可能被指责为改变了受访者的自我呈现。但我认为，绝不提供原文的原则本身就是一种反驳，而努力保留受访者的措辞则是另一种反驳。让读者能够理解受访者的陈述也至关重要。我坚信，如果文字并非出自受访者之口，就不应归于受访者名下；但我同时也认为，对受访者的原话进行绝对的逐字转录可能会妨碍读者理解其内容。

In my book on occupationally successful men, as part of my discussion of how they managed stress, I present the story of a crisis in the business life of a respondent whom I named Mr. Daniels. Mr. Daniels had agreed to arrange a loan for a contractor. Collateral for the loan would be equipment the contractor said that he owned. In reality, the contractor was only renting the equipment. Only after Mr. Daniels had gotten others involved in the arrangement did he learn that the contractor had lied to him. As soon as he learned this, he called the contractor to tell him the deal was off. The contractor then threatened him with violence.

在我那本关于事业成功男士的书中，为了探讨他们如何应对压力，我讲述了一位受访者——我称之为丹尼尔斯先生——在事业上遭遇的危机。丹尼尔斯先生曾同意为一位承包商安排一笔贷款。贷款的抵押品是承包商声称自己拥有的设备。但实际上，承包商只是租用了这些设备。直到丹尼尔斯先生让其他人参与到这笔交易中后，他才发现承包商对他撒了谎。得知真相后，他立即打电话给承包商，告知交易取消。承包商随即威胁要对他使用暴力。

The evening after the blowup with the contractor, Mr. Daniels met with an old friend. Mr. Daniels told us that before meeting with the friend he had hardly been able to think of anything other than the failed business deal. He was chagrined at having blindly accepted the contractor’s assurance and embarrassed at having involved others. He was also a bit worried by the contractor’s threat, although he preferred not to admit that, not even to himself. But when he met with his friend, Mr. Daniels said not a word about what had happened.

与承包商发生争执后的第二天晚上，丹尼尔斯先生与一位老朋友见面。丹尼尔斯先生告诉我们，在与朋友见面之前，他几乎满脑子都是那笔失败的生意。他懊悔自己当初盲目相信了承包商的保证，也为牵连他人而感到尴尬。承包商的威胁也让他有些担忧，尽管他不愿承认，甚至不愿承认自己也曾有过这种担忧。但与朋友见面时，丹尼尔斯先生对发生的事情只字未提。

I wanted to make a couple of points with the following quotation. The first was that Mr. Daniels maintained his functioning by compartmentalizing his distress, keeping it away from the forefront of his consciousness. The second was that to maintain his friend’s respect for him he said his business was going just fine, when in fact he was fending off awareness of a business reversal. What I wanted to show was how Mr. Daniels’s style of stress management—and, by extension, the style adopted by most successful men—implied that when he was troubled he would not confide in a close friend.

我想通过以下引文阐述两点。首先，丹尼尔斯先生通过将自己的痛苦隔离开来，使其不至于占据他意识的最前端，从而维持着正常运转。其次，为了维护朋友对他的尊重，他声称自己的生意一切顺利，而实际上他是在掩盖生意上的挫折。我想说明的是，丹尼尔斯先生的压力管理方式——以及由此延伸出的大多数成功人士所采用的方式——表明，当他遇到麻烦时，他不会向亲密的朋友倾诉。

In the left column is the transcript excerpt; in the right, the material that ended up in the book.

左侧是文字稿摘录；右侧是最终收录到书中的内容。

R ESPONDENT : I didn’t even mention that, this whole thing. I remember at dinner, at one point, toward the end of dinner, we’re having a cup of coffee and he just asked me, “How’s business?” and you know, I was having a nice time and I really didn’t want to, just didn’t want to even bring it up, and go through it all, because

答辩人：我根本没提过这件事。我记得晚饭快结束的时候，我们喝着咖啡，他突然问我：“生意怎么样？”你知道，当时我心情挺好的，我真的不想，根本不想提起这件事，也不想把事情翻来覆去地讲一遍，因为

I didn’t even mention this whole thing. At one point, toward the end of dinner, we were having a cup of coffee and he asked me, “How’s business?” I was having a nice time and I really didn’t want to even bring it up and go through it all. Because there’s no point in it. It wasn’t going to do any good. I really wanted

我根本没提这件事。晚饭快结束的时候，我们喝着咖啡，他问我：“生意怎么样？” 我当时心情很好，真的不想提起这件事，也不想再细说。因为说了也没用，没有任何好处。我真的很想

there’s no point in it. It wasn’t going to do any good.

这样做毫无意义，不会有任何好处。

that to go away, to be gone. So I just said, “Oh, it’s okay. We’re doing all right.”

就是要离开，彻底消失。所以我就说：“哦，没关系。我们一切都好。”

I NTERVIEWER : Sounds like you needed something else …

面试官：听起来你还需要别的东西……

R: Yeah, I really wanted that really to go away, and to be gone, and so, I just said,” Oh, it’s okay. We’re doing all right.”

R：是啊，我真的很希望这件事彻底消失，所以，我就说：“哦，没关系，我们一切都好。”

Immediately preceding the material I used for the quotation was the following material, which I dropped:

在我引用的材料之前，有一段材料被我删掉了：

R: Wells knows what’s going on in my life, but he doesn’t as far as the business thing goes, and I don’t know if you want to hang on to that or what, but as far as that goes, he plays a very small role in that. He could tell you generally that things look good, terrible, crisis time or not, but I would never weigh him down with any of the details because there wouldn’t be any benefit in it. He would not … advise me, I wouldn’t want him to. That’s not what Wells is.

R：威尔斯了解我的生活近况，但他不了解我的生意，我不知道你是否想继续讨论这个话题，但就生意而言，他扮演的角色非常有限。他可以大致告诉你情况如何，是好是坏，是危机时刻还是其他什么情况，但我绝不会让他知道任何细节，因为那样对他没有任何好处。他不会……给我提建议，我也不希望他这么做。威尔斯不是那种人。

I: It sounds like that relationship is for other things.

我：听起来你们的关系另有所图。

R: Yeah, but it’s a very good relationship. It’s one I’m quite fond of … most fond of, really.

R：是啊，但我们关系很好。我很喜欢这段关系……真的，是我最喜欢的一段关系。

This material makes the point that Mr. Daniels, like many men, thinks of friendships as having purposes, with one friendship quite possibly having a different purpose from another. This is an important point to make, and I do make it elsewhere in the book. At this moment, however, the book is dealing with the issue of stress management. The general principle is that the issue to be illustrated should decide where an excerpt begins and ends.

这段材料表明，丹尼尔斯先生和许多男人一样，认为友谊是有目的的，而且不同的友谊很可能有着不同的目的。这一点很重要，我在本书的其他章节也对此有所论述。然而，本书目前探讨的是压力管理的问题。总的来说，要阐明的问题应该决定摘录的开头和结尾。

OTHER PROBLEMS IN HANDLING EXCERPTS

处理摘录时的其他问题

Here are some other problems that may emerge in dealing with quotations from interviews.

以下是在处理访谈引语时可能出现的其他一些问题。

Suppressing Interviewer Contributions

抑制面试官的发言

Note that in preparing the excerpt from the interview with Mr. Daniels for publication I omitted the interviewer’s questions and comments. In consequence, Mr. Daniels’s response to the interviewer saying, “Sounds like you needed something else …” appears as a continuation of Mr. Daniels’s previous statement. Does this distort? My judgment was that although Mr. Daniels might not have said “Yeah, I really wanted that really to go away” had it not been for the question, running his response into his previous response in no way changed its meaning.

请注意，在准备发表对丹尼尔斯先生的采访节选时，我省略了采访者的提问和评论。因此，丹尼尔斯先生对采访者所说的“听起来你还需要别的……”的回应，看起来像是他之前发言的延续。这是否会造成误解？我的判断是，虽然如果不是因为这个问题，丹尼尔斯先生可能不会说“是的，我真的很想摆脱它”，但将他的回答与之前的回答衔接起来，丝毫没有改变其含义。

Occasionally, including an interviewer’s question in the published text is necessary in order to make clear the meaning of a response. Then I would include it. But for the most part, I find interviewers’ questions and comments to be distracting.

有时，为了阐明回答的含义，有必要在已发表的文本中引用采访者的问题。在这种情况下，我会引用。但大多数情况下，我认为采访者的问题和评论会分散注意力。

In this interview, as in any, the interviewer repeatedly made encouraging or sympathetic noises: “Uh-huh” or “Mmm”. The transcriptionist frequently indicated these, but I dropped the indications from the published excerpt. Here again it seemed to me that the interjections were unnecessary distractions in the text, however valuable they may have been in the interview.

和以往的采访一样，这次采访中，采访者也反复发出鼓励或表示赞同的声音，比如“嗯哼”或“嗯嗯”。转录员经常会标注这些声音，但我从发表的节选中删去了这些标注。在我看来，这些插话在文本中是不必要的干扰，尽管它们在采访中可能很有价值。

Dropping Out Conversational Spacers and False Starts

省略对话中的停顿和错误开场白

Most respondents use conversational spacers—“you know” or “uh”—to cover a pause while they search for a word or a continuation of a thought. Or they find a start to a sentence unsatisfactory and begin again. Or they repeat a phrase as though weighing its meaning: “I think that he must have gone, he must have gone …” I almost always edit these out unless the spacer or false start or repeat communicates uncertainty or serves some similar purpose. So when Mr. Daniels said, “And you know, I was having a nice time,” I edited out the “And you know” and rendered the statement as “I was having a nice time.”

大多数受访者会使用一些语气词——比如“你知道”或“呃”——来掩盖他们思考某个词或想继续表达某个想法时的停顿。或者，他们觉得句子开头不够流畅，于是重新开始。又或者，他们会重复某个短语，仿佛在斟酌其含义：“我想他一定走了，他一定走了……”除非这些语气词、错误的开头或重复表达了不确定或具有类似的目的，否则我几乎总是会把这些语气词剪掉。所以，当丹尼尔斯先生说“你知道，我当时玩得很开心”时，我剪掉了“你知道”，把这句话改成了“我当时玩得很开心”。

I am not sure I was right, in this instance, to have regularized Mr. Daniels’s speech as much as I did. His hesitancies, spacers, and repeats do communicate a certain informality in speaking style. I did not, however, in any instance add a word Mr. Daniels did not use or substitute a word of mine for one of his or change a sentence except to drop a spacer or a redundancy.

我不确定在这种情况下，我是否应该像之前那样规范丹尼尔斯先生的讲话。他的犹豫、停顿和重复确实体现了他说话风格的某种随意性。然而，我始终没有添加丹尼尔斯先生没有使用的词语，也没有用我的词语替换他的词语，更没有改动句子，除了删除停顿或冗余的词语之外。

Good transcriptionists will accurately represent common condensations of speech, such as “He’s gotta say what he wants.” I find this useful in reading the transcript, but in reporting I would almost certainly change the “gotta” to “got to.” I see no value in retaining what is a kind of personal dialect. On the other hand, I never correct grammatical errors. If someone says, as Mr. Daniels did at another point, “I think of he and I as close,” I’ll let that stand.

优秀的转录员能够准确地呈现常见的口语缩略形式，例如“他必须说出他想说的话”。我觉得这在阅读转录稿时很有用，但在撰写报告时，我几乎肯定会把“gotta”改成“got to”。我认为保留这种带有个人口语色彩的表达方式毫无意义。另一方面，我从不纠正语法错误。如果有人像丹尼尔斯先生在另一处那样说“我认为他和我关系很亲密”，我会保留这种说法。

In general, I try to be faithful to the respondent’s word choice and sentence structure. In the unusual circumstance that it is necessary to introduce a word to make clear a respondent’s meaning, I put the introduced word in brackets: “I called her [R’s sister] on the telephone.”

一般来说，我会尽量忠实于受访者的用词和句式结构。在特殊情况下，如果需要引入一个词来阐明受访者的意思，我会将引入的词放在括号中：“我给她（R的妹妹）打了电话。”

Reorganizing for Coherence

重组以实现连贯性

I sometimes do a fair amount of reorganizing of a respondent’s report in the interests of coherence. If a respondent developed a theme, went off to something else, and then returned to the original theme, I will bring together all the materials dealing with the theme. It’s asking a lot of a reader to sort out scattered thematic material. It’s possible, of course, to use ellipsis points to indicate that material has been removed, but this rarely seems to me useful.

为了保持报告的连贯性，我有时会对受访者的报告进行相当程度的重新组织。如果受访者提出了一个主题，然后又谈到了其他内容，最后又回到最初的主题，我会把所有与该主题相关的材料集中起来。让读者去梳理这些分散的主题材料确实很费力。当然，也可以用省略号来表示哪些内容已被删除，但我认为这种方法很少有效。

Disguising People, Places, and Institutions

伪装人物、地点和机构

In telling Mr. Daniels’s story I changed the nature of the deal he was involved in while retaining its structure. I cannot say here what was actually going on, but it did involve collateral and a client who lied about the collateral. The changes I made were enough to provide disguise without changing the human elements that were the essential part of the story.

在讲述丹尼尔斯先生的故事时，我改变了他所参与的交易的性质，但保留了其结构。我不能在此透露实际情况，但确实涉及抵押品和一位就抵押品撒谎的客户。我所做的改动足以掩盖真相，同时又不改变故事的核心——人性。

I want to ensure that respondents are not recognizable to others in any quotations I give. I would also like it if they were not recognizable to themselves, but that seems more than I can always achieve. Still, I was once told by a respondent whom I had quoted extensively that he had looked in the book for himself without success.

我希望确保在我引用的任何内容中，受访者的身份都不会被他人认出。我也希望他们自己也认不出自己，但这似乎并非总能做到。不过，我曾经从一位被我大量引用过的受访者那里得知，他自己也曾在书中查找过，但没有找到。

I change names, getting new names from the telephone book. I look for one-syllable or two-syllable names, sometimes with an ethnic flavor not too different from that of the respondent’s name. If I do choose a name of similar ethnicity, I want the code name to be not so strongly ethnic as to constitute a comment; I might turn O’Brien into Conley but not into O’Malley.

我会更改名字，从电话簿里找新名字。我尽量选择单音节或双音节的名字，有时会选择带有民族特色的名字，但不要和受访者的名字差别太大。如果我选择的名字民族特色相似，我希望代号的民族特征不要太明显，以免显得带有明显的种族歧视意味；我可能会把奥布莱恩改成康利，但不会改成奥马利。

If it doesn’t matter, I will try to drop a reference to a place rather than invent a substitute. If a respondent refers to a daughter who lives in California, I might put her in Oregon or “out West,” but I would prefer to drop the place reference entirely. Another possibility is to put a generalized reference in brackets: [in another state].

如果无关紧要，我会尽量避免提及具体地点，而不是编造替代词。例如，如果受访者提到一个住在加州的女儿，我可能会说她住在俄勒冈州或“西部”，但我更倾向于完全省略地点信息。另一种方法是用方括号括起来，给出概括性的描述：[在另一个州]。

I change occupations, trying to find substitute occupations that involve the same general kind of work. Mr. Daniels did indeed arrange business deals involving clients and collateral—I had to keep this for his story to make sense—but the rest of what I described as his work was invention.

我换了工作，试图找到与之前工作性质大致相同的替代职业。丹尼尔斯先生确实安排过涉及客户和抵押品的商业交易——为了让他的故事说得通，我不得不保留这一点——但我所描述的他工作的其他部分都是发明创造。

I try not to distort the character of a respondent’s life situation, but where it doesn’t matter much I will make whatever changes seem useful for disguise. Occasionally I have changed the number of children a respondent had, and once I changed a child’s gender. When material strikes me as truly sensitive—capable of bringing embarrassment or injury if the respondent were identified with it—I give no information, not even false information, about occupation or place. In addition, I may give a new false name to the respondent, different from the false name I used for the respondent elsewhere in the report.

我尽量不歪曲受访者的生活状况，但在无关紧要的情况下，我会做出一些我认为有助于掩饰的改动。我偶尔会更改受访者的子女数量，甚至还更改过一个孩子的性别。如果我认为某些信息非常敏感——如果受访者与这些信息关联起来，可能会造成尴尬或伤害——我会完全不提供任何信息，即使是虚假信息，包括职业或居住地。此外，我可能会给受访者一个新的假名，与我在报告其他部分使用的假名不同。

Checking the Transcript

查阅成绩单

Good transcriptionists, in my experience, will get a respondent’s words almost right but never entirely right. When preparing this chapter I listened again to Mr. Daniels’s tapes. The transcriptionist had been conscientious and was generally accurate. Nevertheless, he had rendered Mr. Daniels’s remark “There’d be no real point in it” as “There’s no point in it.” That’s only a small change in meaning—certainly not as much of a change as would be produced by omitting a “not”—but still a change.

以我的经验来看，优秀的转录员能将受访者的原话准确无误地传达给听众，但永远无法做到完全正确。在准备本章时，我再次听了丹尼尔斯先生的录音。转录员尽职尽责，总体上也比较准确。然而，他把丹尼尔斯先生的“There’d be no real point in it”转录成了“There’s no point in it”。这只是意思上的一个细微差别——当然，远不及省略“not”所造成的影响那么大——但毕竟还是有差别的。

For the most part, I am sure, the transcription was good enough so that I had been right to work from transcripts when writing that project’s report rather than returning to listen to the tapes. And yet, for excerpts that will be used in a project’s report it might be worthwhile to return to the tape if the respondent’s exact wording and indications of the respondent’s intonation and hesitancies could turn out to be important.

我相信，大部分情况下，转录稿的质量都足够好，因此我在撰写项目报告时直接使用转录稿而不是重新听录音是正确的。然而，对于项目报告中将要使用的摘录，如果受访者的确切措辞以及语调和犹豫等细节可能很重要，那么重新听录音或许是值得的。

JUSTIFICATIONS FOR USING QUASI-QUANTITATIVE TERMS RATHER THAN COUNTS AND PROPORTIONS

使用准定量术语而非计数和比例的理由

A problem often encountered in reports of qualitative studies is how to communicate the proportion of cases that have particular characteristics. We tend to use terms that have quantitative implications but that specify no particular number or proportion: terms like “a few” or “some” or “many.” Should we not report instead the actual numbers or proportions of instances we have found? Why do we not report the correlation coefficient rather than saying that people who have one characteristic “seem likely” to have another?

定性研究报告中经常遇到的一个问题是如何传达具有特定特征的案例比例。我们倾向于使用一些带有量化含义但并未明确指出具体数量或比例的词语，例如“少数”、“一些”或“许多”。我们是否应该直接报告我们发现的实际案例数量或比例？为什么我们不直接报告相关系数，而只是说具有某种特征的人“似乎”也可能具有另一种特征？

One reason is that many issues do not require that we code and count. An impression is good enough. “Most respondents found the interview to be interesting” is a statement of this sort. We would not make the study more valuable by the more precise statement “Seventy-three percent of respondents gave evidence that they found the interview to be interesting.” And the more precise statement would suggest either that the proportion was an important finding or that the investigator had no sense of what was important and what was not.

原因之一是，很多问题并不需要我们进行编码和计数。一个大致的印象就足够了。“大多数受访者认为访谈很有趣”就是这样一种表述。即使我们用更精确的表述“73%的受访者表示他们认为访谈很有趣”，也不会让这项研究更有价值。而且，更精确的表述要么暗示这个比例本身就是一个重要的发现，要么暗示研究者根本不知道什么重要什么不重要。

A further reason for using “most” rather than a percent or proportion can be that the sample is so very nonrepresentative, so different from any population to which there might be generalization, that to be more precise would be misleading. Suppose that some members of a sample of retirees were volunteers and others were referred by the personnel directors of the firms they had worked for and still others were obtained from a community sample. It would be more in keeping with this sample of convenience to say “The great majority of the sample have adult children” than to say “Eighty-five percent of the sample have adult children.”

使用“大多数”而非百分比或比例的另一个原因是，样本的代表性极差，与任何可能具有普遍意义的总体都截然不同，因此更精确的表述反而会造成误导。假设退休人员样本中的一些成员是志愿者，另一些是由他们之前所在公司的人事主管推荐的，还有一些则来自社区样本。对于这种便利抽样而言，与其说“85%的样本有成年子女”，不如说“样本中的绝大多数人都有成年子女”。

Notwithstanding these concerns, sample numbers or proportions should probably be reported when an issue is central to a study. In a paper on the processes by which people move into retirement, I told readers how many in our sample had retired for reasons of health, how many had retired because they wanted to, and how many had been pushed out. I thought it important for readers to know how many cases we drew on for our appraisals of the effects of different processes of retirement.

尽管存在这些顾虑，但当某个问题是研究的核心时，报告样本数量或比例或许是必要的。在一篇关于人们退休过程的论文中，我告诉读者，在我们的样本中，有多少人因健康原因退休，有多少人出于自愿退休，以及有多少人被迫退休。我认为，让读者了解我们为了评估不同退休过程的影响而参考了多少案例非常重要。

HOW YOU WRITE ABOUT YOUR INFORMANTS AND RESPONDENTS

你如何描述你的信息提供者和受访者

Any report on people conveys an attitude toward them: sympathetic, indulgent, critical, dispassionate. The attitude may not be made explicit but will in any event be expressed in the way the people are presented to the report’s readers. (Readers will then have their own reactions to the respondents, the author, and the author’s attitudes.) Let us consider three attitudes investigators might display toward their respondents in the report of their study.

任何关于人物的报告都会传递出一种对他们的态度：同情、宽容、批判或冷漠。这种态度或许不会明确表达，但无论如何都会体现在报告呈现人物的方式上。（读者随后会对受访者、作者以及作者的态度产生各自的反应。）让我们来探讨一下研究者在研究报告中可能对受访者表现出的三种态度。

THE INVESTIGATOR AS ADVOCATE, SYMPATHETIC REPRESENTATIVE, OR VIEWPOINT PRESENTER

调查者可以扮演倡导者、同情代表或观点表达者的角色

One test of the adequacy of a report is whether it can convince its readers that had they been in the situation of the respondents, with the respondent’s histories and understandings of their options, they would have behaved just as did the respondents. The rationale for this position is that most people, respondents included, behave reasonably; a fully adequate report, therefore, will make evident to readers that respondents behaved reasonably, given their understanding of their situations.

检验一份报告是否充分的一个标准是，它能否让读者相信，如果他们身处受访者的境地，拥有受访者的经历和对自身选择的理解，他们也会采取与受访者相同的行动。这种观点的理由是，大多数人，包括受访者在内，都会做出合理的行为；因此，一份充分充分的报告应该能够让读者清楚地认识到，鉴于受访者对自身处境的理解，他们的行为是合理的。

But the attempt to demonstrate the reasonableness of respondents’ behavior, if adopted by an investigator of crime or vice, tends to turn the investigator into a defender of that crime or vice. The report appears to demonstrate that the criminal or sinner is not at fault, that crime or vice just happen, that the reader has no right to judge because in the situation of respondents the reader would do no better. To escape this trap the investigator must be able to communicate awareness that the behavior is wrong, even while demonstrating that it is understandable.

但如果犯罪或恶习调查员试图证明受访者的行为合情合理，则往往会使调查员沦为犯罪或恶习的辩护者。报告似乎表明，犯罪者或罪人并无过错，犯罪或恶习只是偶然发生，读者无权评判，因为读者身处受访者的境地，也未必会做得更好。为了避免落入这种陷阱，调查员必须能够传达出对这种行为错误的认知，即便这种行为是可以理解的。

Sometimes investigators, as a consequence of their research relationships with respondents, find themselves acting as their respondents’ representatives to the society at large. The time and emotion and thought investigators have invested in understanding their respondents have fostered a sense of responsibility for their welfare. The investigators feel themselves responsible not only for making their respondents’ situations understandable but also for speaking for their respondents.

有时，由于与受访者建立的研究关系，研究人员会发现自己扮演着受访者代表的角色，向社会大众发声。研究人员投入了大量的时间、情感和思考来了解受访者，这使他们对受访者的福祉产生了一种责任感。研究人员不仅感到自己有责任让受访者的处境被理解，也感到自己有责任代表受访者发声。

Occasionally, investigators “go native.” They incorporate the respondents’ behaviors and worldview. They may then find it difficult to retain the perspective of their field. Yet representing respondents is different both from identifying with them and from endorsing everything about them. A sense of obligation to a group the investigator has studied seems to me at least defensible, whereas identification with the group and endorsement of their values seem to me developments ordinarily to be avoided.

有时，研究者会“入乡随俗”，将受访者的行为和世界观融入自身研究领域。然而，他们可能因此难以保持自身领域的视角。但代表受访者与认同受访者以及赞同受访者的一切截然不同。在我看来，研究者对所研究群体负有责任感至少是可以理解的，而认同受访者群体并赞同其价值观则通常是应该避免的。

THE INVESTIGATOR AS CRITIC

调查员作为评论家

Quite the opposite position from that of identification with respondents is also possible in the writing of a qualitative interview report. A colleague of mine once offered as a general rule that if your report on a group you have studied has truly gotten to the inner dynamics of the group, you can never again visit that group with safety. His idea was that every group has secrets kept from outsiders that the group would be loath to have revealed and still other secrets, even more fundamental, kept from itself, whose surfacing would enrage it. He gave as an instance a study he had conducted of men in a working-class social group whose aggressively masculine displays in drinking, athletics, and quarreling he believed both expressed homosexual impulses and hid their existence.

在撰写定性访谈报告时，也可能出现与认同受访者截然相反的立场。我的一位同事曾提出一条普遍规律：如果你对某个研究群体的报告真正触及了该群体的内部动态，那么你以后就再也无法安全地重返该群体。他的观点是，每个群体都有一些不为人知的秘密，这些秘密是群体不愿向外人透露的；还有一些更为根本的秘密，甚至连群体自身都隐藏着，一旦曝光，就会激怒群体。他举例说，他曾对一个工人阶级社会群体中的男性进行过一项研究，他认为这些男性在饮酒、运动和争吵中表现出的咄咄逼人的男子气概，既表达了同性恋倾向，又掩盖了这种倾向的存在。

Some interviewers seem to subscribe to a milder form of this position, which is that any portrait that has integrity will display unflattering elements as well as flattering ones. The investigator may not be hostile, but balance will require warts along with dimples. Other investigators, however, fully anticipate that their work will damage some respondents or damage groups in which their respondents have membership. Indeed, this may be the investigators’ ultimate aim. Investigative reporters are often out to “get the goods” on people they interview.

有些采访者似乎认同这种观点的温和版本，即任何客观公正的描述都会同时展现被采访者的正面和负面特征。调查者或许并非抱有敌意，但为了保持平衡，就必须同时呈现他们的缺点和优点。然而，另一些调查者则完全预料到他们的工作会损害某些受访者或受访者所属的群体。事实上，这或许正是调查者的最终目的。调查记者往往力求“挖掘”被采访者的“黑料”。

Insofar as investigators are confrontative in their interviewing style, the respondents whom they hope to damage are on notice. This is as far as an investigative reporter is likely to go in obtaining informed consent. No investigative reporter carries consent forms. When investigative reporters have been friendly, understanding, and sympathetic and then use what they were told to damage, respondents may with justification claim they were misled. Investigative reporters can offer as defenses that the respondents were themselves operating in such bad faith that they had no right to expect better from others, and that a higher good was achieved by the investigator’s work. Sometimes these defenses seem good enough.

如果调查人员在采访中采取对抗性的方式，那么他们意图伤害的受访者就已经有所准备。这通常是调查记者在获取知情同意方面所能做到的极限。没有调查记者会随身携带同意书。如果调查记者之前表现得友好、理解和同情，之后却利用他们了解到的信息来伤害受访者，那么受访者完全有理由声称自己受到了误导。调查记者可以辩称，受访者本身就存在恶意行为，因此他们无权期望他人做出更好的行为，而调查人员的工作实现了更高的社会价值。有时，这些辩解似乎足够充分。

THE INVESTIGATOR AS DISPASSIONATE LISTENER AND REPORTER

调查员作为冷静的倾听者和报道者

A third position is to be neither sympathetic nor unsympathetic, nor to attempt to balance the two, but to be concerned only with accurate rendition. The investigator takes the position of telling the facts, just the facts, with no responsibility for the light in which disclosure puts respondents.

第三种立场既不同情也不冷漠，也不试图在两者之间寻求平衡，而只关注准确呈现事实。调查人员的立场是只陈述事实，不承担因披露事实而使受访者处于何种境地的责任。

There is much that is attractive in the notion of the dispassionate investigator. Worth attention, however, is the discordance between the dispassion in the written report and the sense of partnership the investigator is likely to have sought during the interview. The investigator may not be overtly critical, but as Janet Malcolm argues, even a dispassionate report can distress the respondent who provided its material. She sees the problem in the discrepancy between the sense of sympathy that develops in the research interview—and that is an important element in the interviewing partnership—and the more distant stance likely to be displayed in the report:

客观冷静的调查员这一概念固然吸引人。然而，值得注意的是，书面报告中的客观冷静与调查员在访谈中可能寻求的伙伴关系之间存在着矛盾。调查员或许不会公开批评，但正如珍妮特·马尔科姆所言，即使是客观冷静的报告也可能令提供资料的受访者感到不安。她认为问题在于，研究访谈中逐渐形成的同情心——这是访谈伙伴关系的重要组成部分——与报告中可能展现的较为疏离的立场之间存在着差异。

What rankles and sometimes drives [the subject] to extremes of vengefulness, is the deception that has been practiced on him. On reading the article or book in question, he has to face the fact that the journalist—who seemed so friendly and sympathetic, so keen to understand him fully, so remarkably attuned to his vision of things—never had the slightest intention of collaborating with him on his story but always intended to write a story of his own. 10

真正令他耿耿于怀，甚至有时驱使他走向极端复仇的，是他所遭受的欺骗。当他读到那篇文章或书时，不得不面对这样一个事实：那位记者——表面上对他如此友善、如此同情，如此渴望了解他，如此敏锐地捕捉到他的想法——从未想过要与他合作完成他的故事，而是始终打算写一个属于自己的故事。

Investigators, at least when they are starting out, may not always recognize how much printed depictions of respondents can matter to them. I once participated in a class for nonfiction writers. One of the class members was about to publish a story in which the owner of a hairdressing salon was gently ridiculed. A passage in the story pictured the owner delicately eating a chicken wing while talking soothingly to a client on the phone. The class member had sent the owner a prepublication copy of the story, and the owner had responded with an irate phone call threatening legal action. The class, when told this story, couldn’t understand what upset the owner.

调查人员，至少在刚入行时，可能并不总是意识到书面描述对受访者的影响有多大。我曾经参加过一个非虚构写作班。班里有一位学员即将发表一篇报道，文中一位理发店老板受到了温和的嘲讽。报道中有一段描写老板一边优雅地吃着鸡翅，一边轻声细语地和一位顾客通电话。这位学员把这篇报道的预印本寄给了老板，结果老板愤怒地打来电话，威胁要采取法律行动。班里的同学听到这个故事后，都无法理解老板究竟在气什么。

Whether respondents are named or not, investigators have the ability in their reports to present to public view portraits of respondents that are too detailed, authoritative, and permanent for the respondents easily to shrug off.

无论受访者是否被指名道姓，调查人员都可以在报告中向公众呈现受访者过于详细、权威和持久的形象，以至于受访者很难摆脱这些形象的影响。

AN EFFORT AT RESOLUTION

一项寻求解决方案的努力

There is no simple solution to the issue of the stance to be taken toward respondents when writing the report. There may, however, be a variant of the Hippocratic oath that could be adopted by people—investigative reporters excepted—writing up interview materials: at least do no harm.

在撰写报告时，如何对待受访者这个问题并没有简单的解决办法。然而，或许可以借鉴希波克拉底誓言的一种变体，供撰写采访材料的人员（调查记者除外）遵循：至少不要造成伤害。

I like to feel that I can guarantee respondents that although they may not gain by entering into a research relationship with me, they will at least not lose. I may not make this commitment explicit, but I feel it to be necessary for my own moral comfort when engaging a respondent in an interviewing partnership. This does not mean that in writing the report I will necessarily present a sympathetic portrait, although I think it likely that a full portrait will make readers sympathize. It does mean that I will make every effort to make respondents’ own perspective understandable even as I meet my commitment to tell the whole truth.

我希望能够向受访者保证，虽然他们与我建立研究关系未必能从中获益，但至少不会蒙受损失。我可能不会明确做出这样的承诺，但我认为，在与受访者建立访谈合作关系时，这种承诺对于我自身的道德安心至关重要。这并不意味着我在撰写报告时一定会呈现一个充满同情心的形象，尽管我认为，一个完整的形象很可能会引起读者的共鸣。这确实意味着，我将尽一切努力让受访者的视角清晰易懂，同时履行我如实陈述全部事实的承诺。

But what of the investigative reporter? As I have noted, the investigative reporter can argue that the harm suffered by one or more respondents is outweighed by gain for the larger society. And many efforts in this mode have without question made things better for many people, though not for absolutely everyone. 11 Moreover, in investigative reporting the need always to be protective of respondents may need qualification. Some respondents are less vulnerable than others; the rich and powerful, presumably, can take care of themselves. And members of a criminal conspiracy might deserve no concern at all.

那么，调查记者又该如何看待这个问题呢？正如我之前提到的，调查记者可以辩称，对一个或多个受访者造成的伤害，远不及对整个社会带来的益处。毫无疑问，许多此类努力确实改善了许多人的生活，尽管并非对所有人有利。此外，在调查报道中，始终保护受访者的必要性可能需要加以限定。有些受访者比其他受访者更不容易受到伤害；富人和权贵想必能够保护自己。而犯罪团伙的成员则可能根本不值得关注。

But it is a problem for investigative reporting that the harm its reports produce is relatively sure and the gain often less so. So I would worry about a piece strongly critical of the teaching staff of a local high school that would appear in a publication read locally: I would want at least to be sure in my own mind that the piece was as balanced as possible, that it had a chance of producing desirable results, and that there was no better route to encouraging improvement.

但调查性报道面临的一个问题是，其造成的危害几乎是必然的，而带来的益处却往往难以预料。因此，如果一篇措辞严厉地批评当地高中教师的文章发表在当地读者常读的刊物上，我会感到担忧：我至少希望在自己心中确信，这篇文章尽可能地保持平衡，有可能产生理想的效果，并且没有比这更好的方法来促进改进。

It may be that there is no single rule to cover an investigator’s responsibilities to respondents, and that every case must be evaluated separately. But before engaging in investigative reporting I think I would want to be convinced that the justification of the greater good was valid.

或许并没有一条统一的规则可以涵盖调查人员对受访者的责任，每个案件都必须单独评估。但在进行调查报道之前，我认为我应该确信，为了更大的利益而进行调查的理由是充分的。

GETTING IT OUT THE DOOR

把它送出门

Howard S. Becker calls it “getting it out the door.” 12 Lots of research people have trouble getting their report out the door. Yet, as Becker says, that’s what it’s all about.

霍华德·S·贝克尔称之为“把报告发表出去”。许多研究人员都面临着报告发表难的问题。然而，正如贝克尔所说，这才是关键所在。

As I noted earlier, I try to produce a first draft as rapidly as I can. My practice is to dictate a very rough draft of a particular section of the report into a tape recorder, including with it summaries of supporting literature and supporting material from interview transcripts. I rewrite the resulting typescript once or twice and then go on to the next section of the report. I continue in this way until I have a draft of the entire report. Then I rewrite the report, this time spending as much time on a section as it needs. Then I edit.

正如我之前提到的，我会尽可能快地完成初稿。我的做法是，先将报告某一部分的粗略草稿口述到录音机里，同时记录下相关的文献摘要和访谈记录等辅助材料。然后，我会对录好的稿件进行一到两遍的修改，再继续撰写报告的下一部分。如此反复，直到完成整份报告的初稿。之后，我会对报告进行重写，这次会根据需要，在每个部分投入足够的时间。最后，我会进行编辑。

Becker observes that most of writing is rewriting, editing, changing, adding and subtracting. He says: “Few people can write long papers making complex arguments based on complicated data in their heads and get it right on the first try.” 13 It’s necessary to accept that writing is a process of development, and you have to start somewhere. The first draft, if you’ve thought hard about your material, should be partway there. The next draft will be better, and the next better yet. And so on, until you hit diminishing returns or are up against a deadline or can’t stand to work on the material any more.

贝克尔指出，写作的大部分时间都花在重写、编辑、修改、增删上。他说：“很少有人能仅凭脑子里复杂的数据，就写出一篇条理清晰、论证严密的长篇论文。”我们必须接受写作是一个不断发展的过程，而且总要有个开始。如果你认真思考过你的素材，那么初稿应该已经完成了一部分。下一稿会更好，再下一稿会更好。如此反复，直到你遇到瓶颈、面临截稿日期，或者实在无法继续修改为止。

If the first problem in writing is getting the material down on paper, the second is the oppressive presence of standards. No one wants to produce slipshod work. You are likely to want your report to be absolutely firstrate, to meet your own standards and everybody else’s. And you are likely to fear the criticism and loss of people’s respect that would result from work that is flawed. Writing is exposure. 14 Loss of standing as a result of faulty work may indeed occur. But the greater danger, for many investigators, is that fear of producing flawed work will prevent the work from appearing at all.

如果说写作的首要难题在于如何将素材落笔成文，那么第二个难题便是繁复的标准带来的压力。没有人愿意敷衍了事。你肯定希望自己的报告尽善尽美，既符合自己的标准，也符合所有人的标准。你也可能害怕因作品存在缺陷而招致批评，失去他人的尊重。写作是一种展示。 14 因作品缺陷而导致声誉受损的情况确实可能发生。但对许多调查人员而言，更大的危险在于，对作品缺陷的恐惧会让他们最终选择放弃发表作品。

Furthermore, our hopes for our work can set such high standards that it must inevitably fail to meet them. I would like my work to be accurate, precise, absolutely clear, fully inclusive—and besides all that, interesting, even entertaining. But it never is, certainly not the first time through—but not the second or third or fourth time through either. The phrasing isn’t quite right or is repetitious, or the argument isn’t neatly sequential but instead jumps and circles and doubles back. Chapter beginnings are abrupt or else long-winded, chapter sections aren’t in the right order, and chapters don’t end properly. There is too little quotation, or a quotation doesn’t work in context, or there is so much quotation that it overwhelms the narrative. And so on. As I recognize shortcomings, I edit and revise.

此外，我们对作品的期望往往过高，以至于最终作品必然无法达到这些标准。我希望我的作品准确、精炼、清晰、全面——除此之外，还要有趣，甚至引人入胜。但它从来都做不到，第一次肯定做不到——第二次、第三次、第四次也一样。措辞不够恰当，或者重复赘述；论证不够严谨，而是跳跃、兜圈子、兜圈子。章节开头要么突兀，要么冗长；章节内容顺序混乱；章节结尾也不尽如人意。引用太少，或者引用与上下文不符，或者引用过多以至于喧宾夺主。诸如此类的问题不胜枚举。每当我意识到这些不足，我都会进行编辑和修改。

It is good practice to ask for comments from colleagues. At the least, you will remind yourself that you are writing for readers. Colleagues can tell you where your argument is unconvincing or your discussion perplexing, where you have failed to consider existing literature or have misinterpreted the literature you have considered. Some people have established understandings with certain colleagues that enable each to respond reliably to the style and substance of the other’s work. A professional writer I know speaks of “writing buddies” who do this for each other. But colleagues tend to be busy with their own work. Ordinarily they cannot be counted on for close readings. How, then, do you obtain close readings? If you have someone you can call on, whose judgment you respect, you are fortunate. If you do not, you might consider paying for an editorial review from a professional editor in your field.

向同事征求意见是一种很好的做法。至少，这能提醒你，你的文章是写给读者看的。同事可以指出你的论点缺乏说服力或论述令人费解的地方，指出你忽略了哪些现有文献，或者误解了你已参考的文献。有些人与特定的同事建立了默契，彼此能够可靠地对对方作品的风格和内容做出评价。我认识的一位专业作家就提到过“写作伙伴”，他们之间就是这样互相帮助的。但同事们通常都很忙，很难指望他们进行细致的审阅。那么，如何才能获得细致的审阅呢？如果你有可以求助、且你尊重其判断的人，那你很幸运。如果没有，你可以考虑付费请一位你所在领域的专业编辑进行编辑审阅。

Use reactions from others, together with your own assessments, to guide further revisions. But accept that at some point before achievement of the perfect report, the process must end. Getting it out the door, to quote Becker once again, is what it’s all about.

利用他人的反馈以及你自己的评估来指导后续的修改。但也要明白，在最终完成一份完美的报告之前，这个过程终究会结束。再次引用贝克尔的话来说，把报告发出去才是最重要的。

APPENDIX A OTHER NAMES FOR QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWING

附录A 定性访谈的其他名称

The term qualitative interviewing is only one among several terms for the style of interviewing described in this book. Other terms for it include intensive interviewing, in-depth interviewing , and depth interviewing . Each of these characterizations identifies an aspect of the approach. Intensive interviewing emphasizes its concern for detail and completeness in accounts, as does in-depth interviewing. Depth interviewing suggests an effort to obtain the psychological underpinnings of beliefs or opinions.

“定性访谈”只是本书所描述的访谈方法中的几种术语之一。其他术语包括密集访谈、深度访谈和深入访谈。每一种描述都突出了该方法的一个方面。密集访谈和深度访谈都强调对细节和完整性的关注。而深度访谈则旨在探究受访者信念或观点背后的心理机制。

Still other terms for qualitative interviewing are unstructured interviewing and free interviewing . Here what is emphasized is that questions are developed in the course of the interview and flow naturally from what preceded. Related terms are conversational interviewing and narrative interviewing . All these terms draw attention to the relaxed, conversationlike appearance of qualitative interviewing, in contrast to the more formal and distanced appearance of survey interviewing. Actually, none of these terms is entirely accurate. Qualitative interviewing is always constrained by the goals of a study; it is never free to veer off into any area at all. And the structure of qualitative interviewing is unlike that of an ordinary conversation; for one thing, one participant takes responsibility for providing direction, the other for providing content.

定性访谈还有一些其他术语，例如非结构化访谈和自由访谈。这些术语强调的是，问题在访谈过程中逐步形成，并自然地从之前的对话内容中引申出来。相关的术语还有对话式访谈和叙事式访谈。所有这些术语都强调了定性访谈轻松、类似对话的氛围，这与调查式访谈更为正式和疏离的氛围形成对比。实际上，这些术语都不完全准确。定性访谈始终受到研究目标的约束；它绝不能随意偏离主题。而且，定性访谈的结构也不同于普通的对话；首先，一位参与者负责引导访谈方向，另一位参与者负责提供访谈内容。

Another term that emphasizes the style of the interviewing is nondirective research interview . Here what is focused on is the attentive, non-judgmental, and receptive stance of the interviewer and the interviewer’s willingness, like that of a nondirective therapist, simply to listen. Actually, the interviewer in a qualitative interview is not nondirective in the Rogerian manner, that is, reflecting and clarifying but otherwise passive; rather, the interviewer guides the interview through a definite research agenda. And whereas the Rogerian therapist is concerned with helping clients come to terms with themselves, the interviewer must obtain information for a report.

另一个强调访谈风格的术语是非指导性研究访谈。这种访谈方式强调访谈者专注、不评判、接纳的态度，以及访谈者如同非指导性治疗师那样，仅仅倾听的意愿。实际上，在质性访谈中，访谈者并非罗杰斯式的非指导性访谈——即反思和澄清但除此之外保持被动；相反，访谈者会引导访谈围绕既定的研究议程展开。罗杰斯式治疗师关注的是帮助来访者更好地认识自我，而访谈者则必须收集信息以撰写报告。

Social workers, in particular, seem to use the term clinical research interview to refer to qualitative interviewing. The term captures the importance of sensitivity and awareness in this style of interviewing. But it may foster confusion between the aims and approaches of therapeutic work and research interviewing. As I argued in Chapter 5, these are quite different.

社会工作者似乎尤其喜欢用“临床研究访谈”来指代定性访谈。这个术语强调了这种访谈方式中敏感性和意识的重要性。但它也可能造成人们对治疗性工作和研究性访谈的目标和方法的混淆。正如我在第五章中所论述的，这两者截然不同。

Merton, Fiske, and Kendall have described a particular form of qualitative interview as a focused interview . This is a style of qualitative interviewing aimed at eliciting the cognitive and emotional sources of respondents’ reactions to some event. It treats respondents as subjects whose response to the event is the material to be understood, rather than as reporters from whom we will learn about the event itself.1

默顿、菲斯克和肯德尔将一种特殊的定性访谈形式描述为聚焦式访谈。这种定性访谈方式旨在探究受访者对某一事件的认知和情感反应根源。它将受访者视为需要理解的对象，而非事件本身的叙述者。<sup>1</sup>

Still other terms for the approach are regularly being invented. Daniel Levinson referred to his use of qualitative interviewing to learn about respondents’ lives as biographical interviewing .2 The method of qualitative interviewing, although a natural approach to learning from others, is not yet so well established in the world of social science research that it has a single name.

这种方法还有其他一些术语不断涌现。丹尼尔·莱文森将他运用定性访谈来了解受访者生活的方法称为传记式访谈。<sup>2</sup> 定性访谈法虽然是一种自然而然的向他人学习的方法，但在社会科学研究领域尚未得到广泛认可，以至于没有一个统一的名称。

# ↩

APPENDIX B FIELDS THAT USE QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWING

附录 B 使用定性访谈的领域

Qualitative interviewing is important in a number of fields: the social sciences, of course, but also in journalism, advertising research, history, biography, and criminal justice. Different fields have different concerns and use the approach differently. In criminal justice interviewing the goal is highly specific, namely, to learn what happened and who was involved. In the social sciences and in advertising and marketing research, it is important to be able to generalize, to report not just about particular individuals or particular institutions but to make credible assertions about a larger class of individuals or institutions.

定性访谈在许多领域都至关重要：当然包括社会科学，但也包括新闻、广告研究、历史、传记和刑事司法。不同领域关注点不同，运用定性访谈的方法也各不相同。在刑事司法访谈中，目标非常明确，即了解事件经过和涉案人员。而在社会科学以及广告和市场营销研究中，定性访谈则侧重于概括性分析，不仅要报告特定个人或机构的情况，还要对更广泛的个人或机构群体做出可信的论断。

In the social sciences, respondents tend to be treated, as is recommended in this book, as fellow members of the research team, field observers who will report their observations. But in advertising research respondents are more often treated as subjects, guinea pigs in a search for advertising approaches that work. Respondents are led to display in the interview the extent of their knowledge or the nature of their concerns. Investigators can then make assessments of respondents’ cognitive styles, knowledge, intelligence, motivations, or personalities. This use of interviewing treats respondents as psychological subjects rather than as reporters on realities, internal or external, and treats respondents’ reports as test materials.

在社会科学领域，正如本书所建议的那样，受访者通常被视为研究团队的成员，是负责报告观察结果的实地观察员。但在广告研究中，受访者更多地被视为研究对象，是寻找有效广告策略的试验品。受访者在访谈中被引导展现其知识水平或关注点。研究人员随后可以评估受访者的认知风格、知识水平、智力、动机或人格。这种访谈方式将受访者视为心理研究对象，而非对内部或外部现实的叙述者，并将受访者的报告视为测试材料。

In journalism, respondents are sometimes treated as partners in the production of a profile or a story, very much as they might be in a social science effort. But they may also be treated as contestants in a game in which the interviewer seeks factual detail while expecting the respondent to retouch reality to make his or her cause more appealing. Or the respondent may be treated as an antagonist from whom significant material is to be elicited by guile or wrested by confrontation.1

在新闻报道中，受访者有时被视为人物特写或故事创作的合作伙伴，就像在社会科学研究中一样。但他们也可能被视为一场博弈的参与者，采访者在寻求事实细节的同时，也期望受访者对现实进行润色，以使自己的观点更具吸引力。或者，受访者可能被视为对手，需要通过诡计或对抗来获取重要信息。<sup>1</sup>

In criminal justice, respondents who are believed to have information that may incriminate them or people to whom they feel loyal are treated as adversaries to be disarmed, cajoled, confronted, and intimidated into telling their stories. The interviewer tries to establish not partnership with the respondent but moral dominance.2 This approach, although rare in the social sciences, is not unknown; Kinsey’s original interviewing team sometimes acted as friendly cops, assuming the worst of respondents, in the belief that only by taking it for granted that the respondent had engaged in discrediting behavior could they combat attempts to cover up.3

在刑事司法领域，那些被认为掌握可能对自己或自己忠诚的人不利的信息的受访者，会被视为敌对对象，需要通过各种手段解除他们的武装、哄骗、质问和恐吓，迫使他们讲述自己的故事。访谈者试图建立的不是与受访者的伙伴关系，而是道德上的支配地位。<sup>2</sup>这种方法虽然在社会科学领域较为罕见，但也并非闻所未闻；金赛最初的访谈团队有时扮演着“友好警察”的角色，假定受访者最坏的情况，认为只有认定受访者存在诋毁行为，才能有效阻止他们试图掩盖真相。<sup>3</sup>

There is also a difference across fields in the kind of information that is sought. In the social sciences, investigators may hope to provide readers with insight into processes or mechanisms that may explain a range of behaviors or experiences. Historians and journalists are likely to want accurate, vivid, and complete descriptions of particular events and to have relatively less concern for identifying the dynamics of situations. Psychologists and psychiatrists are, like social scientists, concerned with theory, but they are more likely to want either to develop a theory about a particular case or to be able to describe the processes that produce a particular type of case.

不同领域对信息的需求也存在差异。在社会科学领域，研究者可能希望为读者提供对各种行为或经历的解释过程或机制的深刻见解。历史学家和记者则更倾向于对特定事件进行准确、生动和完整的描述，而较少关注情境的动态变化。心理学家和精神病学家与社会科学家一样，也关注理论，但他们更倾向于构建关于特定案例的理论，或者描述产生特定类型案例的过程。

And yet even though every field that uses qualitative interviews does so differently, there is a common core to the approach across fields. In every field the qualitative interview is an effort to elicit from respondents detailed, dense, and coherent reports of external or internal experiences from which descriptions, inferences, and conclusions can be drawn.

尽管各个领域运用定性访谈的方式各不相同，但其核心方法却有共通之处。在所有领域，定性访谈的目的都是为了从受访者那里获取详尽、充实且连贯的外部或内部经验描述，以便从中得出结论和推论。

APPENDIX C SOURCES OF BIAS AND THEIR CONTROL

附录C 偏见的来源及其控制

Experimenters try to guard against “experimenter effects,” that is, effects not due to the experimental treatment but, rather, to the experimenters’ acting, unbeknownst to themselves, to produce the results they expect and want. As a protection against experimenter effects, studies of drug effectiveness use a double-blind procedure in which the experimenter who administers the drug does not know which subjects are in the experimental group and which are controls. We cannot avail ourselves of doubleblind procedures when we do qualitative interview studies. How then can we protect ourselves, and our studies, from experimenter effects?

实验者试图避免“实验者效应”，即并非实验处理本身造成的效应，而是由于实验者在不知不觉中为了获得预期结果而采取的行动所致。为了防止实验者效应，药物疗效研究采用双盲程序，即给药的实验者不知道哪些受试者属于实验组，哪些属于对照组。然而，我们在进行定性访谈研究时无法采用双盲程序。那么，我们该如何保护自己和我们的研究免受实验者效应的影响呢？

A beginning is made if we recognize how vulnerable to experimenter effects the qualitative interview study is. As investigators, we are ourselves present in the study in every phase, from selection of respondents to report writing. In the sampling phase, we can slant the sample toward fellow believers. While interviewing, we can ask leading questions and be friendly toward responses that support our preconceptions. In our analysis of material we can, instead of getting to the heart of the matter, try to find support for a position we brought with us to the study. And in our reporting we can easily give that position the best of the argument. We can do all this without full awareness of what we are doing.

如果我们认识到定性访谈研究极易受到实验者效应的影响，那么一切就都迈出了第一步。作为研究者，我们参与了研究的每一个阶段，从选择受访者到撰写报告。在抽样阶段，我们可能会倾向于选择与我们观点相近的受访者。在访谈过程中，我们可能会提出引导性问题，并对那些支持我们预设观念的回答表现出友好态度。在分析材料时，我们可能会试图寻找证据来支持我们事先带入研究的立场，而不是探究问题的核心。在撰写报告时，我们很容易将最有力的论据赋予我们的立场。而所有这些，我们都可能在不知不觉中完成。

On the other hand, most investigators, I believe, select reasonably adequate samples; conduct interviews whose aim is to learn rather than to demonstrate; perform dispassionate, responsible, and careful analysis; and are faithful to their findings in their presentations. Here, briefly, is how pitfalls might present themselves in the different stages of qualitative interview studies and how they can be avoided.

另一方面，我认为大多数研究者都会选择相当合适的样本；进行旨在学习而非论证的访谈；进行客观、负责和严谨的分析；并在报告中忠实地呈现研究结果。以下简要介绍定性访谈研究不同阶段可能出现的陷阱以及如何避免这些陷阱。

SAMPLING

采样

Biased sampling occurs when we take respondents who have particular points of view as a representative sample of a more inclusive group. A study of political ideas based on interviews at the Republican National Convention would not necessarily be a biased sample of elite Republican belief but would be misleading as a basis for learning about American belief.

当我们选择持有特定观点的受访者作为更具包容性的群体的代表性样本时，就会出现有偏抽样。一项基于共和党全国代表大会访谈的政治理念研究，虽然未必能反映共和党精英的信念，但作为了解美国民众信念的基础，却会产生误导。

A random sample is always an unbiased representation of the population from which it is drawn. When, as is most often the case, we must make do with a convenience sample, we should try to ensure that it contains adequate range on critically important dimensions. For example, in a study of the experience of shared parenthood, this might mean finding instances in settings that are supportive of such efforts, such as a suburb favored by academic couples, and instances in settings that are not supportive of such efforts, such as a working-class ethnic neighborhood. Failing this, we have to make clear the limits of the population to which we can generalize.

随机样本始终是对其所抽取总体的无偏代表。然而，当我们不得不使用便利样本时（这种情况最为常见），我们应该努力确保样本在关键维度上具有足够的代表性。例如，在研究共同抚养子女的经历时，这可能意味着我们需要在支持这种做法的环境中寻找案例，例如学术夫妇偏爱的郊区，以及在不支持这种做法的环境中寻找案例，例如工人阶级聚居的少数族裔社区。如果无法做到这一点，我们就必须明确指出我们可以推广的总体范围。

INTERVIEWING

面试

Biased interviewing occurs when we encourage respondents to provide material supportive of our thesis. This can be done in the way we present ourselves and the study to respondents, by the kinds of questions we ask, and by the way we treat responses. We can guard against bias in the interview by establishing a research partnership in which the respondent understands that what we need is a full and accurate report, by obtaining detailed, concrete material rather than context-dependent generalizations, and by fashioning a substantive frame for our study that effectively captures the complexities of whatever it is we are studying.

当我们鼓励受访者提供支持我们论点的材料时，就会出现访谈偏见。这可能体现在我们向受访者介绍自己和研究的方式、我们提出的问题类型以及我们对待受访者回答的方式上。我们可以通过以下方式避免访谈偏见：建立研究伙伴关系，让受访者理解我们需要的是完整准确的报告；获取详细、具体的材料，而不是依赖于特定语境的泛泛之谈；以及为我们的研究构建一个实质性的框架，有效地捕捉我们所研究对象的复杂性。

We can reassure readers of our report about the quality of our material by providing a copy of our interview guide. Even though every interview is likely to depart from the guide in some respect, the guide will suggest the concerns of the study and the issues it explored. The presentation of interview excerpts can then suggest the adequacy of our interviewing.

为了让读者放心，我们可以通过提供访谈指南来保证报告材料的质量。尽管每次访谈都可能在某些方面与指南有所出入，但指南会阐明本研究的关注点和探讨议题。访谈摘录的呈现方式可以体现我们访谈的有效性。

INTERPRETATION AND REPORTING

解释与报告

The interpretation and reporting of our material are procedures especially vunerable to the introduction of bias. We can easily make an argument come out our way by treating comments that support our view as gospel and subjecting to skeptical scrutiny those that don’t, by reporting material we like and disdaining the rest, and in general by behaving like a lawyer with a brief to advance. Our only defense against this happening is to discipline ourselves to deal fully and fairly with all the evidence and to report everything we’ve learned about an issue, absolutely everything, including cases that don’t fit our theories as well as cases that do.

我们对材料的解读和报道过程特别容易受到偏见的影响。我们很容易通过以下方式使论点朝着有利于我们的方向发展：将支持我们观点的评论奉为圭臬，对不支持的评论进行质疑；只报道我们喜欢的材料，而对其他材料不屑一顾；总而言之，就像律师带着案情陈述一样行事。我们避免这种情况发生的唯一方法是约束自己，全面、公正地处理所有证据，并报道我们对某个问题的所有了解，绝对的所有信息，包括那些不符合我们理论的案例，以及那些符合我们理论的案例。

INTELLECTUAL HONESTY

知识分子的诚实

A former head of a department of government who, while in government, had been determined that a program he was sponsoring be the one adopted, once said to me that he had often sponsored research whose results he thought would support the program. If the results came out the way he wanted them to, he would publicize them for all they were worth. If they did not, he would bury them.

一位曾在政府部门任职的官员曾告诉我，他一心想让由他资助的项目最终被采纳。他经常资助一些研究，认为研究结果会支持该项目。如果结果如他所愿，他会大肆宣传；如果结果不如他预期，他就会将其束之高阁。

I suppose it is all right for people in or out of government to choose the research they will honor. It is not all right, though, for the people doing the research to be determined that their findings should come out the way they want them to. Yet people convinced of the social value of a cause sometimes do feel justified in selecting and stretching research results so that their report supports their cause. They treat research as a form of rhetoric rather than a method of learning.

我认为，无论身处政府内外，人们有权选择他们认可的研究成果。然而，研究人员却不能固执己见，强求研究结果按照他们的意愿呈现。但有些人深信某个事业具有社会价值，因此他们有时会觉得有理由选择并曲解研究结果，以使报告支持他们的事业。他们把研究当作一种修辞手段，而非学习方法。

People who do research should have only one concern in their work, and that is to capture, with scrupulous honesty, the way things are. Then, after the work has been completed, they can think about its implications for social action. As for work done by others that has been slanted to shore up an outlook or program, we can trust that it will ultimately lose value in the marketplace of ideas. Although the validity of a research report is only one among many determinants of its credibility, we can reasonably hope that it will prove decisive in the end.

从事研究的人应该只专注于一件事，那就是以一丝不苟的诚实态度，如实地记录事物的本来面目。研究完成后，他们才能思考其对社会行动的意义。至于那些为了支持某种观点或纲领而带有偏见的研究，我们可以预见，它们最终会在思想市场中失去价值。尽管研究报告的有效性只是其可信度众多决定因素之一，但我们有理由相信，它最终会发挥决定性作用。

# ↩

APPENDIX D CONSENT FORMS

附录D 同意书

Consent forms are required for most studies that are federally funded or that are conducted under the auspices of universities or medical institutions. Exceptions may be made by an institution’s review board for some studies where the forms would be inappropriate, so long as the process of interviewing poses minimal risk to respondents: for example, a study in which visitors to a museum are asked for brief appraisals of exhibits. Studies based on telephone interviews would be required to obtain consent to a verbal statement of the contents of a consent form.

大多数由联邦政府资助或在大学或医疗机构主持下开展的研究都需要知情同意书。对于某些研究，如果访谈过程对受访者的风险极低，例如，一项要求博物馆参观者对展品进行简短评价的研究，则机构审查委员会可以酌情豁免知情同意书。基于电话访谈的研究则需要获得受访者对知情同意书内容的口头陈述。

Consent forms are not universally required. Journalists are for the most part unaware of consent forms, although they do inform respondents that they are journalists. Consent forms are likely to be waived for political scientists who are interviewing important government figures, perhaps on the assumption that people so well placed can take care of themselves. And anthropologists studying another society may be excused on grounds of the likely unfamiliarity to their respondents of the very idea of a consent form.

并非所有情况下都需要签署知情同意书。大多数记者并不了解知情同意书，尽管他们会告知受访者自己的记者身份。政治学家在采访重要政府人物时，通常无需签署知情同意书，或许是因为人们认为身居要职的人能够妥善处理自身事务。而研究其他社会的的人类学家，也可能因为受访者可能不熟悉知情同意书的概念而被免除签署知情同意书的义务。

My own view is that, in the sort of interviewing exemplified in this book, consent forms are usually a good thing. They can help establish that the interviewing relationship is a working partnership, and they can provide the respondent with a clear statement of the aims, auspices, and methods of the study.

我个人认为，在本书所举例的这类访谈中，知情同意书通常是有益的。它们有助于确立访谈关系是一种合作关系，并且可以向受访者清晰地说明研究的目的、组织和方法。

A consent form that covers the following issues would be consistent with federal guidelines for the conduct of social research. 1

一份涵盖以下问题的知情同意书将符合联邦社会研究行为准则。

  1. A statement of the study’s objectives and methods .
    研究目标和方法的说明。
  2. When I draft a consent form I begin by saying what will be the focus of the study in a way that will suggest the topics that might be included within the study’s frame. I also try to make the study seem interesting and potentially valuable.
    起草知情同意书时，我首先会阐明研究的重点，并以此暗示研究可能涵盖的主题。我还会尽量让研究显得有趣且具有潜在价值。
  3. How it happened that the respondent was chosen .
    受访者是如何被选中的？
  4. This isn’t actually required by federal guidelines, but respondents almost always want to know. Federal guidelines do suggest that respondents be told the approximate size of the sample.
    联邦指南实际上并没有强制要求，但受访者几乎总是想知道。联邦指南建议告知受访者样本的大致规模。
  5. What will be asked of the respondent .
    将会向受访者提出哪些问题？
  6. Here I tell respondents that we are asking them to participate in one or more interviews, and that the interviews will be taped and transcribed.
    在这里，我告诉受访者，我们邀请他们参加一次或多次访谈，访谈将被录音并转录。
  7. Who will have access to the respondent’s materials .
    谁可以查阅答辩人的材料？
  8. The name of the responsible person and institution is probably enough, but when I am the study director I generally list not only my own name but also the names of the other members of the study’s staff.
    负责人和机构的姓名可能就足够了，但如果我是研究负责人，我通常不仅会列出我自己的名字，还会列出研究团队其他成员的名字。
  9. A description of reasonably foreseeable risks or discomforts and of reasonably expectable benefits .
    对合理可预见的风险或不适以及合理可预期的益处的描述。
  10. This statement can be weighted toward the negative, because every potential risk in the study should be listed, but only the likely benefits.
    这一说法可能偏向负面，因为研究中所有潜在的风险都应该列出，而可能的好处却只列出。
  11. In most interview studies the primary risk is a breach of confidentiality. Federal guidelines require that there be “a statement describing the extent, if any, to which confidentiality of records identifying the subject will be maintained.” On the benefit side, there is almost always some possible benefit in talking, although it can’t be guaranteed.
    在大多数访谈研究中，主要风险在于泄露隐私。联邦指南要求必须“声明将在多大程度上（如有）维护识别受访者身份的记录的保密性”。从益处方面来看，交谈几乎总能带来一些潜在益处，尽管无法保证。
  12. A statement that participation is voluntary and that respondents’ questions will be answered fully .
    声明参与完全自愿，并保证受访者的所有问题都将得到充分解答。
  13. This is required by federal guidelines.
    这是联邦指导方针的要求。
  14. What will be published .
    将要发表的内容。
  15. This is not required by federal guidelines, but is likely to be among the questions respondents will have. 215
    联邦指南并未对此作出要求，但这很可能是受访者会提出的问题之一。215
  16. To whom questions should be directed .
    问题应该问谁？
  17. Federal guidelines require that the respondent be told whom to contact with questions about the study. I think the respondent should be given the telephone numbers both of the institutional review board and of the study’s director.
    联邦指南要求告知受访者如有任何关于研究的问题，应联系谁。我认为应该向受访者提供机构审查委员会和研究负责人的电话号码。

Consent forms should be kept concise, one page if possible. It seems to me that it takes long enough for a respondent to grasp a single-page form. A longer form strikes me as forbidding. But I have seen consent forms that fill two pages and I can imagine forms in medical settings that are even longer.

知情同意书应尽量简洁，最好只有一页。我觉得，让受访者理解一份只有一页的表格已经足够费时了。篇幅过长的表格会让人望而却步。但我见过两页的知情同意书，而且我能想象在医疗机构中，表格的篇幅可能会更长。

My practice is to bring two copies of a consent form to a first interview, both of them signed by me as director of the study. I give both of them to the respondent, and ask the respondent to read the form, sign one copy and give it to me, and keep the other.

我的做法是，在第一次访谈时携带两份知情同意书，两份都由我作为研究负责人签字。我会将两份知情同意书交给受访者，请受访者阅读，并在其中一份上签字交给我，另一份由受访者自行保留。

以下是一份同意书的示例。

同意书 工作与家庭研究中心

马萨诸塞大学

退休人士研究

  1. What is the aim of the study? The aim of the study is to learn about different ways of organizing life in the retirement years.     这项研究的目的是什么？这项研究旨在了解人们在退休后如何安排生活。我们希望了解不同的人如何决定退休后的生活方式，他们在生活的各个方面有哪些经历，以及哪些因素会影响他们的幸福感。我们的最终目标是帮助社会上的其他人更好地应对退休生活。

    谁会知道我说了什么？只有研究团队的工作人员才能接触到您的录音和文字记录。工作人员包括：马萨诸塞大学波士顿分校的社会学家、该研究的负责人罗伯特·S·韦斯博士；该校的另一位社会学家安娜·桑特安娜；研究办公室经理约翰·德拉比克；文字记录员玛丽·科菲；以及访谈员简·多伊和罗伯特·罗。
  9. What risks and benefits are associated with participation? We do not foresee any risks to you other than a possible breach of confidentiality. APPENDIX E
附录 E
QUANTITATIVE CODING OF
对
QUALITATIVE INTERVIEW
定性访谈
MATERIAL
材料的定量编码

THE CODING OF QUALITATIVE DATA

定性数据的编码

If a set of qualitative interviews has covered more or less the same areas, it is possible to code within those areas in the same way that open-ended items in surveys are coded. That is, it is possible to make up codes for specific issues so that respondents who would be rated as having the same positions on the issue are given the same code.

如果一组定性访谈涵盖的领域大致相同，则可以像对调查问卷中的开放式问题进行编码一样，对这些领域内的问题进行编码。也就是说，可以为特定问题创建代码，以便将在该问题上立场相同的受访者赋予相同的代码。

Depending on the number of issues to be coded and on the ambition and the funding level of the study, coding can be anything from a major undertaking involving several people over the course of months to a single evening’s work. Coding would be a major undertaking if dozens of issues were to be considered and the reliability and validity of the coding were to be assessed. It would be a much simpler enterprise if the investigator wanted only to judge respondents on one issue, such as the quality of their adaptation to their situation. In the simplest case a single code might be worked out, with the investigator applying it. In the most ambitious case many codes might be worked out, tested and retested for reliability and validity, and then used as a basis for assessment of respondents by several coders.

根据需要编码的问题数量、研究的目标和经费水平，编码工作可能耗时数月，需要多人参与，也可能只需一个晚上即可完成。如果需要考虑数十个问题，并评估编码的信度和效度，那么编码工作将是一项艰巨的任务。如果研究者只想评估受访者在某个特定问题上的表现，例如他们对自身处境的适应程度，那么编码工作就会简单得多。最简单的情况下，研究者只需制定一个编码，并应用该编码即可。而最复杂的情况则是制定多个编码，反复测试其信度和效度，然后由多位编码员以此为基础对受访者进行评估。

What follows is a page of a code book used in a coding effort that was part of the analysis of material from my study of occupationally successful men. The code book contained almost two hundred codes dealing with material in the areas of work, family, friendship, and well-being. Each code was devised from a reading of early interviews and then revised after being used for new interviews by several staff members. When the codes seemed both stable (no need for new categories) and reliable (different staff members made the same coding decisions), they were used by a team of five coders. Two to four hours were required to code the three interviews we had with most respondents; where we had four or five interviews with a respondent, more than four hours might be required for coding.

以下是我在对职业成功男性的研究资料进行分析时使用的编码手册的一页。该编码手册包含近两百个编码，涵盖工作、家庭、友谊和幸福感等领域。每个编码都基于对早期访谈的阅读而制定，并在几位工作人员使用新访谈资料后进行了修订。当编码既稳定（无需新增类别）又可靠（不同工作人员做出的编码决定一致）时，便由一个五人编码团队进行使用。大多数受访者的三次访谈需要两到四个小时进行编码；如果受访者有四到五次访谈，则编码可能需要四个多小时。

SEGMENT OF A CODE BOOK:

The material for each of these codes could appear anywhere in the interview transcript. It was necessary for coders to be ready, as they read through the transcript, to use any of the codes in the code book. Thus, a coder might have found that the passage being read provided material for code item 25 and that the next passage provided material for code item 14. Generally, however, material dealing with a particular topic showed up in most transcripts at about the same place: material on experience at work in the first interview, on fathering toward the end of the second, and so on.

这些代码对应的材料可能出现在访谈记录的任何位置。编码员在阅读记录时，必须做好准备，随时使用代码手册中的任何代码。例如，编码员可能发现正在阅读的段落提供了代码项 25 的材料，而下一段则提供了代码项 14 的材料。不过，通常情况下，涉及特定主题的材料在大多数记录中出现的位置都大致相同：第一次访谈中涉及工作经验的材料，第二次访谈末尾涉及为人父的经历的材料，以此类推。

So that coder judgments could be appraised, it was necessary for coders to note in their code books the material on which they based their coding decisions. The “basis for coding” lines were used by the coders for brief quotations or summaries of the respondent’s statements, and coders also indicated the page of the transcript on which such material appeared.

为了便于评估编码员的判断，编码员必须在编码簿中记录他们做出编码决定的依据。编码员在“编码依据”栏中记录受访者陈述的简短引述或摘要，并注明这些内容出现在笔录的哪一页。

To understand the material of this study we found it invaluable to have not only the actual counts of how many respondents reported what but also the quotation and page references. The procedure was expensive but, at least in this particular study, worthwhile.

为了理解这项研究的材料，我们发现，不仅需要统计有多少受访者报告了哪些内容，还需要提供引文和页码参考，这一点至关重要。虽然这种方法成本较高，但至少在本研究中是值得的。

It might happen in another study that there is only one issue important to code: adaptation to retirement, for example. The code building procedure would be the same as if there were many such issues: Read the interviews to identify potential indicators for codings; specify the potential indicators; have several people attempt to use the potential indicators to code new interviews; work together to identify problems with the codings and resolve them; repeat the procedure until the code stabilizes and appears both reliable and valid.

在另一项研究中，可能只有一个重要的编码问题：例如，退休适应。在这种情况下，编码构建流程与存在多个此类问题时相同：阅读访谈记录，识别潜在的编码指标；明确这些潜在指标；让几位研究人员尝试使用这些潜在指标对新的访谈记录进行编码；共同协作，找出编码中的问题并加以解决；重复上述流程，直至编码稳定且可靠有效。

In qualitative interviewing it will almost certainly be the case that not every issue will be explored with every respondent. This means that in most codes a number of respondents will be coded as “Not enough material to judge” or something like this. It may nevertheless be useful to be able to report, “Of the fifty respondents who provided enough material to judge, 56% reported that …”

在定性访谈中，几乎可以肯定的是，并非所有问题都会与每位受访者进行探讨。这意味着在大多数编码中，一些受访者会被标记为“材料不足，无法判断”或类似情况。尽管如此，能够报告“在提供了足够材料以供判断的五十位受访者中，56%的人表示……”仍然可能是有用的。

We found a database program to be useful as a way of dealing with the mixture of numbers and text that our coding approach produced. Such a program can also provide simple statistics, including both the proportions of responses associated with particular coding categories and crossclassifications.

我们发现数据库程序对于处理我们编码方法产生的数字和文本混合数据非常有用。这类程序还可以提供简单的统计数据，包括与特定编码类别相关的响应比例以及交叉分类情况。

Chapter 1 Introduction

第一章 引言

1 When the interviewing conducted for survey studies is subjected to close scrutiny, questions regarding the interpretability of responses arise. Careful empirical study has demonstrated that survey studies involve a good deal of miscommunication; see Lucy Suchman and Brigitte Jordan, “Interactional Troubles in Face-to-Face Survey Interviews,” Journal of the American Statistical Association , 85, no. 409 (March 1990): 232-41. The journal followed the paper with comments by informed discussants. Most agreed that the validity of data from survey studies would be enhanced if the interviewers were permitted more freedom in phrasing and interpreting questions. Another position, however, was that the cure for the ills of survey studies lies in improvement in the Grafting of questions, after which the survey approach should be adhered to unchanged. See also Jean Peneff, “The Observers Observed: French Survey Researchers at Work,” Social Problems , 35, no. 5 (1988): 520. See also Charles L. Briggs, Learning How to Ask (New York: Cambridge University Press, 1986). Survey studies ordinarily do not recognize problems of miscommunication. As Elliot Mishler writes, the more controlled approach of survey research, compared with qualitative interview studies, does not make for lesser involvement with language and intersubjectivity but only obscures the involvement; see his Research Interviewing: Context and Narrative (Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University Press, 1986).

Chapter 3 Preparation for Interviewing

第三章 面试准备

1 The term accounting scheme was, I think, first used by Paul Lazarsfeld and Morris Rosenberg. It appears in their book The Language of Social Research: A Reader in the Methodology of Social Research (New York: Free Press, 1955), pp. 387-491. An example of an accounting scheme is provided by J. Stannard Baker’s study of accidents, “A Framework for Assessment of Causes of Automobile Accidents,” in Lazarsfeld and Rosenberg, pp. 438-48. Baker’s accounting scheme considers early or remote causes that provided conditions for the accident, such as poor highway design; contributing causes that led directly to the accident, such as speeding to get home for dinner; key events, such as sliding off the road; responses to key events (or failures to respond) that made the accident happen in just the way it did, such as trying to steer the car back on the road; the accident event itself, such as coming to rest in a ditch or hitting another car; and the ultimate result in property damage and human hurt. This is not a theory of how accidents happen that can be said to be true or false, but rather a framework for telling the story of particular accidents that, when applied, will prove useful or not useful.

1 我认为，“事故原因分析框架”（accounting scheme）一词最早由保罗·拉扎斯菲尔德（Paul Lazarsfeld）和莫里斯·罗森伯格（Morris Rosenberg）提出。它出现在他们的著作《社会研究的语言：社会研究方法论读本》（纽约：自由出版社，1955年）第387-491页。J·斯坦纳德·贝克（J. Stannard Baker）关于交通事故的研究“汽车事故原因评估框架”（载于拉扎斯菲尔德和罗森伯格的著作第438-448页）提供了一个事故原因分析框架的例子。贝克的分析框架考虑了为事故提供条件的早期或远期原因，例如糟糕的公路设计；直接导致事故发生的促成因素，例如为了赶回家吃晚饭而超速行驶；关键事件，例如车辆滑出路面；对关键事件的应对措施（或应对不力），例如试图将车辆驶回道路，这些措施最终导致了事故的发生；以及事故事件本身，例如车辆最终停在沟渠中或撞上其他车辆。最终导致财产损失和人员伤亡。这并非一套可以断言真假的事故发生理论，而是一个用于讲述特定事故案例的框架，其应用效果可能有用，也可能无用。

2 There are all sorts of functional approaches, including Malinowski functionalism, with its emphasis on individual need; Radcliffe-Brown functionalism, with its emphasis on the needs of the collectivity; and the structure—function Parsonian approach modeled on biological description. I offer here a version of Radcliffe-Brown functionalism that seems to me often useful in synchronie studies. Robert Merton provides a justly celebrated exposition of functional analysis in the chapter “Manifest and Latent Functions” in his Social Theory and Social Structure (New York: Free Press, 1968 Enlarged Edition), pp. 73-138.

2 功能主义方法多种多样，包括强调个体需求的马林诺夫斯基功能主义；强调集体需求的拉德克利夫-布朗功能主义；以及以生物学描述为模型的帕森斯结构-功能方法。我在此提出一种拉德克利夫-布朗功能主义的版本，我认为它在共时性研究中常常很有用。罗伯特·默顿在其著作《社会理论与社会结构》（纽约：自由出版社，1968年增订版）的“显性功能与隐性功能”一章（第73-138页）中对功能分析进行了广受赞誉的阐述。

3 Matthew B. Miles and A. Michael Huberman believe that conceptual frameworks may largely be implicit in the preconceptions of the investigator. They write that “terms such as ‘social climate,’ ‘stress,’ or ‘role conflict’ are typically labels we put on bins containing a lot of discrete events and behaviors. When we assign a label to a bin, we may or may not know how all the contents of the bin fit together, or how this bin relates to another one. But any researcher, no matter how inductive in approach, knows which bins to start with and what their general contents are likely to be.” Bins come from the investigator’s theory and experience, as well as from the general objectives of the study envisioned. “Laying out those bins, giving each a descriptive or inferential name, and getting some clarity about their interrelationships is what a conceptual framework is all about.” See their Qualitative Data Analysis: A Sourcebook of New Methods (Beverly Hills, Calif.: Sage Publications, 1984), p. 28.

3 马修·B·迈尔斯和A·迈克尔·胡伯曼认为，概念框架很大程度上可能隐含在研究者的预设观念中。他们写道：“诸如‘社会氛围’、‘压力’或‘角色冲突’之类的术语，通常是我们用来标记包含大量离散事件和行为的类别的标签。当我们给一个类别贴上标签时，我们可能知道也可能不知道类别中的所有内容是如何相互关联的，或者这个类别与其他类别之间有何联系。但任何研究者，无论其研究方法多么归纳，都知道应该从哪些类别入手，以及这些类别通常包含哪些内容。” 这些类别来源于研究者的理论和经验，以及研究的总体目标。“将这些类别划分出来，给每个类别赋予一个描述性或推断性的名称，并明确它们之间的相互关系，这就是概念框架的全部意义所在。”参见他们的著作《定性数据分析：新方法资源手册》（加利福尼亚州比佛利山庄：Sage出版社，1984年），第39页。 28.

4 Dean Hammer and Aaron Wildavsky, writing about guides to be used with a panel of informants, recommend keeping guide questions to a minimum. 4 迪恩·哈默和亚伦·维尔达夫斯基在撰写关于与一组受访者一起使用的访谈指南时，建议尽量减少指南问题的数量。然而，他们认为预先设想可能出现的尴尬情况并事先拟定合适的提问措辞可能很有用；参见他们的“开放式半结构化访谈”，第57-101页。

Chapter 5 Issues in Interviewing

第五章 面试中的问题

1 The concept of talking at a middle distance is Tom Scheff’s. He discusses it in Catharsis in Healing, Ritual, and Drama (Berkeley: University of California Press, 1979).

1 “中距离谈话”的概念是汤姆·谢夫提出的。他在《治愈、仪式和戏剧中的宣泄》（伯克利：加州大学出版社，1979 年）一书中对此进行了讨论。

2 For an extended discussion of the usefulness of talk, see James W. Pennebaker, Opening Up (New York: William Morrow, 1990).

2 有关谈话的益处的更详细讨论，请参阅 James W. Pennebaker 的《敞开心扉》（纽约：William Morrow，1990 年）。

3 Barbara Laslett and Rhona Rapoport describe handling a situation in which an interviewer asked questions a respondent resented: “During the first interview with both parents, there appeared to be an openness and willingness to discuss events in the family’s early history. At the second interview (which was scheduled for the father separately) the mother, in a side conversation with the interviewer, voiced her feelings of resentment that the first interview covered material that was, in her mind, an illegitimate subject of inquiry. Following the supervision in which this reaction was discussed, the interviewer dealt directly with the issue…. On the telephone … the interviewer apologized for having moved into areas of inquiry which the mother did not feel were ‘proper’ without first working through with her what her attitudes were. Once the legitimacy of the mother’s feelings were acknowledged, the mother became more receptive.” See Laslett and Rapoport, “Collaborative Interviewing and Interactive Research,” Journal of Marriage and the Family , 37 (November 1975): 968-77.

3 芭芭拉·拉斯莱特和罗娜·拉波波特描述了如何处理面试官询问受访者反感的问题的情况：“在第一次与父母双方面谈时，他们似乎都愿意坦诚地讨论家庭早期的历史。在第二次面谈（单独安排与父亲面谈）中，母亲在与面试官的私下交谈中表达了她的不满，认为第一次面谈涉及的内容在她看来是不恰当的。在督导讨论过这一反应后，面试官直接处理了这个问题……在电话中……面试官为自己未经事先了解母亲的态度就擅自进入她认为‘不恰当’的询问领域而道歉。一旦母亲的感受得到认可，她就变得更加愿意接受采访了。”参见 Laslett 和 Rapoport，“合作访谈和互动研究”，《婚姻与家庭杂志》，37（1975 年 11 月）：968-77。

Cicourel, “Fertility, Family Planning, and the Social Organization of Family Life: Some Methodological Issues,” Journal of Social Issues , 23, no. 4 (1967): 57-81. Cicourel’s approach was to have interviewers end the first interview early if they felt they couldn’t get along with the subject or felt uncomfortable within the household or with the subject’s spouse. Cicourel would then send in another interviewer.

10 某些访谈员可能与特定受访者不合拍，原因不明，而换一位访谈员或许效果更好。拉斯莱特和拉波波特在《合作访谈与互动研究》以及亚伦·V·西库雷尔在《生育、计划生育与家庭生活的社会组织：一些方法论问题》（《社会问题杂志》，第23卷，第4期（1967年）：57-81页）中描述了为实现良好的访谈员与受访者匹配所做的努力。西库雷尔的方法是，如果访谈员感觉与受访者相处不融洽，或者在受访者家中或与受访者的配偶相处感到不自在，就提前结束第一次访谈。然后，西库雷尔会安排另一位访谈员接手。

11 See also John P. Dean and William Foote Whyte, “How Do You Know If the Informer Is Telling the Truth?” Human Organization , 17, no. 2 (1958): 34-38.

11 另见 John P. Dean 和 William Foote Whyte，“如何知道告密者是否在说真话？”《人类组织》，17，第 2 期（1958 年）：34-38。

12 Tamara Hareven has suggested that in interview-based historical research only the corroborated statement should be accepted as fact. See her Family Time and Industrial Time: The Relationship Between the Family and Work in a New England Industrial Community (New York: Cambridge University Press, 1982). Hareven tells the story of a former worker in the textile factory whose history she studied who reported that her employment at the factory ended at the time of a strike. The company’s ledger book, however, showed that the respondent had continued to be employed. Told of the discrepancy, the respondent said that the strike had so changed the factory’s culture that it became a different place. However, if the respondent’s employment history had been a central concern of the study, she could have been asked “Could you walk me through how it happened that you left the factory?” and her perception of the situation, in which it was the factory that had left her, would have surfaced.

12 塔玛拉·哈雷文 (Tamara Hareven) 认为，在基于访谈的历史研究中，只有经过核实的陈述才能被视为事实。参见她的著作《家庭时间与工业时间：新英格兰工业社区的家庭与工作关系》(纽约：剑桥大学出版社，1982)。哈雷文讲述了一位曾在她研究过的纺织厂工作的前工人的故事。这位工人声称，她在工厂的雇佣关系是在一次罢工期间结束的。然而，公司的账簿显示，这位受访者仍在职。当被告知这一矛盾之处时，这位受访者表示，罢工彻底改变了工厂的文化，使之变成了一个截然不同的地方。然而，如果研究的重点是这位受访者的雇佣经历，那么可以问她：“您能跟我说说您离开工厂的经过吗？”这样，她对当时情况的看法——是工厂抛弃了她——就会浮出水面。

Appendix C Sources of Bias and Their Control

附录C 偏见的来源及其控制

Mark Kramer brought to my attention “The Art of the Confrontational Interview,” by Chris Ison and Lou Kilzer, reporters for the Star Tribune in Minneapolis. Their article appeared in the 1991 volume of Writing Coach , a newsletter for journalists published in Milwaukee. Ison and Kilzer won the 1990 Pulitzer Prize for investigative journalism for a series on people who profited from fires. The interviewing techniques they describe include confronting respondents with evidence that they were lying, as a way of pressing them to be more truthful; indicating to respondents that they, the reporters, were already fully informed even when they weren’t; and returning to respondents again and again, whenever new information could justify new questions.

马克·克雷默向我推荐了克里斯·艾森和卢·基尔泽合著的《对抗式采访的艺术》。艾森和基尔泽是明尼阿波利斯《明星论坛报》的记者，他们的文章发表在1991年出版的《写作教练》通讯上，这是一份面向记者的通讯。艾森和基尔泽凭借一系列关于火灾中牟利者的调查报道，荣获1990年普利策调查新闻奖。他们描述的采访技巧包括：用证据揭露受访者撒谎，以此迫使他们说实话；即使并非完全知情，也要暗示受访者记者已经掌握了所有信息；以及只要有新信息出现，就反复追问受访者。

The following excerpts are from a text by Arthur S. Aubry, Jr., Criminal Interrogation , 3rd ed. (Springfield, III.: Charles C. Thomas, 1980), chaps. 16 and 17:

以下摘录自 Arthur S. Aubry, Jr. 所著《刑事审讯》（第3版，斯普林菲尔德，伊利诺伊州：Charles C. Thomas 出版社，1980 年），第 16 章和第 17 章：

“The interrogator seeks the defeat and final surrender of the subject—the securing of the confession being the final objective…. The interrogator crumbles the defenses of the subject…. He knocks out strong points. He demonstrates that the subject is lying. He destroys alibis by pointing out their absurdity or impossibility.”

审讯者寻求的是彻底击败并迫使受审者投降——获取供词是最终目标……审讯者会瓦解受审者的防御……他会击溃受审者的有力论点。他会证明受审者在撒谎。他会指出不在场证明的荒谬或不可能之处，从而摧毁它们。

“Another specific technique that works well with a wide variety of subjects is the relatively simple procedure of inviting the subject to tell the story, or tell his side of the story, and let him ramble on without interruption…. The interrogator may also ask the subject to repeat his story, perhaps on the pretext that he didn’t understand it; the idea is to tangle the subject in discrepancies.”

“另一种对各种对象都行之有效的技巧是，邀请对象讲述故事，或者讲述他自己的版本，让他畅所欲言，不要打断他……审讯者还可以要求对象重复他的故事，也许以没听懂为借口；目的是让对象陷入前后矛盾的境地。”

“The interrogator wants to maintain the psychological advantage over the subject and so refuses to address the subject as Mr. but insists on being called Mr.—or Officer—in response: “Good afternoon, Tom, I’m Mr. Caputo.”

“审讯者想要保持对受审者的心理优势，因此拒绝称呼受审者为‘先生’，而是坚持要求受审者称呼他为‘先生’或‘警官’，回应道：‘下午好，汤姆，我是卡普托先生。’

See the discussion of interviewing techniques in Alfred Kinsey, Wardell B. Pomeroy, and Clyde E. Martin, Sexual Behavior in the Human Male (Philadelphia: W. B. Saunders, 1948).

请参阅 Alfred Kinsey、Wardell B. Pomeroy 和 Clyde E. Martin 合著的《男性性行为》（费城：W. B. Saunders，1948 年）一书中关于访谈技巧的讨论。
